title: Para-Taekwondo Sınıflandırma Deneyimleri: Nitel Bir Araştırma ve Kavramsal Çerçeve Önerisi
title_original: Para-Taekwondo Sınıflandırma Deneyimleri: Nitel Bir Araştırma ve Kavramsal Çerçeve Önerisi
summary: Bu araştırma, para-taekwondo sporcularının sınıflandırma sistemine ilişkin deneyimlerini incelemeyi ve sistemin eşitlik, rekabet ve yönetsel süreçler bağlamında nasıl değerlendirildiğini ortaya koymayı amaçlamaktadır. Araştırma, yorumlayıcı paradigma çerçevesinde yürütülen nitel bir çalışmadır. Veriler, müsabaka kategorisindeki K41 ve K44 sınıflarında ve poomsae kategorisindeki P20 sınıfında yer alan toplam 20 aktif para-taekwondo sporcusuyla gerçekleştirilen yarı yapılandırılmış görüşmeler aracılığıyla toplanmış ve refleksif tematik analiz yöntemiyle çözümlenmiştir. Bulgular, katılımcıların bir bölümünün sınıflandırma sistemini adil rekabeti destekleyen bir yapı olarak değerlendirdiğini; buna karşılık bazı katılımcıların boy, uzuv uzunluğu, yaş, engel türü ve farklı sınıflardaki sporcuların birlikte yarışması gibi durumları eşitsizlik kaynağı olarak algıladığını göstermiştir. Ayrıca sınıflandırma deneyiminin motivasyon, özgüven ve spora bağlılık süreçleriyle ilişkili olabileceği belirlenmiştir. Görüşmelerden oluşturulan temalardan hareketle, sınıflandırma deneyiminin yapısal, deneyimsel ve yönetsel boyutlarını birlikte ele alan sporcu merkezli bir ön kavramsal çerçeve olarak Para-Taekwondo Sınıflandırma Deneyimi Kavramsal Çerçevesi (PTSDKÇ) önerilmiştir.

title: Time–Frequency Analysis of Muscle Activation Patterns during the Instep Kick in Elite and Amateur Soccer Players
title_original: Time–Frequency Analysis of Muscle Activation Patterns during the Instep Kick in Elite and Amateur Soccer Players
summary: The instep kick is a frequently performed, high-load soccer skill that requires precise intermuscular coordination around ball contact. This study compared time-frequency activation patterns between elite and amateur male soccer players across two kicking phases and identified the key time windows and dominant muscle contributions. Surface electromyography was recorded from seven muscles of the kicking leg in 15 elite and 15 amateur players: rectus femoris, vastus medialis, vastus lateralis, biceps femoris, tibialis anterior, medial gastrocnemius, and lateral gastrocnemius. The instep kick was divided into Phase 1, from maximum hip extension to ball contact, and Phase 2, from post-contact follow-through to maximum hip flexion. Morlet wavelet analysis was used to generate time-frequency intensity maps. Global principal component analysis was then performed to extract PC1 to PC6, and between-group differences in PC score trajectories were assessed using SPM1D independent-samples t tests, with significance evaluated under a Bonferroni adjusted threshold for the 12 PC phase comparisons. In Phase 1, PC3 showed a significant between-group difference at 54-75% of the normalized time (peak t = 7.62, p < 0.001, Hedges' g = 2.96), with higher scores in the elite group. In Phase 2, PC1 differed significantly between groups at 60-70% of the normalized time (peak t = -9.88, p < 0.001, Hedges' g = -2.03), with higher scores in the amateur group. Elite players showed a more temporally focused pre-contact activation pattern centered on mid-frequency components of the biceps femoris, whereas amateur players showed greater reliance on higher-frequency components of the medial gastrocnemius during the post-contact follow-through. These findings suggest that skill-level differences are expressed as phase-specific redistribution of muscle and frequency-band activity within critical time windows, rather than as a simple global difference in activation magnitude.

title: DISEÑO Y VALIDACIÓN DE UNA SECUENCIA DIDÁCTICA PARA LA ENSEÑANZA DE LOS ELEMENTOS TÉCNICOS BÁSICOS DEL TENIS EN SILLA DE RUEDAS
title_original: DISEÑO Y VALIDACIÓN DE UNA SECUENCIA DIDÁCTICA PARA LA ENSEÑANZA DE LOS ELEMENTOS TÉCNICOS BÁSICOS DEL TENIS EN SILLA DE RUEDAS
summary: This research focuses on the design and validation of a didactic sequence for teaching the basic technical elements of wheelchair tennis to athletes with physical disabilities in the Tennis League of the Tolima Department. The study addresses the lack of specific pedagogical resources for this Paralympic sport, which is significant in contexts like Colombia, with high disability rates due to armed conflicts and diseases. Using a mixed-methods approach (qualitative-quantitative) and a sequential exploratory design, the study characterized existing teaching strategies through observations, interviews, and questionnaires. The results showed a technical focus on stroke execution but difficulties in perception and structured evaluation, aligned with the information processing theory. Based on these findings, a 79-page didactic guide was developed, covering wheelchair movements and technical elements such as grips, serves, forehands, and backhands. The guide, validated by three experts, received high ratings for structural and content validity, with suggestions for enhancing psychological aspects and resource accessibility. The conclusions highlight the guide as an innovative tool to optimize motor learning and promote Paralympic inclusion, aligned with Colombian inclusion policies. Pilot implementations and longitudinal studies are recommended to assess its impact on athlete performance and well-being.

title: The Effects of Organizational Culture and Financial Factors on the Performance of Muay Thai Athletes in Tanah Laut Regency
title_original: The Effects of Organizational Culture and Financial Factors on the Performance of Muay Thai Athletes in Tanah Laut Regency
summary: Organizational and financial conditions constitute important contextual factors in athlete development because they shape the environment in which training, competition preparation, and performance support are implemented. This study aimed to examine the partial and simultaneous effects of organizational culture and financial factors on the performance of Muay Thai athletes in Tanah Laut Regency. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory survey design was employed. The study involved 34 male and female Muay Thai athletes who met the eligibility criteria and were included using total population sampling. Data were collected through structured questionnaires measuring organizational culture, financial factors, and athlete performance, supported by documentation of competition participation and achievement records. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression after testing the relevant classical assumptions. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov test indicated that the residuals were normally distributed (p = 0.200 > 0.05). No multicollinearity was detected, as both predictors showed a tolerance value of 0.432 and a variance inflation factor of 2.316. Heteroscedasticity testing also showed no violation for organizational culture (p = 0.153) or financial factors (p = 0.929). Partial hypothesis testing demonstrated that organizational culture did not significantly affect athlete performance (p = 0.658 > 0.05), while financial factors also showed no significant independent effect (p = 0.151 > 0.05). However, the simultaneous test revealed a significant joint effect of organizational culture and financial factors on athlete performance (F = 3.884; p = 0.031 < 0.05). The coefficient of determination was R² = 0.200, indicating that the two predictors collectively explained 20% of the variance in athlete performance, while 80% was associated with other factors. These findings suggest that organizational culture and financial support are more meaningful when functioning together within an integrated athlete-development system rather than as isolated determinants of Muay Thai performance.

title: Exclusion or Empowerment? The Role of Sports as a Tool for Social Inclusion in Ghana for People Who Experience Disability
title_original: Exclusion or Empowerment? The Role of Sports as a Tool for Social Inclusion in Ghana for People Who Experience Disability
summary: Ghana is a signatory to major international treaties which protects the rights of people who experience disability (PWEDs), including the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD), and was the first sub-Saharan African country to enact disability specific legislation. Despite these developmental milestones, PWEDs remain among the most marginalized, most stigmatized, discriminated against, and socially excluded. Existing intervention policies have so far had limited impact on the lived experiences of PWEDs. Within this context, sports have emerged as a viable tool for addressing social inequality. The study examines how disability sports can be used as a tool for promoting social inclusion among PWEDs by interrogating historical, cultural, and structural factors that shape and influence the lived experience of PWEDs. Drawing on Bourdieu’s concepts of habitus, field, and capital and Foucault’s genealogy, the study examines disability through a historical, cultural, and religious lens, connecting historical discourses with contemporary practices. Literature indicates that PWEDs have been marginalized across precolonial, colonial, and postcolonial periods, with few communities that accept PWEDs through a communal care lens but exhibit no real inclusion. Following this, the study employs a reflexive and relational ethnographic approach centered on the voices and lived experiences of PWEDs, enabling a sociological analysis of how disability is produced, reproduced, and contested across different fields. The findings revealed that disability in Ghana is a socially constructed and historically contingent phenomenon shaped by culture, religion, and colonial legacies. These factors influence access to disability sports through unequal distribution of capital(s), stigma, structural inequalities and institutional gaps. Hence, disability sport emerges as a contested space, offering opportunities for empowerment, visibility, and skill development, while capable of reproducing dominant norms. The study concludes that sport’s potential for social inclusion is not automatic but depends on the reconfiguration of power relations, redistribution of resources, and transformation of cultural meanings attached to disability. By applying Bourdieu’s and Foucault’s theories, this thesis contributes to both disability studies and the sociology of sport, by offering a nuanced understanding of disability and revealing how disability sports can contextually be used to address challenges experienced by PWEDs.

title: Penguatan Kompetensi Guru dan Pelatih Melalui Para Throwball Adaptif Berbasis Kolaborasi Tiga Pilar
title_original: Penguatan Kompetensi Guru dan Pelatih Melalui Para Throwball Adaptif Berbasis Kolaborasi Tiga Pilar
summary: This community engagement program aimed to strengthen the capacity of special school teachers and disability-sport coaches through an adapted Para Throwball program based on a Three-Pillar collaboration involving special school teachers, National Paralympic Committee (NPC) Indonesia coaches, and athletes with disabilities. The program employed a participatory approach consisting of five stages: initial coordination, development of adapted media and instructional modules, theoretical workshop, collaborative field practice, and monitoring and evaluation. Eighteen participants were involved, including six students with disabilities, two special school teachers, two coaches, and eight athletes with disabilities. The intervention used soft-foam balls, an adjustable portable net, and a task-analysis-based instructional module integrated with video tutorials. Evaluation indicated an aggregate 74.5% increase in teachers' and coaches' understanding of instructional and tactical content, exceeding the 70% program target. Athletes served as role models and enhanced learning experiences, while coaches bridged technical and tactical knowledge with school-based instruction. The program demonstrates potential for strengthening an adapted sport ecosystem from school participation toward disability sport development. However, because individual pre-test and post-test scores were not fully available, the 74.5% figure is treated as an aggregate achievement rather than evidence of statistical significance. Future programs should employ validated instruments, larger samples, and longitudinal follow-up.

title: Exploring the Backgrounds, Experiences, Motivations, and Development of School-based Wheelchair Sport Coaches
title_original: Exploring the Backgrounds, Experiences, Motivations, and Development of School-based Wheelchair Sport Coaches
summary: Coaching in adapted sport is a complex and demanding practice that requires both specialized technical expertise and a deep understanding of disability. This study explored the motivations, backgrounds, and developmental pathways of interscholastic school-based wheelchair sport coaches. We examined how coaches are introduced to wheelchair sport coaching, their initial and ongoing development, and their perspectives on effective coaching and training practices. A total of 17 coaches (10 men, 7 women) with 1 to 17 years of experience in wheelchair sports coaching from 7 interscholastic wheelchair sports teams participated in one 60-minute mini focus group discussion and responded to a set of open-ended guiding questions. Responses were recorded and transcribed. Using an interpretive phenomenological approach, data were analyzed by inductive thematic analysis. A total of five themes were identified: a) Coaching by Connection and Chance: Journey into Wheelchair Sport, (b) Guided, Observed and Informed: Building Coaching Knowledge, (c) Beyond the Game: Cultivating Care, Accountability, and Athlete Growth, (d) Navigating Coaching without a Rulebook, and (e) Learning through Adaptation: How Openness, Patience and Experiential Learning Shaped Coaching. Consistent with the adapted sport literature, formal coaching developmental experiences were limited for interscholastic school-based wheelchair sport coaches. Participants employed an athlete-centered coaching style, with most having prior coaching experience working with athletes without disabilities. The findings of this study offer practical insights, inform strategic approaches for program directors and coaches, and provide recommendations for future research. (232 words)

title: Seeking Sustainable Success in Turkish Sports Management: Structural Analysis of Athlete Selection, Development, and Performance Systems
title_original: Seeking Sustainable Success in Turkish Sports Management: Structural Analysis of Athlete Selection, Development, and Performance Systems
summary: The aim of this study is to examine the capacity of Turkish sports administration to produce sustainable success at the Olympic level from a public policy perspective and to analyze it through its institutional structure. Based on the assumption that sports services constitute a strategic public service in terms of national identity construction, social integration, and the realization of public benefit, it is accepted that Olympic success, embodied in medals, is directly related to the state's planning capacity, institutional coordination power, and human resource management. In this study, the legislation of Athlete Training Centers (SEM) and Turkish Olympic Preparation Centers (TOHM), which hold a significant place within Turkish sports administration, is examined comparatively, and talent scouting and Olympic performance monitoring mechanisms are evaluated within the context of systemic integrity. The findings suggest that the multi-actor executive structure based on sports federations and sports clubs has structural limitations in its capacity to produce sustainable Olympic success; conversely, it is predicted that a centralized management model based on early talent identification, central planning, and merit-based human resource management will offer a more systematic foundation for athlete development. In conclusion, sustainable Olympic success; This is a sensitive and national issue that is too strategic to be reduced to individual initiatives, too long-term to be left to temporary preferences, and must be addressed beyond electoral concerns. In this context, it seems possible to make the Olympic athlete training system more predictable, accountable, and sustainable if the ongoing transformation process in sports management in Turkey is supported by a strong managerial framework based on the proposed Turkish Sports Model. Accordingly, this study goes beyond a detailed legislative analysis and offers a conceptual contribution to the reassessment of the institutional transformation of Olympic athlete training policies in Turkey within the context of public sports management literature, and provides a perspective on future policy designs based on Strategic Focus.

title: Despite what we know, physical activity continues to decline: can integrating physical activity and education be a way forward?
title_original: Despite what we know, physical activity continues to decline: can integrating physical activity and education be a way forward?
summary: Despite decades of robust evidence on the benefits of regular physical activity, the fitness and health of young people are in worrying decline worldwide. Today, around 80% of adolescents fail to meet recommended daily activity levels, a trend which parallels an increase in youth overweight and obesity rates. This perspective paper examines the wide-ranging consequences of inactivity in adolescence, ranging from heightened long-term risks of chronic disease and rising healthcare burdens, to negative impacts on mental health, well-being, and the development of self-efficacy in adolescence. We discuss the possible promises and pitfalls of organized sport as a traditional strategy to engage youth in physical activity: while sports participation is linked to better physical and mental health outcomes, many adolescents seems to drop out of sport in their mid-teens due to factors such as early specialization, competitive pressures, cost, and social disparities. Therefore, we argue that youth inactivity will require a broader, more inclusive approach that goes beyond the sports club model, and propose integrating substantial daily physical activity into school curricula as a universal foundation for fitness and health. By reimagining schools as key platforms for physical activity-in partnership with community sports programs-and by implementing bold, multi-sector policies to reduce barriers to active lifestyles, society can begin to bridge the gap between what we know and what we practice. Translating knowledge into action is crucial to safeguard the health, well-being, and future resilience of the next generation.

title: Electromyographic analysis of muscle activation and co-activation across smash phases in para-badminton: an exploratory investigation of neuromuscular coordination
title_original: Electromyographic analysis of muscle activation and co-activation across smash phases in para-badminton: an exploratory investigation of neuromuscular coordination
summary: Objective This study aimed to examine and compare muscle activation and co-activation across the backswing and forward swing phases of the para-badminton smash to improve understanding of phase-specific neuromuscular coordination that may inform future biomechanical and injury-related research. Methods Nine elite para-badminton players were recruited for the study (body mass: 79.0 ± 7.9 kg; height: 172.1 ± 5.2 cm). Surface electromyography (sEMG) signals were recorded using a wireless EMG system, and data were collected from eight muscles (flexor carpi ulnaris, extensor carpi ulnaris, biceps brachii, triceps brachii, infraspinatus, latissimus dorsi, rectus abdominis, and erector spinae longissimus). Results The results indicated that the wrist (flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris) and elbow (biceps and triceps) muscles showed significantly greater activation during the forward swing ( p < 0.01–0.001), with peak activity in the early-to-mid acceleration phase; however, only the wrist demonstrated a significant change in the co-activation index (CoI) ( p < 0.001), while elbow agonist–antagonist balance remained stable. At the shoulder, the infraspinatus maintained consistent activation, whereas the latissimus dorsi was selectively recruited during the forward swing ( p < 0.01), resulting in an increased CoI ( p < 0.001). Similarly, trunk muscles exhibited phase-specific behavior, with stable erector spinae activity and significant rectus abdominis recruitment during the forward swing ( p < 0.001), leading to elevated trunk CoI. Overall, these findings indicate coordinated, segment-specific modulation of activation and co-activation to support force generation and stabilization during the acceleration phase. Conclusion Overall, the findings indicate that muscle co-activation is segment-specific and adapted to the mechanical demands of each joint within the kinetic chain. Imbalances such as excessive wrist co-activation or insufficient proximal stabilization may increase injury risk. Therefore, injury prevention in para-badminton should focus on optimizing wrist stability, maintaining elbow muscle balance, enhancing shoulder control, and improving trunk stability to support efficient force transfer and performance.

title: Beyond the Games: Media Visibility and Framing of the Paralympic Games in Greece (2016–2024)
title_original: Beyond the Games: Media Visibility and Framing of the Paralympic Games in Greece (2016–2024)
summary: In recent years, the media visibility and framing of the Paralympic Games have received considerable attention because of their potential to raise awareness of disability and promote societal change. This study had two objectives: (i) to examine the media visibility of the 2016, 2020, and 2024 Paralympic Games in Greek media, and (ii) to analyse how the Games were framed in selected national newspapers and news websites. Quantitative and qualitative content analyses were employed. The quantitative analysis measured the total hours of coverage provided by ERT, Greece's official Paralympic media rights holder, and the number of articles published by nine selected national newspapers and news websites (N = 814: 203 in 2016, 210 in 2020, and 401 in 2024). The qualitative analysis examined the same 814 articles using nine coding units: Informative, Athlete First, National Success, Publicity, Supercrip/Superhuman, Multidimensional, Impact of the PG, Business, and Political/Legal. The visibility of the Paralympic Games in the selected newspapers and news websites increased by 3.45% from 2016 to 2020 and by 90.95% from 2020 to 2024. In contrast, ERT television coverage declined by 6.95% from 2016 to 2020 and by a further 9.35% from 2020 to 2024. In 2016, Athlete First and National Success were the dominant coding units, while Athlete First remained dominant in 2020 and 2024. The underrepresentation of foreign athletes' achievements, including world records, and the continued prominence of the National Success frame indicate a strong nationalistic focus and suggest that the broader significance of the Paralympic Games may be undervalued in Greek media. Although the low prevalence of the Supercrip/Superhuman frame is encouraging, the nationalistic focus may limit broader recognition of Paralympic accomplishments.

title: Beyond physical limitations: A narrative synthesis of psychological mediators in competitive para-sport and able-bodied sport
title_original: Beyond physical limitations: A narrative synthesis of psychological mediators in competitive para-sport and able-bodied sport
summary: Competitive performance is frequently interpreted through physiological, biomechanical, technical, and tactical characteristics. However, athletes’ performance, well-being, persistence, and adaptation to competitive demands are also influenced by psychological processes. In para-sport, these processes may be shaped by disability-related and environmental contexts, including classification, accessibility, assistive technology, health variation, stigma, disability identity, and the availability of specialist support. Objective This narrative synthesis examines psychological mediators of performance and related outcomes in competitive para-sport and able-bodied sport. It aims to identify shared psychological mechanisms, examine context-specific pathways in para-sport, and outline implications for coaching, sport psychology, athlete support, and future research. Methods An integrative narrative-review approach was used. Literature was purposively identified from sport psychology, adapted physical activity, rehabilitation, disability sport, coaching, and athlete well-being research. The synthesis was guided by narrative-review quality principles, with attention to explicit aims, transparent conceptual reasoning, relevance of cited evidence, and critical interpretation of methodological limitations. Psychological factors were organised into shared mediators—self-efficacy, motivation, resilience, coping, anxiety regulation, identity, and social support—and para-sport-specific contextual influences, including classification, accessibility, equipment, health variation, and disability-related social experiences. Results The literature indicates that self-efficacy, autonomous motivation, coping, emotional regulation, resilience, athletic identity, and perceived social support are relevant in both para-sport and able-bodied sport. In para-sport, these factors may be influenced by additional conditions such as accessible facilities, specialist coaching, equipment reliability, classification processes, disability identity, travel logistics, and social attitudes. Psychological skills training may be beneficial for para-athletes, although interventions should be adapted to athletes’ sport-specific and impairment-related circumstances.

title: THE IMPACT OF THE MOTOGP RACE ON LOCAL ACCESSIBILITY TO HEALTHCARE MEASURED VIA TWO-STEP FLOATING CATCHMENT AREA MODELS
title_original: THE IMPACT OF THE MOTOGP RACE ON LOCAL ACCESSIBILITY TO HEALTHCARE MEASURED VIA TWO-STEP FLOATING CATCHMENT AREA MODELS
summary: This study investigates the impact of a major event, the MotoGP race, on local accessibility to healthcare using two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) models integrated with actual traffic data. The research focused on the region surrounding Brno, Czech Republic, analyzing accessibility changes at different times of the day over three weeks: during the event week, the following week, and three weeks after. Although increased traffic and congestion were associated with the event, the findings indicate that MotoGP’s impact on healthcare accessibility was localized and did not significantly affect the wider region. Accessibility was found to oscillate over time due to traffic and other unidentified factors, suggesting that temporal dynamics should be incorporated into 2SFCA analyses. Clustering revealed that, at most, 20% of populations experienced notable accessibility changes, primarily those west of the racetrack. This study contributes novel insights into the methodological application of 2SFCA models under event-driven traffic disruptions and provides reassurance that the annual MotoGP does not broadly impair medical access in the affected area.

title: Qualitative investigation evaluating Team USA Paralympic athletes: resources and recommendations for enhancing support systems
title_original: Qualitative investigation evaluating Team USA Paralympic athletes: resources and recommendations for enhancing support systems
summary: OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to explore athletes' perspectives on existing US Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) resources and to identify their recommendations for enhancing future initiatives aimed at promoting Paralympic athlete health, well-being and performance. DESIGN: Phenomenological qualitative study SETTING: Online. PARTICIPANTS: A convenience sample of 19 Team USA Paralympic athletes 18 years of age or older participated (female n=11; age 31±9 years) representing four categories of conditions recognised by the International Paralympic Committee (muscle and movement, bone-related, visual and central nervous system). RESULTS: The resulting codebook included 2 themes and 10 corresponding categories. Theme 1, titled Resources for Paralympic Athletes, includes five categories: (1) community-level; (2) university-level; (3) USOPC; (4) National Governing Body and (5) Resources Access, Awareness and Satisfaction. Theme 2, titled Recommendations for Improvements to the USOPC, also included five categories: (1) sports medicine; (2) disability-specific needs and classification systems; (3) sports performance; (4) resources and (5) community awareness. Study participants recognised meaningful improvements in organisational support, including expanded financial assistance and mental-health services yet persistent structural inequities continue to limit equitable access to high-quality resources. Fragmented and geographically uneven sports medicine, coaching and performance infrastructures, along with ongoing challenges in classification transparency and disability-specific programming, remain key barriers to athlete development. CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the need for decentralised clinical and performance networks, enhanced evidence-based classification practices and more robust transition planning from collegiate to elite settings. Including athlete perspectives and strengthening equitable resources creates more accessible, consistent and performance-optimising environments within the US Paralympic system.

title: Team USA Paralympic athletes’ experiences with sport participation: a socioecological qualitative study
title_original: Team USA Paralympic athletes’ experiences with sport participation: a socioecological qualitative study
summary: OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to understand Paralympic athletes' positive and negative experiences associated with their participation in Paralympic sport. DESIGN: Phenomenological qualitative study contextualised using the socioecological framework SETTING: Online. PARTICIPANTS: 19 Team USA Paralympic sport athletes (females, n=11; males, n=8; age, 31±9 y) representing 11 sports and 4 categories of eligible permanent medical conditions recognised by the International Paralympic Committee impairment classifications: (1) muscle and movement (impaired passive range of motion and impaired muscle power); (2) bone-related conditions (limb deficiency, short stature and leg-length discrepancy); (3) visual impairments and (4) central nervous system disorders (hypertonia and ataxia). RESULTS: The resulting codebook included three themes titled: (1) Journey to Becoming a Paralympic Athlete; (2) Challenges of Paralympic Sport Participation and (3) Advantages of Paralympic Sport Participation. Athletes described Paralympic participation as shaped by interconnected personal, social, organisational and policy-level influences. Inclusive sport environments, family/community support and rehabilitation experiences facilitated athletic identity development and participation pathways, although many participants reported delayed awareness of Paralympic opportunities. Challenges included financial strain, healthcare accessibility, travel demands, chronic injury management and balancing sport demands with employment, education and family responsibilities. Despite barriers, athletes described physical, psychological and social benefits including improved self-acceptance, resilience, belonging and professional growth. CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the dual reality of Paralympic sport participation: a journey characterised by resilience, achievement and community, yet marked by persistent inequities and systemic barriers. Inclusive sport environments, social support and increased institutional recognition contribute to athlete well-being and performance; however, addressing the identified challenges is essential for advancing equity and inclusion in high-performance sport. Future research should aim to quantify the barriers and benefits experienced by Paralympic athletes in relation to their health and wellness.

title: Municipal infrastructure for physical exercise and sport in Veracruz: Diagnosis of supply and service gaps toward 2030
title_original: Municipal infrastructure for physical exercise and sport in Veracruz: Diagnosis of supply and service gaps toward 2030
summary: Objective To analyze the distribution of municipal sports infrastructure and evaluate whether there are statistically significant differences in space availability across sports disciplines. Methodology: A quantitative, descriptive, and inferential study based on a census of 28 municipal sports facilities. The recorded spaces were categorized (N = 71 main facilities), and a Chi-square (X2) goodness-of-fit test was applied to assess distribution equity among the four most frequent sports categories (soccer, volleyball, multipurpose spaces, and basketball). Results: Findings show a strong prevalence of soccer (26 fields/courts) and volleyball (22 courts), compared to a scarce supply of dedicated basketball courts (6 courts) and 17 multipurpose areas. Inferential analysis confirmed statistically significant differences in facility distribution (X2=12.64, df =3, p=0.0054), indicating a clear bias toward soccer and a deficit of dedicated basketball infrastructure. Conclusions: Municipal sports facility planning exhibits structural inequality in surface allocation. Public policy strategies aligned with the 2030 Agenda are proposed to diversify sports spaces, ensure universal accessibility, and implement a continuous digitalized census.

title: Gastrointestinal temperature of elite and recreational adult runners during a 100‐mile ultramarathon under heat exposure
title_original: Gastrointestinal temperature of elite and recreational adult runners during a 100‐mile ultramarathon under heat exposure
summary: Abstract This study examined gastrointestinal temperature (T GI ) during and body mass (BM) changes pre/post the Western States Endurance Run 100 (WSER), a 100‐mile ultramarathon in hot conditions. Thirty‐nine participants ingested a telemetric pill 30–90 min before the WSER start, and BM was measured pre‐ and post‐race. Environmental conditions were recorded every 30 min at 15 locations along the course. In‐race T GI data were obtained from 23 finishers (54%; 7 females; 42 ± 11 years), including 2 podium finishers and an additional top‐10 finisher. Participants finished in 14–18 h ( n = 4), 19–25 h ( n = 6), and 26–30 h ( n = 13). Peak T GI averaged 38.90°C ± 0.55°C (range 37.76°C–40.09°C) with 9 runners exceeding 39°C and 2 exceeding 40°C. Faster finish times were associated with higher peak T GI ( r = −0.57, p = 0.004). Seven runners (30%) reached peak T GI in the final 2% of the race. Mean BM change was −1.8% ± 3.1% (range −7.4% to +6.4%), with no associations observed between BM change and peak T GI or finish time. Ambient temperature ranged 5°C–39.6°C and was associated with higher T GI ( r = 0.80, p = 0.008). Despite ambient temperatures approaching 40°C, T GI >40°C were rare and transient. Faster runners experienced greater thermal strain, likely reflecting higher metabolic heat production and exposure to the hottest course segments. Hyperthermia risk may be highest near the race finish and during the most demanding segments.

title: Barreras y facilitadores de la adherencia al fútbol recreativo en adolescentes varones con riesgo cardiometabólico: un estudio cualitativo derivado de un ECA
title_original: Barreras y facilitadores de la adherencia al fútbol recreativo en adolescentes varones con riesgo cardiometabólico: un estudio cualitativo derivado de un ECA
summary: Adherence to physical exercise programs among adolescents with cardiometabolic risk is a complex phenomenon linked to individual, social, and contextual experiences. The aim of this study was to understand the experiences of adolescents with cardiometabolic risk who participated in two recreational football modalities, identifying barriers and facilitators associated with adherence or dropout. A qualitative interpretive study was conducted with 17 male adolescents aged 11 to 15 years who participated in a randomized controlled trial comparing two football training modalities designed to promote cardiometabolic health. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven adolescents who dropped out of the program or showed low adherence, and focus groups were conducted with ten highly adherent participants. Reflexive thematic analysis was carried out by the research team through an inductive, iterative, and reflexive process, strengthened by a systematic record of analytical decisions and critical discussions among researchers, which enabled the construction of three central themes. Logistical and contextual barriers, such as transportation, weather, schedules, and organizational changes, were perceived as obstacles to continuity. Support from coaches, peers, and families emerged as a facilitator of belonging and motivation. In addition, some participants associated small-sided games with greater active participation, perceived competence, and satisfaction. The findings suggest that adherence may not depend solely on sporting interest, but also on access conditions, social support, psychological safety, perceived competence, and enjoyment. Future interventions should be inclusive, feasible, and meaningful

title: Development of an eight-shaped field test for aerobic capacity assessment in wheelchair basketball: a pilot study
title_original: Development of an eight-shaped field test for aerobic capacity assessment in wheelchair basketball: a pilot study
summary: Wheelchair basketball (WB) requires sport-specific assessment procedures that reflect the propulsion and turning demands of on-court performance. Traditional shuttle-based field tests may not fully reproduce the movement patterns of WB, particularly regarding bidirectional turns and continuous wheelchair propulsion. This pilot study aimed to develop and describe a novel eight-shaped field-test protocol designed to better reflect WB-specific propulsion and turning demands, and to explore its feasibility and preliminary cardiorespiratory responses compared with a laboratory treadmill protocol. Two male WB athletes with different functional classifications (1.0 and 3.0) completed a maximal incremental treadmill protocol and the proposed on-court test, both performed with Oxycon Jaeger® metabolic gas analysers. VO2max values reached during the field test were lower than those recorded in the laboratory for both participants (38.6 vs. 44.42 mL/kg/min for class 3.0; 32.35 vs. 38.33 mL/kg/min for class 1.0). Despite these differences, absolute VO2max values ranged from 2.11 to 2.49 L/min across both testing conditions, while ventilation responses followed the same overall pattern, with higher values generally observed in the laboratory. The proposed test is presented here as a novel protocol for future validation; it may provide a promising on-court alternative to VO2max measurement by offering greater ecological specificity than traditional shuttle run tests. Its structure allows bidirectional turns and smoother propulsion, which could help mitigate mechanical asymmetries inherent to conventional protocols. Given these preliminary results, broader validation is needed to confirm reproducibility and to establish reference percentiles across functional classes, age, and gender.

title: La práctica del Goalball como ocupación significativa: identidad, espiritualidad y significado en personas con discapacidad visual
title_original: La práctica del Goalball como ocupación significativa: identidad, espiritualidad y significado en personas con discapacidad visual
summary: Goalball, a Paralympic sport designed for people with visual impairments, has been studied mainly for its physical and social benefits, with little attention to subjective dimensions such as occupational identity, spirituality, beliefs, and values. This qualitative research, framed within the interpretive paradigm, analyzed the experiences of five athletes from the Biobío Region (Chile) through semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. The results show that the practice of Goalball operates as a meaningful occupation that transforms limiting beliefs —moving from discouragement to autonomy and self-efficacy—, promotes values such as empathy, respect, cooperation, and resilience, and channels spiritual dimensions linked to life purpose and mental strength. Furthermore, the sport contributes to the construction of a positive occupational identity, acting as a mirror of personal and collective growth. However, structural tensions persist: discontinuity of public policies, political instrumentalization of disability, and a gap between the inclusive sports environment and other social contexts that limit the transfer of learning. From the perspective of Occupational Therapy and the Model of Human Occupation, it is concluded that Goalball not only favors identity reconstruction but also requires a collective approach aimed at transforming restrictive environments. Expanding the sample and conducting longitudinal follow-ups are recommended to deepen understanding of these processes.

title: The Health Benefits of Exercise: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms
title_original: The Health Benefits of Exercise: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms
summary: Exercise is a low-cost lifestyle intervention that can prevent and alleviate various diseases. It is a potent physiological stimulus that activates conserved molecular signaling pathways. Through the coordinated integration of multiple molecules, pathways, and systems, it leads to systemic health benefits. However, most studies focus on individual systems or molecular mechanisms, lacking systematic integration of the cross-system regulation induced by exercise. We summarize the molecular mechanisms of exercise in the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, nervous systems, among others. Exercise induces the release of exerkines (e.g., irisin, interleukin-6, and brain-derived neurotrophic factor) and extracellular vesicles, which activate key signaling pathways to enhance mitochondrial function, metabolism and physiological adaptation, while suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress, thereby alleviating diseases and delaying aging through cross-system coordination. We further explore exercise-induced adaptive regulation in extreme environments, including microgravity, hyperbaria, and hypoxia, offering a multifaceted perspective on organismal health regulation. Finally, we outline the prospects and challenges of multiomics, artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine, personalized exercise prescriptions, and exercise mimetics. Overall, this review provides a more integrated perspective on the molecular basis of exercise and offers directions for future mechanistic and translational studies.

title: Sun exposure and photoprotection: Habits, knowledge, and attitudes among elite beach soccer players
title_original: Sun exposure and photoprotection: Habits, knowledge, and attitudes among elite beach soccer players
summary: Beach soccer players are exposed to prolonged ultraviolet radiation (UVR) due to the outdoor nature of the sport, minimal clothing coverage, and frequent participation in coastal environments with highly reflective surfaces. This study aimed to evaluate sun exposure habits, photoprotection practices, attitudes, knowledge related to skin cancer prevention, and the prevalence of sunburn episodes among elite beach soccer players. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted during the European Beach Soccer Qualifying Championship held in October 2025. A total of 257 elite male players from 21 European countries completed a standardized questionnaire assessing UVR exposure, photoprotection behaviors, sun-related attitudes, knowledge, and skin surveillance practices. Overall, 76% of athletes reported at least one sunburn during the previous sports season, and 35% experienced three or more episodes. Although 84% reported regular sunscreen use and 93% used products with a sun protection factor (SPF) ≥30, only 31% reported reapplying sunscreen every 2 h as recommended. Positive attitudes toward tanning remained common, while the overall knowledge score regarding skin cancer prevention was moderate (6.7 ± 1.6 points out of 10). In addition, 72% of players did not regularly perform skin self-examinations. These findings indicate that elite beach soccer players represent a high-risk population for UVR-related skin damage and highlight the need for targeted photoprotection and skin cancer prevention strategies.

title: Medical service utilization under heat stress at Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: A 6-month time series study
title_original: Medical service utilization under heat stress at Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan: A 6-month time series study
summary: This study examined the exposure–response relationships between ambient heat and medical service utilization at Expo 2025 Osaka, Japan, from April 13 to October 13, 2025. Distributed lag non-linear models with negative binomial regression were fitted to daily counts of patient presentations (PP), heat-related patient presentations (PP-HRI), and emergency transports to the hospital (TTH), using daily maximum temperature (T max ) as the primary heat exposure with daily attendance as an offset and day-of-week adjustment (maximum lag: 5 days). The median PP rate was 7.5 per 10,000 attendees, and 97.2% of cases were managed onsite. Medical encounters exhibited daily fluctuations that tracked alongside peak summer temperatures from June to August and increased in attendance toward the end of the event period. Cumulative risks at the 75th percentile of T max (34.9 °C) were elevated relative to the median (31.2 °C) for PP (RR 1.50; 95% CI 1.35–1.67) and PP-HRI (RR 4.23; 95% CI 2.51–7.10).TTH exhibited a distinct bimodal cumulative risk pattern, reaching its secondary peak of 1.71 (95% CI: 1.19–2.46) within this range. Lag-specific risks for PP and PP-HRI were elevated at lag 0–1 and attenuated at longer lags. TTH showed a more complex lag pattern, with a modest increase at lag 5. These findings characterize the temporal dynamics and exposure–response patterns of medical encounters under extreme heat and provide a basis for medical planning at mass gatherings.

title: Perceived coach autonomy support and burnout in Chinese university athletes: Basic need satisfaction as an indirect link across gender and sport type
title_original: Perceived coach autonomy support and burnout in Chinese university athletes: Basic need satisfaction as an indirect link across gender and sport type
summary: Perceived coach autonomy support is consistently associated with adaptive athlete functioning, but the specific link to burnout and its subgroup consistency remain less clear. Guided by self-determination theory (SDT), this study tested whether basic psychological need satisfaction formed a theoretically ordered indirect association between perceived coach autonomy support and athlete burnout, and whether that indirect association differed by gender or sport type. We analysed three-phase self-report data from 430 Chinese university athletes (230 men, 200 women; 291 individual-sport, 139 team-sport) from three institutions. The study had institutional review board approval (Ref. No. IRB/D-2667; 27 August 2024), and all participants provided informed consent. Analyses included a parcel-level three-factor confirmatory factor analysis, reliability and discriminant-validity checks, bias-corrected bootstrap estimation of the indirect association (5000 resamples), indices of moderated mediation, and interaction-sensitivity calculations. The parcel model showed close fit, χ 2 (24) = 25.80, CFI = 0.999, RMSEA = 0.013. The standardized indirect association was −0.295, 95% CI [−0.373, −0.221]. No statistically detectable moderation emerged for gender (index of moderated mediation = −0.109, 95% CI [−0.261, 0.037]) or sport type (0.046, 95% CI [−0.120, 0.211]). The findings are consistent with basic psychological need satisfaction as a proximal statistical link between perceived coach autonomy support and burnout in this sample. They do not establish causal mediation, subgroup equivalence, or intervention effects.

title: Greater Goal Difference is Associated with Lower Physical Demands in Cerebral Palsy Football Referees
title_original: Greater Goal Difference is Associated with Lower Physical Demands in Cerebral Palsy Football Referees
summary: This study examines the association between match outcome variables, total goals, goal difference, and the physical demands placed on referees in cerebral palsy (CP) football. Thirteen international referees were monitored via global positioning devices during 42 official matches at the 2022 CP Football World Cup and World Championships. Physical demands, including distances covered at various speeds and acceleration/deceleration metrics, were analyzed. Results revealed moderate to high negative correlations between goal difference and total, explosive, walking, jogging, me- dium-intensity running, high-intensity running and sprinting distances; maximum speed, accelerations, low intensity acceleration in zones 1 and 2, low intensity deceleration in zones 1 and 2, and player load (ρ = -0.30 to -0.54; p <0.001 to 0.04). In contrast, total goals showed only isolated, moderate correlations with medium-intensity running distance and deceleration Z1 (ρ = -0.33; p < 0.03 to 0.04). These findings indicate that match competitiveness, reflected by the goal difference, is a key factor associated with referees’ physical workload in CP football, with closer matches eliciting higher physical demands on the referees. The results highlight the importance of considering match context in referees’ training, recovery management, and match allocations, ensuring they are adequately prepared for the high demands of closely contested matches and can recover effectively during international-level CP football competitions.

title: Understanding psychological development in high performance coaching: Coaches perceptions on key attributes, facilitators and barriers.
title_original: Understanding psychological development in high performance coaching: Coaches perceptions on key attributes, facilitators and barriers.
summary: The study aims to explore HP coaches’ perceptions and experiences of psychological development within elite sport environments. Specifically, the study will examine how coaches conceptualise psychological development, which psychological attributes they perceive as important for effective coaching performance, and the factors they perceive as facilitating or limiting their psychological development. The study will adopt an exploratory qualitative design informed by a critical realist ontological position and an interpretivist epistemological position. Data will be generated through semi-structured interviews with 10–12 HP coaches currently working within elite, Olympic or Paralympic sport environments. Participants will be selected using criterion-based purposive sampling. To be eligible, coaches must have at least 10 years of coaching experience and have coached an athlete to medal success at a major sporting competition. Interview data will be analysed using inductive, latent reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s (2006, 2021) six-phase approach. NVivo will be used to support data management and organisation. A reflexive diary and critical friend process will be used throughout analysis to support researcher reflexivity and analytical development. The study will provide insight into coaches’ psychological development and the factors that may shape this process.

title: Rebordering the banlieue: Saint-Denis, Paris Olympics and the politics of place
title_original: Rebordering the banlieue: Saint-Denis, Paris Olympics and the politics of place
summary: This article sheds light on contested place-making practices in Saint-Denis, a marginalized banlieue in northern Paris, at a conjuncture when the commune was positioned as the epicenter of the Paris 2024 Summer Olympic Games. It conceptualizes the reconfiguration of a racialized urban margin into the epicenter of a mega-event as urban rebordering—that is, the reconfiguration of techniques of distancing that render the banlieue selectively incorporable while fragmenting it across spatial, temporal, and discursive registers. The analysis relies on a topological understanding of urban politics and borders, whereby proximity is understood as relational rather than territorially fixed, pointing to the profound social distances within conditions of geographical proximity, such as those emerging in Saint-Denis in the context of hosting the Games. Drawing on twelve months of ethnographic research, it traces rebordering across multiple dimensions of urban life in the banlieue, situating the emerging ruptures in relation to longer histories of marginalization.

title: O ENSINO DO ESPORTE ADAPTADO NAS AULAS DE EDUCAÇÃO FÍSICA DO ENSINO MÉDIO INTEGRADO NO INSTITUTO FEDERAL DE CIÊNCIA E TECNOLOGIA DA BAHIA.
title_original: O ENSINO DO ESPORTE ADAPTADO NAS AULAS DE EDUCAÇÃO FÍSICA DO ENSINO MÉDIO INTEGRADO NO INSTITUTO FEDERAL DE CIÊNCIA E TECNOLOGIA DA BAHIA.
summary: Introdução: O presente estudo é um relato de experiência que se desenvolveu nas turmas do ensino médio integrado num campus do Instituto Federal de Ciência e Tecnologia da Bahia. A inquietação surge a partir da necessidade de discutir a Educação Física Adaptada e o Esporte Adaptado no ambiente escolar. Objetivo apresentar uma proposta de ensino, baseada nas aulas de Educação Física com o tema esporte adaptado no ensino médio integrado, com o intuito de promover discussões sobre pessoas com deficiência e a prática esportiva. Método: A proposta de ensino inicia-se com uma análise histórica das pessoas com deficiência, desde o período histórico que promovia o extermínio das pessoas com deficiência, até o momento em que as pessoas com deficiência passam a ter direito à escolarização, sendo inseridas no ambiente escolar. Neste contexto de análise histórica, apresentamos a Educação Física Adaptada, posteriormente apresentamos a discussão referente ao Esporte Adaptado. Com este conteúdo, apresentamos os aspectos históricos com o seu surgimento na Inglaterra e o desenvolvimento de algumas modalidades paralímpicas no Brasil até os dias atuais. Possibilita-se aos estudantes a vivência prática de alguns esportes Adaptados (Vôlei sentado, Bocha, Tênis de mesa adaptado, futebol de cegos e Goalball) Resultados: Durante a análise histórica em relação à pessoa com deficiência, muitos estudantes ficam perplexos com o sofrimento vivenciado por estas pessoas e a luta constante pela busca de espaço na sociedade, quando se iniciam os estudos referente ao esporte adaptado é despertado o interesse pelos estudantes em conhecer alguns esportes e em particular as modalidades paralímpicas, os discentes ficam encantados com a vivência dessas modalidades, proporcionando a experimentação de colocar-se no lugar do outro durante a realização das atividades práticas. Conclusões: Compreende-se que essa proposta de ensino realizada no ambiente escolar, possibilita aos docentes do ensino médio serem desafiados a realizarem essa contextualização e a vivência do esporte adaptado para os estudantes, a fim de que se promova uma perspectiva de análise e reflexão em torno das potencialidades da pessoa com deficiência e a mesmo tempo diminuir a visão referente à Educação Física na escola que se resume apenas as atividades esportivas realizadas na quadra.

title: Development and Validation of a Sitting-Balance Confidence Scale for Individuals with Spinal Cord Injury
title_original: Development and Validation of a Sitting-Balance Confidence Scale for Individuals with Spinal Cord Injury
summary: Background/Objectives: Participation in sport and daily activities among individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) is influenced not only by physical capacity but also by psychological factors such as balance confidence. Existing measures primarily assess performance or fear of falling, leaving a gap in evaluating how perceived balance impacts activity choice. This study aimed to (1) develop a Patient-Reported Sitting Balance Confidence (PR-SBC) interview instrument to enable therapists to assess and evaluate non-ambulatory individuals with SCI, (2) incorporate participation-based activities relevant to perceived confidence in community and sport activities, and (3) evaluate its psychometric properties. Methods: Instrument development used a Delphi process with clinicians, researchers, individuals with SCI, and care partners to create and refine items. The final 19-item PR-SBC was administered to 31 individuals with SCI (inpatient and outpatient). Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), internal consistency via Cronbach’s alpha, and validity through correlation with the SCI Falls Concern Scale (SCI-FCS). Exploratory regression analyses examined demographic and clinical predictors of PR-SBC scores. Results: The PR-SBC demonstrated promising inter-rater reliability (ICC = 0.96) and internal consistency (α = 0.931). A moderate inverse correlation with SCI-FCS scores was also observed (r = −0.51). Outpatient setting and manual wheelchair use were associated with higher balance confidence, while injury-related variables were not significant predictors. Conclusions: The PR-SBC is a potential interview instrument for assessing sitting balance confidence in individuals with SCI. By capturing perceived balance across functional and participation contexts, it complements existing measures and may support improved clinical decision-making, targeted interventions, and enhanced participation outcomes.

title: Case Report: Reduced lactate response despite maintained performance: a case study of a world-class Paralympic sprinter undergoing pre-games hypoxic training
title_original: Case Report: Reduced lactate response despite maintained performance: a case study of a world-class Paralympic sprinter undergoing pre-games hypoxic training
summary: This case study describes the physiological adaptations and performance outcomes of a high-intensity interval training in hypoxia (HITH) intervention in a world-class female Paralympic sprinter during her final preparation for the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games. The participant was a Tier 5, T47 national record-holder in the 400 m. Over an approximately 13-week (≈3-month) period leading up to the Games, she performed HITH on a cycle ergometer, generally twice weekly, in a normobaric hypoxic chamber (FiO 2 14.5%, ∼3,000 m). Performance was assessed via periodic anaerobic power tests and official 400-m race times, and 3-min post-set blood lactate concentration was measured after each HITH session. Throughout the intervention, no clear improvement was observed in maximal or mean power output during laboratory tests, and the athlete's 400-m time at the Paralympic Games was consistent with her 2023 season best, indicating performance maintenance. During the intervention, 3-min post-set blood lactate during repeated-sprint sessions conducted within a broadly consistent framework showed an overall downward trend (Set 1: ∼21 to ∼18 mmol·L⁻¹) while mean and peak power were maintained or slightly increased. The HITH intervention was not associated with enhanced maximal power or a faster 400-m time; the reduced blood lactate response is interpreted cautiously and, because potential mechanisms were not directly measured, is offered as a hypothesis of altered lactate kinetics rather than a demonstrated adaptation.

title: High-performance sport in a developing country through the lens of coaches and sports directors
title_original: High-performance sport in a developing country through the lens of coaches and sports directors
summary: The importance of identifying the key factors for success in high performance sport has been studied for several years. Although the focus during the competition is on the sporting result, it is important to note that the result in sport is preceded by a series of circumstances and factors closely linked to the context of the athlete's preparation process. Therefore, this study aims to identify the potential factors affecting the high-performance sport in a developing country like Colombia from the perception of high-performance coaches. High-performance coaches (HPC) and high-performance directors (HPD) were asked to answer two questionnaires. Descriptive and factorial analyses were performed to identify the decisive factors. Likewise, a one-way ANOVA between groups was performed to assess whether the responses were significantly different. The principal results showed that more than half of the factors identified by developed countries as determinants of success in high performance sport are perceived as weaknesses within the current high-performance system of the emerging country studied. The factors that emerged from this study were Process, Technical and social support, Structure of sports policies, Competition level, and Contractual conditions. This study identifies some factors that have been limiting or facilitating the results of Colombian athletes in elite sports. It also opened new perspectives of research on the field of HPC and HPD, especially inside Latin America Caribbean region and for developing countries more generally.

Likewise, a one-way ANOVA between groups was performed to assess whether the responses were significantly different. The principal results showed that more than half of the factors identified by developed countries as determinants of success in high performance sport are perceived as weaknesses within the current high-performance system of the emerging country studied. The factors that emerged from this study were Process, Technical and social support, Structure of sports policies, Competition level, and Contractual conditions. This study identifies some factors that have been limiting or facilitating the results of Colombian athletes in elite sports. It also opened new perspectives of research on the field of HPC and HPD, especially inside Latin America Caribbean region and for developing countries more generally.

title: YUQORI MALAKALI BOCCIA O‘YINCHILARINING MASHG‘ULOTLARINI ANIQLIK, TAKTIK VA FUNKSIONAL TAYYORGARLIKNI UYG‘UNLASHTIRISH ASOSIDA INDIVIDUALLASHTIRISH
title_original: YUQORI MALAKALI BOCCIA O‘YINCHILARINING MASHG‘ULOTLARINI ANIQLIK, TAKTIK VA FUNKSIONAL TAYYORGARLIKNI UYG‘UNLASHTIRISH ASOSIDA INDIVIDUALLASHTIRISH
summary: The article substantiates a methodological approach to organizing training sessions for highly qualified boccia players, in which throwing accuracy is considered not as an isolated motor quality but as the result of coordinated interaction among the technical, tactical, functional, and psychoregulatory components of training. Based on contemporary research, a training session structure is proposed that includes initial diagnostic assessment, movement calibration, variable accuracy training, tactical modeling of an end, and controlled throwing under progressively increasing loads. The methodology provides for the differentiation of training tasks according to sport class, individual motor profile, and ball delivery method. The proposed pedagogical criteria include mean distance error, within-series variability, the proportion of successful tactical decisions, stability of accuracy during the final part of the training session, and subjective perception of load. The proposed approach integrates the content of sports training, pedagogical monitoring, and adaptive individualization into a unified system for managing athletes’ preparedness.

title: Ice and Snow Sports Behavior Recognition Technology Based on EM Algorithm and RepVGG Neural Network
title_original: Ice and Snow Sports Behavior Recognition Technology Based on EM Algorithm and RepVGG Neural Network
summary: Lane-specific characteristics, traffic flow, vehicle properties, and atmospheric conditions profoundly impact successive vehicle time intervals. A lane position plays an important role due to the differences in flow properties, such as speed, density, and overtaking maneuvers, which can vary significantly across different lanes. Larger or heavier vehicles, which are assigned to specific lanes, tend to require although time more space from each other due to their dimensions and braking requirements. Driver behavior, as determined by reaction times and compliance with rules, introduces variability, especially in challenging weather or road conditions, such as rain, snow, or icy roads. In addition to geographical location and distance of travel, temporal factors also influence perception and choice, including the day of the week and variations in light intensities. Effective modeling approaches and effective traffic control require a comprehensive analysis of these factors. In the current work, a dataset of independent traffic roads with all the above-mentioned variables was constructed, and time-gap prediction between two consecutive cars driving along every road lane was performed using Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Random Subspace (RSS). In addition, new optimization algorithms, referred to as the Partial Reinforcement Optimizer (PRO) and the Walrus Optimizer (WO), were utilized to enhance predictive capability, resulting in strong hybrid models. In this evaluation approach, we also employed Analysis of Variance (ANOVA’s) sensitivity analysis technique to identify the most contributing feature in our data, providing us with the importance of each variable in the prediction process. The SVPR hybrid model performed the best for lane 1, with the highest R² of 0.997, the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2.36E+07, and the lowest Ratio of RMSE to Standard deviation (RSR) of 0.059 during testing, thereby reflecting its superior predictive accuracy and minimal error. For lane 2, the hybrid SVWO model emerged as the most effective, achieving the highest R² of 0.989, the lowest RMSE of 3.36×10^7, and the smallest RSR of 0.107, demonstrating its robust capability in capturing lane-specific traffic dynamics. These findings highlight the potential of hybrid optimization techniques to enhance predictive performance and minimize errors in practical traffic management systems.

title: The Effects of Dry Needling and Tecar Therapy on Post-Exercise Gastrocnemius Muscle Recovery in Mixed Martial Arts and Crossfit Athletes
title_original: The Effects of Dry Needling and Tecar Therapy on Post-Exercise Gastrocnemius Muscle Recovery in Mixed Martial Arts and Crossfit Athletes
summary: This study investigated the recovery effects of combining dry needling (DN) with Tecar therapy (T) compared to each treatment alone on gastrocnemius muscle recovery in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) and CrossFit athletes after a fatigue protocol. Forty-eight athletes were randomly assigned to one of the four groups: DN/T, DN/sham T, shamDN/T, and a control group. DN involved needling three trigger points per muscle, while Tecar therapy used electromagnetic waves applied via capacitive transfer. Assessments of perfusion (PU), elasticity (ME), the pain threshold (PPT), and the reactive strength index (RSI) were taken at rest, post-fatigue, post-treatment, and 48 hours post-treatment. A mixed ANCOVA showed the DN/T group had significantly higher PU scores post-treatment compared to all other groups (p < 0.001). ME was significantly lower in the DN/T group at both post-treatment and 48 hours into recovery (p < 0.05). PPT was significantly higher in the DN/T group at both time points, particularly compared to the control condition (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001). The RSI was also significantly higher in the DN/T group at both time points compared to all other groups (p < 0.001). In conclusion, combining DN with T demonstrated superior recovery benefits for blood perfusion, muscle elasticity, the pain threshold, and reactive strength compared to either treatment alone or control, suggesting a synergistic effect beneficial for athletes' muscle recovery.

title: Midstance instant identification methods in sprinting: comparative assessment and biomechanical implications in able-bodied athletes and athletes with lower limb-amputation
title_original: Midstance instant identification methods in sprinting: comparative assessment and biomechanical implications in able-bodied athletes and athletes with lower limb-amputation
summary: Introduction: Midstance is a key instant in running, marking the transition from braking phase to propulsion phase. Despite its significance for stability and force transmission, a standard identification method of midstance instant is lacking, leading to inconsistent data interpretations. This study aimed to systematically compare different midstance instant identification methods and to highlight how they affect trunk and lower-limb kinematics in both able-bodied sprinters and sprinters with lower limb amputation. Methods: 22 able-bodied athletes, 4 athletes with unilateral transtibial and 4 athletes with unilateral transfemoral amputation performed two maximal 60-m sprints on an instrumented track. Kinematic and kinetic data were recorded using 10 infrared cameras and 9 embedded force platforms. Seven methods were considered, including kinematic and kinetic approaches. Sagittal absolute angles of trunk, thigh, and shank segments, as well as the hip, knee and ankle joints were extracted at the instants identified by each method. Both temporal differences and corresponding body postures at the detected instants were evaluated across methods and against the theoretical midpoint of stance (50%). Differences were assessed using either one-way repeated measures ANOVA or Friedman tests, depending on data normality, followed by Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons when appropriate. Results: Instants identified as midstance consistently preceded the temporal midpoint of the stance phase across methods considering both able-bodied and athletes with lower-limb amputation. Kinematic methods showed limited consistency, identifying different instants within the stance phase. Their agreement with kinetic-based methods was only partial and depended on both the identification method and the athlete group. Consequently, midstance identified with different methods reflected distinct body postures within the stance phase. This resulted in significant variations in segment and joint angles, potentially leading to different biomechanical interpretations of sprinting. Discussion: Since the present findings suggest that method performance may differ across able-bodied athletes, athletes with transtibial amputation, and athletes with transfemoral amputation, researchers and practitioners should carefully consider the choice of method, clearly disclose it and ensure its consistent application.

title: Towards a new approach to hosting sports mega-events in the era of climate change: the climate resilience framework
title_original: Towards a new approach to hosting sports mega-events in the era of climate change: the climate resilience framework
summary: Rapid changes to the climate have impacted on the planning, implementation, and legacies of major sports events due to extreme conditions, escalating expenditures, resource limitations, and heightened demands for environmental responsibility. At present, sustainability frameworks utilised in sporting events are in part fragmented, tend towards the generic, or are simply inadequate to address the specific vulnerabilities of the sports events’ ecosystem. This mismatch is exacerbated by the fact that sports mega-events (SMEs) are increasingly taking place in challenging climates (e.g. Qatar andSaudi Arabia) and are becoming more bombastic. SMEs are especially vulnerable to the impact of climate change, given their substantial consumption of resources on one hand, and their ecological impact on the other. Current approaches to hosting SMEs tend to concentrate mostly on carbon accounting or infrastructure efficiency, neglecting wider climate-related hazards such as heatwaves, air pollution, biodiversity deterioration, and disruptions to supply chains and transportation. By building on previous work, we advance the argument that a more tailored approach is urgently needed and introduce a new framework designed specifically for SMEs in the climate change era, structured around six core pillars: ethics, agility, flexibility, vulnerability management, mitigation, and collaboration. To illustrate its practical value, the framework is applied to the case study of the Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games 2024 as a test case, highlighting how it can enhance resilience to support sports events and planners better respond to climatic impact.

title: Assessment of the development of adaptive physical culture and sports in Krasnoyarsk Region
title_original: Assessment of the development of adaptive physical culture and sports in Krasnoyarsk Region
summary: The aim of the study is to assess the state of adaptive physical culture and sports in the Krasnoyarsk Territory for the period 2023–2024. The work is based on aggregated statistical data obtained from organizations of the region's municipalities that work with people with disabilities. The authors conducted a comparative analysis of the dynamics of key indicators across a number of sections. The research methods included: surveys and questionnaires of employees of specialized organizations, analysis of scientific and methodological literature, as well as mathematical and statistical data processing. As a result, key trends in the development of adaptive sports in the region were identified, problem areas were determined (insufficient accessibility of facilities, shortage of specialized personnel) and positive shifts (growth in the number of participants, expansion of the range of sports). title: Systematic Review of Literature: Biomechanical Analysis of the Long Jump Hitch-Kick Technique Using Kinovea
title_original: Systematic Review of Literature: Biomechanical Analysis of the Long Jump Hitch-Kick Technique Using Kinovea
summary: A common flight strategy for the long jump is the hitch-kick, which assists the athlete in preparing for a good landing and controlling the forward angular momentum generated at takeoff. This systematic review included open-access studies published from 2016 to 2026, which specifically stated Kinovea as the video-analysis software used for the biomechanical or kinematic analysis of the long jump. Eight qualifying studies were combined in total. The other investigations provided supporting information on takeoff, center-of-mass behavior, joint angles, landing mechanics and technique evaluation. Two specifically compared or evaluated the flight mechanics of the hitch-kick. The most convincing direct evidence is that the hitch- kick, compared with the hang technique, can generate better center-of-mass trajectory features, jump distance, and multiple positive take-off/flight metrics in a single-subject comparison study. In larger long-jump research, take-off velocity, take-off center of mass height and knee- angle parameters have all commonly been linked to performance. However, the evidence base is heterogeneous, with predominance of descriptive/correlational designs, 2-D analysis of video in the sagittal plane and small samples. Therefore, a pooled effect-size meta-analysis was not warranted.

title: The Effect of Relative Age in Paralympic Sports: A Systematic Review
title_original: The Effect of Relative Age in Paralympic Sports: A Systematic Review
summary: The relative age effect (RAE) is a phenomenon characterized by the significant selection of athletes born in the first months of the year, which gives them an advantage over those born in the second half of the year throughout their athletic careers. The objective of this study is to identify the effects of relative age on para-athletes in Paralympic sports. A search equation was designed using PIO (population/intervention/outcomes) parameters with Boolean operators (AND and OR) to group relevant studies in a search across four databases (Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus), guided by the PRISMA guidelines. Five (5) studies met the eligibility criteria: involving athletes of both sexes, in individual and team sports within the Paralympic movement, of any category and competitive level, with birth data organized by quartiles (1960–2025), and published in Spanish, English, or Portuguese. The data from the five included studies will be synthesized descriptively by country, sport type, category, and competitive level. If comparable data are available, a random-effects meta-analysis and a subgroup analysis (by sport type, category, and competitive level) will be explored. The results of this systematic review are expected to determine whether the relative age effect (RAE) is present among Paralympic athletes and whether its magnitude varies according to sport type, category, or competitive level. If its presence is confirmed, this research will provide pioneering evidence to expand the theoretical understanding of RAE beyond conventional sports and may guide future decisions regarding talent identification and functional classification processes within Paralympic sports.

title: Neuromuscular coordination and motor adaptability in the fencing lunge and attack: a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review
title_original: Neuromuscular coordination and motor adaptability in the fencing lunge and attack: a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review
summary: Competitive fencing is a rapid, open-skill combat sport in which offensive success depends on precise organisation, timing, and adaptability of whole-body movement rather than speed alone. This systematic review synthesised empirical evidence on neuromuscular coordination, movement variability, and motor adaptability during fencing lunges and attacks. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and used PICOS-based eligibility criteria for English-language, peer-reviewed empirical quantitative studies of competitive fencers, including able-bodied and wheelchair fencers, that examined movement, motor control, coordination, or adaptability of the lunge/attack. Searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 712 records published across 2000-2026; 20 studies were included after screening and full-text assessment. Study quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) 2018. Because the included studies were heterogeneous in population, weapon, task, measurement, and outcome, findings were synthesised narratively using thematic coding rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Across the corpus, expertise was associated with earlier anticipatory and postural adjustments, more efficient muscular sequencing, greater rear-leg propulsion, and stronger capacity to correct ongoing actions under uncertainty. Movement variability appears functional rather than merely error, but standardised variability metrics are lacking. Future research should prioritise longitudinal and intervention designs, broader para-fencing evidence, and standardised biomechanical reporting.
