title: PTCG: Persona-guided Tree-based Counterargument Generation
title_original: PTCG: Persona-guided Tree-based Counterargument Generation
summary: The ability to generate counterarguments is important for critical thinking and balanced discourse, yet existing approaches typically produce only a single counterargument, failing to capture the diversity and persuasiveness required in real-world debates. To address this limitation, we propose Persona-guided Tree-based Counterargument Generation (PTCG), a framework that combines Tree-of-Thoughts-inspired step-wise generation and pruning with speaker persona selection. By estimating the author's persona from the original argument and incorporating speaker personas representing distinct perspectives, PTCG operationalizes perspective-taking and enables the generation of diverse counterarguments. Results from LLM-as-a-Judge, classifier-based assessment, and human evaluations indicate that PTCG shows consistent improvements in both the diversity and persuasiveness of counterarguments compared to baseline methods.

title: Anticipation and decision-making in fencing: a systematic review of neuromuscular and cognitive correlates
title_original: Anticipation and decision-making in fencing: a systematic review of neuromuscular and cognitive correlates
summary: This review evaluated how neuromuscular, perceptual-cognitive, neural, and training-related markers are associated with anticipation and decision-making in fencing, and identified consistency and methodological limitations. Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect were searched using predefined PICOS-based terms. Of 114 records, 15 duplicates were removed, 99 records screened, 34 full texts assessed, and 22 reports included: 21 empirical studies and one narrative review for contextual synthesis. Study quality was appraised using the MMAT 2018. Participant totals were not pooled because a verified cross-study count was unavailable and overlapping cohorts could cause double counting. Meta-analysis was not defensible because outcomes, tasks, instruments, comparison groups, and reporting formats were heterogeneous; findings were synthesised narratively according to SWiM principles. Inter-rater kappa was not calculated and could not be reconstructed retrospectively. Expertise was associated with earlier muscle activation, more economical EMG coordination, faster or stable responses, stronger cortical preparation, and efficient visual search. Evidence for trainability remained limited.

title: SMHAT-1 mental health screening in Russian male professional soccer players: associations with age, competition level, and self-perceived team status
title_original: SMHAT-1 mental health screening in Russian male professional soccer players: associations with age, competition level, and self-perceived team status
summary: Introduction Mental-health symptoms in professional athletes may impair performance, making timely screening important. This study examined Athlete Psychological Strain Questionnaire (APSQ; SMHAT-1 Step 1) scores and their associations with competition level, age, and self-rated team status in 170 male Russian soccer players. Methods This cross–sectional study included 170 male Russian soccer players (mean age 21.1 ± 4.3 years). APSQ scores and their associations with competition level, age, and self–rated team status were assessed using ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors. Results Mean APSQ score was 17.8 ± 4.4, and 101/170 players screened positive at the ≥17 triage threshold (59.4%; 95% CI 51.9–66.5%). Age was positively associated with APSQ score ( b = 0.28 points/year, 95% CI 0.07–0.48, p = 0.010). Self-rated team status showed an uncertain negative association ( b = 0.28, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.07, p = 0.113). The overall four-level competition term was significant in the full model ( F (3,164) = 3.37, p = 0.020); however, no planned contrast remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and the overall league test was not significant after exclusion of the four-player First League subgroup ( F (2,161) = 1.52, p = 0.221). Discussion These cross-sectional findings require cautious interpretation and confirmation in longitudinal, team-linked studies with further psychometric evaluation of the Russian adaptation.

title: Performance, Biomechanical Demands, Injury Burden, and Health Surveillance in Wheelchair Court Sports and Selected Para Sport Cohorts: A Systematic Review
title_original: Performance, Biomechanical Demands, Injury Burden, and Health Surveillance in Wheelchair Court Sports and Selected Para Sport Cohorts: A Systematic Review
summary: Background: Research examining performance, biomechanics, workload, injury, and health in Para sport is heterogeneous and is particularly focused on wheelchair-based sports. This systematic review synthesized quantitative evidence focused predominantly on wheelchair basketball, wheelchair rugby, and wheelchair tennis, with additional evidence from Para-cycling, mixed wheelchair-sport populations, and broader Paralympic cohorts. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance and predefined eligibility criteria, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar were searched without publication-date restrictions. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, sports, measurements, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was evaluated using design-specific appraisal tools. Results: Twenty-two quantitative studies were included. Evidence was focused on wheelchair basketball, wheelchair rugby, and wheelchair tennis, with additional evidence from Para-cycling, mixed wheelchair-sport populations, and broader Paralympic cohorts. Findings indicated associations among trunk function, functional classification, wheelchair mobility, upper-body function, propulsion characteristics, workload responses, and sport-specific performance. In one small study involving 10 wheelchair tennis athletes, medicine-ball throw performance was strongly correlated with serve accuracy (r = 0.874); this finding should not be generalized beyond that study. Prospective surveillance studies also identified meaningful injury and illness burdens across Para athlete populations. Conclusions: Available evidence suggests that performance and health in the represented Para sport populations are influenced by interacting functional, biomechanical, workload, and health-related factors. However, the evidence base is limited by small samples, heterogeneous methods, and a predominance of observational designs. Individualized assessment, workload monitoring, and health surveillance therefore represent provisional practice considerations rather than established best-practice recommendations.

title: Egyptian Sports Soft Power
title_original: Egyptian Sports Soft Power
summary: Like wealthy Arab Gulf states, Egypt uses sports to boost its international image and tourism, and, despite its poor human rights record and economic problems, position itself in a more positive light internationally at a time when the country&s;s geopolitical clout is low. Moreover, sports as a strategic soft power tool is a pillar of Egypt&s;s 2030 national sustainable development agenda. Egypt&s;s elite sports ranking falls in the middle range of countries&s; performance, compared to that of the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, suggesting that money in and of itself does not determine performance. Similarly, the ranking suggest that Egypt lacks a critical mass of sport assets to successfully push it into the top rankings, even though it has a dominant position in squash, relies on football superstar Mohammed Saleh and other international Egyptian athletes to promote tourism and attract global media coverage, has successfully hosted international sporting events, and can point to the performance of Egyptian athletes at the Olympics and Paralympics.

title: From park courts to podium: How sports science transformed GB Wheelchair Tennis
title_original: From park courts to podium: How sports science transformed GB Wheelchair Tennis
summary: Over the past three decades, GB wheelchair tennis has evolved from a largely informal participation sport into a highly professional, performance-driven discipline underpinned by applied sports science. This transformation has been driven by sustained collaboration between athletes, practitioners, and academic institutions, enabling the development of evidence-based approaches to training, equipment design, and competition preparation. Early stages were characterised by limited infrastructure, minimal scientific understanding, and unstructured training. However, targeted research in physiology, biomechanics, and performance analysis established the foundation for structured athlete development. Advances in field- and laboratory-based testing have enabled practitioners to identify key determinants of performance, including aerobic and anaerobic capacity, mobility efficiency, and technical proficiency. Research has highlighted the importance of movement efficiency and the athlete-wheelchair interface, with optimised chair configuration and propulsion mechanics enhancing performance and reducing injury risk. Interdisciplinary support, including nutrition, recovery, and thermal management strategies, has further improved athlete preparation. Collectively, the GB model demonstrates how integrated sports science can transform Paralympic sport, contributing to sustained international success and providing a framework for future innovation.

title: Exercise and Autonomic Cardiovascular Function—Insights From Spinal Cord‐Injured Humans: A Narrative Review
title_original: Exercise and Autonomic Cardiovascular Function—Insights From Spinal Cord‐Injured Humans: A Narrative Review
summary: The cardiovascular response to acute exercise is mediated by the autonomic nervous system (ANS) control mechanisms that modulate vascular resistance to support blood pressure and ensure adequate blood flow to active muscles. These autonomic neurocirculatory control mechanisms include a feedforward mechanism, known as central command, and three feedback mechanisms, namely, (1) the exercise pressor reflex, (2) the baroreflex, and (3) the arterial chemoreflex. The purpose of this narrative review is to present the alterations in autonomic cardiovascular function during dynamic exercise with insights from individuals living with spinal cord injury (SCI). To fully appreciate these alterations, we first provide a general overview of ANS control of cardiovascular responses to exercise in non-injured individuals with intact supraspinal control, followed by an overview of the acute cardiovascular response to exercise in individuals with SCI. We also review the impact of exercise interventions in individuals with SCI on autonomic cardiovascular control and cardiac and vascular adaptations.

title: Pre-competitive anxiety in padel: the role of sex and competitive level
title_original: Pre-competitive anxiety in padel: the role of sex and competitive level
summary: Introduction: Padel is an intermittent racket sport characterised by physical, technical-tactical, and psychological demands. Competitive anxiety may affect performance and well-being. Objective: This study aimed to analyse pre-competitive anxiety in padel players according to sex and competitive level. Methodology: The sample comprised 136 players, including 68 men and 68 women, classified as professionals (n = 20) or amateurs (n = 116). The Sport Anxiety Scale-2 was used to assess somatic anxiety, worry, and concentration disruption. Descriptive statistics and two-way analyses of variance examining sex, competitive level, and their interaction were conducted, with significance set at p < .05. Results: No significant sex-by-level interaction was observed for any anxiety dimension. Somatic anxiety did not differ significantly according to sex or competitive level. Worry was significantly higher in women than in men (mean difference = 3.21 points; p < .001) and in amateurs than in professionals (mean difference = 2.17 points; p = .015). Concentration disruption was also higher in women (mean difference = 1.93 points; p = .005) and amateurs (mean difference = 1.85 points; p = .007). Amateur women recorded the highest concentration disruption score (10.6 ± 3.3 points), whereas professional women also showed elevated worry (13.9 ± 3.4 points). Items concerning poor performance received the highest ratings, while somatic symptoms received the lowest. Conclusion: These findings are consistent with greater cognitive and attentional involvement than somatic expression in pre-competitive anxiety. Psychological preparation should be tailored to players’ needs, particularly women and amateurs.

title: PREVALÊNCIA DE DORES E LESÕES ENTRE ATLETAS DE PARACICLISMO E SEUS FATORES ASSOCIADOS
title_original: PREVALÊNCIA DE DORES E LESÕES ENTRE ATLETAS DE PARACICLISMO E SEUS FATORES ASSOCIADOS
summary: Paracycling is a growing sport in the national and international Paralympic scene, characterized by high physical and biomechanical demands. Prolonged exposure to training and competitive loads can contribute to the development of musculoskeletal pain, thereby compromising athletes' performance and functionality. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of injuries and pain among paracyclists and to identify potential associated factors. Thirty-one athletes from various paracycling functional classes participated in the study and were assessed during the Brazil Paracycling Cup held in Maringá, Paraná, in 2025. Data collection involved a descriptive health history interview, the McGill Pain Questionnaire, and the Wisconsin Pain Inventory. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t test and Spearman's correlation. Although most athletes reported making biomechanical adjustments to their equipment, pain was observed in 74.2% of the participants, with the highest frequency and intensity reported in the lumbar region. Furthermore, 18 athletes (58.1%) stated they had sustained a paracycling-related injury within the previous 12 months; the most common injuries were tendinitis (lumbar, hip, and knee), followed by dislocations (shoulder and ankle) and fractures (clavicle and forearm). The study concludes that paracyclists exhibit a high prevalence of pain, particularly in the lumbar region and the lumbopelvic complex. These results underscore the importance of systematic pain monitoring, the implementation of preventive strategies, and multidisciplinary care in competitive paracycling. title: Intensity‐dependent ventilatory and cardiopulmonary patterns during exercise in trained individuals with cerebral palsy: An exploratory study
title_original: Intensity‐dependent ventilatory and cardiopulmonary patterns during exercise in trained individuals with cerebral palsy: An exploratory study
summary: Abstract Cerebral palsy (CP) is associated with altered exercise physiology, but it remains unclear how ventilatory and cardiopulmonary responses are expressed under high physiological demand in individuals with CP. Six athletes with CP (spastic CP: n = 3, all GMFCS III, all male, mean age 24 years; ataxic CP: n = 3, GMFCS I/I/III, two female, mean age 28 years) and three non‐disabled controls (CON: two female, mean age 28 years) performed a heart rate‐matched incremental rowing protocol. Oxygen uptake, minute ventilation (), tidal volume ( V T ), respiratory frequency and O 2 pulse were described across sitting rest and target heart rate stages of 120, 140, 160 and 180 bpm. Descriptive analyses with effect sizes were performed. Peak , recorded at the 180‐bpm stage, appeared lower in CP subtypes than in CON (spastic CP: 33.9, 44.8, 31.7; ataxic CP: 35.3, 32.3, 28.3; CON: 49.3, 39.8, 48.5 mL kg − 1 min − 1 ). With increasing exercise intensity, O 2 pulse tended to increase progressively in CON and ataxic CP; in spastic CP, the increase appeared more attenuated. V T appeared lower in CP than CON across all stages. At the 180‐bpm stage, spastic CP showed a narrow inter‐individual range (71.4–88.3 L min − 1 ) relative to CON (90.3–138.3 L min − 1 ); ataxic CP showed wide variability (48.3–112.9 L min − 1 ). title: Características Antropométricas, Morfológicas y Composición Corporal En Practicantes de Goalball: Una Revisión Sistemática.
title_original: Características Antropométricas, Morfológicas y Composición Corporal En Practicantes de Goalball: Una Revisión Sistemática.
summary: Esta revisión sistemática tiene como propósito identificar, analizar y sintetizar la evidencia científica disponible sobre las características antropométricas, morfológicas y de composición corporal en practicantes de goalball, deporte paralímpico para personas con discapacidad visual. Se busca establecer un perfil físico de referencia para este grupo poblacional, considerando variables como sexo, nivel competitivo (élite/no élite), clasificación funcional visual y edad. La búsqueda se realizará en bases de datos como PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science y SPORTDiscus, siguiendo las directrices PRISMA para revisiones sistemáticas, e incluirá estudios observacionales que reporten mediciones antropométricas (talla, peso, longitudes, perímetros), morfológicas (somatotipo, proporcionalidad) y/o de composición corporal (porcentaje de masa grasa, masa muscular, masa ósea) en jugadores de goalball. Se espera que los resultados permitan construir un perfil antropométrico y de composición corporal de referencia para este deporte, identificar diferencias asociadas al sexo, nivel competitivo y clasificación funcional, y detectar vacíos metodológicos en la literatura actual. Esta síntesis aportará evidencia útil para entrenadores, preparadores físicos y profesionales de la salud en procesos de detección de talento, planificación del entrenamiento y prevención de lesiones, además de sentar las bases para futuras investigaciones en el ámbito del deporte paralímpico.

title: Indicators of the functional state of adolescents with visual impairment
title_original: Indicators of the functional state of adolescents with visual impairment
summary: This article examines the functional state and physical performance indicators of adolescents aged 12–15 with visual impairment. The study assessed the functional capabilities and strength indicators of the respiratory, cardiovascular, and vestibular systems using vital lung capacity (VLC), heart rate (HR), the Ruffier–Dickson index, the Yarotsky test, and hand dynamometry. The results revealed that in adolescents with visual impairment, the functional capabilities of the cardiorespiratory system, physical performance, and certain coordination indicators are insufficiently developed. According to the Ruffier–Dickson index, satisfactory results were recorded in 12-year-old girls, while the indicators for the remaining groups were rated as below average. The slow recovery process after physical exertion and the results of the Yarotsky test indicate the need to improve the functional preparedness of this cohort through an individualized approach. The findings substantiate the importance of considering the functional state when organizing adaptive sports and physical education classes for adolescents with visual impairment.

title: Effects of Cervical Motion Restriction on Wheelchair Propulsion Velocity and Upper-Limb Kinematics in Healthy Individuals
title_original: Effects of Cervical Motion Restriction on Wheelchair Propulsion Velocity and Upper-Limb Kinematics in Healthy Individuals
summary: Forward head flexion during wheelchair propulsion has been suggested to compensate for reduced trunk muscle strength in individuals with spinal cord injury, but the influence of restricting head-neck movement on propulsion remains unclear. This study examined wheelchair propulsion under cervical fixation and non-fixation conditions. Fourteen healthy young men (20.7 ± 0.5 years) performed 5 m wheelchair propulsion under both conditions. Propulsion was recorded with a smartphone camera, and coordinates of the left ear, shoulder, elbow, and wrist were extracted using You Only Look Once version 7 (YOLO v7) to calculate upper-arm segment and elbow angles and angular accelerations. Analysis focused on the first three propulsion cycles after movement onset. Propulsion velocity showed a significant main effect of measurement point, but neither the main effect of cervical fixation nor the condition-by-point interaction was significant. Velocity increment differed significantly among measurement intervals, whereas the condition effect and interaction were not significant. Cervical fixation was associated with a smaller minimum upper-arm segment angle and greater upper-arm segment excursion, maximum elbow angle, and elbow range of motion. A significant condition-by-cycle interaction was found for minimum elbow angle, with a smaller angle under fixation during the first cycle. Minimum upper-arm segment angular acceleration in the flexion direction also differed among cycles. Thus, cervical fixation was associated with changes in upper-limb kinematics, but a statistically significant change in propulsion velocity was not demonstrated. These preliminary findings provide a basis for future studies in wheelchair users and athletes.

title: Mental health literacy and mental health in at-risk populations
title_original: Mental health literacy and mental health in at-risk populations
summary: This thesis explores mental health literacy (MHL) and mental health difficulties in at-risk populations. Young people, particularly males, are vulnerable to the onset of mental health difficulties, failing to access support and increased risk of suicide. Supporting people with mental health difficulties and improving prognosis is an important area of public health concern. Chapter one is a systematic review of gender differences in MHL of young people (ages 12-25 years). 14 studies were identified and critically assessed. The nature of gender differences in MHL of young people is complex but most consistently reported in depression. Females tended to have higher levels of MHL than males. The implications for public health interventions and future research are discussed. Methodological components of MHL research, such as the use of case vignettes are also considered. Chapter two is a qualitative research study of male professional footballers’ lived experiences of mental health difficulties and help-seeking using interpretative phenomenological analysis. One superordinate theme emerged from the data; Survival. This is discussed through six subordinate themes and alongside existing literature pertaining to identity, transition, personality and emotional development. The clinical implications of the findings are discussed, as well as suggestions for future research. Chapter three is a reflective paper considering the use of Cognitive Analytic Therapy as a tool for reflexivity in qualitative research. The opportunities and limitations of this approach are considered, alongside reflections on the research process.

title: Evaluation of Child Protection Practices of Sports Federations in Türkiye Within the Framework of International Practices
title_original: Evaluation of Child Protection Practices of Sports Federations in Türkiye Within the Framework of International Practices
summary: This study examines child protection practices of national sports federations in Türkiye in comparison with the child safeguarding policies and institutional mechanisms identified in the countries included in the document analysis. A two-stage qualitative research design was adopted. In the first stage, official policy and institutional documents relating to child protection in the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Germany, Australia, the Netherlands and Türkiye were examined using document analysis. In the second phase, semi-structured individual interviews were conducted with six federation officials from the Turkish Football, Fencing, Curling, Skiing, Table Tennis, and Orienteering Federations who are responsible for or directly involved in practices related to the protection of children. The documents were analysed using document analysis, while the interview data were analysed using thematic content analysis. The findings indicate that the level of institutionalisation of child protection practices in sport in Türkiye remains limited compared with international examples. Awareness-raising initiatives within federations are primarily directed towards coaches, whereas measures targeting athletes and other stakeholders remain limited. Furthermore, key safeguarding mechanisms-including independent reporting systems, a safe sport helpline, child protection procedures, safer recruitment policies, and systematic monitoring processes have not yet been institutionalised at the national level. The interview findings highlight the need for a national child protection system supported by standardised policy documents, compulsory training programmes, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and effective monitoring mechanisms. The findings further suggest that establishing a centralised child protection in sport system, coordinated by the Ministry of Youth and Sports and aligned with Türkiye's legal, institutional, and cultural context, could contribute to the institutionalisation of child protection practices, the implementation of common safeguarding standards across sports federations, and the development of safer sporting environments.

In the first stage, official policy and institutional documents relating to child protection in the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Germany, Australia, the Netherlands and Türkiye were examined using document analysis. In the second phase, semi-structured individual interviews were conducted with six federation officials from the Turkish Football, Fencing, Curling, Skiing, Table Tennis, and Orienteering Federations who are responsible for or directly involved in practices related to the protection of children. The documents were analysed using document analysis, while the interview data were analysed using thematic content analysis. The findings indicate that the level of institutionalisation of child protection practices in sport in Türkiye remains limited compared with international examples. Awareness-raising initiatives within federations are primarily directed towards coaches, whereas measures targeting athletes and other stakeholders remain limited. Furthermore, key safeguarding mechanisms-including independent reporting systems, a safe sport helpline, child protection procedures, safer recruitment policies, and systematic monitoring processes have not yet been institutionalised at the national level. The interview findings highlight the need for a national child protection system supported by standardised policy documents, compulsory training programmes, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and effective monitoring mechanisms. The findings further suggest that establishing a centralised child protection in sport system, coordinated by the Ministry of Youth and Sports and aligned with Türkiye's legal, institutional, and cultural context, could contribute to the institutionalisation of child protection practices, the implementation of common safeguarding standards across sports federations, and the development of safer sporting environments.

title: Optimising Wheelchair Sprint Power Output Through Standardised and Individualised Force–Velocity Profiling
title_original: Optimising Wheelchair Sprint Power Output Through Standardised and Individualised Force–Velocity Profiling
summary: ABSTRACT This study aimed to develop a standardised individualised wheelchair sprinting protocol with increasing resistances to generate linear force–velocity and parabolic power–velocity profiles, applicable across wheelchair sports with various classification levels. Twenty‐seven wheelchair athletes (16 wheelchair rugby [WR] and 11 wheelchair basketball [WB]) completed six 10 s sprints on a wheelchair ergometer with 2 min rest in between. Sprint 1 was completed at the same resistance coefficient for all athletes (μ = 0.012, court resistance). For the remaining five sprints, resistances were individually increased based on predicted peak power output values. Linear regression equations were determined between forces and velocities per push for both peak and mean values. Linear relationships were more stable using the mean values compared to peak values per push ( R 2 : 0.78 for mean power output and R 2 : 0.72 for peak power output). Across the six sprints, forces increased (WR: +59%, and WB: +53%), whereas velocities decreased (WR: −40% and WB: −33%). The highest mean power output per push were achieved in sprint 3 for WR and sprint 4 for WB. On average, the peak of the power parabola occurred at a mean velocity of 2.85 ms −1 and mean power output of 414 W. This wheelchair sprint protocol with individualised increases in resistance provides an applicable force–velocity relationship across sports with various classification levels when modelled using the mean force and velocity per push. Together with the subsequent power–velocity relationship, this protocol can be used to optimise power production relative to individual baselines and help work towards the most optimal force–velocity profile.

title: What is known about pressure injury prevention and management approaches among individuals with mobility impairments participating in disability sport? A scoping review
title_original: What is known about pressure injury prevention and management approaches among individuals with mobility impairments participating in disability sport? A scoping review
summary: INTRODUCTION: Pressure injuries are a significant health concern for individuals with mobility impairments, impacting participation and quality of life. Sport is a meaningful leisure occupation for many but poses unique occupational, physical, and environmental challenges which increase the risk of pressure injuries. Occupational therapists can support those with mobility impairments in balancing pressure injury risk and participation in sport; however, little is known about effective management in sport. This scoping review aimed to map existing evidence on pressure injury prevention and management approaches among individuals with mobility impairments participating in disability sports. METHODS: A systematic search of six databases, grey literature, policy documents, and guidelines was conducted in August 2025. Sources were included if they addressed individuals of any age, participating in sports using adaptive equipment and reported prevention or management approaches for pressure injuries. Findings were synthesised using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework. CONSUMER AND COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT: Consumers and community members were not involved in this scoping review. RESULTS: Ten sources met inclusion criteria, with representation from eight disability sports: seven quantitative studies, one mixed methods study, one position statement, and one clinical guideline. Owing to the immaturity of the field, both the clinical guideline and position statement drew on minimal evidence specific to sport, limiting their applicability. CONCLUSION: Evidence on pressure injury prevention and management in disability sport is largely focused on the body functions and structures domain, with limited consideration for activities, participation, and environmental factors that influence risk. The evidence base remains underdeveloped, limiting occupational therapists' access to evidence-informed strategies for pressure injury prevention and management in this population. Future research should prioritise occupational analyses of sports participation, mapping tasks, environments, and equipment interfaces across different sports and athlete groups. Generating sport-specific evidence will enable robust guidelines and occupation-based interventions that align with athletes' real-world experiences.

title: Center of gravity at the point of contact during single and double leg stepback and punch techniques in boxing: A comparative study
title_original: Center of gravity at the point of contact during single and double leg stepback and punch techniques in boxing: A comparative study
summary: Introduction: The position of the center of gravity (COG) relative to the base of support influences balance, mobility, and force transfer in boxing, still little is known about how the footwork used in a stepback affects COG position when a counter punch delivery. Objectives: This study aimed to compare the height of the center of gravity at the moment of contact during single leg stepback and punch (COG 1) versus double leg stepback and punch (COG 2) techniques in boxing. Methodology: Ten boxers (n = 10) participated in this comparative study, with mean age of 22.1 ± 1.63, height of 164.5 ± 2.3 cm, and weight of 60.1 ± 3.2 kg. Center of gravity height was measured as a percentage of body height at the precise moment of punch contact for both single-leg and double-leg stepback techniques. Data normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, standard error) were calculated for both conditions. A paired-samples t-test was conducted to determine statistical significance between the two techniques, with alpha set at .05. Results: The Shapiro-Wilk normality test confirmed that both COG 1 (W = .813, df = 10, p = .313) and COG 2 (W = .727, df = 10, p = .124) were normally distributed. Descriptive statistics revealed that COG 1 had a mean of 77.12% body height (SD = 8.33, SE = 2.14), while COG 2 had a mean of 71.22% body height (SD = 6.12, SE = 1.15). The paired t-test demonstrated a statistically significant difference between the two techniques (Mean difference = 3.17, SD = 2.01, SE = .731, 95% CI [2.87, 4.13], t(9) = 4.1, p = .004). Discussion: The findings indicate that single-leg stepback techniques result in a significantly higher center of gravity at the moment of punch contact compared to double leg stepback techniques. A higher COG during single leg stepback may compromise stability but could potentially facilitate faster recovery and mobility. Conversely, the lower COG in double-leg stepback suggests enhanced stability and grounding, which may contribute to more powerful punch delivery but at the cost of reduced mobility. Conclusion: This study provides empirical evidence that single leg and double leg stepback and punch techniques produce significantly different center of gravity positions at the moment of contact phase.

title: Three-dimensional crustal structure of Mount Isa, metallogenic province in northern Australia from ambient noise tomography
title_original: Three-dimensional crustal structure of Mount Isa, metallogenic province in northern Australia from ambient noise tomography
summary: SUMMARY The Mount Isa Province in northern Australia represents one of the largest exposed Proterozoic crustal regions within the Australian continent and is recognized globally for its world-class mineral deposits. The underlying crustal architecture has been investigated using a series of geophysical profiles informed by geological mapping, gravity, magnetic, magnetotelluric and seismic data. In this study, we reanalyse legacy passive seismic data recorded across the entire province to generate a high-resolution crustal shear wave velocity model using ambient noise tomography. These results are interpreted alongside reflection seismic profiles acquired along the same survey lines to provide complementary constraints on crustal composition, also with an association of surface geology. Our model reveals distinct velocity contrasts at some major crustal boundaries, including the Gidyea Suture Zone and several major fault zones. Mapped upper crustal intrusive bodies based on seismic reflections appear to cluster around high-velocity anomalies at 5 km depth in our model, and they seem to be linked to the broader higher velocities within the Mount Isa Inlier at 15–20 km depth. These fast, mid-to-lower-crust features probably represent mafic intrusions associated with a trans-lithospheric magmatic system that also involves felsic volcanism and associated metallogenic activity across the broader region. The research results of this area show how passive seismology can be integrated with other geophysical data sets to improve our understanding of fundamental structures for large mineral deposit systems worldwide.

title: Scalable Production of Lead-212 and Actinium-225 Generators with Fusion Neutrons
title_original: Scalable Production of Lead-212 and Actinium-225 Generators with Fusion Neutrons
summary: Targeted alpha therapy will require a large expansion of ${}^{212}$Pb and ${}^{225}$Ac production. We propose neutron- and photon-driven routes that convert ${}^{230}$Th, ${}^{231}$Pa, ${}^{232}$Th, and ${}^{237}$Np into generator parents ${}^{228}$Th and ${}^{229}$Th. The most direct ${}^{225}$Ac route is ${}^{230}$Th(n,2n)${}^{229}$Th. A 10 MW deuterium-tritium (D-T) neutron source irradiating thorium with a 27% ${}^{230}$Th isotopic fraction accumulates about 250 Ci of ${}^{229}$Th in six months, initially enough for five million ${}^{225}$Ac dose-equivalents per year, and its 7916 yr half-life makes it useful for millennia. This requires only $\sim$2 gigawatt-days of D-T fusion operations. Thermal-neutron irradiation of tens of grams of ${}^{230}$Th produces gram quantities of ${}^{232}$U, a decades-long source of ${}^{228}$Th for millions of ${}^{212}$Pb dose-equivalents per year. Alternate routes proceed through ${}^{231}$Pa: fusion neutrons produce 1 to 2 tonnes of ${}^{231}$Pa per gigawatt-year from ${}^{232}$Th, and a thermal reactor converts up to 0.4 g of ${}^{232}$U per gram of ${}^{231}$Pa. Each gram of stored ${}^{232}$U produces 10 mg (8.2 Ci) of ${}^{228}$Th per year. Subsequent ${}^{228}$Th(n,$γ$)${}^{229}$Th converts 0.07 to 0.34 g of ${}^{229}$Th per gram of ${}^{228}$Th. We also analyze the ${}^{237}$Np(n,2n)${}^{236\mathrm{m}}$Np route to ${}^{228}$Th. These pathways scale from kilowatt to megawatt D-T sources and could secure millions of ${}^{212}$Pb and ${}^{225}$Ac dose-equivalents per year.

title: Probing the Structure and Dynamics of LLM Value Expression through Value Conflicts
title_original: Probing the Structure and Dynamics of LLM Value Expression through Value Conflicts
summary: Ethical evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs) often characterizes model values as static and monolithic. In contrast, we argue that LLM value expression is better understood as a structured yet dynamic phenomenon. To investigate this, we introduce Conflict-driven Value Probing, a controlled framework that places LLMs in value conflicts and implements four types of interventions that perturb these conflicts to probe LLM value expression. Applying this framework to ten LLMs, we identify three recurring patterns. (1) Expression duality: models shift from broad idealistic orientations in abstract assessment toward more pragmatic priorities in concrete conflicts. (2) Functional steerability: models readily reconfigure their expressed value profiles toward task-defined value objectives. (3) Bounded plasticity: such reconfiguration is not without constraints, i.e. pressure induces a security- and goal-oriented priority shift while negative framing distinguishes protected values from those more amenable to redirection. Together, these findings characterize both the structure and dynamics of LLM value expression: context flexibly reconfigures expressed priorities, yet within behavioral boundaries. This behavioral account provides a foundation for understanding controllability, alignment, and safety in LLMs. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ZeroGen-Lab/CFProbe.

title: Feeling the nation together: Offline esports spectatorship and the sensorial imagined community in China
title_original: Feeling the nation together: Offline esports spectatorship and the sensorial imagined community in China
summary: Offline esports spectatorship has become an important setting in which nationalist feeling generated online is acted out through the body. This article draws on participant observation at four cinema screenings held in Zhuhai during the 2025 League of Legends World Championship, together with semi-structured interviews with eleven participants, to propose the analytical concept of the “sensorial imagined community.” The concept describes how a physical venue converts loose online sentiment into a felt experience of collective identity, and it does so along four interlocking dimensions: spatial anchoring, sensory synchronization, bodily co-presence, and narrative negotiation. Where the body re-enters the communicative process, we argue, the mechanism by which a community is imagined widens from the asynchronous reading Anderson described to synchronous sensory contact and shared physical practice. The framework thus extends imagined community theory into sensory and bodily territory.

title: Beyond the Games: Sustainable Infrastructure for Staycations
title_original: Beyond the Games: Sustainable Infrastructure for Staycations
summary: Mega sports events, such as the Olympics and the FIFA World Cup, require large-scale infrastructure development, often leading to underutilized “white elephants” post-event. This paper explores sustainable strategies for repurposing such sports infrastructure to support staycations and community well-being. It examines challenges, including economic burdens and environmental impacts, while highlighting successful examples of adaptive reuse worldwide. The study proposes transforming mega-event venues into multifunctional hubs to promote local tourism, community engagement, and economic growth. By integrating cultural events, wellness retreats, adventure sports, and eco-friendly practices, these structures can enhance urban vibrancy and sustainability. The findings underscore the importance of long-term legacy planning and community-centred approaches, ensuring that mega-event investments yield continuous economic, social, and cultural benefits.

title: “As the Developing Situation Warrants”: U.S. Counterterrorism Policy Considered Through the 1994 Gerry Adams Visa Debate
title_original: “As the Developing Situation Warrants”: U.S. Counterterrorism Policy Considered Through the 1994 Gerry Adams Visa Debate
summary: This thesis analyzes the 1994 U.S. decision to grant Sinn Féin leader Gerry Adams a visa and what it reveals about American counterterrorism policy in the immediate post–Cold War period. Long suspected of senior involvement in the Provisional Irish Republican Army during the Troubles (1968–1998), Adams had previously been denied entry under terrorism-related immigration provisions. His case became a flashpoint inside the U.S. government: officials debated whether diplomatic opportunity, domestic political incentives, and momentum toward peace in Northern Ireland warranted a departure from the prior “no concessions” posture toward IRA-linked figures. Situating the controversy within U.S. terrorism discourse from the 1970s through the early 1990s, the thesis argues that counterterrorism considerations, while real, were ultimately subordinated to political and institutional agendas. Using oral histories, press coverage, and declassified intelligence and diplomatic records, it traces how interagency conflict, the Irish-American lobby, and the National Security Council’s framing of U.S. mediation shaped the outcome. The visa approval signaled a willingness to accept perceived security risk for a larger strategic payoff and underscores how U.S. leaders apply the “terrorist” label selectively, enabling tactical diplomacy while complicating counterterrorism coherence in principle and practice.

title: IMPLICATION IN YOUNG ADULT NOVELS ABOUT THE GDR: HISTORICAL FICTION FOR A DEMOCRATIC FUTURE
title_original: IMPLICATION IN YOUNG ADULT NOVELS ABOUT THE GDR: HISTORICAL FICTION FOR A DEMOCRATIC FUTURE
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines the pedagogical potential of young adult literature about East Germany to help readers reflect on the legacies of authoritarian rule and questions of responsibility, accountability and agency. Drawing on Michael Rothberg's concept of the implicated subject, I argue that young adult literature exploring implication offers crucial frameworks for strengthening democratic consciousness. While much young adult literature about the GDR perpetuates problematic victim/perpetrator binaries that obscure the complex realities of life under authoritarianism, Dorit Linke's Jenseits der blauen Grenze demonstrates an alternative approach. Through analysis of Linke's sophisticated narrative techniques, including her use of fragmented storytelling and montage, I show how the novel positions readers as active interpreters who must recognise patterns of complicity and implication in everyday social relations. Rather than presenting clear‐cut heroes and villains, Linke reveals how ordinary people become entangled in systems of power through accommodation, silence and their positioning within social structures that sustain authoritarian rule. This nuanced exploration of implication proves especially relevant for contemporary Germany, where young people face rising authoritarianism and need tools for understanding how individual choices shape political systems and democratic institutions.

title: Soft Power and Sport in Germany
title_original: Soft Power and Sport in Germany
summary: This chapter argues that Germany&s;s years of enforced demilitarisation, after the atrocities of World War II, coupled with Germany&s;s unique role in the politicisation of modern sport, have combined to lead the country becoming adept at developing mechanisms suitable for using sport to acquire soft power. These seemingly juxtaposed threads have been inter-woven throughout German history with the politicisation of modern sport taking place from the early 19th century to what is often considered the first sports mega-event (SME), the 1936 Olympic Games, through to the specialised nurturing of elite sport in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). The expertise in soft power acquisition was developed during the post-war period in West Germany (1949–1990) and accelerated after German unification in 1990. This expertise led to the very successful hosting of the 2006 FIFA World Cup and the generation of soft power. The chapter sets out to unravel this paradoxical legacy through a brief discussion of Germany&s;s influence on the politicisation of modern sport, an overview of its post-war development as a demilitarised ‘civilian power’ and through the example of the 2006 FIFA World Cup which ultimately led to Germany&s;s rise as a soft power nation.

title: “Should I stay or should I go?” Is there a use by date on coach-athlete relationships? Shifting, temporal and contextual notions of power-relations within track and field athletics
title_original: “Should I stay or should I go?” Is there a use by date on coach-athlete relationships? Shifting, temporal and contextual notions of power-relations within track and field athletics
summary: In high-performance sport, the coach–athlete relationship is often framed as central to athlete development and well-being. Yet, such relationships are dynamic, contested, and deeply embedded within broader sociocultural and institutional landscapes. This study critically reconsiders how athletes experience and interpret these relationships in UK high-performance track and field athletics. Drawing on poststructural and postmodern theory and sensibilities, this research explores how athletes navigate, resist, and engage with complex power relations. Semi-structured interviews with twelve high-performance athletes were analysed through a Neo-Foucauldian lens producing a paired extended vignette. Findings suggest that dominant model-based approaches to coach-athlete relationship research are both limited and limiting, and ignore complex social dynamics. Power is shown to be fluid, temporal, relational, and non-possessive, challenging traditional conceptualisations of power. This work contributes a theoretically rich and empirically grounded reconceptualisation of coach–athlete dynamics, offering new ways to understand how power operates in high-performance sport.

title: How Has Brazil used Sport as a Soft Power Tool?
title_original: How Has Brazil used Sport as a Soft Power Tool?
summary: This chapter aims to discuss the strategies that Brazil has used to expand its soft power through using sport. Brazil gained some soft power during the last decades of the 20th century through the success of the men&s;s national football team. That happened by chance, as the country had not invested in cultural diplomacy to use football as a soft power tool. At the beginning of the current century, Brazil adopted a more strategic approach by hosting sports mega-events as a vehicle to help the country expand its soft power and diplomatic status. Hosting the two top-tier sport events in the world – the FIFA Men&s;s World Cup and the Olympic Games – in the same decade seemed a golden opportunity. However, the lack of planning on how to leverage potential impacts and legacies of the sports mega-events and the overreliance on the traditional approach of improving image led the country to “soft disempowerment” instead. Brazil could have improved its diplomatic status by using sports mega-events, if a more strategic approach had been implemented. Nevertheless, the long-term structural problems of the country have made the task of using sport achievements (either on or off field) a big challenge.

title: Beijing 2008–2022: fast-evolving policy, planning, and architectural approaches to the Summer and Winter Olympic Games
title_original: Beijing 2008–2022: fast-evolving policy, planning, and architectural approaches to the Summer and Winter Olympic Games
summary: Throughout the twentieth century, mega-events have long been framed as a one-off spectacle that cannot be readily duplicated. Recently, several cities have begun organizing these mega projects in quick succession. Until now, research has explored little of the planning dynamics between multiple events, their wider impacts and legacy. By providing a historic overview covering Beijing’s 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games, we explore the relationships between mega-event planning, delivery, and legacy. Through this investigation, we examine the long-term spatial visions in regional, urban, and architectural scales across the two events. We then identify continuity or changes in approaches, in particular with reference to the re-use of mega-event infrastructures and facilities and how these affect the legacies of the events. Our findings show a clear policy learning amid shifting urban objectives, with the scale of intervention expanded from the metropolitan to macro-regional.

title: Case Studies in Disaster Response and Emergency Management
title_original: Case Studies in Disaster Response and Emergency Management
summary: Designed to enable practitioners and students to evaluate a variety of real-life emergencies from every angle, this full-featured third edition of Case Studies in Disaster Response and Emergency Management provides clear, thorough, step-by-step descriptions of more than 100 major disasters or emergencies. Arranged chronologically, the case studies explore incidents from around the globe, including natural disasters, industrial accidents, epidemics, and terrorist attacks. A series of questions offered alongside each case study encourages the reader to think critically about the problem at hand, to evaluate courses of action, and to understand both anticipated and unforeseen outcomes of decisions that are made. This hands-on approach invites practitioners and students to apply theoretical emergency management techniques in a safe test environment. Case Studies in Disaster Response and Emergency Management, Third Edition provides readers with the most modern and current case studies in disaster response and emergency management. This book can be used in group project settings, as individual homework assignments in training courses for first responders, law enforcement, and government employees, or to complement existing emergency management textbooks in Public Administration, Public Management, and Public Affairs programs.

title: An intimate understanding : the rise of British musical revue 1890-1920
title_original: An intimate understanding : the rise of British musical revue 1890-1920
summary: A close examination of more than 100 play scripts and the unpublished writings of Revue impresario Andre' Charlot (1882-1956) provides the original bases for this thesis. Although it is usually assumed that British musical Revue's origins must be French, a close look at its genealogy shows that the elements of Revue existed in British musical theatre before 1890. These included Burlesque, Burletta, Musical Comedy, Variety, Concert Party and Ballet. The rise of the up-to-date thing called Revue was partly the product of general social change during the late Victorian and Edwardian eras. Of particular importance to the development of Intimate Revue--the notably British contribution to the genre--was the physical development from 1890 of London's West End, particularly the building of many small and medium-sized theatres. A number of "proto-revues" and short "revues" included in Variety bills preceded the arrival of "real" Revue in 1912. In that year, Revue escaped Variety via the latest of many changes in jurisdiction which finally allowed its presentation in "theatres". Revue might not have developed beyond the Spectacular type except for the 1914-1918 war and its austerities. Charles B. Cochran's serendipitous Odds and Ends (1914-1915) is properly the first Intimate Revue, though the genre was subsequently given its definitive shape by Charlot. The development of its distinctive theatrical form is characterised in the development of Revue specialists, the most important of which are shown to be the literary-minded authors of mini-dramas: "sketches." All the elements of the developed form meet in the Charlot revue Buzz Buzz (1918-1920). It is argued that Intimate Revue, while gradually losing its "musical" aspect, held to this model for more than three decades; it is also argued that Intimate Revue's example altered the course of Revue in the United States.

title: The British colonial legacy: sport and politics in multi-ethnic Malaysia from 1800 to 2000
title_original: The British colonial legacy: sport and politics in multi-ethnic Malaysia from 1800 to 2000
summary: The objective of the research was to explore the development of modern sport in Malaysia and to identify the socio-political and ethnic issues and other problems associated with it. The time period studied is from the year 1800 to the year 2000, which covers the periods of British colonial rule and Malaysia as an independent nation. The extended period of British administration left a paramount effect on the Malaysian society. Eight sport enthusiasts, forty schools, twelve sport associations, the Ministry of Youth and Sport of Malaysia, the Ministry of Education of Malaysia, and the Olympic Council of Malaysia were approached to gather the primary or raw data for the study. In addition, historical facts and sociological perspective on sport and physical education gathered from library research were combined to form the main ingredients and cross-analysed for discussion in the thesis. A chapter was constructed to understand the reason for British global expansion, their sport idealism and eventually the socio-political impact on Malaysia. A subsequent chapter was constructed discussing the independent government's attempt to redress the ethnic groups imbalance in economy, education and sport, as a result of the colonial legacy, in order to develop a just and harmonic society. Sport was found to be both the `enhancing' and `deterring' factors for a genuine national unity to materialise. Issues on power politics, economy, education and sport were found to be very much entangled and intertwined with the ethnic phenomenon. The research concluded that Malaysia's short history as an independent nation with very distinguished multi-ethnic and multicultural society provided an unsettled and unstable platform for a suitable environment for sport to develop successfully. Universal sport sociological theories related to the main issues investigated were compared and tested on the Malaysian sport scene to identify the `grounded theory'. Finally several `grounded theories' were presented as closure of the thesis.

title: Translation of humour with special reference to the cartoons in 'Leman' and other popular weekly humour magazines of Turkey
title_original: Translation of humour with special reference to the cartoons in 'Leman' and other popular weekly humour magazines of Turkey
summary: In this dissertation, the various strategies of humour translation have been analysed by taking various cartoons with speech bubbles from the popular Turkish humour weekly magazine Leman and other similar publications. Generally considered as an extremely problematic, sometimes next to impossible, task within the translation studies, humour translation requires and deserves special attention since, as it was explained in the related sections, it may unite or separate people within the context of one single joke. As we also have stated elsewhere in the text, the description of both humour and translation, as two separate concepts, are not available in certain and decisive terms. This is especially true for the concept of humour which also covers the areas of laughter, jokes, wit, satire, irony and many others which are all interchangeable with each other. This fact makes an all-round definition very difficult. We also tried to show that, the visual humour or the visual aspect of humour could be a valuable asset for a foreign recipient who genuinely wishing to understand humour products from a different and remote culture. We wanted to show, and to some extent share, that the cartoons, provided they are not strictly political or crammed with regional issues and accents, could be fathomed by an outsider with the help of a decent translation and an adequate amount of contextual and cultural background information. We have assumed, from the very beginning of this project, that the contemporary Turkish humour, particularly cartoons that are represented in Leman and other similar publications, was interesting enough to become a dissertation subject, particularly those with stock types or characters since they have the potential of becoming snapshots of a country which is still considered as alien (or other) by the West. As far as this writer concerned, the main points of interest concerning Turkey by the British public could roughly be summarised in two points: a bargain trip to the seaside during the summer season and some occasional football matches Manchester United plays against Turkish teams in Istanbul. Especially the latter always attracts heavy press coverage during and after a match. We wanted to show that there are other cultural aspects exist in Turkey as well and such aspects could be transferred to other cultures by ways of translation. The material we have chosen is both visual and prose at the same time and although they function as a unity, they also complement each other. It is proposed that, although a perfect translation is always a desirable concept in almost every field, the translation of humour is possible within certain frameworks. The visual side of cartoons, as in situation comedies, contributes immensely to the comprehension of the message, which should be considered as the most important feature of the joke. To this end, a variety of cartoons are selected from both Lenicyn and other similar humour weeklies and translated with an adequate amount of background and contextual information that provided beforehand. This background information also includes, as far as the material in question permits, a close analysis of the language and the subject matter. To provide a better insight for the reader, a summary of Turkish humour and humour magazines are added alongside a section on the issue of humour itself.

summary_ru: In this dissertation, the various strategies of humour translation have been analysed by taking various cartoons with speech bubbles from the popular Turkish humour weekly magazine Leman and other similar publications. Generally considered as an extremely problematic, sometimes next to impossible, task within the translation studies, humour translation requires and deserves special attention since, as it was explained in the related sections, it may unite or separate people within the context of one single joke. As we also have stated elsewhere in the text, the description of both humour and translation, as two separate concepts, are not available in certain and decisive terms. This is especially true for the concept of humour which also covers the areas of laughter, jokes, wit, satire, irony and many others which are all interchangeable with each other. This fact makes an all-round definition very difficult. We also tried to show that, the visual humour or the visual aspect of humour could be a valuable asset for a foreign recipient who genuinely wishing to understand humour products from a different and remote culture. We wanted to show, and to some extent share, that the cartoons, provided they are not strictly political or crammed with regional issues and accents, could be fathomed by an outsider with the help of a decent translation and an adequate amount of contextual and cultural background information. We have assumed, from the very beginning of this project, that the contemporary Turkish humour, particularly cartoons that are represented in Leman and other similar publications, was interesting enough to become a dissertation subject, particularly those with stock types or characters since they have the potential of becoming snapshots of a country which is still considered as alien (or other) by the West. title: The sport of lions: the Punjabi-Sikh sporting experience: a study into the place of sport in the socio-cultural landscape of Punjabi-Sikhs in Britain
title_original: The sport of lions: the Punjabi-Sikh sporting experience: a study into the place of sport in the socio-cultural landscape of Punjabi-Sikhs in Britain
summary: By first detailing the religious, cultural and sporting heritage of Punjabi-Sikhs, the study focuses on how this sporting legacy of has been translated in Britain and how such translation has served to augment the perceived cultural traditions of British Punjabi-Sikhs. The inception of the Shaheedi Games tournaments and the proliferation of all-Punjabi-Sikh football teams are located within the wider phenomenon of post-war South Asian immigration to Britain. The first-hand oral testimonies of pioneering Punjabi-Sikh immigrants serve to script the narrative of the history and evolution of these tournaments. This work is also ethnographically informed through my association/interaction with a Punjabi-Sikh football club. The players/affiliates of this club provided a research environment and subject base allowing the investigation of their manifold identification with sport. The subjects of playing football and supporting professional football teams, along with the conspicuous absence of South Asians from top-flight professional football are used to highlight issues of racism(s) and the (re)negotiations of ethnic, cultural and regional identities. The Shadeedi Games tournaments are unique Punjabi-Sikh sporting/cultural events that have profound significance for Punjabi-Sikhs. The themes/principles of the carnival inform the discussion/exposition of these tournaments and point to their assumed counter-cultural motifs. This thesis aims to disavow uncritical conjecture that denies South Asians a diverse and prominent sporting pedigree/prowess. By uncovering and exploring the Punjabi-Sikh history and experience of sport, this thesis illustrates how this specific British South Asian community has an established, accomplished and multifariously dynamic identification with sport.

title: Transnational Encounters in Peri-Brexit Cinema
title_original: Transnational Encounters in Peri-Brexit Cinema
summary: Filmic representations of the transnational coupling US woman/English man, rife in Anglo-American cinema, tend to rely on commodified iterations of British and US-American identities, which are recognisable by audiences and adaptable to the transnational cultural market. This article explores representations of these “special relationships” in the attempt to detect identity construction processes and negotiations that were relevant in the context surrounding Brexit, understood not only as a political event but as a larger cultural phenomenon. This transnational coupling, the article argues, allows for a contraposition of identities that results in a rendering of commodified, exportable versions of Englishness that resonate with the discourses of what this article calls peri-Brexit cinema: films that were released around the times of Brexit, chronologically speaking, but also discursively. Following this framework, this article analyses the depoliticised idea of Englishness at stake in Richard Curtis’ About Time (2013) and explores how Sean Durkin’s The Nest (2020) offers examples of identity work that are in tune with the disenchanted post-referendum affective landscape.

title: Mega Sport Events Infrastructure Effect on Social Legacy
title_original: Mega Sport Events Infrastructure Effect on Social Legacy
summary: Mega sport events reshape host cities through substantial infrastructure investments that generate long‑term, tangible and intangible legacies. While such projects can enhance mobility, walkability, and everyday amenity, they also attract scrutiny due to cost overruns and risks of under‑utilised assets post‑event. Consequently, residents’ quality of life (QOL), social cohesion, and civic pride have become central to assessing event legacies, yet evidence on how infrastructure outcomes translate into social legacy remains fragmented. This study addresses that gap by examining how infrastructure usability and accessibility relate to residents’ perceptions of social legacy in a region with recent and forthcoming mega‑event hosting. The Olympics consistently exceed their budgets, with average overruns of 179% and 27% for transport projects. Increasing public scrutiny has emerged owing to these events’ reliance on limited public resources for infrastructure that often lacks sustainable use post-event. Research on the built environment shows infrastructure improvements promote walkability, leisure, and active transport, enhancing wellbeing and QOL. Empirical research has demonstrated that negative resident perceptions are closely associated with diminished social legacy, whereas positive legacies have been shown to enhance public support for future events. Research supports infrastructure needing to be strategically aligned with long-term destination development goals in the host community. In research, there remains a gap specifically examining how infrastructure affects the social legacy of mega sport events. The effect of infrastructure on social legacy is long-term for the host community since infrastructure outcomes have the longest duration of impact on the host community. Once infrastructure is built, it remains for a long time in the host destination, or it needs to have a long lifetime. Planning for legacy focuses on the event’s long-term impacts; furthermore, it is argued that the success of the event legacy depends on the quality of the planning. Notably, current research focuses only on short-term impact rather than on the long-term impact of mega sport events on the host community. Infrastructure is linked to its effect on social legacy; it has, however, been researched holistically in mega sport event legacy contexts. Infrastructure research argues that transportation enhances mobility in the urban area for mega sport events, but also that it needs planning and monitoring to ensure positive impact on QOL. This study explored and measured the social impacts of infrastructure built by mega sport events. This study used SET in a sequential exploratory design, underpinning by the pragmatist paradigm. Pragmatism emphasises consequences and real-world applications. Pragmatism also prioritises real-world problem solving over abstract theorising. This provided a strong basis for the study’s mixed-method approach of semi-structured interviews followed by questionnaires. The aim was to examine infrastructure outcomes’ effect on social impacts such as civic pride, social cohesion, QOL, and wellbeing, and to understand infrastructure’s contribution to social legacy for the host community. The thesis proposes a model of infrastructure’s effect on social legacy through social cohesion, civic pride, QOL, human rights violations, and wellbeing. The findings showed that infrastructure outcomes play a significant positive and/or negative role in producing social legacy for mega sport events. Infrastructure with high usability and accessibility has a positive effect on civic pride, social cohesion, QOL, wellbeing, and on the social legacy of mega sport events. The implication of this research is that social infrastructure (homes, hospitals, schools, and mobility infrastructure) is important for producing positive social legacy and needs to be prioritised by organisers to enhance social impacts in the host community.

title: The CISO Playbook
title_original: The CISO Playbook
summary: Guiding security leaders and executives who hold the privilege of defending modern organizations, The CISO Playbook: The Adversarial Mindset is a leadership-focused blueprint for outmaneuvering adversaries that iterate relentlessly. In an era where attackers view corporate defenders as “dumb, weak, and ineffective” due to organizational drag and over-reliance on static tools, this book empowers leaders to reclaim the initiative by adopting a true adversarial mindset. Harnessing the concept of decision advantage, the book moves beyond treating incidents as isolated technical events by thinking in adversary terms: objectives, constraints, and tradecraft. It bridges the gap between attacker methods and board-level risk, showing how to translate security outcomes into the language of economics, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), and revenue protection. Operationalizing lessons from real-world campaigns like SolarWinds, Volt Typhoon, and Operation Aurora, the text connects tradecraft to operational reality. It introduces the unique metric of time-to-hazard neutralization, moving past ticket metadata to focus on the verified removal of risk from the environment. Spotlighting the rise of the “Artificial Adversary,” a central thread details how artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced human actors and autonomous systems act with malicious intent. From industrialized “vibe hacking” to active scanning and autonomous reconnaissance, the book reveals how AI accelerates the attacker’s Observe, Orient, Decide, and Act (OODA) loop and how Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs) must respond by compressing their own defensive cycles. Translating theoretical models into repeatable methods, the text provides strategies for terrain engineering, deception, and resilience-centric incident response. Written for CISOs, deputies, and security leaders, it serves those who both brief members of C-Suites and boards and also run outcome-based programs. Instead of remaining a reactive enforcer, readers will find a blueprint for becoming a proactive Enterprise Risk Leader. Navigating this shift ultimately rewards the disciplined observation required to outthink the opponent.

title: Contemporary Silvicultural Practices in the Western Portion of the Pacific Northwest, USA
title_original: Contemporary Silvicultural Practices in the Western Portion of the Pacific Northwest, USA
summary: Abstract The western portion of the Pacific Northwest (PNW) has some of the most productive and iconic forests of the United States. Management of these forests has changed dramatically over the past three decades, driven by the primary objectives and constraints associated with major forest landowner groups. Key changes include 1) increased focus on the establishment phase and a reduction in intermediate treatments for ownerships practicing intensive management (e.g., forest industry), 2) an increase in the use of variable retention harvesting on state, Bureau of Land Management, and tribal managed lands, and 3) and a shift to almost exclusive use of thinning on National Forest System lands. Most silvicultural activity is focused on Douglas-fir on privately owned timberlands despite federal ownerships comprising more than half of all timberland in the region. Regeneration is primarily accomplished via planting using both genetically improved and wild-collected seed depending on species and ownership. Increased fire occurrence and severity have given rise to a broad class of treatments related to fuels reduction and thinning to increase resiliency, which is likely to continue to expand. Future changes in practice will be driven by evolving objectives of major forest landowner groups, but we anticipate increased focus on the establishment phase across all groups. Reduced investment in silviculture research and a trend towards standardized silvicultural prescriptions are key challenges to future innovation in the region at a time when the need for innovation to maintain forests and the benefits they provide has never been greater.

title: Beyond the Playing Field
title_original: Beyond the Playing Field
summary: Sport events are now used not only for competition but also to improve the image and reputation of cities, regions, and countries. This chapter explains how events such as the Olympic Games, FIFA World Cup, Commonwealth Games, and Tour de France help attract tourists, investment, and global attention while strengthening local identity. It discusses the main ideas of destination branding, place identity, stakeholder participation, media promotion, and event legacy using recent research and international examples. The chapter also highlights common challenges, including high costs, environmental concerns, weak governance, and poor legacy planning. To address these issues, it proposes an Integrated Sport Event Destination Branding Framework (ISEDBF) that connects event planning, stakeholder collaboration, communication, visitor experience, and legacy management. The chapter concludes with practical recommendations for policymakers, destination managers, event organizers, and researchers.

title: Abe Shinzo and His Legacies
title_original: Abe Shinzo and His Legacies
summary: Offering an assessment of Abe Shinzo's complex legacy as Japan's longest-serving prime minister, this book shows that beyond the acclaim for "Abenomics" and his diplomatic initiatives lies a more nuanced reality that will continue to shape Japan's trajectory for years. The book focuses on Abe's transformational security policy, his flawed economic vision, his diplomatic initiatives and the implications of "Abenesia" for regional reconciliation. The analysis extends to the gap between upbeat "womenomics" rhetoric and Japan's low gender equality rankings. Poor management of the COVID-19 pandemic and the ill-fated Tokyo 2020 Olympics further tarnish Abe’s legacy. His tragic assassination uncovered damning ties with the Unification Church and prompted extensive revelations about its coercive fundraising tactics.The book further explores how successors Kishida Fumio and Takaichi Sanae have navigated these legacies, and the challenges of increased immigration that Abe promoted from 2018. Abe Shinzo and His Legacies will appeal to students, scholars, and general readers interested in contemporary Japan and Asian geopolitics.

title: Conduct problems and associated factors among governmental secondary school students in Dessie City, Northeast Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
title_original: Conduct problems and associated factors among governmental secondary school students in Dessie City, Northeast Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
summary: Abstract Introduction: Conduct disorder is a behavioral and mental health disorder that typically develops in childhood or adolescence and is characterized by a persistent pattern of violating the rights of others or social norms. It is linked with aggression towards people or animals, destruction of property, deceitfulness, or theft but little is known about conduct disorder among government secondary school students in Dessie City, Ethiopia. This study aimed to assess the magnitude of conduct disorder and its associated factors among secondary school students in Dessie City, Northeast Ethiopia. Methods An institution-based cross-sectional study design was conducted from June 1–30/ 2024. A multistage stratified sampling technique was used to select 570 government secondary school students. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire. A Disruptive Behavior Disorder (DBD) rating scale was used to measure conduct disorder among students. The collected data were coded and entered into Epi-data version 4.6 and then exported to SPSS version 26 for further analysis. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regressions with odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence interval (CIs) at p-value < 0.05 were employed as the result. Results The magnitude of conduct disorder among government secondary school students was 7.4% (95% CI: 5.3, 9.6). Approximately 87(15.3%) participants experienced moderate to high-stress levels, and 62(10.9%) experienced high levels of adverse childhood abuse. In multivariable logistic regression analyses, the associated factors for conduct disorder were being male (AOR = 2.519, 95% CI: 1.045–6.071), age category (16–18) (AOR = 4.07 95% CI:1.29–12.77), problematic substance use (AOR = 3.00, 95% CI: 1.31–6.91), adverse childhood abuse (AOR = 2.72 95CI: 1.02–7.26), maternal educational status (AOR = 4.33, 95% CI: 1.19–15.63) and permissive parenting style (AOR = 3.53, 95% CI:1.48–8.40). Conclusions The magnitude of conduct disorders among secondary school students in Dessie City was comparable to the estimated global prevalence rate. Being male, age category, problematic substance use, adverse childhood abuse, maternal educational status, and permissive parenting style were significantly associated with conduct disorders. Therefore, increasing parental knowledge and strengthening parental skills, advocating for mothers' education, and preventing substance use among students could help reduce youth’s conduct problems.
