title: Classifying stadium-city coupling through figure-ground image clustering: Evidence from 100 global cases
title_original: Classifying stadium-city coupling through figure-ground image clustering: Evidence from 100 global cases
summary: Large stadiums are land-intensive public infrastructures whose planning implications depend not only on event operations, but also on how their edges, buffers, streets, open spaces, and host fabrics connect with everyday urban environments. Existing stadium classifications mainly emphasize event hierarchy, ownership, capacity, or architectural form, offering limited guidance for diagnosing district-scale morphological coupling. This study develops a reproducible morphology-based typology of stadium-city coupling using 100 large stadiums worldwide. For each case, a standardized 2 × 2 km figure-ground image was constructed and processed through an ML-based image-embedding workflow implemented with a pretrained Inception v3 model. Each image was converted into a 2048-dimensional embedding vector, producing a 100 × 2048 feature matrix without pre-assigned type labels. Normalized Euclidean distances were then calculated between embedding vectors, and Ward hierarchical clustering was used to identify recurrent figure-ground similarity structures. The resulting clusters were interpreted through post-clustering morphological reading and tested through a 20-run random-subsampling stability analysis. Comparison of K = 3–7, followed by a 20-run K = 5/K = 6 sensitivity test, supported five clusters as the most interpretable and parsimonious primary resolution. The analysis identifies five relational types: Inner-city Block-Embedded, Waterfront/Infrastructure Composite, Mega-Core with Concentric Buffers, Institutional/Training-Base Anchored, and Peripheral Enclave/Island. Stability testing distinguishes 51 stable core prototypes from 14 borderline cases and shows that the Mega-Core condition is more internally heterogeneous than the other types. A post-clustering comparison of construction years further suggests that embedded and composite configurations have persisted across long historical periods, whereas buffered mega-core forms are more often associated with later large-scale development regimes. By translating ML-derived image clusters into interpretable urban morphological types, the study offers an early-stage diagnostic framework for identifying whether a stadium district is primarily characterized by embedded interface pressure, linear-edge barriers, buffer underuse, institutional enclosure, or peripheral isolation.

Existing stadium classifications mainly emphasize event hierarchy, ownership, capacity, or architectural form, offering limited guidance for diagnosing district-scale morphological coupling. This study develops a reproducible morphology-based typology of stadium-city coupling using 100 large stadiums worldwide. For each case, a standardized 2 × 2 km figure-ground image was constructed and processed through an ML-based image-embedding workflow implemented with a pretrained Inception v3 model. Each image was converted into a 2048-dimensional embedding vector, producing a 100 × 2048 feature matrix without pre-assigned type labels. Normalized Euclidean distances were then calculated between embedding vectors, and Ward hierarchical clustering was used to identify recurrent figure-ground similarity structures. The resulting clusters were interpreted through post-clustering morphological reading and tested through a 20-run random-subsampling stability analysis. Comparison of K = 3–7, followed by a 20-run K = 5/K = 6 sensitivity test, supported five clusters as the most interpretable and parsimonious primary resolution. The analysis identifies five relational types: Inner-city Block-Embedded, Waterfront/Infrastructure Composite, Mega-Core with Concentric Buffers, Institutional/Training-Base Anchored, and Peripheral Enclave/Island. Stability testing distinguishes 51 stable core prototypes from 14 borderline cases and shows that the Mega-Core condition is more internally heterogeneous than the other types. A post-clustering comparison of construction years further suggests that embedded and composite configurations have persisted across long historical periods, whereas buffered mega-core forms are more often associated with later large-scale development regimes. By translating ML-derived image clusters into interpretable urban morphological types, the study offers an early-stage diagnostic framework for identifying whether a stadium district is primarily characterized by embedded interface pressure, linear-edge barriers, buffer underuse, institutional enclosure, or peripheral isolation.

title: Naga Politics Between Past Aspirations and Present Realities: A Critical Analysis
title_original: Naga Politics Between Past Aspirations and Present Realities: A Critical Analysis
summary: This article critically interrogates the trajectory of Naga politics by situating its contemporary realities within the longue durée of historical aspirations for sovereignty, identity and self-determination. Moving beyond conventional state-centric and insurgency-focused analyses, it advances a relational framework that foregrounds the interplay among indigenous political imaginaries, postcolonial state formation and evolving geopolitical constraints. This study argues that the disjuncture between past aspirations and present realities is not merely a product of failed negotiations but stems from a deeper epistemic tension between customary institutions and modern governance regimes. The article introduces the concept of ‘fragmented sovereignty’ to capture the layered and often contradictory modes of authority that characterize Naga political life today. Through a critical reading of peace accords, civil society interventions and factional dynamics, it reveals how competing claims to legitimacy have reconfigured the political field. Also, it examines the role of historical memory, identity and narrative in sustaining political mobilization despite structural impasses. By bridging political theory and grounded analysis, this article contributes to a more nuanced understanding of indigenous politics in contested borderlands, offering fresh insights into the limits and possibilities of negotiated autonomy in the contemporary era.

title: Digital media and women’s issues in Egypt and Saudi Arabia
title_original: Digital media and women’s issues in Egypt and Saudi Arabia
summary: This thesis investigates how digital media participate in and contribute to the emergence and discussion of women’s issues in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, in complex intersections of online and offline activity. Specific focus is placed on digital media’s intrinsic complexity and agency, and their interplay with socio-political, economic, legal, and cultural practices. I will specifically ask questions such as, how does an issue work through technological forms of development, and how is it techno-socio-political? How do digital media enrich, reshape, and co-constitute women’s issues in Egypt and Saudi Arabia? In answering these questions, I explore how certain women’s issues are formed, emerge, and become central in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. These explorations involve a reflection on the computational turn of current cultural and social practices2 and the significance of algorithms and software in the making of our socio-cultural realities. They also necessitate an understanding of the countries’ locales, accounts of women’s movements, struggles, and discourses that, inevitably, involve Islamic Tradition. Asking such questions also means exploring how online activities enrich current discourses of women and gender studies in a Middle Eastern context. The resulting work sits In between a number of disciplines and approaches and calls for a bespoke conceptual and methodological approach, built on a combination of methodologies, including close reading of history and literature on the topic, and qualitative and quantitative analysis of digital content through digital media tools. For this purpose I have employed software such as Gephi, Netvizz, and MOZ SERP. Moving beyond an understanding of media as a tool and construing them as constitutive parts of an entangled network made of heterogeneous actants, I introduce the concept of a multi-layered and networked map. This concept is a mode of investigation and a tool of analysis that seeks to understand and discuss the diverse and continuous transformations of certain women’s issues in these two countries as they emerge and evolve online. The visualisations of the quantitative part of my analysis are published on the website that I have created, available at http://www.oxycoms.com/clb. This thesis tries to find a location at the intersection of digital media, gender studies, and studies of the Middle East. At times, specific problematic aspects of each field are at odds with each other, and I attend to the ways in which they touch and contradict each other. Through the concept of the multi-layered and networked map I will trace and follow the intersection of theoretical thoughts, accounts of women’s activities and movements, online activities, and findings of the new methodologies and tools of online social networking analysis. I will discuss how they combine and coalesce, bringing to life what I address as technowomen. I hope to contribute to the current theoretical and methodological discussions in digital media, media, and cultural studies, to discussions in women and gender studies on the digitised reality of movements and activities.

title: Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension
title_original: Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension
summary: We introduce a model of dark matter charged under a new confining gauge group akin to the Standard Model's quantum chromodynamics (QCD). The fermionic sector contains both heavy and light quark-like fermions charged under the dark QCD. As the Universe cools, the gauge force confines and dark radiation transitions from free particles to low-mass dark pions. This form of dark radiation behaves as an imperfect fluid with nonzero viscosity. If the confinement occurs at the MeV scale, the model can alleviate the tension between early- and late-time measurements of the Hubble parameter, with a Bayesian posterior of $H_0 = 71.60\pm 0.63$ km/s/Mpc and a $3σ$ residual tension across Planck, ACT, BBN, Pantheon+, DESI DR2, and SH0ES. In the late Universe, the heavy dark matter can evade existing constraints on dark matter self-interactions while containing a rich phenomenology that may be accessible in future observations.

title: From Static Logistics to Dynamic Ecosystems: Evaluating the Emergence of an Event Mobility Governance Framework in Dubai's Mega-Event Sector
title_original: From Static Logistics to Dynamic Ecosystems: Evaluating the Emergence of an Event Mobility Governance Framework in Dubai's Mega-Event Sector
summary: Mega-events compress months of ordinary travel demand into days, and they do so on top of a city that must keep working. This white paper examines how Dubai has moved from event-specific, largely reactive transport logistics towards a formalised Event Mobility Governance Framework (EMGF) that treats surge mobility as a permanent institutional capability rather than a temporary project. Drawing on the mobilities paradigm and on collaborative and adaptive governance theory, we describe the framework as a four-layer architecture: a tripartite institutional layer (Roads and Transport Authority, Dubai Police and venue authorities), a shared data and decision layer, a set of supply, demand and network levers, and an outcomes layer. Two contributions are original to this paper. The first is the Event Mobility Governance Maturity Index (EMGMI), a weighted five-dimension composite that scores how far a jurisdiction has institutionalised event mobility. The second is the Surge Absorption Ratio (SAR), a simple published-data metric of how much of an event's attendance the public transport system actually carries. We compare two embedded cases within one jurisdiction, Expo 2020 (a supply-side, fixed-infrastructure baseline) and COP28 (a demand-side, predictive model), against a pre-framework baseline. Because passenger-level operational data are not public, the inferential analysis uses an illustrative event-day panel (n = 255) calibrated to published RTA magnitudes; it is presented as a reproducible analytic template rather than as audited evidence. On that panel, one-way ANOVA shows large regime effects on corridor delay (F(2, 252) = 53.3, η² = 0.30), crowd dispersal time and incident response, and hierarchical OLS shows that public-transport share and digital integration jointly explain most of the regime difference (adjusted R² rising from 0.05 to 0.47). The EMGMI rises from 30.5 (baseline) to 59.7 (Expo 2020) and 79.1 (COP28). We close with ownership-assigned recommendations for RTA leadership and a research agenda for validating the index with operational data.

title: The Powerhouse & Blak Collections: Sitting with Trouble and Standing Up for Truth
title_original: The Powerhouse & Blak Collections: Sitting with Trouble and Standing Up for Truth
summary: The Tandanya-Adelaide Declaration came to the Powerhouse Museum in late 2019 and has underpinned sincere positive transformation of collection care standards ever since. Enacting its commitments allowed unprecedented Indigenous accesses and advances through the historic Powerhouse Collection Digitisation and Relocation Project, which further informed the founding of the Powerhouse First Nations Directorate in 2021. Since then, many profound improvements are being enabled by fulfilling the assertions and commitments offered in the Tandanya-Adelaide Declaration. This article is presented as a firsthand account of how it has informed positive developments in documentation, storage, handling and access as well as towards correct recognitions, protocol adherences and approaches to acquisition all of which affirm the rights of Indigenous people over their cultural heritage that the Powerhouse is safeguarding.

title: The representation of evil in the late novels of Victor Hugo
title_original: The representation of evil in the late novels of Victor Hugo
summary: Evil in Hugo’s later novels has rarely been examined. This subject is clearly incompatible with the received image of Hugo(based on earlier works such as Les Misérables) as a prophet of optimism and progress. This thesis will demonstrate that it is reasonable that Hugo should have expressed negative thoughts in the novels that he wrote in the 1860s and 1870s, since contemporary Western writers were also producing pessimistic works. Attention will be drawn to the personal anxieties and disappointments which only served to intensify Hugo’s experience of the universal fin de siècle malaise. The thesis will posit that the universe of Hugo’s later novels is much darker than that which is delineated in his earlier novels. Hugo’s renewed interest in the works of de Sade indicates his increasingly pessimistic perception of human nature (Introduction). The representation of benevolent motherhood that is found in the earlier novels has been supplanted by the depiction of vampiric female monsters in their successors (Chapter 1). Justice can be seen to be done in the earlier novels because evildoers are eradicated, but in their successors villains prosper whilst the innocent are treated harshly (Chapter 3). Disdain for human existence is most vividly suggested by ravenous mouths which seek to ingest mankind into the foul chaos they contain and this chaos is predominantly feminine (Chapter 5). Whilst the thesis would not deny Hugo’s belief in God, it will assert that in his later novels Hugo portrays a universe in which the forces of darkness are extremely powerful (Conclusion).

title: Ageing in urban neighbourhoods in Beijing, China : an ethnographic study of older Chinese people's neighbourhood experiences
title_original: Ageing in urban neighbourhoods in Beijing, China : an ethnographic study of older Chinese people's neighbourhood experiences
summary: This thesis explores Chinese older people’s perception and experiences of ageing and age care in an urban neighbourhood in Beijing China. It is informed by a growing body of theoretical and empirical research regarding ageing and also draws upon research that has made linkage between ageing and place. However, little research has investigated older people’s experiences of ageing in a rapid changing urban neighbourhood and how these environmental changes affect their day to day lives in China. Thus, by conducting 34 in-depth interviews, participant observation in three urban neighbourhoods in urban Beijing and photography produced by the researcher, this study took a social constructionist stance and ethnographic research design to explore older people’s ageing experience in a rapidly changing environment, in this case, the role of the neighbourhood outdoor places in their day to day lives. The findings from this study demonstrate that the Western understanding of AIP is not sufficient to apply to the current social, economic and cultural context in urban Beijing. As the nascent concept of Ageing in place (AIP) has been embedded within broad socio-cultural institutions, numerous institutional legacies and socio-cultural factors directly and indirectly related to AIP serve as the discursive resources that shape and inform individuals’ disputant discourses. These factors not only frame their basic logics, vocabularies and moral reasoning but also shape their structural positions on housing access, pension rights and later-life care. Participants in these three neighbourhoods have been constantly constructing and reconstructing their understanding of ageing and AIP with the wider economic, political, social and cultural influences. These interesting perceptions of and attachment to neighbourhood engagement invite further theoretical reflections, as ageing and age care for older people in China have been greatly influenced by existing cultural norms, as well as new social trends, in a far more complicated and ambivalent fashion than commonly assumed and observers have envisioned.

title: A 'zone of legal exemption' for sports violence? : Form and substance in the criminal law.
title_original: A 'zone of legal exemption' for sports violence? : Form and substance in the criminal law.
summary: This study examines the criminal liability that may be incurred by participants in contact sports for violence that results in injury to a fellow participant. For these purposes, I concentrate on boxing, rugby and soccer; sports that involve a level of physicality that risks, and regularly causes, injury. The violence that is intrinsic to their practice is in some senses archetypically criminal, and yet, that self-same violence is also constitutive of sports that are perceived to have enormous personal, social and cultural value, and which have been declared by the House of Lords to amount to ‘lawful activities’. A formal account of the criminal law of sports violence posits the consent of the participants as the primary determinant of the imposition of liability for acts of violence committed during the course of contact sports. In this thesis, I examine this formal account and propose that the substance of the lawfulness of sports violence needs to be understood in terms of its socio-historical development, and the sophisticated rule-systems and pluralistic regulatory backdrop against which modern sports operate. This thesis contributes a new understanding of the offences that pertain to sports violence, and the normative role and doctrinal function of the participants’ consent, in order to understand the way in which the criminal law accommodates violent sports practices. The thesis also suggests new ideas in relation to the ‘playing culture’ of sport and its relationship to the criminal law, and the role of prosecutorial discretion in effectively shaping the lawfulness of ‘legitimate sport’.

title: The status of race and racism in policy : an analysis of project interviews
title_original: The status of race and racism in policy : an analysis of project interviews
summary: At the June 2015 Advisory Board meeting for the SES Race, Racism and Education study the project team identified several themes recurring in project interviews. These included: •The landscape of race (whether talking about race is now seen as ‘racist’; policy and the ‘white working class’) •The significance of the Lawrence case (stakeholders v policymakers) •The extent to which current political figures understand race/racism critically? •Did policy ever really take racism seriously? •Hindsight, memory and reconstructing the past Subsequently, individual team members have taken the lead in developing analysis of the interview data and exploring emerging themes. The particular focus of this working paper is on interviewees’ perceptions of the shifting status of race and racism within education and within the wider public space, c.1993-2013. It encompasses discussion of the significance of the Lawrence murder case; the extent to which politicians and policy makers understand race and racism critically; and the availability of a public language for discussing race. The period 1993-2013 saw the murder of Stephen Lawrence; the Macpherson Inquiry; the Race Relations (Amendment) Act (2000); London/ City Challenge; the growth of ethnic performance data; and debates on the black/ white gap in UK schools. In form, it comprises a type of oral history, using of interview data to reconstruct multiple viewpoints of a historical period. By shifting the focus of inquiry to foreground ‘hidden’ narratives, this approach enables accounts that might otherwise be trivialised as complaints or as anecdotes to stand as legitimate historical narratives.

title: Logics of foreign policy : discourse, fantasy and Germany's policies in the Iraq crisis.
title_original: Logics of foreign policy : discourse, fantasy and Germany's policies in the Iraq crisis.
summary: The thesis develops a discourse-theoretical framework for foreign policy analysis and utilises it to account for Germany’s policies in the Iraq crisis of 2002/2003. Germany’s response was deeply contradictory, as it included rhetorical opposition to the war and diplomatic activities aiming at blocking it, but also tacit and indirect cooperation with the United States that made the war possible. Intriguingly, such policies were pursued against the background of an existential and emotional discourse, which portrayed Germany’s very identities as at stake. This intersection of affectivity and contradictoriness presents the research problem of the thesis. To address it, the dissertation revisits the concepts of discourse, subjectivity and foreign policy. Building on poststructuralist and psychoanalytical impulses, it argues that the focus on discursivity should be complemented with a deeper analysis of affect. The subject is reconceptualised as incomplete and split; not only between her different identities, but also between her discursive and affective sides. Foreign policy is then understood as an articulatory practice through which subjects attempt to recapture their identity, a process that is strongly affective and ultimately futile. These arguments are operationalised with the help of three sets of logics: social logics, which capture sedimented aspects of social reality; political logics, which focus on contestation of orders and symbolic reconstruction of political spaces; and the logic of fantasy, which accounts for the subjects’ attachment to sociopolitical orders. After discussing methodological problems, the dissertation turns to the empirical study of Germany’s policies in the Iraq crises, which is structured around the three types of logics. The key conclusion is that Germany’s policymakers operated in a discursively and affectively disordered terrain, in which their own subjectivities were split between different identities, principles and expectations. They were unable to resolve these dilemmas, because, at the same time, multiple of the contradictory identities and policy options were underpinned by strong affective investment, which made it virtually impossible to choose an unequivocal course of action. This inability also functioned as a reminder of the failure to secure a stable and complete identity, further fueling the desire for it that was manifested in the perpetuation of the existential and emotional discourse.

title: The political culture of university students in South Korea : a comparison of before the democratic transition and today
title_original: The political culture of university students in South Korea : a comparison of before the democratic transition and today
summary: This thesis compares the political culture of university students in South Korea before and after the democratic transition in 1987. It identifies the changes in the following: the attitudes to politics, government and media; the political socialization process; the experience of political participation; and the reasons for political participation and non-participation. Qualitative analysis was used to analyse the data collected from interviews and surveys conducted on respondents who were university students in the 1980s and current university students. It was found that compared to university students in the 1980s, current university students held less intensely negative attitudes towards the government. However, although current university students were interested in politics, they were still distrustful of politicians, did not have a political party they supported and had low levels of perceived political efficacy and political participation. Based on these findings, this thesis examined three different types of theories to explain the changes in the political culture of university students. First, demand-side theories that focus on underlying socioeconomic changes to explain changes in the political culture were used to analyse the changes in the reasons for political participation and the changes in the political socialization process. title: Clean-air regulation reduces childhood wasting and overweight in China
title_original: Clean-air regulation reduces childhood wasting and overweight in China
summary: Whether large-scale air-quality policies improve child nutrition remains uncertain. Here we show that China’s Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan reduces wasting and overweight among children under five. We use annual data from 2759 counties between 2005 and 2017 and a matched difference-in-differences design to evaluate the policy as a natural experiment. The policy is associated with a 0.760% reduction in wasting and a 3.950% reduction in overweight relative to control areas. Reductions in fine particulate matter explain an estimated 57.7% and 68.9% of these respective effects. The benefits are generally larger in northern regions, resource-based cities, and counties with greater initial pollution or stronger regulation. The policy also generates at least US$120.87 million in direct health-care savings across pilot areas. These findings provide population-level evidence that clean-air regulation improves early-childhood nutrition and suggest that coordinating air-quality management with child-health policy can deliver substantial health and economic benefits in highly polluted settings. In China, the rollout of clean-air regulation has reduced both wasting and overweight in early childhood, according to analyses of county-level health and pollution data.

title: The historical development of fencing in the Czech lands up to 1948: Institutionalisation, clubs, personalities, and the international context
title_original: The historical development of fencing in the Czech lands up to 1948: Institutionalisation, clubs, personalities, and the international context
summary: Background: Fencing represents a traditional component of European physical culture, yet its development in the Czech lands has not been comprehensively examined within broader social and institutional contexts. Previous research has tended to focus on individual personalities or specific periods, while the long-term continuity between military tradition, associational life, and modern sport has remained outside systematic analysis. Objective: The aim of this study is to analyse the development of fencing in the Czech lands from the Middle Ages to the second half of the twentieth century, with emphasis on processes of institutionalisation, professionalisation of instruction, and transformations of organisational structures within changing social and political contexts. Methods: The study is based on a historical-analytical approach drawing on archival documents, period press, club and federation materials, and scholarly literature. Methods of source analysis and comparative analysis were applied to interpret the development of fencing in relation to broader trends in the institutionalisation of sport in Central Europe. Results: The findings show that fencing gradually transformed from a combat skill associated with military and aristocratic environments into a modern sport with stable club and federation structures. A key role was played by clubs and associations, particularly the Czech Fencing Club Riegel, as well as the Association of Fencing Masters founded in 1928, which contributed to the unification of professional standards of instruction. Development was significantly influenced by political disruptions in 1939 and 1948; nevertheless, continuity of professional tradition was preserved. Conclusions: The development of fencing in the Czech lands illustrates how a sporting discipline was able to maintain professional continuity despite repeated institutional disruptions. The study shows that the development of fencing in the Czech lands was shaped by the interaction of civic associations, specialised clubs, and professional fencing masters, while international contacts played an important role in its institutionalisation and long-term continuity.

title: Continuity and change : the role of trade unions in state industrial relations policy in Britain, 1910-1921
title_original: Continuity and change : the role of trade unions in state industrial relations policy in Britain, 1910-1921
summary: This thesis examines continuity and change and the role of trade unions in state industrial relations policy in Britain in the period 1910-21. Contrary to orthodox interpretations which point to a watershed during World War 1, it is argued that state industrial relations policy remained remarkably consistent in this period. To a significant extent this consistency was due to the scale and character of worker organisation. The influence of syndicalism and industrial unionism added a new and threatening dimension to worker organisation because of the emphasis these movements placed on empowering the rank and file rather than trade union leaders. This shift was perceived as a threat to the national interest- which forced the state to intervene but limited the forms which intervention could take. The form of intervention with the fewest repercussions was conciliation which involved the promotion of "responsible" trade unionism. This policy was based on the idea that responsibly led trade unions acted as a discipline and control on their members. They could prevent industrial conflict from reaching the point where repressive state intervention became inevitable. This view of trade union leadership is a central theme in an influential body of literature in industrial relations known as "rank and filism". The thesis highlights the problems with this approach between 1910 and 1921 notably that the actions of trade union leaders' were less significant than those of the rank and file. It argues for a more sophisticated and qualified version of rank and filism.

title: Following the yellowcake road: exploring the colonial roots and routes of Australian radioactive minerals, 1900s–1950s
title_original: Following the yellowcake road: exploring the colonial roots and routes of Australian radioactive minerals, 1900s–1950s
summary: Over the past 40 years, environmental justice activists and scholars have drawn greater attention to the disproportionate environmental burdens borne by marginalised communities. This includes the consequences of ‘nuclear colonialism’, a phenomenon defined as constituting ‘a system of domination through which governments and corporations target indigenous peoples and their lands to maintain the nuclear production process’. In this article, I seek to complicate this definition of nuclear colonialism by exploring the role of uranium mining in consolidating both British and Australian settler colonial power during the first half of the twentieth century. I will do so through an examination of Australian uranium’s roots and routes as both a manifestation and facilitator of settler colonialism in Australia between 1900 and 1955. Combining sources from both British and Australian archives, this article seeks to contribute to emergent scholarship on the colonial dimensions of mineral extraction in two ways. Firstly, by explicating the role uranium played in fuelling the extractive mentalities of settler colonial Australia. And secondly, by exploring uranium extraction’s contribution to the consolidation of the British Empire’s waning power in the mid-twentieth century.

title: Displaying Ukraine, Negotiating Europe: An Unexpected “Success Story” at the Eurovision Song Contest
title_original: Displaying Ukraine, Negotiating Europe: An Unexpected “Success Story” at the Eurovision Song Contest
summary: The paper examines two decades of Ukraine’s participation in the Eurovision Song Contest (ESC), charting the trajectory from “no place” at the periphery to a “success story” and a safe bet at the ESC. Departing from the positionality of a “double subaltern” in a blind zone between the West and Russia, it sought visibility and recognition to validate its claims to sovereignty and Europeanness. Moving beyond the commercial logic of accessing the pan-European music market, it prioritized elevating its geocultural status by disentangling from the Russian orbit, embedding itself in the European cultural space, and contributing to it. The empirical basis of the research is the author’s fieldwork at the 2024 ESC in Malmö, where successful strategies of artistic performances and Ukraine’s national projections, as perceived by external observers, were identified. Ukraine has carved out its distinct cultural profile at the ESC as “making folk cool and modern”: bridging and blending authentic musical traditions with contemporary aesthetics, it has advanced to the position of a subversive hegemon, simultaneously mimicked and contested by others.

title: Beyond the boundary: locating a more adequate framework to study the global development of cricket outside the British Empire
title_original: Beyond the boundary: locating a more adequate framework to study the global development of cricket outside the British Empire
summary: Cricket’s global diffusion has traditionally been understood through the lens of British imperial legacy, with scholarship focusing primarily on former colonies that now constitute the Commonwealth cricketing world. The sport’s accelerating expansion into non-Commonwealth contexts, marked above all by its inclusion in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, exposes the limits of this predominantly post-colonial scholarship. Taking cricket in China as a theoretical challenge, this article critically reviews dominant approaches in cricket studies and argues that they remain constrained by either teleological assumptions or imperialist analytical categories. Drawing on figurational sociology as an analytical lens, the article proposes a three-dimensional framework for analysing cricket development beyond the British Empire, centred on institutional embedding, governance structures, and gender power relations. It further develops the concept of a post post-Westernization of cricket, characterized by leapfrog developmentand inverted gender relations. The article argues that cricket’s contemporary expansion beyond the Commonwealth is increasingly shaped by the game’s incorporation into sport mega events, its embedding within local institutional architectures, and the strategic prioritization of the women’s game.

Taking cricket in China as a theoretical challenge, this article critically reviews dominant approaches in cricket studies and argues that they remain constrained by either teleological assumptions or imperialist analytical categories. Drawing on figurational sociology as an analytical lens, the article proposes a three-dimensional framework for analysing cricket development beyond the British Empire, centred on institutional embedding, governance structures, and gender power relations. It further develops the concept of a post post-Westernization of cricket, characterized by leapfrog developmentand inverted gender relations. The article argues that cricket’s contemporary expansion beyond the Commonwealth is increasingly shaped by the game’s incorporation into sport mega events, its embedding within local institutional architectures, and the strategic prioritization of the women’s game.

title: ‘No soy una más’: a transwoman’s quest for acceptance, safety and belonging in football
title_original: ‘No soy una más’: a transwoman’s quest for acceptance, safety and belonging in football
summary: Transgender inclusion in sport has become a complex and widely debated issue in recent years. Academic scholarship has explored the issue from a range of perspectives, yet little is known about trans athletes’ experiences of elite sport. This paper addresses this omission by centralising the story of Alba Palacios, the first transgender woman officially registered to play in the Spanish women’s football league. Data were generated via an in-depth individual semi-structured interview with Alba and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. A storytelling approach was then adopted, using creative non-fiction vignettes to illuminate key moments of Alba’s embodied experiences at the intersections of gender, sport and her transition. The vignettes reveal three key areas that influenced her journey toward acceptance in women’s sport: institutional and structural barriers; social dynamics in football spaces; and the personal emotional struggles of playing football as a trans woman. The paper concludes by emphasising the disadvantages faced by trans athletes as a means of reframing the pervasive ‘trans women as a threat’ rhetoric that often shapes debates on trans inclusion.

title: Architectural Design Strategies for Enhanced Crowd Management in Aquatic Centers
title_original: Architectural Design Strategies for Enhanced Crowd Management in Aquatic Centers
summary: Public aquatic centers are complex socio-technical environments characterized by high-density occupancy, varying user demographics, and unique environmental stressors such as high humidity and slippery surfaces. This paper investigates architectural design strategies to mitigate safety risks and optimize crowd flow in a proposed aquatic facility in Port Harcourt, Nigeria. Through a mixed-methods approach involving literature synthesis, case study analysis (Sydney Olympic Park and Garden City Mall), and spatial configuration modeling, the study identifies critical bottlenecks in traditional aquatic layouts. The findings propose a "Dynamic Safety Framework" that integrates spatial zoning, anti-slip materiality, and real-time monitoring technologies. Results suggest that radial egress patterns and clearly defined "wet-dry" transitions can reduce crowd turbulence by up to 30%.

title: Percy Florence Shelley revisited : new perspectives through private and amateur theatre research
title_original: Percy Florence Shelley revisited : new perspectives through private and amateur theatre research
summary: This article offers a reappraisal of Sir Percy Florence Shelley through analysis of his private and amateur theatricals. It draws attention to his labour as a builder of private theatres and as an amateur scene painter, photographer, actor, stage carpenter, machinist, composer and playwright. It also highlights his lifelong theatrical patronage and his philanthropy for local and artistic causes. The article explains how Shelley’s dedication to the production arts over the performance arts, retained in the private and amateur domain, has enabled his work to go unnoticed. In addition, this article uses the Shelley case study to demonstrate how new perspectives on theatre histories can be gleaned by putting private and amateur activities under the spotlight. Finally, it makes visible the historiographical challenges pertinent to researching and writing about the amateur theatrical past including a distinct contextual knowledge that currently can only be accessed through extensive engagement with archival traces.

title: Cosmopolitanism in hybrid Caribbean novels : a world-literature perspective?
title_original: Cosmopolitanism in hybrid Caribbean novels : a world-literature perspective?
summary: This dissertation explores the mapping of the national allegory in the selected Caribbean fictional national novels, in order to establish whether there is a transition present with regards to the texts’ level of worldliness. The following eight titles will be discussed: Jamaica Kincaid - At the Bottom of the River (1983), Oonya Kempadoo - Buxton Spice (1998), Ramabai Espinet - The Swinging Bridge (2003), Andrea Levy - Small Island (2004), Zadie Smith - On Beauty (2005), Lakshmi Persaud - Daughters of Empire (2012), Bernardine Evaristo - Girl Woman Other (2019), Ingrid Persaud - Love After Love (2020). Primarily, the research analysis addresses: Goethe, Marx, Engels, Wallerstein, Damrosch, Moretti, Casanova, Trotsky, WReC, Hall, Löwy, and Jameson to investigate the notion of the national allegory and to broaden its scope in order to transform the selected novels. The dissertation’s main research question is: how do Caribbean fictional novels transform into sites of multiple belongings in order to awaken their level of consciousness? In order to answer the main question the following sub questions are used: 1. What are national allegorical Caribbean Third World texts? 2. How can transnationalism, hybridity and diaspora as notions (de)construct the chosen Caribbean novels in regards to their globalised identity? 3. In what manner is an activated sense of consciousness through Caribbean cosmopolitanism and globalisation portrayed in the chosen novels? 4. How has feminist literary theory influenced the portrayal of Caribbean women writers in the chosen historical period? The analysis focuses on comparative character analysis and their capabilities for various belongings in order to see if proof can be found that these selected novels are able to portray a degree of (un)consciousness mapping with regards to the national allegory. In addition, the dissertation examines whether Third World texts embed national allegories, and whether these differ or are similar. Methodologically, the thesis draws from comparative literature, world-literature, and feminist literary theory in order to analyse the following concepts: cosmopolitanism, globalisation, hybridity, (diasporic) identity, transnationalism, gender, and intersectionality. So, I investigate whether the specific positionality of the Caribbean contexts enable me to locate a transformation or a certain (un)consciousness of a globalised identity. This dissertation’s temporal scope from the 1980s to the present takes into account the specific historical events of this period that redefined the Caribbean region. This dissertation thus aims to analyse the level of (un)consciousness mapping with emphasis on the national allegory in the chosen novels in relation to their awareness of the world around them.

title: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport
title_original: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport
summary: Race, Protest, and the Power of the Body in Sport explores how and why athletes use public performance to bring audience’s attention to structural racism. The book it focuses on the case of Colin Kaepernick and his decision to take the knee, which eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to structural racism. In doing so, the book provides the reader with a clear understanding of how audiences respond to athlete activists in the US and in global contexts who seek to bring their attention to structural issues. Through the central case study of taking the knee, the book analyses how Kaepernick was able to bring attention to structural racism, and why taking the knee eventually became a global gesture for bringing attention to police brutality. The book also situates taking the knee in a history of athlete activism to recognise patterns in public response to athlete activism and suggests why different performative features can reduce the hostility athlete activists face. This book is intended for students and scholars interested in athlete activism, sports, and how sports fans respond to activism.

title: Teaching Visual Communication Design Histories Through Critical Annotation and Public Archiving: A Story in Five Artefacts
title_original: Teaching Visual Communication Design Histories Through Critical Annotation and Public Archiving: A Story in Five Artefacts
summary: Abstract This pedagogical case study explores how participatory pedagogy might transform design history education. The study draws on 8 years of working with design history students to recuperatively document visual communication design history artefacts and practitioners. For 3 years, this experience focused on collaborating with students to contribute 1000+ entries directly to the People's Graphic Design Archive (PGDA), an online, crowd‐sourced archive of diverse design histories. Approaching self‐reflexive teaching praxis as action research, this article synthesises the work of writing personalised weekly responses to +/− 5580 annotated design artefacts. The qualitative, mixed methods approach combines auto‐ethnographic writing, document analysis and critically informed historical contextualisation. After interrogating what design history means and situating crowd‐sourced archival work within a disciplinary framework, the author presents five representative examples of designed artefacts that typify students' contributions to the PGDA. In conversation with each artefact, the author demonstrates shared pain points experienced by student archivists/future design practitioners: generalisations, potentially productive misunderstandings and/or lack of access. This approach is transformative in that it equips students to contribute to disciplinary knowledge production while building historical research and contextual interpretation skills into their process of professional identity development.

title: Sport Event Branding
title_original: Sport Event Branding
summary: In the evolving landscape of global sport branding, major sport events have become influential platforms for shaping international perceptions and projecting national identity. This chapter examines sport event branding through the lens of soft power and introduces SportPower as an integrative framework explaining how sport can be strategically mobilized by governments, organizations, and athletes to influence global audiences. The chapter outlines a strategic process for sport event branding that emphasizes identity articulation, narrative construction, experiential engagement, media amplification, and legacy evaluation. It also discusses emerging trends and challenges, including technological innovation, ethical governance, sustainability, and geopolitical controversy. Through illustrative cases including the PyeongChang Winter Olympics, the Qatar World Cup, and the NBA China reconnection, the chapter demonstrates how sport event branding operates as a strategic instrument of global influence within contemporary sport branding theory and practice.

title: Metal geochemistry in bottom sediments from an urbanized tropical estuary: implications for land disposal of dredged materials
title_original: Metal geochemistry in bottom sediments from an urbanized tropical estuary: implications for land disposal of dredged materials
summary: Abstract The Fundão canal (RJ/Brazil) is an urbanized estuary impacted by eutrophication, metal contamination and silting, and was subjected to dredging operations to fulfill the demands of the 2016 Olympic Games. Given the scarcity of studies focused on the degradation of tropical estuaries and the need to evaluate the environmental Olympic legacy, this study assesses metal biogeochemistry in bottom sediments of the Fundão canal ( n = 18) and examines ecological implications for land disposal of dredged materials. Three lines of evidence were adopted: sediment and soil characterization; metal determination; and acute toxicity, reproduction and avoidance bioassays with Eisenia andrei using mixtures of local soils (Spodosol and Ferralsol) amended with a composite dredged sediment sample prepared by equally mixing all sediment samples. The sediments are predominantly muddy and organically enriched. These characteristics control metal distribution and are influenced by coastal morphology, mangrove vegetation, and marine and fluvial inputs. A sandy and silted sector was identified in the middle of the canal, exhibiting lower metal concentrations. Overall, metal concentrations exceeded Brazilian sediment quality guidelines and were associated with domestic and industrial waste inputs, particularly Zn (684.0 ± 318.8 mg/kg), Cu (161.1 ± 64.2 mg/kg), and Hg (1.2 ± 0.8 mg/kg). The acute toxicity of the dredged sediment sample was higher in sandy soils (Spodosol LC 50 = 2.50%) compared to clayey ones (Ferralsol LC 50 = 4.54%). Earthworm reproduction was the most sensitive endpoint (Spodosol EC 50 = 0.68%), followed by avoidance responses (Spodosol EC 50 = 1.73%). These results suggest that dredging without accompanying sanitation and source-control measures may offer only short-term benefits.

title: Distance and Coexistence: The Urban Transformation of Itaewon and the Seoul Central Mosque
title_original: Distance and Coexistence: The Urban Transformation of Itaewon and the Seoul Central Mosque
summary: Recently, intensifying resident opposition and the proliferation of exclusionary discourses surrounding mosque construction in one of major cities in South Korea have generated significant public controversy, contributing to the continued delay of such projects; yet, in contrast, there exists a single, historically established case—the Seoul Central Mosque (SCM), constructed in the 1970s in Itaewon, Seoul. By focusing on this specific and nationally situated case, the article examines how a Muslim community has formed around the mosque and how it has interacted with local residents over time. It then investigates how the SCM in Itaewon has both reflected and shaped the spatial politics of otherness in South Korea. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork, the article traces Itaewon’s transformation from a U.S. military camp town into a multicultural district and shows that coexistence among heterogeneous groups has been maintained through spatial and temporal negotiation rather than integration. Building on Nancy’s notion of inoperative community and Valentine’s critique of the contact hypothesis, it argues that coexistence in Itaewon is sustained through the maintenance of distance that enables relations without forcing assimilation. The strong ideology of ethnic homogeneity in Korean society paradoxically brought together diverse marginal groups in Itaewon, where different groups have coexisted without asserting dominance. Finally, the persistence of the mosque amid urban redevelopment symbolizes how otherness endures within the city, revealing coexistence as a pragmatic negotiation of difference embedded in Seoul’s changing urban landscape.

title: Representations of the Ancient Olympic Games in Polish Literature Before 1795
title_original: Representations of the Ancient Olympic Games in Polish Literature Before 1795
summary: Between the decline of the ancient Olympic Games and the revival of the modern Olympic Games in 1896, literature played the most fundamental role in preserving the Olympic heritage. Descriptions of the ancient Olympics and metaphorical references to their traditions were featured in literature. Literature also served as a means of disseminating information about other aspects of the Olympic legacy and contributed to the development of pseudo-Olympics. Olympic themes appeared in Old Polish literature as well. From the first mentions in the fifteenth century onward, Polish authors demonstrated an increasing interest in the ancient Olympic Games, as evidenced by the growing quantity and improving quality of their works. Olympic themes in Old Polish literature mirrored ideas and trends that originated in other European countries. Polish authors were familiar with ancient works and European texts devoted to Olympic matters and made successful use of them. Factual accounts predominated, and during that period, literature was the sole source of information about the Olympics. When used appropriately, literature could serve as a model for organizing physical exercises designed to strengthen the body for utilitarian purposes and provide an example of the physical fitness essential to a well-rounded upbringing and education.

title: Cultural proximity reveals a local premium in collective memory
title_original: Cultural proximity reveals a local premium in collective memory
summary: Collective memory-shared information about the past that shapes a group's identity-is often examined through constructs such as familiarity or salience, conflating its local and global components. Here, we untangle these components using multilingual online attention traces for over 50,000 Wikipedia biographies spanning 137 billion pageviews and a large-scale behavioral recognition experiment in which more than 41,000 participants answered factual questions about famous biographies. Our experiment reveals a robust local memory premium, with people being around 10% points more likely to answer correctly questions about someone from their country and about five points more likely to answer correctly questions about biographies with whom they share a language. Finally, we study the impact of three major life events: Nobel Prizes, Oscars, and deaths in local and global online attention, finding these events produce brief but strong surges in local attention and slower but sustained increases in global attention. These findings add important spatial and temporal nuances to our understanding of collective memory.

title: The Dialogue Within: Transforming Metacognitive Writing Instruction Through Individuation Theory in A Pre-Tertiary Singaporean Language and Argumentation Classroom
title_original: The Dialogue Within: Transforming Metacognitive Writing Instruction Through Individuation Theory in A Pre-Tertiary Singaporean Language and Argumentation Classroom
summary: This paper introduces a new, extended theory of the human psyche known as Individuation Theory, and describes how it was used to teach the subject 8807 H1 General Paper in a government school in Singapore from October 2020 to August 2022. Beyond simply preparing 140 students for the Singapore-Cambridge General Certificate of Education Advanced Levels examination (GCE A-Levels) in November 2020 and 2022, Individuation Theory sought to satisfy multiple affective and socio-emotional student outcomes related to motivation, self-efficacy, citizenship education, empathy, resilience and intellectual curiosity via a focus on dialogue with the self through applied and scaffolded metacognition that encouraged students to decolonise and decompartmentalise their self-perception, self-orientation and understanding of the nation, world and universe, fostering critical thinking founded on an ever-expanding, fractal-like inquiry into the self, psyche and mind. After a discussion of the theory’s history and how the author came to assemble it, the theory is unpacked in some detail in the abstract, and thereafter in the context it was first applied as delineated above, examining the writing curriculum that was enacted, the dialogic practices it nurtured, and its results on the students who participated in it. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of wider use of the theory both in Singapore and elsewhere, and a call to action for the facilitation and promotion of greater self-dialogue toward a more equitable, just and meaningful 21st-century experience of human life, regardless of where one lives.

title: Hydration status and repetitive head impacts: neurophysiological responses and functional implications
title_original: Hydration status and repetitive head impacts: neurophysiological responses and functional implications
summary: Combat sport athletes frequently experience two distinct yet potentially interacting physiological stressors: repetitive head impacts (RHIs) and rapid weight loss through hypo-hydration. While each has been studied independently, limited research has examined their combined neurophysiological consequences. This thesis aimed to investigate how RHIs and hypo-hydration influence neuromuscular and cortical function, using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and motor nerve stimulation (MNS) as assessment tools. An initial survey of over 100 combat sport athletes highlighted widespread engagement in rapid weight loss practices, with many reporting overlapping symptoms of hypo-hydration and concussion. In addition, some athletes reported exacerbation of concussion symptoms after undergoing a weight-cut. A reliability study confirmed that TMS and MNS measures could be used with sufficient precision in ensuring robustness for subsequent investigations. In the first experimental study, exercise and heat-induced hypo-hydration impaired maximal strength and voluntary activation but did not significantly alter corticospinal excitability or inhibition, suggesting preserved central drive under fluid-restricted conditions. In contrast, the following study examined responses to a single sparring session and found significant increases in cortical inhibition and motor thresholds, along with reduced maximal strength and voluntary activation, all of which resolved within 48 hours. A follow-up longitudinal study using instrumented mouthguards revealed that impact magnitude e.g., cumulative angular acceleration predicted the degree of increased cortical inhibition. Finally, a 10-week case series tracked three fighters through their fight camps. Voluntary activation and strength showed the most frequent meaningful changes, and over 200 RHIs were recorded in approximately 35% of their monitored sparring sessions. In summary, repeated head impacts elevated cortical inhibitory activity and central fatigue, while heat-induced hypo-hydration produced a contrasting neurophysiological response. These opposing effects may suggest a complex physiological interplay if they occur concurrently, whereby head-impact-related neural inhibition could disrupt or override compensatory mechanisms associated with fluid loss, potentially increasing vulnerability to injury and impairing athletic performance.

Finally, a 10-week case series tracked three fighters through their fight camps. Voluntary activation and strength showed the most frequent meaningful changes, and over 200 RHIs were recorded in approximately 35% of their monitored sparring sessions. In summary, repeated head impacts elevated cortical inhibitory activity and central fatigue, while heat-induced hypo-hydration produced a contrasting neurophysiological response. These opposing effects may suggest a complex physiological interplay if they occur concurrently, whereby head-impact-related neural inhibition could disrupt or override compensatory mechanisms associated with fluid loss, potentially increasing vulnerability to injury and impairing athletic performance.

title: Concussion in live sport broadcast coverage: How do the public perceive it?
title_original: Concussion in live sport broadcast coverage: How do the public perceive it?
summary: Sport-concussion is widely reported in the mass media. This reporting includes live sport broadcasts that reach, and influence, widespread audiences. From a public health perspective, broadcast information about concussion should be accurate. An understanding of public perceptions of sport-concussion coverage is needed to understand potential impacts. One-hundred and sixty-three people completed an online cross-sectional survey. The survey comprised structured and open-ended questions to gather perceptions about the media portrayal of sport-concussions (portrayal-perceptions) in sport broadcasts, and recommendations to improve it (recommendations). Twelve of 30 portrayal-perceptions were endorsed (agreed or disagreed) by >50% of respondents, including that the portrayal should be improved. Ten of 12 recommendations were agreed, including that the portrayal should prioritise player health. No statistically significant differences in perceptions were found based on participant background (e.g., their concussion history). This research, through considering the way people experience sport-concussion coverage, elucidates its potential to shape understanding about sport-concussion and its management. Community members support changes to the media portrayal of sport-concussion to increase its informative value for audiences.

title: The Origin of the Work of Art in Fashion: Art, Craft, and Mass Production, and the Significance for Fashion Copyright
title_original: The Origin of the Work of Art in Fashion: Art, Craft, and Mass Production, and the Significance for Fashion Copyright
summary: Abstract Fashion may well be the quintessential “art” through which to elaborate both the distinction and the relation between craft and art, between art and technology, between technē and episteme . Indeed fashion, comprising objects of beauty and of utility, is an exemplary lens through which to examine the manner of originality itself. not only the originality in object, but also in relations between makers and consumers as mediated through those objects. And in doing so, originality emerges not as confined to the object, but necessarily in the author’s design, as it were; in other words, in the relation between the maker and the consumer as mediated through those objects. The tools of mass production as materials of originality, and the intentionality of marketability as creative choices, are especially salient in fashion. Towards understanding this kind of creative work and considering its relationship to copyright, this article explores an approach to fashion as mass art. It examines this historical tension between craft and art, and inevitably utility and aesthetics, through the lens of fashion and its relationship to technology, from early industrialisation to current tensions around artificial intelligence. In particular, the judgment of Mio/konektra establishes an approach to originality that goes some way to resolving this socio-cultural distinction and clarifying the relevance of intellectual property as a cultural institution. Mio/konektra is thus significant for its influence in understanding the origin (and originality) of the work of art in fashion, and at the same time, insight from fashion enlightens the reasoning in Mio/konektra .

title: Exploring the Path of Promoting the Construction of a Strong Cultural Country through the Red Sports Spirit during the“15th Five-Year Plan”Period
title_original: Exploring the Path of Promoting the Construction of a Strong Cultural Country through the Red Sports Spirit during the“15th Five-Year Plan”Period
summary: The 15th Five‑Year‑Plan period constitutes a pivotal starting‑point for building a modern socialist country in all respects, as well as a historical convergence phase for accelerating the development of both a strong sports nation and a strong cultural nation. As a valuable spiritual asset forged over a century‑long CPC‑led sports practice, the Red‑Sports Spirit embodies firm ideals and convictions, indomitable fighting will, profound patriotism and self‑dedication. It serves as a vital spiritual driving force for consolidating cultural self‑confidence and advancing theconstruction of a strong cultural country in the new era. Grounded in Xi Jin Thought on Culture and important expositions on sports, this paper systematically dissects the internal logic and practical pathways for leveraging the Red‑Sports Spirit to advance the building of a strong cultural country throughout the 15th Five‑Year‑Plan period. This study identifies a symbiotic relationship of “spiritual empowerment and cultural soul‑forging” between the Red‑Sports Spirit and the construction of a strong cultural country. The Red‑Sports Spirit acts as a spiritual engine and practical carrier for cultural‑power‑building, while the construction of a strong cultural country provides institutional guarantees and an era‑specific platform for inheriting and promoting the Red‑Sports Spirit. Its endogenous driving forces stem from the continuous awakening power of historical memories of red sports, the value‑oriented appeal of the Chinese Sports Spirit, and the vivid motivational power derived from national fitness and sports‑power‑building practices. Its exogenous driving forces originate from the top‑level guidance of the strong‑cultural‑country strategy, the scenario‑reshaping effect of digital technologies, and the strategic demands of sports‑cultural games amid a complex international environment.

title: Kinematics and electromyographic analysis of the airtrack in breaking: a comparison between expert and amateur break dancers
title_original: Kinematics and electromyographic analysis of the airtrack in breaking: a comparison between expert and amateur break dancers
summary: Breaking was introduced as a competitive event at the 2024 Paris Olympics, yet the biomechanics of its technically demanding power moves remain largely unexplored. This exploratory study compared three-dimensional joint kinematics, center-of-mass (CoM) variables, and dominant-side muscle activation during the airtrack, a power move involving whole-body rotation through inverted hand-support postures, between expert (EG, n = 6) and amateur (AG, n = 6) break dancers. Joint kinematics were recorded using a three-dimensional motion-capture system, and surface electromyography was recorded from nine dominant-side muscles. The airtrack cycle was divided into five events and four phases based on hand contact and lift-off. All comparisons were exploratory, and all p values are unadjusted. The EG showed greater dominant knee extension at selected events and greater hip abduction during single-arm support. Anteroposterior CoM dispersion was greater in the EG during selected phases, and resultant CoM velocity was higher during Phase 1 and Phase 3. No dominant-side muscle–phase comparison met the nominal screening threshold; therefore, the EMG findings are reported descriptively. These findings provide an initial biomechanical characterization of the airtrack and identify event- and phase-specific kinematic and CoM features that differed between expert and amateur dancers. Further research should examine how these features relate to airtrack performance.

title: Treatment of anterior cruciate ligament injuries in older adults: A clinical review
title_original: Treatment of anterior cruciate ligament injuries in older adults: A clinical review
summary: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is essential for knee joint stability.Although ACL injuries primarily affect young and middle-aged athletes, their incidence among older adults is increasing.Substantial or complete ACL rupture may cause persistent instability despite conservative treatment; in such cases, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) surgery is generally considered the standard surgical treatment.Because older adults often have osteoporosis, joint degeneration, and comorbidities, as well as lower functional demands than younger patients, some surgeons recommend conservative treatment.However, recent studies have found that patients who undergo ACLR and ACL repair have better postoperative functional recovery than those who receive conservative treatment, although there remains no clear consensus regarding the optimal treatment.This review examines the characteristics of ACL injuries in older adults and compares treatment methods, with the aim of improving the management of these patients.Current evidence indicates that older adults who undergo ACLR achieve comparable functional outcomes to younger patients, suggesting that treatment decisions should focus on functional needs and overall health rather than age or comorbidities alone.All-inside techniques may provide better outcomes in older adults, while supplementary reinforcement fixation may benefit patients with osteoporosis.

title: Digital registration of the spatial distribution of contact load on the striking surface of a boxing glove during hook punches in the «strike force» discipline
title_original: Digital registration of the spatial distribution of contact load on the striking surface of a boxing glove during hook punches in the «strike force» discipline
summary: Relevance. Digital measurement systems in combat sports enable quantitative assessment of contact parameters, force and the spatial structure of impact. The microstructure of the glove–target contact patch remains insufficiently characterized in the «strike force» discipline. Aim. To evaluate a sensor-equipped boxing glove for recording the spatial distribution of contact load during maximal-intensity hook punches and to characterize between-athlete variability. Methods. This was an observational, instrumental, cross-sectional study. Peak punch force was recorded with the CROCUS system (3500 Hz), whereas contact-load distribution was recorded with a wearable 8×8 piezoresistive matrix integrated into a 12 oz GREEN HILL glove. The best hook-punch attempts of 32 boxers aged 20.2±2.3 years were analysed. Mean, SD, 95% confidence intervals and coefficients of variation were calculated; CV was interpreted as between-athlete variability rather than test–retest reliability. Results. Mean maximal hook-punch force was 2975.5 N (SD=486.2 N; 95 Conclusions. The sensor glove provides additional spatial information about glove–target contact. Its summed load must not be interpreted as a force-transfer coefficient, and repeatability should be evaluated separately using repeated trials and ICC/SEM.

title: Biomechanical and Technical Indicators of Talent Identification and Swimming Performance in Young Swimmers
title_original: Biomechanical and Technical Indicators of Talent Identification and Swimming Performance in Young Swimmers
summary: The identification of talented young swimmers is a major focus in sports science, with increasing attention being directed toward biomechanical and technical indicators associated with future performance. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence regarding biomechanical and technical factors related to swimming performance and talent identification in young competitive swimmers. A systematic search was conducted in the PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases following PRISMA guidelines. Eleven studies published between 2007 and 2023 met the inclusion criteria. The findings consistently demonstrated that higher-performing young swimmers exhibited superior biomechanical profiles characterized by higher stroke index, optimal combinations of stroke frequency and stroke length, greater swimming velocity, lower velocity fluctuations, and enhanced propulsive efficiency. Among these variables, stroke index emerged as the most consistent predictor of swimming performance and potential future success. Longitudinal studies further emphasized the importance of monitoring the development of these characteristics throughout growth and maturation. Overall, the evidence suggests that biomechanical and technical indicators should complement competition outcomes in talent identification programs and may provide valuable information for supporting long-term athlete development in youth swimming.

title: Multi-domain physical fitness profiles and machine learning classification by sport category across 13 competitive sports
title_original: Multi-domain physical fitness profiles and machine learning classification by sport category across 13 competitive sports
summary: Background: Comparative multi-sport fitness profiling using a common institutional assessment framework remains limited in Southeast Asian competitive sport. Aims: To compare multi-domain fitness profiles across 13 sports grouped into four sport categories and to evaluate machine-learning classification of sport category. Methods: This cross-sectional STROBE-reported study included 197 KONI athletes (137 males, 60 females; age 20.6 ± 5.8 years). Standardized procedures were used within applicable sport groups, although several tests were category-dependent. Athletes were grouped as Combat (n=69), Team (n=72), Individual Technical (n=37), and Precision/Shooting (n=19). Between-category analyses and Random Forest (RF) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) with 5-fold out-of-fold cross-validation were performed. Results: The largest between-category effects were observed for vertical jump (η²=0.438, p<.001), the Bleep Composite/estimated VO₂max signal (η²=0.217, p<.001), and sit-up endurance (η²=0.199, p<.001). RF achieved 79.7% accuracy and macro-AUC=0.907; the three largest Gini importances in the final nine-variable model were vertical jump (0.211), Bleep Composite (0.162), and push-up endurance (0.144). Conclusion: Multi-domain fitness patterns differed across the four administrative sport categories, but age, maturation, sex composition, and category-linked test availability constrain interpretation. The classifier is exploratory and requires external validation; the findings describe already-trained athletes and do not establish prospective talent-identification validity.

title: Exploration on the Practical Path of Physical Training in the Improvement of Sprint Performance
title_original: Exploration on the Practical Path of Physical Training in the Improvement of Sprint Performance
summary: Sprint events rely on the anaerobic phosphagen system for energy supply and are typical high-intensity competitive sports. An athlete's performance and final results largely depend on their ability to deliver peak power output in specific events. In grassroots track and field training and competition practice, a common phenomenon exists: some athletes exhibit standard technical movements and sufficient daily training loads, yet struggle to achieve significant breakthroughs in event-specific speed. The domestic grassroots track and field training system has clear shortcomings in developing event-specific physical fitness, primarily due to inadequate adaptation of physical training to specific events, fragmented overall training systems, and poor integration between old and new training models. This study employs literature review, logical analysis, and practical training synthesis methods, integrating the energy supply characteristics, force-generation patterns, and dynamic technical features of sprinting, to systematically clarify the complete composition and core training logic of sprint-specific physical fitness. It identifies various common issues in grassroots sprint training and proposes an optimized physical fitness training framework with practical applicability across four dimensions: hierarchical annual periodization, precise enhancement of event-specific abilities, integration of diversified training models, and training monitoring with injury prevention. The research outcomes can further refine the theoretical framework for grassroots sprint physical training and provide solid, feasible practical guidance for cultivating specialized abilities in youth sprint ers and implementing scientific training at the grassroots level.

title: Limited Predictive Value of Concentric Knee and Trunk Isokinetic Peak Torque for Maximal Force and Stretch-Shortening Cycle Performance in Highly Trained Youth Optimist Sailors
title_original: Limited Predictive Value of Concentric Knee and Trunk Isokinetic Peak Torque for Maximal Force and Stretch-Shortening Cycle Performance in Highly Trained Youth Optimist Sailors
summary: Background: Concentric knee and trunk strength may contribute differently to maximal force and stretch-shortening cycle performance in youth sailors. This study evaluated the predictive value of concentric knee and trunk isokinetic strength for these outcomes in highly trained youth Optimist sailors. Methods: Forty highly trained Optimist sailors (20 boys and 20 girls; age, 13.03 ± 1.40 years) completed knee and trunk isokinetic testing at 60°·s−1 and 180°·s−1, isometric mid-thigh pull, squat jump, and countermovement jump tests. Velocity-specific multiple linear regression models included a composite of dominant and nondominant knee extensor and flexor strength, trunk extensor strength, trunk flexor strength, and sex. Results: The models explained 60.7% and 49.4% of the variance in isometric mid-thigh pull peak force at 60°·s−1 and 180°·s−1, respectively. The knee strength composite was independently associated with peak force at both velocities (β = 0.51, p = 0.003; β = 0.56, p = 0.006). The models explained 1.3–3.5% of dynamic strength index variance and 17.8% and 4.5% of eccentric utilization ratio and elastic index variance at 60°·s−1 and 180°·s−1, respectively. Trunk flexor strength was associated with eccentric utilization ratio and elastic index at 60°·s−1 (β = 0.52, p = 0.029), although these outcomes are mathematically dependent. Sex was not associated with any outcome. Conclusions: Concentric isokinetic strength showed greater predictive value for maximal force than for stretch-shortening cycle performance. Combined knee extensor and flexor strength was consistently associated with maximal force, whereas limited variance was explained in stretch-shortening cycle outcomes.
