title: Thinking and looking produce distinct patterns of gaze aversion during a structured social interaction
title_original: Thinking and looking produce distinct patterns of gaze aversion during a structured social interaction
summary: Systematic differences in eye gaze patterns emerge when attention is directed externally versus internally in non-social contexts. Here we asked whether these differences also apply to structured social interactions. Gaze aversion during conversations may occur because conversation partners are referencing an object in their environment (an externally directed looking gaze) or because they are thinking and wish to reduce visual information from the other person's face (an internally directed thinking gaze). We measured eye movements in 28 participants while prompting these two types of gaze aversion. Compared to looking gaze aversion, thinking gaze aversion involved scanning a larger spatial area with shorter and fewer fixations. In addition, head and eye movements were more strongly coupled during looking than during thinking gaze aversion, and participants exhibited consistent individual variation in the direction of thinking gaze aversion. These findings shed light on how individuals manage social attention and suggest that observable social cues are available for others to infer interlocutors' intentions during conversations.

Gaze aversion during conversations may occur because conversation partners are referencing an object in their environment (an externally directed looking gaze) or because they are thinking and wish to reduce visual information from the other person's face (an internally directed thinking gaze). We measured eye movements in 28 participants while prompting these two types of gaze aversion. Compared to looking gaze aversion, thinking gaze aversion involved scanning a larger spatial area with shorter and fewer fixations. In addition, head and eye movements were more strongly coupled during looking than during thinking gaze aversion, and participants exhibited consistent individual variation in the direction of thinking gaze aversion. These findings shed light on how individuals manage social attention and suggest that observable social cues are available for others to infer interlocutors' intentions during conversations.

title: Before the World Was Watching: Qatar and the 1981 FIFA World Youth Championship
title_original: Before the World Was Watching: Qatar and the 1981 FIFA World Youth Championship
summary: Much of the existing scholarship on sport in Qatar has been shaped by the 2022 FIFA World Cup and the broader issues around it. However, many of the earlier moments in Qatar’s sporting history that were vital in shaping the country’s sporting identity have been largely overlooked. These include the hosting of the 1976 Arabian Gulf Cup, the 1981 FIFA World Youth Championship in Australia, and Qatar’s first victory in the AFC Asian Cup in 2019. The 1981 FIFA World Youth Championship, as a shared experience around which national pride and collective memory took. Using material from Al-Raya, one of Qatar’s most influential newspapers, The tournament is read as a foundational moment in Qatar sport history. By doing so, it is made clear that football was embedded as a social and cultural practice in Qatar long before the 2022 World Cup, that on-field achievements were used as a measure of Qatar’s social progress, and that this success helped to define the country’s sporting identity in the subsequent decades.

title: Effects of a swimming training program on physical fitness components in children aged 6–12 years
title_original: Effects of a swimming training program on physical fitness components in children aged 6–12 years
summary: Background and Study Aim. Swimming is a form of physical activity that engages major muscle groups and may contribute to the development of physical fitness during childhood. Regular swimming training may influence several components of physical performance, including strength, flexibility, speed, and explosive strength. However, the extent to which a structured swimming programme improves these physical performance components in children compared with usual physical education remains of practical interest. The aim of this study was to determine the effect of 12 weeks of regular swimming training on physical performance parameters in girls aged 6–12 years. Materials and Methods. Thirty girls aged 6–12 years were randomly allocated to a swimming training group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). The swimming training group completed a 12-week structured programme consisting of four 90-minute sessions per week, whereas the control group participated only in regular physical education lessons. Height, body weight, and body mass index were assessed at baseline. Flexibility, vertical jump, standing long jump, handgrip strength, back strength, leg strength, and 20-m sprint performance were assessed before and after the intervention. Intervention effects were evaluated using 2 × 2 mixed-design analyses of variance, with time as the within-subject factor and group as the between-subject factor. Holm correction was applied to the seven time × group interaction tests. Results. Significant main effects of time were observed for standing long jump performance (p = .030), handgrip strength (p = .047), and leg strength (p < .001). The unadjusted time × group interactions were significant for flexibility (p = .008) and standing long jump performance (p = .030); however, neither remained statistically significant after Holm correction (p = .054 and p = .179, respectively). After adjustment for multiple comparisons, no significant time × group interaction was observed for any physical performance outcome. Conclusions. A 12-week structured swimming programme can be incorporated into regular physical activity programmes for girls aged 6–12 years as a means of supporting physical fitness development. When evaluating its effectiveness, changes in individual fitness components should be considered alongside normal growth, maturation, and other physical activity during childhood.

title: Profile of Basic Football Skills among 10–12-Year-Old Students at SDN 1 Girimarto
title_original: Profile of Basic Football Skills among 10–12-Year-Old Students at SDN 1 Girimarto
summary: This study described the basic football skills of 10–12-year-old students at SDN 1 Girimarto. A quantitative descriptive survey design using performance tests and measurement was employed. The population comprised 58 fourth- and fifth-grade students, while the analyzed sample consisted of all 34 male students aged 10–12 years within those grades, selected through a non-probability criterion-based approach consistent with the study scope. Data were collected using the football skill test battery developed by Daral Fauzi, consisting of the Short Pass Test, Dribbling Test, and Shooting at the Goal Test. Scores were standardized and classified using the instrument norms, and the distributions were summarized with frequencies and percentages. Dribbling was dominated by the moderate category (52.9%), as was passing (61.8%), whereas shooting was most frequently classified as poor (35.3%). These findings indicated an uneven skill profile: students generally demonstrated functional dribbling and passing competence, but shooting accuracy remained comparatively weaker. The results provide a descriptive basis for teachers to plan age-appropriate football learning activities, particularly practice that gives adequate attention to shooting without neglecting dribbling and passing.

title: Covid-19 and the Entertainment Industry: A Test of Market Efficiency
title_original: Covid-19 and the Entertainment Industry: A Test of Market Efficiency
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the COVID-19 outbreak a global pandemic on March 11, 2020. This study examines how the entertainment industry’s stock market reacted to the announcement and tests semi-strong form market efficiency. The pandemic significantly disrupted entertainment markets as lockdowns and restrictions on public gatherings forced the closure of cinemas and live entertainment venues. In response, companies shifted toward on-demand content and streaming platforms, while demand for digital entertainment, including streaming services and video games, increased substantially. Companies such as Netflix and Disney experienced significant growth as consumers remained at home. However, the broader financial impact of the pandemic created uncertainty and substantial pressure across industries. Using standard event-study methodology, this study analyzes risk-adjusted stock price returns for ten major large-cap entertainment companies surrounding the WHO announcement, with day 0 representing March 11, 2020. The event window spans day -30 to day +30. Results support the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) and indicate that the entertainment industry experienced a significant negative effect during the event period.

title: Local site fidelity and long-distance migration: twelve years of Nathusius’ pipistrelle ecology in the UK
title_original: Local site fidelity and long-distance migration: twelve years of Nathusius’ pipistrelle ecology in the UK
summary: Abstract Migratory bats remain poorly understood despite their ecological importance and increasing exposure to anthropogenic threats. We present twelve years of monitoring of Pipistrellus nathusii at Bedfont Lakes, the first bat box site in the UK to document use by this species. Using recapture data from box checks and trapping, alongside automated telemetry, we investigated box occupancy, roost fidelity, social structure and migratory movements. Box occupancy was highly dynamic, varying by sex and season, with a clear autumn peak coinciding with migratory aggregations and mating activity. Occupancy was significantly influenced by box orientation and design, while microclimatic effects were limited. Roosting area fidelity was high, with several males recaptured across years, suggesting the coexistence of resident strategies alongside wide-ranging migrants. Social organisation ranged from solitary males to mixed-sex groups, reflecting seasonal variation in group composition consistent with seasonal harem formation. Network analysis revealed a sparse, highly clustered structure with no deviation from random associations. Long-distance ring recoveries, including a female recorded 2,018 km away in Russia, and Motus detections across Europe confirmed transboundary migration. These findings highlight the value of long-term, multi-method monitoring in revealing complex movement strategies in P. nathusii . The long-distance movements documented here also emphasise the transboundary nature of bat conservation, as migratory individuals may encounter multiple anthropogenic pressures, including wind-energy infrastructure, across different countries and jurisdictions. Effective conservation of migratory bats therefore requires international coordination and a better understanding of how local sites contribute to broader migratory networks.

title: Pengaruh Self-Efficacy dan Motivasi Intrinsik terhadap Konsistensi Latihan Keterampilan Gerak Dasar Siswa dalam Pembelajaran PJOK.
title_original: Pengaruh Self-Efficacy dan Motivasi Intrinsik terhadap Konsistensi Latihan Keterampilan Gerak Dasar Siswa dalam Pembelajaran PJOK.
summary: Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PESH) instruction plays a vital role in developing students' fundamental movement skills; however, the consistency of student practice remains a challenge. Low levels of student engagement and persistence in practicing suggest the influence of psychological factors—such as self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation—that warrant deeper investigation. This study aims to analyze the impact of self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation on the consistency of students' fundamental movement skill practice within PJOK lessons. The study employs the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method, a research approach involving the systematic, transparent, and structured identification, examination, and synthesis of findings from previous research. The results indicate that self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation significantly influence the consistency of students' fundamental movement skill practice in PESH. Self-efficacy plays a crucial role in shaping students' belief in their ability to perform movement activities, fostering greater confidence and resilience, and enabling sustained practice. Consequently, a linear relationship exists: higher levels of self-efficacy and intrinsic motivation among students correlate with greater consistency in practicing fundamental movement skills during PESH instruction.

title: Effects of Different Loading Strategies on Kinematic and Neuromuscular Responses During the Back Squat
title_original: Effects of Different Loading Strategies on Kinematic and Neuromuscular Responses During the Back Squat
summary: Sırt çömelmesi, alt vücut kuvveti ve atletik performans terapisi için yaygın olarak kullanılan direnç egzersizlerinden biridir. Son yıllarda, hareket özellikleri ve nöromüsküler tepkilerin değişme potansiyelleri nedeniyle, geleneksel direnç antrenmanına alternatif bir yaklaşım olarak dengesiz yükleme yöntemi giderek daha fazla ilgi görmektedir. title: Modeling the Training Process to Support Physical Fitness and Movement Performance in Triathletes
title_original: Modeling the Training Process to Support Physical Fitness and Movement Performance in Triathletes
summary: The preparation of triathletes requires the coordinated development of swimming, cycling, running, general physical capacities, and discipline-specific technical skills. Contemporary endurance-training research emphasizes progressive specialization, systematic training-load management, and the integration of general and sport-specific preparation throughout the annual cycle. Purpose. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a training process model for supporting physical fitness and movement performance in triathletes through the integration of developmental and lead-up exercise complexes and segment-specific training programs into general physical preparation. Methods. A one-year controlled quasi-experimental study involved 20 male triathletes aged 18–23 years who held Category I or Candidate Master of Sport qualifications at baseline. Participants were assigned by a matched-group procedure to an experimental group (EG; n = 10) and a control group (CG; n = 10), with matching based on age, sports qualification, training experience, and baseline physical performance; no randomization was applied. Outcomes included the 60 m sprint, 500 m swimming test, 3000 m run, shoulder mobility, and standing long jump. Within-group pre–post changes were analyzed using paired-samples t-tests and Cohen’s d_z. Direct between-group comparisons of change scores were used to evaluate the comparative intervention effect, with Hedges’ g and 95% confidence intervals reported. Results. The EG showed statistically significant within-group improvements in all five outcomes, whereas the CG reached significance only for the 500 m swimming test. Direct between-group comparisons of change scores did not reach statistical significance for the 60 m sprint (p = .338), 500 m swimming (p = .069), 3000 m run (p = .341), shoulder mobility (p = .194), or standing long jump (p = .238). Between-group standardized effects favored the EG and ranged from g = 0.42 to 0.83, but all 95% confidence intervals included zero. Conclusion. The proposed model was associated with large within-group improvements in the EG and moderate-to-large between-group effect estimates; however, the small non-randomized sample did not provide sufficient evidence to establish statistically significant superiority over conventional training. Larger randomized or adequately controlled studies are required to confirm the comparative effect.

title: Injuries in alpine skiing: risk factors, injury mechanisms and prevention: a review of current evidence
title_original: Injuries in alpine skiing: risk factors, injury mechanisms and prevention: a review of current evidence
summary: Background. Alpine skiing is a highly popular winter sport, with approximately 380 million skier days annually worldwide. Despite a decline in recreational injury rates over the past 40 years (from 5–8 to 0.5–3.0 injuries per 1,000 skier days), severe knee ligament injuries and traumatic brain injuries remain common. In elite racing, injury rates are substantially higher, reaching 36.2–36.7 injuries per 100 World Cup athletes per season. Aim of the study. This review synthesizes current evidence on risk factors, biomechanical injury mechanisms, and prevention strategies in recreational and competitive alpine skiing. Materials and methods. The review was conducted using publications published in the PubMed, Google Scoolar and UpToDate. Our search included the following keywords: alpine skiing, anterior cruciate ligament, rick factors, injury mechanisms. References include systematic reviews, but also clinical trials, as well as case reports. Conclusion. Reducing alpine skiing injuries requires a multidisciplinary approach combining safer equipment, regulated standing heights, neuromuscular and core-stability training, video-based risk awareness, and safer slope and course design. Such interventions can significantly reduce injury risk, with video-based programs reporting a 45% reduction in ACL injuries.

title: Reframing Motivational Typologies of Long-Term International Academic Mobility
title_original: Reframing Motivational Typologies of Long-Term International Academic Mobility
summary: Contemporary higher education is increasingly shaped by internationalisation and long-term academic mobility. This study re-examines motivational typologies of long-term mobility, typically involving sustained employment, relocation and institutional integration, building on Richardson and McKenna's metaphorical framework. Through interviews with 31 academics from 14 countries across 16 Chinese universities, it confirms four established types (explorer, refugee, mercenary and architect) and identifies three additional types (pioneer, follower and embedder), capturing motivations related to institution-building, relationship-based mobility and gradual embeddedness. The findings show that motivations are shaped through interaction of structural conditions, relational ties and individual meaning-making over time. By linking these patterns to underlying mechanisms, the study reframes metaphor-based typologies as context-dependent and processual rather than fixed categories. It thus offers a process-oriented basis for analysing how mobility motivations are formed and evolve across contexts, and provides a context-sensitive understanding of long-term academic mobility in rapidly internationalising systems as China.

title: Glocalization Practice from the Perspective of Curatorial Capital: Reflections on Public Pedagogy with Margin as Method
title_original: Glocalization Practice from the Perspective of Curatorial Capital: Reflections on Public Pedagogy with Margin as Method
summary: Curatorial work in exhibitions is no longer a neutral organisation of exhibitions but a type of cultural production driven by the logic of capital. This paper introduces the idea of "curatorial capital" and studies how symbolic capital, social capital and economic capital are combined in the public education of art museums. The three selected cases for comparison are the "Spatial Productivity" project of Suzhou Contemporary Art Museum (over 40 free public activities as supporting programming). A comparative analysis of the 2025 international solo exhibitions and concurrent public education programs of UCCA (Ullens Center for Contemporary Art), and the "Interiors of Wanderings—Swiss Contemporary Comics Art Exhibition" held by Shanghai Minsheng Modern Art Museum in 2025. Research shows that the deep problem of public education is not cultural opposition between global and local, but rather a structural mismatch in the knowledge hierarchy and resource allocation for the flow of curatorial capital. "Taking the Margins as Method" is not passive acceptance of the marginal position; instead, it turns the margin into cognitive resources to disrupt the current operational order and reconstruct the knowledge foundation and participation system of public education. The effectiveness of local-global public education is not determined by the proportion of the two, but rather by the continuous involvement of marginal forces to foster a new public cultural logic in the conflict between difference and connection.

title: From the Soviet Invasion to the Rise of the Taliban: Political Transformation in Afghanistan
title_original: From the Soviet Invasion to the Rise of the Taliban: Political Transformation in Afghanistan
summary: Afghanistan became one of the principal arenas in which great power rivalry, regional intervention, and internal political fragmentation intersected during the Cold War. This study analyses the political transformation of Afghanistan from the Soviet invasion of December 1979 to the Taliban’s capture of Kabul in September 1996 within its historical context. It aims to demonstrate how this transformation was shaped at the intersection of the international conjuncture, regional dynamics, and domestic political developments. Methodologically, the study is based on qualitative historical analysis and is situated at the intersection of political history and international relations. Within this framework, historical causal relations are examined through document-based analysis. The study addresses the strategic and ideological factors behind the Soviet Union’s decision to invade, the reflections of Cold War policies shaped by the Carter and Reagan Doctrines of the United States, the organizational structure of the mujahideen resistance, and the support mechanisms provided by regional actors such as Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The findings indicate that the Soviet withdrawal did not produce stability in Afghanistan; on the contrary, the limited effectiveness of Najibullah’s National Reconciliation policy, combined with the power struggle among mujahideen groups, deepened the civil war and created a political and social environment conducive to the rise of the Taliban. By evaluating dependency theory together with the proxy war approach, the study concludes that the interaction of great power competition, regional interventions, and internal political divisions generated a prolonged period of instability in Afghanistan. In this respect, the period from 1979 to 1996 should be regarded as not only a phase of regime change but also as a critical period, that transformed Afghanistan’s political structure and shaped the historical background of contemporary regional security dynamics.

title: The Effect of Training Load Regulation Based on Heart Rate Variability Using Wearable Devices on Heart Rate Variability and Estimated Maximal Oxygen Uptake in Weightlifters
title_original: The Effect of Training Load Regulation Based on Heart Rate Variability Using Wearable Devices on Heart Rate Variability and Estimated Maximal Oxygen Uptake in Weightlifters
summary: This study aimed to test the effectiveness of a training program according to regulated training load using heart rate variability readings (HRV) and estimated VO₂max in weightlifters. The researcher employed an experimental design with two equivalent groups (experimental and control) using pre- and post-tests as this method was appropriate for the nature of the problem and the research objectives. The research population included of weightlifters at the Police Sports Club during the 2026 sports season totaling 12 athletes. The research sample comprised 10 athletes choose purposively and randomly assigned to two equivalent groups: five athletes in the experimental group and five in the control group. Two athletes were used for a pilot study. The research instruments included a Polar H10 device and the Kubios HRV software for measuring heart rate variabilit, as well as a 12-minute Cooper test for estimating VO₂max. The main trial lasted for eight weeks, comprising 24 training sessions. The experimental group adjusted their training load based on heart rate variability readings while the control group continued with the traditional training program. Statistical analysis using SPSS demonstrated improvements in both heart rate variability (from 34.80 to 48.60 ms) and the estimated maximum oxygen consumption (from 45.72 to 52.18 ml/kg/min) in the experimental group demonstrating statistically significant superiority over the control group (38.10 ms and 47.80 ml/kg/min, respectively) in the post-tests. The researcher determined that adjusting training load based on heart rate variability readings using wearable devices is an effective method for developing recovery, functional adaptation and the development of important physiological indicators in weightlifters.

title: Technical-tactical indicators associated with winning in elite amateur boxing: A matched-pair analysis
title_original: Technical-tactical indicators associated with winning in elite amateur boxing: A matched-pair analysis
summary: Identifying technical-tactical indicators associated with winning in elite amateur boxing remains challenging because each bout contains a naturally dependent winner-loser pair. Using a matched-pair notational design, we analysed 108 international elite amateur bouts (216 boxer observations) from 2019 to 2025 based on official competition videos and official results. Coded indicators were total punches thrown, punches landed, punching accuracy, successful counterattacks, defensive success rate, ring-centre control and warnings. Winner-loser differences were assessed with paired tests, and independent associations with winning were examined using conditional logistic regression stratified by bout ID, followed by 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation. Compared with losers, winners showed higher punching accuracy (30.41 ± 5.87% vs 26.84 ± 5.79%; mean difference 3.57%, 95% CI 2.10 to 5.05; p < 0.001), more successful counterattacks, higher defensive success rate and higher ring-centre control. In the matched-pair multivariable model, punching accuracy (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.43), defensive success rate (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.30), ring-centre control (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.13) and total punches thrown (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.09) were independently associated with winning, whereas successful counterattacks were not independently significant after adjustment. The model showed strong internally described discrimination (AUC 0.95, 95% CI 0.91 to 0.98; bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.93) and acceptable prediction error (Brier score 0.09; bootstrap-corrected Brier score 0.11). These findings suggest that winning in elite amateur boxing is associated with an integrated profile combining scoring efficiency, defensive quality, spatial control and sustained offensive output.

title: Heat stress reveals divergent pollen viability responses across species and populations of monkeyflower
title_original: Heat stress reveals divergent pollen viability responses across species and populations of monkeyflower
summary: Abstract Premise Rising temperatures can reduce plant reproductive success by disrupting pollen development, yet little is known about how reproductive heat sensitivity varies among natural populations. We evaluated pollen viability responses to elevated temperature in two closely related taxa of yellow monkeyflowers across multiple geographic scales to determine whether heat sensitivity varies among species, between populations and across elevations. Methods We conducted three common garden growth chamber experiments. First, we compared pollen viability responses to heat stress between Mimulus guttatus and members of the M. tilingii species complex. Second, we tested whether broad elevational categories explained variation in heat responses. Third, we evaluated heat sensitivity among nine eastern Sierra Nevada populations of M. guttatus spanning an elevational gradient. Pollen viability was assessed following exposure to control and heat treatments. Key results Heat exposure reduced pollen viability in all experiments. In the species comparison experiment, pollen viability decreased more strongly in the high-elevation restricted M. tilingii species complex than the widespread M. guttatus . We found substantial population-level variation in pollen viability within M. guttatus but not members of the M. tilingii complex. Broad elevational categories did not explain this variation in pollen viability responses. However, within eastern Sierra Nevada populations, reductions in pollen viability became stronger with increasing source elevation. Several populations deviated from this trend, indicating reproductive responses to heat cannot be explained by elevation alone. Conclusions Pollen heat sensitivity varies substantially among species and populations of yellow monkeyflowers. Elevation alone is insufficient to predict pollen viability responses to elevated temperatures, suggesting that local adaptation or genetic variation may contribute to reproductive heat tolerance. Some populations of M. guttatus may contain greater capacity to maintain reproductive function under future warming, highlighting the importance of considering intraspecific variation when predicting plant responses to climate change.

title: IMPACT OF PLYOMETRIC TRAINING AND STATIC STRETCHING IN FEMALE ADOLESCENT HANDBALL PLAYERS BY USING SARGENT JUMP TEST: AN EXPERIMENTAL STUDY
title_original: IMPACT OF PLYOMETRIC TRAINING AND STATIC STRETCHING IN FEMALE ADOLESCENT HANDBALL PLAYERS BY USING SARGENT JUMP TEST: AN EXPERIMENTAL STUDY
summary: Introduction: Handball is a high-intensity sport requiring explosive lower-limb power for jumping, sprinting, and rapid directional changes.Stretching and plyometric exercises are commonly incorporated into training programs; however, evidence comparing the effects of static stretching and plyometric training on vertical jump performance in female adolescent handball players is limited.Aim: To compare the effects of plyometric training and static stretching on vertical jump performance in female adolescent handball players using the Sargent Jump Test.Method: An experimental study was conducted on 40 female adolescent handball players aged 15-17 years, selected through convenient sampling.Participants were randomly divided into two groups: Group A (Static Stretching, n=20) and Group B (Plyometric Training, n=20).Both groups underwent their respective intervention protocols for 3 weeks (4 sessions per week) following a standardized warm-up.Vertical jump performance was assessed using the Sargent Jump Test before and after the intervention period.Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 20, with significance set at p < 0.05.Result: Both groups demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in Sargent Jump Test performance following the intervention (p < 0.05).The plyometric training group showed a greater mean improvement compared to the static stretching group.However, between-group comparison revealed no statistically significant difference in post-intervention jump performance.

title: Detection of previous knee injuries using lower limb‐worn inertial measurement units: A cross‐sectional machine‐learning study
title_original: Detection of previous knee injuries using lower limb‐worn inertial measurement units: A cross‐sectional machine‐learning study
summary: PURPOSE: Previous knee injury increases the risk of subsequent injury, even after functional recovery, yet residual gait, running or load alterations often go undetected in routine assessment. Wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) may enable scalable detection of such alterations outside laboratory settings. The primary aim of this study was to determine whether IMU-derived gait and running features can distinguish physically active individuals with a history of knee injury from uninjured controls using machine learning. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 108 sports science students completed injury-history questionnaires and a walking-running-walking protocol on a 400 m track while wearing four IMUs. Of 90 participants with complete data, 23 reported prior knee injury and 67 were uninjured controls. Left- and right-side sensor data were combined into one per-participant feature vector. The model classified any prior knee injury (yes/no), not limb-specific injury. From 220 candidate features covering baseline gait, post-run changes, walk-to-run transitions, inter-limb asymmetry, variability and composite indices-a fixed pipeline (e.g., median imputation, mutual-information selection) was applied within leave-one-out cross-validation (primary) and repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (secondary). RESULTS: Leave-one-out cross-validation correctly classified 76/90 participants (65/67 true negatives, 11/23 true positives), yielding an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.74, balanced accuracy of 0.72, sensitivity of 0.48, specificity of 0.97, positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.85 and negative predictive value of 0.84. Five-fold cross-validation produced more variable estimates, indicating substantial model instability across resampling partitions. CONCLUSIONS: As a proof of concept, IMU-derived features distinguished individuals with previous knee injury at high specificity but limited sensitivity. High specificity and PPV depend on the classification threshold and injury prevalence in this selected sample, not intrinsic model properties. Because predictors were not aligned to the injured side, findings cannot be interpreted biomechanically. Potential applications (e.g., targeted monitoring) require prospective external validation. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II.

title: Comparison of Wingate Anaerobic Test (WAnT) and Running-based Anaerobic Sprint Test (RAST) in Combat Athletes: A Reliability and Validity Study
title_original: Comparison of Wingate Anaerobic Test (WAnT) and Running-based Anaerobic Sprint Test (RAST) in Combat Athletes: A Reliability and Validity Study
summary: This study compared outcomes from the Wingate Anaerobic Test (WAnT) and the Running-based Anaerobic Sprint Test (RAST) and evaluated the test-retest reliability of both protocols in taekwondo and kickboxing athletes. Fifteen active athletes (taekwondo, n = 7; kickboxing, n = 8) participated in the study. The WAnT was conducted under laboratory conditions, while the RAST was administered as a field-based assessment. Peak power (PP), average power (AP), minimum power (MP), fatigue in-dex (FI), and total exercise duration (TED) were recorded. Between-group differences were analyzed using the Mann–Whitney U test, and differences between test outcomes were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Relationships among variables were examined using Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient, and test-retest reliability was determined using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). Significant differences were observed between WAnT and RAST for PP, AP, PP·kg⁻¹, AP·kg⁻¹, FI, and TED (p < 0.05), while MP and MP·kg⁻¹ did not differ significantly (p > 0.05). Very strong, highly positive correlations were found for relative PP, AP, and MP. In contrast, FI demonstrated a low, non-significant correlation. Test-retest analyses indicated excellent reliability for all absolute and relative power variables in both protocols, except for WAnT MP, which showed moderate reliability, and FI, which exhibited lower reliability in both tests. RAST is a reproducible and practically useful field-based test for assessing general anaerobic performance in taekwondo and kickboxing athletes, demonstrating good concurrent validity relative to WAnT for most power-related variables. However, as the two tests produced different absolute values for several outcomes, RAST should not be considered a direct substitute for WAnT. FI values should be interpreted with caution due to weaker between-test associations and lower reliability. RAST is recommended as a practical field-based option, but direct comparisons with WAnT values should be avoided.

title: Comparison of changes in estimated VO₂max following fartlek and continuous running training in adolescent pencak silat practitioners
title_original: Comparison of changes in estimated VO₂max following fartlek and continuous running training in adolescent pencak silat practitioners
summary: Background: Cardiorespiratory endurance is an important component of performance in pencak silat because competition requires athletes to sustain high-intensity activity across repeated bouts interspersed with recovery periods. However, evidence comparing changes in aerobic capacity following fartlek and continuous running training among adolescent pencak silat practitioners remains limited.Objective: This study aimed to compare changes in estimated VO₂max following fartlek and continuous running training among students participating in a pencak silat extracurricular program.Methods: A two-group pretest–posttest design was used involving 24 students from SMP Darul Ikhlas Cikarang. Participants were selected using total sampling and were equally allocated to a fartlek group (n = 12) and a continuous running group (n = 12) through ordinal pairing. Estimated VO₂max was assessed using the 20-m Multistage Fitness Test before and after the training program. Data were analyzed using assumption tests, paired-samples t-tests to evaluate within-group changes, and an independent-samples t-test to compare changes between groups at a significance level of 0.05.Results: Estimated VO₂max in the fartlek group increased from 33.48 to 40.10, while the continuous running group increased from 33.20 to 38.50. Both groups showed significant improvements; however, no significant difference was found in the change in estimated VO₂max between the fartlek and continuous running groups (t = 0.693, df = 22).Conclusion: These findings indicate that both training programs were associated with improvements in estimated VO₂max, but the study did not provide evidence that one method produced a greater improvement than the other.

title: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
title_original: Sports Policy and National Development: A Comparative Study of India & China
summary: Sports, we now know, are not just a form of entertainment or physical activity; they are also linked to health, education, social inclusion, economic development, youth empowerment and the global identity of a country. Sports are a major part of India and China's national development agendas, yet the sports policies of India and China have a different structure, priority and approach. China has achieved a lot of success in elite competitive sports with a centralized and goal-oriented system. In recent years, India has focused more on the mass movement of sports, talent identification and sports infrastructure, the participation of women and differently-abled athletes, and international excellence. The Khelo Bharat Niti-2025 has been introduced by India on 10 July 2025. It is aimed at a more inclusive sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the Olympic stage. It is all about talent identification, sports science, sports medicine, sports infrastructure, social inclusion and sports as a career. Sports policy is in its first phase in China now with a vision of becoming a "Sports power" nation. China's "Plan for Building a Sports Power during the 15th Five-Year Period," published in 2026, focuses on public health, sports competition quality, sports governance and the development of the sports sector. In this research paper we compare the sports policies of both countries in terms of similarities, differences and achievements, and potential lessons for India.

title: Banking governance of external AML evidence: UK ownership, crypto benchmarking and temporal signals
title_original: Banking governance of external AML evidence: UK ownership, crypto benchmarking and temporal signals
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstract Banks rely on ownership, transaction, and institutional information to support anti-money-laundering decision-making, yet these sources differ in decision proximity, uncertainty, and evidentiary strength. This multi-study article evaluates three external anti-money-laundering signals within a decision-governance framework emphasizing provenance, auditability, and bounded interpretation. Study 1 examines United Kingdom Persons with Significant Control records as ownership-verification workload signals. Of 6.2 million active companies, 745,200 (12.0%) met at least one verification-priority rule. Among flagged companies, 58.3% were assigned to multi-layered control structures, 25.0% to non-United Kingdom or foreign-linked controllers, 11.2% to high officer/controller turnover, and 5.5% to circular ownership patterns. Study 2 compares extreme gradient boosting, graph convolutional networks, Graph Sample and Aggregate, and graph attention networks on the Elliptic transaction-network benchmark. Graph attention networks recorded the highest point estimates (AUROC = 0.960; AUPRC = 0.740), followed by Graph Sample and Aggregate (0.930; 0.610), graph convolutional networks (0.910; 0.560), and extreme gradient boosting (0.820; 0.370). Study 3 identifies a reported −6.8% posterior mean deviation in the Persons with Significant Control Anomaly Index after the late-June 2020 filing-regime boundary (95% credible interval: −10.9% to −2.4%), interpreted descriptively rather than causally. Overall, the findings establish an evidentiary hierarchy for governing heterogeneous anti-money-laundering signals while preserving boundaries between decision support, adjudication, and causal inference. The empirical objects are companies, transaction nodes, and register observations rather than banks.

title: Masterclass: Running-related injuries — bringing evidence together for clinical decision-making
title_original: Masterclass: Running-related injuries — bringing evidence together for clinical decision-making
summary: Running is one of the most accessible and widely practised forms of physical activity promoting multiple health benefits. However, running-related injuries (RRI) are common. In novice runners, the incidence is estimated as 17.8 (95% CI 16.7 to 19.1) injuries per 1000 running hours. In contrast, in recreational runners it is approximately 7.7 (95% CI 6.9 to 8.7) injuries per 1000 running hours. RRIs have significant individual, physical, social, and economic consequences, including moderate pain, withdrawal from running training, increased use of medical resources (e.g., healthcare consultations), productivity loss (e.g., absenteeism from work), costs, and dropout from running practice altogether. Misconceptions and misinterpretations regarding RRI epidemiology, risk factors, prognosis, management and prevention may arise and be propagated within the running community. Together, these misconceptions contribute to misinformation for runners and clinicians, potentially hindering evidence-based decision making. This masterclass aims to provide a clinically relevant, evidence-based overview of topics related to RRIs (including epidemiology, risk factors, prognosis, prevention and management), while critically addressing common assumptions in clinical decision-making and highlighting priorities for future research.

title: NSAID use as a shared decision-making variable in musculoskeletal rehabilitation and strength and conditioning: a perspective
title_original: NSAID use as a shared decision-making variable in musculoskeletal rehabilitation and strength and conditioning: a perspective
summary: Pain relief is often considered a key indicator of musculoskeletal rehabilitation and load progression in physical training. However, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can alter pain perception and symptom expression, posing new interpretive challenges to symptom-based clinical judgment. During NSAID use, decreased pain and improved training completion do not necessarily indicate a synchronous recovery of tissue load tolerance. Adjusting load solely based on immediate symptom changes may lead to an overestimation of rehabilitation progress. This article explores the potential impact of NSAID use on rehabilitation decisions from the perspectives of symptom interpretation and load management. Pharmacological status should be considered a crucial variable influencing clinical reasoning, rather than merely background information in the medical history. Based on the shared decision-making principle, this article proposes the DICE framework (Document, Interpret, Coordinate, Educate), which integrates NSAID-related information into rehabilitation and load-management decisions by standardizing medication information recording, interpreting symptom changes in conjunction with medication context, promoting multidisciplinary team collaboration, and strengthening medication education. This framework is intended to support more consistent symptom interpretation, more informed load progression decisions, and improved communication within rehabilitation teams. This article argues that NSAID use should be incorporated into a dynamic assessment system for rehabilitation and training decisions to more accurately differentiate changes in symptom control, functional recovery, and load tolerance, thereby supporting safer, more transparent, and patient-centered rehabilitation practices.

title: Football in the Byelorussian SRR in the Light of the Newspaper “Fizkulturnik Byelorussii” in the 1950s–1980s
title_original: Football in the Byelorussian SRR in the Light of the Newspaper “Fizkulturnik Byelorussii” in the 1950s–1980s
summary: Zgodnie z doktryną ideologiczną ZSRR sport miał służyć promocji osiągnięć ustroju socjalistycznego i radzieckiego modelu wychowania fizycznego zarówno na arenie międzynarodowej, jak i w obrębie Związku. Źródłami informacji były specjalistyczne wydawnictwa sportowe, działy sportowe w czasopismach i gazetach społeczno-politycznych, radio i telewizja, gdzie regularnie nadawano różnego rodzaju reportaże, felietony i wiadomości sportowe. Głównym wydawnictwem sportowym Białoruskiej Republiki był „Fizkulturnik Białorusii”. Opierając się na materiałach opublikowanych w gazecie, w opracowaniu przedstawiono analizę białoruskiej prasy radzieckiej jako źródła historii lokalnej piłki nożnej. Obejmuje ona okres od początku lat 50., kiedy powstała gazeta, a radzieccy sportowcy stali się stałymi uczestnikami wszystkich międzynarodowych zawodów, do końca lat 80., kiedy w warunkach polityki “Pieriestrojki” („Przebudowy”) i “Głasnosti” („Jawności”) środki masowego przekazu przeszły od radzieckiego paradygmatu intelektualnego do tematów skierowanych do masowego odbiorcy. W artykule przeanalizowano źródła pisane i wizualne dotyczące historii piłki nożnej w Białoruskiej SRR, publikowane w gazecie “Fizkulturnik Białorusii”, a także prześledzono tematy, które były najintensywniej poruszane na łamach czasopisma w latach 50. i 80. XX wieku.

title: ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ ОЗДОРОВЧОЇ РУХОВОЇ АКТИВНОСТІ В СИСТЕМІ АДАПТИВНОГО ФІЗИЧНОГО ВИХОВАННЯ БАСКЕТБОЛІСТІВ 14-15 РОКІВ ДЛЯ РОЗВИТКУ СПЕЦІАЛЬНОЇ ВИТРИВАЛОСТІ
title_original: ЗАСТОСУВАННЯ ОЗДОРОВЧОЇ РУХОВОЇ АКТИВНОСТІ В СИСТЕМІ АДАПТИВНОГО ФІЗИЧНОГО ВИХОВАННЯ БАСКЕТБОЛІСТІВ 14-15 РОКІВ ДЛЯ РОЗВИТКУ СПЕЦІАЛЬНОЇ ВИТРИВАЛОСТІ
summary: The article substantiates the effectiveness of applying health-oriented motor activity within the system of adaptive physical education for the development of special endurance in basketball players aged 14-15 years. In the context of this study, the term adaptive physical education is interpreted not in its traditional sense related to persons with disabilities, but as a system of adapting physical loads to the age-related, functional, and individual characteristics of healthy adolescent athletes. This approach is based on the variable selection of training methods and means, individualized physical loads, their rational dosage, and the prevention of overfatigue, thereby ensuring the safe development of physical qualities, improving functional capabilities, and increasing the effectiveness of the educational and training process. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing demands of modern basketball for a high level of functional fitness and the necessity of considering the morphofunctional characteristics of adolescents during the period of intensive growth and development. Scientific evidence indicates that the age of 14-15 years is characterized by significant changes in the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems, which require scientifically grounded regulation of training loads and the implementation of health-oriented approaches to physical training. The purpose of the study was to substantiate and experimentally verify the effectiveness of health-oriented motor activity within the system of adaptive physical education for improving the special endurance of young basketball players. The research methods included the analysis and synthesis of scientific literature, pedagogical observation, a pedagogical experiment, assessment of physical performance using the PWC170 test, evaluation of cardiovascular functional indicators, and methods of mathematical statistics. The proposed training program combined aerobic, aerobic-anaerobic, functional, and game-based exercises. The program included continuous and variable running, interval sprints, ball-handling drills, defensive movement exercises, bodyweight functional exercises, circuit training, and modified 3×3 and 4×4 basketball games on a reduced-size court. Particular attention was paid to the individualization of physical loads according to the athletes’ level of physical development, functional state, and adaptive capacity, which contributed to improving endurance while preventing excessive fatigue and reducing the risk of injuries. The results of the pedagogical experiment confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. After the implementation of the program, significant improvements were observed in the absolute and relative PWC170 indices, prolonged exercise duration until reaching a heart rate of 170 beats·min⁻¹, and a reduction in heart rate during standardized exercise. These findings indicate enhanced aerobic capacity, improved efficiency of the cardiovascular system, increased adaptive capacity, and a higher level of special endurance in basketball players aged 14-15 years. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the development and experimental substantiation of a comprehensive methodology for improving special endurance through the integration of health-oriented motor activity with individualized training loads. The practical significance of the research is determined by the possibility of implementing the proposed methodology in youth sports schools and basketball clubs for athletes aged 14-15 years in order to improve functional fitness, preserve health, and increase the effectiveness of the long-term training process.

title: INTELLECTUAL METHOD FOR CLASSIFICATION OF GYMNASTICS ELEMENTS IMAGES
title_original: INTELLECTUAL METHOD FOR CLASSIFICATION OF GYMNASTICS ELEMENTS IMAGES
summary: Context. Automated analysis of sports movements is an important area of modern intelligent computer systems and sports science. In gymnastics, assessing the quality of a performance depends largely on subjective judgment, which limits the accuracy and reproducibility of results. The use of image analysis and artificial intelligence methods opens up the possibility of creating automated systems for recognizing gymnastic elements, but the high dimensionality of visual data complicates the practical implementation of such solutions. This necessitates the search for approaches that increase accuracy and reduce computational complexity.Objective. The purpose of the work is to determine the impact of using the method of main components in combination with deep neural networks on the accuracy, speed and generalization ability of models for classifying gymnastic elements by images.Method. The paper uses an approach that combines the preliminary reduction of the dimensionality of images by the method of main components and subsequent classification using neural networks of different architectures. The study was performed on a set of images of gymnastic elements with preliminary normalization and unification of data. A comparative experimental analysis of models with full and reduced dimensionality of the input space was carried out.Results. The results obtained show that the reduction of dimensionality allows to significantly reduce the computational complexity of models without a significant loss of classification quality. It has been established that the combination of the principal component method with a fully connected neural network provides accuracy comparable to resource-intensive convolutional architectures with significantly lower requirements for computing resources. An optimal balance between preserving the information content of data and noise filtering has been revealed.Conclusions. The scientific novelty of the work lies in the complex experimental substantiation of the effectiveness of the hybrid approach to the classification of gymnastic elements in the compressed feature space. The practical significance of the results lies in the possibility of creating compact and high-speed systems for automated analysis of sports movements, suitable for use in mobile and embedded applications. further work in this direction

title: The Japanese diet of 1975 and health promotion: What can we learn from Japan?
title_original: The Japanese diet of 1975 and health promotion: What can we learn from Japan?
summary: Japan has one of the longest life expectancies in the world, which is often attributed to the Japanese diet. While this diet is likely to have contributed to increased life expectancy in the past, the growing popularity of Western food may now be leading to an increase in lifestyle-related diseases in Japan. Evidence from animal and human studies suggests that the Japanese diet in 1975 was healthier and more beneficial for life expectancy than the typical Japanese diet today. Key ingredients in the 1975 Japanese diet that appear to have health benefits include fish, fruit, vegetables, seaweed, soybean products, dashi soup stock, fermented seasonings and green tea. Other distinguishing features of this diet include the 'ichijū-sansai' dining style, which involves a wide variety of ingredients and low intake of sugary beverages. Main nutrient intake in Japan was almost ideal in the 1970s, except for high salt and low calcium intake. Further exploration, development and promotion of the Japanese diet of 1975 is of worldwide interest, as it is a way to maintain good health and delay ageing.

title: Effect of low-intensity blood flow restriction combined with high-intensity resistance training on lower limb strength and stroke effect of table tennis players
title_original: Effect of low-intensity blood flow restriction combined with high-intensity resistance training on lower limb strength and stroke effect of table tennis players
summary: This study aimed to investigate the effects of different strength training protocols on lower limb strength and stroke effect in table tennis players. A single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) design was employed. A total of 30 table tennis players were recruited and randomly assigned into three groups: the low-intensity blood flow restriction training (LI-BFRT) group, high-intensity resistance training (HI-RT) group, and combined training (CB-RT) group. All participants completed an 8-week strength training intervention with three sessions per week. Key indicators including knee peak torque, squat jump (SJ) height, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, peak rate of force development (PRFD), and stroke effect were measured before and after the intervention. No significant differences in all baseline indicators were observed among the three groups (p > 0.05). After the intervention, the CB-RT group exhibited extremely significant improvements in knee flexion and extension peak torques, SJ and CMJ heights, PRFD, and stroke effect (p < 0.01). In the LI-BFRT group, left knee extension PT was extremely significantly improved (p < 0.01); Meanwhile SJ height, PRFD, and forehand topspin loop effect were all significantly enhanced (p < 0.05). In the HI-RT group, left knee extension PT was extremely significantly increased (p < 0.01); Meanwhile, left knee flexion PT, right knee flexion and extension peak torques, CMJ height, PRFD, and forehand backspin loop effect were all significantly improved (p < 0.05). The results indicate that compared with single LI-BFRT or HI-RT, CB-RT exhibited a greater improvement trend in lower limb strength and stroke effect among table tennis players.

title: Photovoltaic‐Integrated Textiles in Buildings: Materials, Integration Strategies and Applications
title_original: Photovoltaic‐Integrated Textiles in Buildings: Materials, Integration Strategies and Applications
summary: Abstract Photovoltaic‐integrated textiles (PV textiles) are emerging lightweight multifunctional building skins that combine architectural textile systems with on‐site renewable energy generation. This paper reviews current PV‐textile development and examines three main integration strategies between flexible photovoltaics (FPV) and architectural technical textiles: direct deposition, lamination‐based stacking, and weaving or embedding. Based on representative built projects and experimental prototypes, three application paradigms are identified: primary structural envelopes, adaptive secondary skins, and temporary deployable systems. Each paradigm presents different trade‐offs in energy efficiency, durability, flexibility, and environmental performance. Despite recent progress, broader architectural application remains limited by insufficient long‐term durability data, the lack of PV textile standards, and the mismatch between manufacturing processes and building lifecycle requirements. The study highlights the need for performance‐driven co‐design, application‐specific certification frameworks, and design‐for‐disassembly strategies to enable reliable and scalable architectural adoption.

title: The Politicization of Soviet–Icelandic Sport Relations before the 1980 Moscow Olympics
title_original: The Politicization of Soviet–Icelandic Sport Relations before the 1980 Moscow Olympics
summary: This chapter examines the politicization of Soviet–Icelandic sport relations prior to the 1980 Moscow Olympic Games, focusing on the bilateral sport agreement signed in 1978. It argues that the Soviet initiative formed part of a broader nation-branding strategy linked to the Olympics and the cultural Cold War, through which sport functioned as a tool of soft power. The chapter also analyses the domestic impact of the agreement, highlighting tensions between the Icelandic government and the national sport movement. Despite their formal autonomy, Icelandic sport organizations were excluded from the negotiation process, prompting criticism and raising questions about the relationship between state authorities and non-governmental actors. Finally, the chapter considers whether the agreement influenced Iceland’s decision to participate in the Moscow Olympics despite international boycott pressures. Although no direct link can be established, the case illustrates how a small state navigated geopolitical tensions during the Cold War and underscores the political significance of sport in international relations.

title: The Umbra Pavilion : A lightweight shading structure composed of Heliotextile and a cable net
title_original: The Umbra Pavilion : A lightweight shading structure composed of Heliotextile and a cable net
summary: Abstract This paper presents the design and construction process of the Umbra Pavilion , a lightweight textile shading structure designed in collaboration with the municipality of Arnhem (The Netherlands). The pavilion is first presented at the Dutch Design Week 2025 in Eindhoven (The Netherlands). The textile parts of the structure are made of Heliotextile, an architectural textile that is currently being developed by Studio Pauline van Dongen and Tentech BV. The pavilion consists of a steel cable net structure, a flexible tensioned steel cable system, which supports the newly developed textile panels. The cable net is supported by three steel columns and is designed to follow a U‐shape. The U‐shape is highlighted by concrete slabs which are used as foundation blocks for the pavilion. The cable net is the primary load‐bearing structure of the pavilion. Therefore, assembly begins with installing the cable net, after which the Heliotextile panels are attached one‐by one to the load‐bearing structure to complete the pavilion. When the structure is loaded due to wind, the Heliotextile panels will transfer the forces to the cable net, which will transfer them to the foundation. The development of the Umbra Pavilion encountered some design challenges regarding the desired shape of the pavilion, activating all parts of the foundation, complex steel nodes and the size and shape of the fabric panels. Overcoming these challenges resulted in the first application of Heliotextile at architectural scale.

The cable net is supported by three steel columns and is designed to follow a U‐shape. The U‐shape is highlighted by concrete slabs which are used as foundation blocks for the pavilion. The cable net is the primary load‐bearing structure of the pavilion. Therefore, assembly begins with installing the cable net, after which the Heliotextile panels are attached one‐by one to the load‐bearing structure to complete the pavilion. When the structure is loaded due to wind, the Heliotextile panels will transfer the forces to the cable net, which will transfer them to the foundation. The development of the Umbra Pavilion encountered some design challenges regarding the desired shape of the pavilion, activating all parts of the foundation, complex steel nodes and the size and shape of the fabric panels. Overcoming these challenges resulted in the first application of Heliotextile at architectural scale.

title: Relegation, promotion and the components of scoring in water polo
title_original: Relegation, promotion and the components of scoring in water polo
summary: Relegation, not the championship, decides the outcome of many European water polo leagues: one club has won every recent national title in Italy, Spain and Hungary. We make the relegation decision our object of inference. Serie A1 relegates one club for finishing last and a second through a three-match play-out, and we ask at each stage how much can be known and when. Promoted clubs arrive with no top-flight record, so we also compare four ways of setting their prior. These analyses rest on the first Bayesian hierarchical model of water polo, which splits scoring into even-strength, man-up and penalty components, models opportunities and conversions separately, and lets abilities evolve between seasons. Treating the components as independent proves untenable, since they compete for a common budget of possessions. Fitted to a new dataset of 940 matches, the model identifies the directly relegated club from the ninth round, before the league table does, predicts the play-out field better than the table, and shows the play-out itself to be close to a coin toss. Promoted clubs start below the league on every component except drawing exclusions: knowing a club was promoted improves forecasts; knowing how does not.

title: Shadow Education: Broadening and Deepening Research in the Field
title_original: Shadow Education: Broadening and Deepening Research in the Field
summary: ABSTRACT This Editorial frames a collection of 10 papers on private supplementary tutoring, which is widely known as shadow education. The Editorial has two main starting points. First is a predecessor collection published in the European Journal of Education in 2020; and second is a 2025 publication developed from a UNESCO Policy Forum. The Editorial also places this new collection in the context of wider literature to show advances in both broadening and deepening research on shadow education. Then, looking forward, it presents possible agendas for continuing research across individual, local, national, regional, and global contexts.

title: AVALANCHE RISK MANAGEMENT AT WHISTLER MOUNTAIN UTILIZING STRATEGIC MINDSET AND DE-BIASING STRATEGIES
title_original: AVALANCHE RISK MANAGEMENT AT WHISTLER MOUNTAIN UTILIZING STRATEGIC MINDSET AND DE-BIASING STRATEGIES
summary: With over two million annual skier visits, and an operational season that runs from November to May and switches to an industrial forecasting program in the off-season; Whistler Mountain has one of the largest ski resort avalanche risk management and mitigation programs in North America.High level expectations of avalanche safety within the ski resort while operating in constantly changing complex alpine terrain due to glacial recession and subsequent large rockfalls has created a new operational challenge, due to the reduced relevance of historical avalanche observations.This coupled with the increased frequency of extreme weather events producing large storm cycles with heavy precipitation, fluctuating freezing levels, and strong-to-extreme winds, adds to the creation of persistent weak layers (PWL), often resulting in large avalanches within the ski resort.Further to changing terrain and weather patterns, large turnover in operational staff has created constraints on the program and has influenced timely lift access, the availability of avalanche mitigation resources and influenced avalanche technician experience.As a result, the program has had to significantly adapt to continue to provide safety for staff and guests while maximizing operational efficiencies.Despite these challenges, risk management strategies at Whistler Mountain are constantly evolving, and the program continues to adapt to this dynamic environment through changes in policies and procedures.This paper aims to illustrate one such adaptation, the inclusion of the strategic mindset in daily forecasts which uses inflection points to help de-bias this large avalanche program.This coupled with a daily reflection and debriefing process has helped to improve communication, strengthen mentorship, and create consistency within our large and ever-changing program.

title: Beyond visualization: Elite alpine skiers and coaches’ insights into simulation training
title_original: Beyond visualization: Elite alpine skiers and coaches’ insights into simulation training
summary: In many performance domains, practitioners struggle to accumulate sufficient training under conditions that mimic performance demands. Elite athletes face this challenge while preparing for high-stakes performance. When realistic practice is restricted, performers can turn to simulation training to recreate performance elements without full physical engagement. Action simulation includes the theoretically distinct strategies, imagery and action observation, often applied together in research and practice. In comparison, representative simulation training uses more interactive technologies aiming to provide feedback. Action simulation is extensively used in sport, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Elite alpine skiing provides a compelling case for exploring these mechanisms, combining high physical demands and limited access to competition environments. Using a critical realist thematic analysis of interviews with 16 elite alpine skiers and 8 coaches, we identified patterns in action simulation use and explored plausible causal mechanisms. Three patterns emerged. Action simulations of familiar environments supported embodied recall and tactical planning. Unfamiliar environments prompted more abstract preparation with individual variation. The absence of feedback emerged as a fundamental barrier for motor learning with action simulation in more complex sports. These findings reveal situated contextual familiarity as a critical but underestimated factor that may determine action simulation effectiveness. Drawing on Grounded Cognition and Internal Model theory, we propose three plausible mechanisms shaping these action simulation outcomes. These insights establish design principles emphasizing embodied familiarity and integration into practice for action simulation training. The findings also point toward representative simulation approaches in alpine skiing, for developing course inspection skills.

title: Eating disorders, the female athlete triad and relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) in young athletes: a narrative review of screening and assessment tools
title_original: Eating disorders, the female athlete triad and relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) in young athletes: a narrative review of screening and assessment tools
summary: Background: Disordered eating (DE), the Female Athlete Triad and Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S) are common, consequential and frequently concealed conditions in young athletes, and because restrictive eating and heavy training are normalised in sport their detection depends on appropriate screening rather than reactive diagnosis. Aim: To summarise, compare and critically appraise the screening and assessment tools used to detect DE and eating disorders (ED), low energy availability (LEA), the Triad and RED-S in adolescent and young adult athletes, and to define how these instruments should be combined in practice. Material and methods: Narrative review of 41 open-access publications identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and SPORTDiscus, encompassing narrative and systematic reviews, validation and prevalence studies, and consensus-derived clinical tools relevant to young athletes of both sexes. Results: Generic ED screens (EAT-26, SCOFF, EDI, EDE-Q) dominate practice but were not developed for athletes; athlete-specific tools (BEDA-Q, EDSA, ATHLETE, Physiologic Screening Test) perform better in this population; and LEA/RED-S tools (LEAF-Q, LEAM-Q, RED-S CAT/CAT2, Triad Cumulative Risk Assessment, DEAQ) capture physiological risk. At-risk prevalence is high but tool-dependent: a meta-analysis of 6,118 athletes reported LEA in 44.7%; 64.7% of youth footballers were at Triad/RED-S risk on the LEAF-Q (sensitivity 78%, specificity 90%); and the EDSA showed sensitivity 96% and specificity 80% in males. No validated male-specific ED tool exists and RED-S awareness is low. Conclusions: No single instrument suffices; pairing a validated athlete-specific ED screen with a LEA/RED-S tool, confirming positive screens by clinical interview within a multidisciplinary team, and embedding screening in education is the most defensible approach, particularly for male, younger and non-aesthetic-sport athletes.

title: Monitoreo Fisiológico Basado en Tecnología Wearable en el Período Precompetitivo Mediante Entrenamiento de Precisión en Atletas de Pencak Silat
title_original: Monitoreo Fisiológico Basado en Tecnología Wearable en el Período Precompetitivo Mediante Entrenamiento de Precisión en Atletas de Pencak Silat
summary: Antecedentes: En los deportes de combate como el Pencak Silat, el monitoreo preciso de las respuestas fisiológicas durante el entrenamiento es fundamental para optimizar el rendimiento, prevenir el sobreentrenamiento, mejorar la gestión de la recuperación y aumentar la seguridad de los atletas. Los recientes avances en la tecnología wearable han permitido el monitoreo en tiempo real de parámetros fisiológicos, proporcionando a entrenadores y atletas datos objetivos para respaldar decisiones de entrenamiento basadas en evidencia. Sin embargo, la implementación práctica de la tecnología wearable en el entrenamiento de Pencak Silat sigue siendo un campo poco explorado. Objetivo: Este estudio tuvo como objetivo examinar la implementación del monitoreo fisiológico basado en tecnología wearable para el entrenamiento de precisión en atletas de Pencak Silat mediante la evaluación en tiempo real de la frecuencia cardíaca, la saturación de oxígeno y el estado de recuperación. Métodos: Se empleó un diseño de investigación cualitativa con la participación de 30 estudiantes de la Facultad de Ciencias del Deporte de la Universidad Estatal de Padang que tenían interés en el Pencak Silat. Los participantes fueron seleccionados mediante muestreo intencional y participaron en sesiones de entrenamiento monitoreadas utilizando dispositivos wearables, incluidos relojes inteligentes y rastreadores de actividad física. Los datos se recopilaron mediante observación directa, entrevistas semiestructuradas y documentación de los resultados del monitoreo fisiológico durante las actividades de entrenamiento. Resultados: La frecuencia cardíaca aumentó progresivamente con la intensidad del entrenamiento, mientras que la saturación de oxígeno mostró una ligera disminución durante los ejercicios de alta intensidad, lo que indica una mayor demanda fisiológica y fatiga. El monitoreo de la recuperación reveló que los participantes involucrados en entrenamientos intensivos requirieron períodos más prolongados para regresar a condiciones fisiológicas estables. La tecnología wearable permitió realizar ajustes más precisos en la intensidad del entrenamiento basados en respuestas fisiológicas en tiempo real. Además, los participantes informaron una mayor conciencia de su condición física, nivel de fatiga y preparación para la recuperación. Conclusiones: El monitoreo fisiológico basado en tecnología wearable favorece un entrenamiento de precisión adaptativo, individualizado y fundamentado en la evidencia en el Pencak Silat. A pesar de las limitaciones relacionadas con la comodidad de los dispositivos y la precisión de los sensores durante movimientos dinámicos, el monitoreo wearable demuestra un potencial considerable para mejorar la eficacia del entrenamiento, la seguridad de los atletas y la gestión de la recuperación en entornos de artes marciales

title: Green Regeneration or Green Gentrification? The Effect of Early Information and Residential Support
title_original: Green Regeneration or Green Gentrification? The Effect of Early Information and Residential Support
summary: This study investigates how early information about an urban green regeneration project influences residents' support and residential intentions. Using a scenario-based survey design in order to collect primary data clearly, which involves three different scenarios. The findings indicate that the displacement anxiety arises from the project itself, rather than the information about potential increases in higher rents. By contrast, rising rents serve as a powerful signal of the project's success, reducing uncertainty about whether the urban regeneration project will deliver wider improvements to the local area. On top of that, residents tent to prioritize the comfort of better environment as well as the improvement of social status over the related social cost triggered by regeneration project. These findings illustrate the trade-offs between the benefits and negative consequences of green regeneration. This research advanced the understanding of how early signals shape support and offers practical insights of designing equitable urban regeneration projects.

title: Cyber trends in sport as a new environment for guided human development
title_original: Cyber trends in sport as a new environment for guided human development
summary: Relevance. Cyber trends in sport are considered as a manifestation of an anthropotechnological shift in which sports activity is organised within a single circuit of interaction between the brain, the body, the digital environment and management systems. Digitalisation develops along two lines: as a means of managing preparation, monitoring the functional state and analysing competitive activity, and as a source of new lines of practice – virtual and simulated disciplines, esports, phygital and operator disciplines, as well as adaptive and rehabilitation applications of digital technologies. Objective. To examine cyber trends in sport as digital and hybrid environments for guided human development, to identify the main types of cyber-sport practices, to describe the types of activity subject they actualise, and to define the tasks of medical-biological and psychophysiological support. Methods. A conceptual comparative review of the Olympic line of virtual and simulated disciplines, esports, phygital and operator disciplines, and adaptive and rehabilitation applications of digital technologies. It employs analysis of literature on sports psychophysiology, sports medicine and esports research, analysis of International Olympic Committee documents and Russian regulatory acts, and a comparative analysis of environments by the type of activity subject they form and their functional demands. Results. It is proposed to distinguish virtual sports, simulated sports and esports as different anthropotechnical environments that differ in the structure of bodily action, cognitive and sensorimotor load and the way the result is formed. Traditional sports develop a bodily-motor athlete; digital replicas of classical disciplines – one acting in a virtual or simulation model; esports – a cognitive-interface competitive subject; phygital disciplines – a cyberphysical athlete; and operator disciplines – an athlete-operator working through a technical interface under conditions of high speed and uncertainty. The support of such environments should include assessment of the functional state, cognitive load, stress, sleep, visual fatigue and recovery. Conclusion. Cyber trends reflect a transition from sport as a predominantly bodily-motor practice to a spectrum of digital and hybrid anthropotechnical environments in which the result is determined by a combination of physical, cognitive, sensorimotor and interface components of activity. This potential is realised only with scientifically grounded support: control of load, recovery, sleep and visual fatigue, and prevention of problematic gaming behaviour.
