title: Body image dissatisfaction, anxiety, and lifestyle of college athletes
title_original: Body image dissatisfaction, anxiety, and lifestyle of college athletes
summary: This study aimed to explore the relationship between college athletes' body image dissatisfaction (BID), lifestyle, and anxiety. While lifestyle (LS) and BID have been individually associated with anxiety in the general population, few studies have examined these factors together in college athletes. Understanding their combined impact is vital for creating targeted interventions for this high-risk group. This was an observational, correlational, and cross-sectional study involving 127 university athletes (median age: 20.4 years; IQR: 4.0; 69.3% women). Participants completed 4 questionnaires: FANTASTIC for lifestyle, BSQ for body image (BI), and Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) for anxiety symptoms (AS). All participants provided informed consent. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, correlations among LS, BID, and AS, and a binary logistic regression model. Significance was set at p < 0.05. The results showed that females had greater BI concerns and higher AS than males. Males scored higher on LS [82] than females [78]. Positive correlations were found between anxiety and BID, whereas anxiety was negatively correlated with LS and age. In the logistic regression model, higher anxiety was associated with greater BID, poorer LS, and lower BMI. The findings indicate that higher BID is correlated with increased anxiety, whereas a healthy lifestyle is associated with lower anxiety levels. These results highlight a significant inverse relationship between a healthy lifestyle and anxiety symptoms in young university athletes, even when body image issues are present. This underscores the importance of implementing supportive programs for this group.

title: Enabling and Constraining Factors in Community-Based Inclusive Sports Programs: The Moderating Role of Parental Engagement for Children with Intellectual Disabilities
title_original: Enabling and Constraining Factors in Community-Based Inclusive Sports Programs: The Moderating Role of Parental Engagement for Children with Intellectual Disabilities
summary: Background: The effectiveness of community-based inclusive sports program is shaped by a complex interplay of facilitating and constraining factors. While structural barriers are documented, the moderating role of parental engagement in program outcomes remains underexplored, particularly in Global South educational contexts. Objective: To examine facilitating and constraining factors within a community-based inclusive sports program and to determine how parental engagement functions as a moderating variable in shaping outcomes for children with intellectual disabilities. Methods: A qualitative phenomenological study with embedded deviant case analysis was conducted with fourteen participants (seven teachers, seven parents) at a government-run special education school in Indonesia. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Two subthemes captured the systemic context: (1) a supportive ecosystem comprising institutional leadership, teacher dedication, collaborative teamwork, and external organizational frameworks; and (2) persistent barriers including human resource constraints, facility limitations, inconsistent parental engagement, and tension between inclusive participation and competitive development. Deviant case analysis revealed that low parental involvement, limited program awareness, and absence of home-school reinforcement may attenuate otherwise positive program effects. Conclusion: While institutional support and teacher dedication constitute primary success drivers, parental engagement functions as a critical moderating variable. The findings propose a parental engagement continuum and identify actionable strategies for strengthening the home-school partnership.

title_original: The impact of work pressure on the occupational wellbeing of coaches in grassroots sports schools: a chain mediation effect of emotional intelligence and self-efficacy
summary: Objective: Occupational wellbeing is an important resource to actively promote the development of social work practice. However, how the working pressure affects the occupational wellbeing of coaches in grass-roots sports schools in China has not been fully discussed. The purpose of this study is to investigate the influence of working pressure on the professional wellbeing of coaches in grass-roots sports schools in China, especially the chain intermediary mechanism of emotional intelligence and self-efficacy related to individual coaches. Methods: Using cross-sectional design and structured questionnaire, 518 coaches from grass-roots sports schools in China were investigated. Results: Working pressure can directly and negatively predict the professional wellbeing of coaches in grass-roots sports schools in China, and at the same time, it indirectly shows the relationship with professional wellbeing through three ways. (1) the independent intermediary role of emotional intelligence, (2) the independent intermediary role of self-efficacy, and (3) the chain intermediary role of emotional intelligence and self-efficacy. Conclusion: These findings illustrate that coaches' emotional intelligence and self-efficacy are positive psychological mechanisms to promote professional wellbeing, and highlight their key roles in improving the professional wellbeing of coaches in grass-roots sports schools in China.

title: Ruang Terbuka Hijau dan Luaran Kesehatan Masyarakat: Analisis Data Panel di Provinsi Jawa Barat, Indonesia
title_original: Ruang Terbuka Hijau dan Luaran Kesehatan Masyarakat: Analisis Data Panel di Provinsi Jawa Barat, Indonesia
summary: Luaran kesehatan masyarakat merupakan salah satu indikator keberhasilan pembangunan yang dalam penelitian ini diukur melalui diabetes melitus, stunting, dan kematian neonatal. Provinsi Jawa Barat dipilih sebagai lokasi penelitian karena memiliki karakteristik demografis, sosial-ekonomi, dan spasial yang beragam, sehingga dapat menggambarkan dinamika pembangunan dan kesehatan masyarakat hingga tahun 2024. Penelitian terdahulu mendukung kebijakan RTH (Ruang Terbuka Hijau) dimungkinkan mampu berpotensi meningkatkan kualitas hidup perkotaan dan keberlanjutan lingkungan, serta meningkatkan kualitas luaran kesehatan masyarakat. Penelitian ini menggunakan pedekatan data sekunder, dengan variabel luaran kualitas kesehatan masyarakat diantaranya kematian neonatal, stunting dan diabetes mellitus. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan analisis regresi binomial negatif untuk memeriksa hubungan empiris antara indikator kesehatan masyarakat dan variabel lingkungan di Jawa Barat. Hasil estimasi data panel menunjukkan bahwa ruang terbuka hijau (RTH) memiliki pengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap luaran kesehatan masyarakat. Dengan peningkatan RTH sebesar 1 KM2 ini berkorelasi dengan penurunan insiden diabetes mellitus, kematian neonatal, dan stunting masing-masing sebesar 1%. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa intervensi medis bukan satu-satunya faktor yang mempengaruhi hasil kesehatan masyarakat; pembangunan wilayah dan lingkungan hidup juga berperan. Penemuan penelitian ini menegaskan secara kebijakan dan praktis bahwa pendekatan kebijakan tata ruang, kebijakan fiskal, dan strategi pembangunan ekonomi harus disusun secara bersamaan.

title: Sports activities and people with intellectual disabilities
title_original: Sports activities and people with intellectual disabilities
summary: NASLOV MAGISTRSKEGA DELA: Športne dejavnosti in osebe z motnjo v duševnem razvoju Podpisana izjavljam, da sem avtorica zaključnega dela z naslovom Športne dejavnosti in osebe z motnjo v duševnem razvoju S svojim podpisom zagotavljam, da:je predloženo zaključno delo izključno rezultat mojega lastnega raziskovalnega dela, sem poskrbela, da so dela in mnenja drugih avtorjev oz.avtoric, ki jih uporabljam v predloženem zaključnem delu, navedena oz.citirana v skladu z navodili fakultete, sem poskrbela, da so vsa dela in mnenja drugih avtorjev oz.avtoric navedena v seznamu virov, ki je sestavni element predloženega zaključnega dela in je zapisan v skladu z navodili fakultete, sem pridobila vsa dovoljenja za uporabo avtorskih del, ki so v celoti prenesena v predloženo zaključno delo in sem to tudi jasno zapisal/-a v predloženem zaključnem delu, se zavedam, da je plagiatorstvo -predstavljanje tujih del, bodisi v obliki citata bodisi v obliki skoraj dobesednega parafraziranja bodisi v grafični obliki, s katerim so tuje misli oz.ideje predstavljene kot moje lastne -kaznivo po zakonu (Zakon o avtorskih in sorodnih pravicah (Uradni list RS, št.16/07 -uradno prečiščeno besedilo, 68/08, 110/13 in 56/15), prekršek pa podleže tudi disciplinskim ukrepom UP PEF v skladu z njenimi pravili, se zavedam posledic, ki jih dokazano plagiatorstvo lahko predstavlja za predloženo zaključno delo in za moj status na UP PEF, je zaključno delo lektorirano in urejeno skladno z navodili fakultete.

title: Between love and pain: A qualitative analysis of menstrual distress and romantic relationships
title_original: Between love and pain: A qualitative analysis of menstrual distress and romantic relationships
summary: Menstrual distress - the physiological and emotional stress response to menstrual symptoms that are perceived as threatening and difficult to manage - is common among menstruating people and can have a profound negative impact on mental health and well-being. Romantic partners can support dealing with emotional and physical stress, yet their role in dealing with menstrual distress specifically remains underexplored. Adopting a biopsychosocial perspective, this qualitative study aims to shed light on the experience of menstrual distress within romantic relationships. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 27 individuals (aged 19-59 years, living in Austria), who were in romantic relationships (n = 23 heterosexual, n = 3 homosexual/queer, n = 1 unlabelled) and who self-reported to have experienced menstrual distress. Indeed, romantic partners play a crucial role in shaping both the impact of and coping mechanisms for menstrual distress. Due to the intimate nature of romantic relationships, partners influence experiences of menstrual distress, whether actively engaging with the topic or not. Supportive relationships fostering authenticity, communication and teamwork enhance coping, whereas negative partner responses can perpetuate negative stereotypes, stigma and symptom trivialisation. To enhance individuals' and couples' well-being, educational campaigns should raise menstrual health awareness early, and couples may benefit from guidance in managing the challenges effectively.

title: From play to profession: understanding the professionalization of e-sports athletes from a civilizing process perspective
title_original: From play to profession: understanding the professionalization of e-sports athletes from a civilizing process perspective
summary: Introduction Despite the rapid expansion of the e-sports industry in terms of economic scale, tournament systems, and professional demand, the issues of identity transformation, bodily discipline, emotional management, and their associated alienation during the professionalization of e-sports athletes remain insufficiently discussed. Grounded in Elias’s theory of the civilizing process, this study aims to explore the professionalization process of e-sports athletes as they transition from amateur players to professional competitors, as well as the relationships among social constraints, bodily practices, and emotional internalization within the digital competitive arena. Methods Using historical analysis, case study, and semi-structured interviews, this study takes current and former professional e-sports athletes in China as empirical subjects. Results The study reveals three civilizing mechanisms in the professionalization process of e-sports athletes, namely the institutionalization of identity, the rationalization of bodily discipline, and the internalization of emotional management. The findings indicate that the professional development of e-sports athletes is driven by interdependency networks composed of capital, leagues, clubs, data platforms, and fan communities, with digital technology serving as a mediator to facilitate the transformation from external constraints to individual self-constraint. Discussion The study points out that the professionalization of e-sports also faces dilemmas such as the alienation of bodily discipline, imbalance in power dependency, and lack of health protection. This study proposes that a sustainable support mechanism for the professional development of e-sports athletes should be improved from two aspects, which are a dual-dimensional health protection system encompassing both physical and psychological aspects, and the enhancement of individual subjectivity.

Results The study reveals three civilizing mechanisms in the professionalization process of e-sports athletes, namely the institutionalization of identity, the rationalization of bodily discipline, and the internalization of emotional management. The findings indicate that the professional development of e-sports athletes is driven by interdependency networks composed of capital, leagues, clubs, data platforms, and fan communities, with digital technology serving as a mediator to facilitate the transformation from external constraints to individual self-constraint. Discussion The study points out that the professionalization of e-sports also faces dilemmas such as the alienation of bodily discipline, imbalance in power dependency, and lack of health protection. This study proposes that a sustainable support mechanism for the professional development of e-sports athletes should be improved from two aspects, which are a dual-dimensional health protection system encompassing both physical and psychological aspects, and the enhancement of individual subjectivity.

title: Thirty years of running together: mothers who run with strollers in Runner’s World magazine 1993–2022
title_original: Thirty years of running together: mothers who run with strollers in Runner’s World magazine 1993–2022
summary: The popularity of distance running has increased dramatically since the 1960s and 1970s. Alongside that popularity has been an increased potential for inclusion, with one especially visible cohort being parents who run with their infants or young children in strollers. Focusing on the popular lifestyle magazine Runner’s World over the 30-year period 1993–2022, this article seeks to understand the discursive construction of the stroller-pushing runner-mother. It argues that mothers who align with conventional conceptions of the ‘good mother’, managing their athletic engagement independently while parenting and making no demands on the running community, are valorized by the magazine. However, those who do make demands to inclusion in community events, such as in races or club meetups, are subject to more complex and often negative representations. This article highlights the limits of inclusivity in running communities and the importance of recognizing mothers as a unique cohort in sporting cultures.

title: Listening first: mapping the inner game of an elite women's rugby national team and its staff
title_original: Listening first: mapping the inner game of an elite women's rugby national team and its staff
summary: Introduction: A well-developed intake assessment can identify athletes' and staff members' initial psychological needs and thus lay the foundation for targeted, evidence-based sport psychology interventions. However, empirical descriptions of such needs in elite women's collision-sport settings remain scarce. Methods: In collaboration with the Italian Rugby Federation, the Italian Women's Rugby National Team, and its staff, this study used a mixed-methods intake assessment protocol to identify the priority psychological needs of the team. Qualitative results from 32 athletes and 12 staff members showed cohesion as the primary team need requiring strengthening. Individually, players most frequently requested improvements in self-confidence and emotional regulation. Results: Quantitative findings revealed low self-rated mental health scores among both athletes and women staff members, underscoring the importance of mental health support. Among staff, gender was associated with higher stress (women reported greater stress), and having a dual career, defined as the successful combination of education, training, and/or work with sport, was associated with higher happiness. Discussion: Taken together, these results offer sport psychologists a clear, participant-driven map of the psychological targets to address in elite women's team sports, directly informing the design and evaluation of future tailored interventions.

title: Sports Health Education: Injury Treatment in Karate Training in Pekanbaru City
title_original: Sports Health Education: Injury Treatment in Karate Training in Pekanbaru City
summary: This community service activity aims to improve the knowledge and skills of karate athletes in preventing and treating sports injuries, particularly through education on injury care using the RICE method (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation). The methods used are educational and participatory, including interactive lectures, demonstrations and practical workshops on RICE, discussions and question and answer sessions, and evaluation through interviews. Participants consisted of 29 karate athletes from various clubs in Pekanbaru. The results of the activity showed enthusiasm and active participation from the participants. Based on observations and interviews, there was an increase in understanding of common types of injuries (such as sprains, bruises, muscle strains, and cramps) as well as an increase in psychomotor skills and confidence in performing first aid independently using the RICE principle.

title: Differences in Mental Toughness Among Mixed Martial Artists and Physically Active Individuals
title_original: Differences in Mental Toughness Among Mixed Martial Artists and Physically Active Individuals
summary: Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) is a physiological and psychological demanding sport. While the majority of the literature conducted in MMA regards physiological health and risk of injury, researchers are beginning to assess the psychological profiles of MMA athletes. Previous studies have evaluated mental toughness (MT) within MMA; however, no study has examined MT in MMA athletes at the professional division. Therefore, the primary purpose of this research was to evaluate the difference in mental toughness between professional MMA athletes and physically active individuals. Secondary aims are to evaluate potential variations in mental toughness within the professional level between champion and non-champion athletes, and finally, to determine if a relationship exists between anthropometrics of professional MMA athletes and mental toughness. A total of forty participants (n = 40) were recruited, comprising twenty physically active and twenty professional MMA athletes consisting of champions (n = 8) and non-champions (n = 12) Participants were provided with a letter of information and consent; completion of the survey served as implied consent to participate in the research. These participants were administered the Sports Mental Toughness Questionnaire (SMTQ). The results indicate that professional MMA athletes possess significantly higher levels of GMT and confidence compared to physically active individuals; however, no significant difference in GMT or its subscales were found between champion and non-champions nor any relationship between anthropometrics and MT in professional MMA athletes.

title: The legal battle against lone wolf terrorism: Addressing challenges and implementing solutions
title_original: The legal battle against lone wolf terrorism: Addressing challenges and implementing solutions
summary: Terrorism remains one of the most significant and persistent threats to global security. The challenges it poses are constantly evolving due to changes in the patterns of individual and collective violence. Despite the increasing number of studies and research on collective terrorism, particularly organized terrorist groups, recruitment, and financing, individual acts of terrorism, defined as “lone wolf terrorism” have received relatively little attention. This reveals a gap in the legal understanding and security approach to this issue. This article critically examines lone wolf terrorism, which refers to individuals who carry out terrorist attacks independently or in allegiance to organized terrorist groups. It assesses the classification of their actions and the adequacy of existing legal frameworks that criminalize terrorism in general, or whether they should be treated as ordinary crimes such as violence and unlicensed possession of weapons. The study explores the psychological backgrounds and motivations behind these acts, their drift toward violent extremism, and the ideologies and paths they adopt. It also focuses on the role of technology in facilitating these attacks, carried out independently without affiliation to or support from any formal terrorist organization. The findings reveal shortcomings in current legal frameworks, particularly in addressing this type of extremism, as well as the complexities involved in detecting these crimes due to their clandestine nature and the occasional inability to identify the perpetrators. Significant challenges also exist regarding the effectiveness of counter-terrorism measures, including prosecution and prevention. Finally, this article attempts to offer practical recommendations to policymakers and decision-makers, aiming to foster a more effective legal response through early intervention, appropriate prevention programs, and a balance between public rights and freedoms and national security.

title: Hormonal Cyclicity and Physical Performance - Review of the Literature
title_original: Hormonal Cyclicity and Physical Performance - Review of the Literature
summary: Introduction: The menstrual cycle involves a complex interaction of hormonal fluctuations that can influence various aspects of female athletic performance. Understanding these relationships has become increasingly important for optimizing training programs and supporting female athletes across different competitive levels. Objective: This review synthesizes current evidence on how menstrual cycle phases and hormonal contraception affect physical performance in female athletes. Material and methods: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across major databases including PubMed, Web of Science, and SPORTDiscus, focusing on studies published between 2020 and 2025 that examined menstrual cycle effects on athletic performance. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that menstrual cycle phase effects on performance are generally small and highly individualized. While some athletes do experience performance decrements during specific phases particularly the early follicular and late luteal phases, group-level effects are often minimal or inconsistent. Interestingly, perceptual symptoms and psychological well-being appear to influence performance more consistently than hormonal fluctuations alone. Hormonal contraception shows variable effects depending on type and formulation. Rather than applying universal cycle-based training modifications, we recommend individual monitoring and personalized approaches.

title: Physical Activity and In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Stage-by-Stage Narrative Review
title_original: Physical Activity and In Vitro Fertilization Outcomes: A Stage-by-Stage Narrative Review
summary: Background. Infertility affects approximately 17.5% of the adult population worldwide. Physical activity is promoted as an element of a healthy lifestyle, yet clinical practice still limits it at selected stages of IVF treatment. Aim. The aim of this review is to systematize the current literature on the influence of physical activity of the woman, the man, and the couple on treatment outcomes at the individual stages of IVF. Material and methods. PubMed was searched using two search queries, supplemented with targeted searches. Results. For women, evidence on the pre-treatment phase is heterogeneous, resembling a "reverse J-curve": benefit at moderate activity, no benefit or risk at extremely high levels. Data on stimulation and embryo transfer are more consistent, not supporting routine restriction and suggesting a psychological benefit of continued activity. In men, evidence is consistent, with no adverse effects. Oocyte retrieval, sperm collection, and joint couple activity remain almost unexamined. Conclusions. Available evidence does not justify the routine restriction of physical activity during IVF treatment. A recurring theme is the nonlinear dose–response relationship, indicating a benefit of moderate activity. Further studies with objective measurement of exposure, including those focused on the couple, are needed.

For women, evidence on the pre-treatment phase is heterogeneous, resembling a "reverse J-curve": benefit at moderate activity, no benefit or risk at extremely high levels. Data on stimulation and embryo transfer are more consistent, not supporting routine restriction and suggesting a psychological benefit of continued activity. In men, evidence is consistent, with no adverse effects. Oocyte retrieval, sperm collection, and joint couple activity remain almost unexamined. Conclusions. Available evidence does not justify the routine restriction of physical activity during IVF treatment. A recurring theme is the nonlinear dose–response relationship, indicating a benefit of moderate activity. Further studies with objective measurement of exposure, including those focused on the couple, are needed.

title: Puerto Rican Sporters as Ecotonal Nodes of Connection and Justice
title_original: Puerto Rican Sporters as Ecotonal Nodes of Connection and Justice
summary: Drawing on insights across geography, anthropology, sociology, and sports studies, we examine the connection between outdoor sports, coastal ecotonal environments, and environmental justice in Puerto Rico (PR). Four themes emerged from survey, interview, and ethnographic data: (1) the power and breadth of “sports” as word/category/phenomenon in people’s lives; (2) the reciprocal connection between sensing sporting body/mind/soul and coastal environments; (3) the role of sports in knowing and defending places and regions; and (4) the sports-community connection in environmental and other social justice struggles. This study is novel because of its geographic scope connecting diverse ecotonal regions, and its focus on multiple sports. Conceptualizing the sporting body as an ecotonal node of connection across diverse domains advances sports as a geohumanities lens to further probe human-environment relations, place making and belonging, and the values affirmed by movement in people’s everyday lives. While findings are relevant for cases beyond PR, we highlight the intensifying environmental crises and development pressures on coastal communities by helping connect luchas across PR.

title: Anatomy of a Spreadsheet Failure, Analysing the EuSpRIG Horror Story Corpus
title_original: Anatomy of a Spreadsheet Failure, Analysing the EuSpRIG Horror Story Corpus
summary: Spreadsheet disasters have been documented for more than thirty years, but they have not gone away. This paper examines the EuSpRIG horror stories archive as evidence of how ordinary spreadsheets fail and the consequences that follow. After cleaning and deduplication, 121 incidents from 1995 to 2026 were classified into twelve failure categories and analysed by mechanism, context and consequence. Formula errors, data-entry slips and data-handling mistakes account for 71 cases and recur across the whole period, from Fidelity's missing minus sign in 1995 to a mistyped date that cost Norway's sovereign wealth fund about $92 million in 2024. A second pattern concerns information present in a workbook but not visible to the recipient: hidden rows, hidden sheets, pivot-table caches, embedded objects and retained source layers can cause harm even when no calculation is wrong. The clearest rise in reported cases is in this hidden or embedded data category, whose most serious example is the 2022 Ministry of Defence spreadsheet that exposed details of roughly 18,700 Afghan applicants through hidden rows. The paper argues that spreadsheet risk is no longer only a problem of wrong numbers. It also involves visibility, disclosure, governance and trust. Existing taxonomies remain useful for formula, entry and handling errors, but do not fully capture the public harm caused by spreadsheets used as uncontrolled operational infrastructure. The same mistakes have persisted for three decades, what has changed is the authority organisations give to the spreadsheets that contain them.

title: Skill Profiling with Attributable Reasoning (SPAR): A Wearable Analysis System for Boxing
title_original: Skill Profiling with Attributable Reasoning (SPAR): A Wearable Analysis System for Boxing
summary: A punch is a ballistic, full-body action driven by a kinetic chain running from the legs through the trunk to the arm, where a small sequencing error separates a scoring strike from a miss. Wearable sensors can capture this movement in the gym, but most deployable systems only classify which punch was thrown rather than assess how well it was thrown. We present Skill Profiling with Attributable Reasoning (SPAR), an eight-IMU garment and pressure-insole system that classifies each punch as expert or novice and treats an explanation of that prediction as feedback. Feedback is only useful if the person receiving it can act on it, so SPAR explains the prediction at three tiers, a per-joint attribution for the analyst, a counterfactual over kinetic-chain layers for the coach, and a plain-language narrative of the two for the athlete. Across 17 participants and 4,713 punches, SPAR reaches a leave-one-participant-out AUC of 0.842 (95% CI [0.769, 0.907] over participants). A frozen time-series foundation model encodes the joint-angle and plantar-force series, and a small transformer trained on the cohort classifies the encoding. We audit the two quantitative tiers and report six themes from a thematic analysis of interviews with six practicing boxing coaches.

title: Beyond Goodwill: Eight Arguments for Mandatory Foundational Training for Volunteer Coaches
title_original: Beyond Goodwill: Eight Arguments for Mandatory Foundational Training for Volunteer Coaches
summary: Although volunteer coaches comprise a substantial proportion of the coaching workforce, estimated to exceed 100 million worldwide, many lack formal preparation aligned with contemporary standards of athlete development, safeguarding, and ethical practice. In an increasingly complex and regulated sports environment, reliance on informal and non-formal learning is insufficient to ensure athlete welfare, professional standards, and organizational accountability. By situating volunteer coaching alongside other professions that require standardized preparation and oversight, we address persistent inconsistencies in public protection and professional expectations. Drawing on international evidence and current coaching data, we present eight research-informed arguments in support of a compulsory education framework. Coordinated, government-guided programs and certifications are necessary to reinforce safeguarding structures, elevate professional expectations, and strengthen public trust in sport. In this paper, the mandatory foundational training is presented as a feasible and accessible professional intervention that can reduce preventable harm while enhancing coaching effectiveness.

title: Propositional and imagistic incongruity: a dual-route cognitive account of humor processing
title_original: Propositional and imagistic incongruity: a dual-route cognitive account of humor processing
summary: This paper develops a theoretical account of humor processing in terms of two interacting routes of cognitive processing. Building on the distinction between propositional and imagistic modes of language comprehension, it argues that humorous incongruity may arise through conceptual, perceptual, or cross-representational discrepancies. The propositional route involves relatively abstract and amodal representations, in which humor emerges from a mismatch between conceptual expectations and asserted or implied meanings. The imagistic route involves mental imagery, perceptual simulation, and sensorimotor representation, in which humor emerges from discrepancies between expected and activated perceptual or multimodal representations. In addition, the paper proposes that humorous effects may arise through between-route incongruity, where propositional and imagistic representations conflict, as in cases where verbal content and gesture, visual imagery, or embodied cues convey incompatible meanings. This dual-route account is not intended to replace existing theories of humor, but to specify a processing-level distinction that clarifies how incongruity is represented and resolved across verbal, visual, and multimodal forms of humor. By linking humor processing to conceptual processing, mental imagery, and embodied cognition, the account provides a framework for explaining why formally similar humorous expressions may differ in cognitive demands, perceptual salience, and affective impact. The paper concludes by outlining implications for future behavioral, cognitive, and multimodal research on humor processing.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Intellectual Disability: Indian Innovations for Inclusive Policy and Practice
title_original: Artificial Intelligence in Intellectual Disability: Indian Innovations for Inclusive Policy and Practice
summary: Introduction: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a transformative force in healthcare, education, and rehabilitation, offering new possibilities for persons with intellectual disability (PwID) in India. This study situates AI within the broader context of disability care, highlighting the challenges of stigma, limited infrastructure, and shortage of trained professionals. Aims and Objectives: The primary aim is to examine how AI can enhance assessment, intervention, and inclusion for persons with PwID in India. Specific objectives include mapping global and Indian applications of AI, analyzing policy and institutional framew4orks, and identifying ethical, cultural, and psychological considerations. Method: A conceptual and comparative framework was adopted, integrating clinical, cultural, and technological perspectives. The study draws on global case studies, Indian policy documents, institutional reports, and anecdotal evidence from clinical and educational settings to provide a comprehensive analysis. Results: Findings reveal that AI is increasingly applied in clinical diagnosis, personalized education, vocational training, and assistive communication tools. In India, institutions such as AIISH, NIMHANS, and NIEPID are pioneering AI-based interventions, though challenges remain in infrastructure, accessibility, and workforce training. Comparative insights show that while India is progressing, global benchmarks highlight the need for stronger ethical safeguards and culturally sensitive design. Conclusion: AI holds significant promise for inclusive development in India, but its integration must be guided by ethical princ0iples, cultural sensitivity, and systemic readiness. The study underscores the importance of collaboration among academia, industry, and government to ensure equitable outcomes. Implications: The research has implications for policy, practice, and future scholarship. Policymakers must prioritize accessibility and ethical safeguards, practitioners should adopt culturally responsive AI tools, and researchers are encouraged to explore interdisciplinary pathways that integrate tradition and technology for inclusive futures.

title: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
title_original: Disclosure, Concealment, and Accountable Testimony: A 20-Year Comparative Textual Analysis of Islamic Moral Reasoning in a Muslim Athlete's Autoethnographies
summary: Autoethnography can connect embodied experience to the social organisation of sport, but writing the self also exposes relationships, institutions, and other people. Relational ethics addresses this problem, yet sport scholarship has given comparatively less attention to the explicit moral traditions through which authors decide both what to disclose and what to withhold. This article conducts a critical autoethnographic textual comparison of two works written twenty years apart. The first is a 2006 doctoral study of power, coercion, injury, and the coach-athlete relationship. The second is a 2026 book that locates sporting development within a broader life history and the Maldives’ inaugural Olympic participation. 16 focal representational decisions were analysed through a comparison matrix and five situated Islamic concepts: amanah (trust), 'adl (justice), niyyah (intention), satr (protective concealment), and hisab (accountability). The comparison shows a shift from an individuated pseudonym carrying diary-derived speech towards named individuals, selective paraphrase, recurrent retrospective self-correction, and wider structural framing. Both texts declare reconstruction rather than transcription, so what changes across the twenty years is the unit of representation rather than the evidential claim. title: Role of Panchakarma in Sports Medicine: An Ayurvedic Perspective on Recovery, Musculoskeletal Health and Injury Rehabilitation
title_original: Role of Panchakarma in Sports Medicine: An Ayurvedic Perspective on Recovery, Musculoskeletal Health and Injury Rehabilitation
summary: Sports medicine is a multidisciplinary field concerned with the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation and long-term management of sports-related conditions. Athletes are exposed to repetitive mechanical loading, high training volumes, psychological stress, fatigue and risk of acute and overuse injuries. Contemporary sports rehabilitation primarily uses exercise therapy, physiotherapy, load management, pharmacological interventions and, when indicated, surgical procedures. Ayurveda provides an additional traditional framework emphasizing prevention, individualized care, and restoration of functional capacity and maintenance of physical resilience. Panchakarma is a group of classical Ayurvedic therapeutic procedures traditionally employed for the management of aggravated Dosha under appropriate clinical circumstances. Selected procedures, particularly Snehana (Abhyanga etc.), Swedana and Basti, may have potential relevance to recovery, musculoskeletal health and rehabilitation when appropriately selected and integrated with contemporary sports medicine. Available literature suggests promising applications of Ayurvedic interventions in musculoskeletal disorders and rehabilitation; however, direct high-quality evidence involving competitive athletes remains limited. Recent research has begun to investigate Ayurvedic massage using objective sports-related outcomes such as flexibility, muscle stiffness and stretch tolerance¹. Therefore, Panchakarma should currently be considered a potential complementary approach rather than an established replacement for evidence-based sports medicine.

title: The Development Challenges of English Sevens Rugby in China: A Multidimensional Analysis Based on the Project's Essential Attributes
title_original: The Development Challenges of English Sevens Rugby in China: A Multidimensional Analysis Based on the Project's Essential Attributes
summary: Since becoming an official Olympic event in 2009, seven-a-side rugby has achieved unprecedented development opportunities worldwide. As a staunch executor of Olympic strategy, China has invested substantial resources in this sport, with the women's team securing a historic sixth-place finish at the Paris Olympics. However, this achievement has not altered the fundamental landscape of seven-a-side rugby being a "niche sport" in China. This paper constructs a three-dimensional analytical framework-"sporting characteristics-system compatibility-cultural soil"-based on the intrinsic attributes of seven-a-side rugby to systematically examine the deep-seated challenges in its development within China. Research reveals a structural mismatch between the sport's high-intensity, fast-paced, and high-contact nature and China's state-led talent cultivation model in competitive sports. Its Western-originated, physically confrontational cultural DNA also creates a cognitive gap with traditional Chinese body concepts and athletic aesthetics. Additionally, its reliance on campus promotion and grassroots club development conflicts with China's institutional inertia of concentrating sports resources in Olympic-dominant events. The convergence of these three tensions forms the structural root cause behind seven-a-side rugby's "over a decade post-Olympic inclusion yet still struggling for widespread adoption" in China. The study proposes that overcoming this predicament requires transcending the "Olympic-driven" singular development logic, returning to the sport's intrinsic attributes, and establishing a tripartite collaborative development path encompassing "campus promotion-social engagement-elite competition."

title: The Mediating Role of Mental Well-Being in The Effect of Mindfulness on Happiness among Athletes
title_original: The Mediating Role of Mental Well-Being in The Effect of Mindfulness on Happiness among Athletes
summary: Objective: The aim of this study was to determine the mediating role of mental well-being in the effect of mindfulness on happiness among athletes. Method: A total of 416 athletes—173 women and 243 men—participated in the study, which was based on a correlational survey model. The “Personal Information Form,” “Mindfulness Scale,” “Mental Well-Being Scale,” and “Oxford Happiness Scale” were used to collect data in the study. Pearson correlation and the PROCESS Macro were used to conduct regression-based mediation analysis in the evaluation of the data. Findings: An analysis of the research findings revealed significant positive correlations between mindfulness and mental well-being, between mindfulness and happiness, and between mental well-being and happiness. Mindfulness significantly predicted mental well-being and accounted for 4.4% of the variance in mental well-being. Additionally, mindfulness and mental well-being significantly predicted happiness and together explained 41.2% of the variance in the happiness variable. The results of the mediation analysis indicated that mental well-being plays a partial mediating role in the relationship between mindfulness and happiness. Conclusion: The study concluded that mindfulness is a significant predictor of happiness among athletes and that this effect is partially mediated by mental well-being. The findings suggest that promoting mindfulness and mental well-being may be important in interventions aimed at enhancing athletes’ happiness.

title: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
title_original: Biomechanics of the Snatch and Clean and Jerk in Olympic Weightlifting: A Systematic Review
summary: Biomechanical studies of the Olympic snatch and clean and jerk use heterogeneous samples and measurement protocols. This systematic review summarizes measurement approaches, technical findings, lift-specific coverage, and sex representation. Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed and Scopus were searched on 20 September 2026, retaining publications first available by 30 June 2026. The exports contained 241, 151 and 264 records (656 in total); 314 duplicate entries were removed, leaving 342 distinct database records. The authors confirmed full-text assessment of the previously assembled evidence set. Of its 74 publications, one narrative review (Bartonietz, 1996) was reclassified as contextual rather than original research, leaving 73 primary publications. Fifty-two of the original 74 entries matched the new electronic exports by DOI or title; 21 additional primary publications were retained from the authors’ previously assembled reference set. Among the 73 primary publications, 45 examined the snatch only, 15 examined clean/jerk movements without snatch data, and 13 examined both categories; 23 included female athletes. Eight publications are cited only for methodological or contextual interpretation. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. The review highlights the uneven coverage of the competition lifts, limited female representation and need for comparable, field-validated multimodal measurements. No prospective review protocol was registered.

title: Enhancing relay exchange efficiency through smart relay baton and multisensor wearable technology
title_original: Enhancing relay exchange efficiency through smart relay baton and multisensor wearable technology
summary: Background and Study Aim. Relay sprint performance depends heavily on efficient baton exchange and precise coordination between incoming and outgoing runners. Conventional relay training typically relies on coach observation and technical feedback, whereas sensor-based technologies can provide objective information on movement timing and synchronization. Despite the use of these different approaches, their relative effectiveness in improving relay exchange efficiency remains of practical interest. This study evaluated the effects of a Smart Relay Baton integrated with multisensor wearable technology on relay exchange performance compared with conventional relay training. Materials and Methods. This pragmatic assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial involved 96 sprint relay athletes from regional athletics training centers in Central Java, Indonesia. Athletes were randomly allocated to an intervention group using the Smart Relay Baton system (n = 48) or a control group receiving conventional relay training (n = 48). The intervention lasted eight weeks. The system integrated accelerometer-based motion tracking, multisensor wearable monitoring, and MQTT-based IoT synchronization to provide real-time coordination analytics. Primary outcomes included transition time, synchronization delay, and Relay Exchange Efficiency Score (REES). Secondary outcomes included entry speed, acceleration, heart-rate response, and rating of perceived exertion. Results. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in transition time (−0.18 s), synchronization delay (−0.12 s), and REES (+4.8 points) than the control group (all p < .05). Synchronization delay was the strongest predictor of REES (r = −0.58, p < .01), exceeding the contributions of entry speed and physiological variables, suggesting that temporal coordination represents the primary mechanism underlying relay exchange efficiency. Conclusions. The proposed Smart Relay Baton system integrates wearable sensing and real-time analytics to support coordination-oriented motor learning rather than performance monitoring alone. This approach provides a promising evidence-based framework for relay coaching and future wearable-assisted sprint training interventions.

title: The power of the smart city cognitive map
title_original: The power of the smart city cognitive map
summary: The study describes the mechanisms by which the cognitive map of the smart city will write and rewrite behavioral patterns, starting with a definition of the phenomenon of behavioral influences generated by the architectural landmarks, and continuing with the classification of these influences into two types: direct and indirect, completed with description of the two directions and classification criteria. The indirect influence categories are further examined: "spectacle" type influence, influence through symbol, and influence through the generation of urban atmospheres in the smart city, with an emphasis on the spectacle of architectural landmarks in contemporary visual culture determined and shaped by technology. Architectural images and landmarks form a psychological cognitive map, which reflects the decisions made under effective leadership at a given moment. The materialization of architectural creation in an urban context is commissioned and financed by the structures of power, with an immediate effect on social behavior regarding that power. More than that, they have the particular characteristic of generating attachment and often a behavior of copying and re-edifying them across space or time. This is an effect, a behavioral influence, a power of the cognitive map over the functioning of the smart city, whether at the individual or mass level. Architecture generates behavior, even if we can, by reduction to the absurd, simplistically view this behavior merely as the construction and functionality themselves. The social and political meaning of the decisions made towards reproduction, even copying, of architectural elements is what concerns us in this study. Important architecture is manipulative. In architecture commissioned and financed by the authorities and signed by architects trained and certified by it, power is exerted by the exact copying and implementation of a certain style/manner in different places/sites, or those distanced from the seat of that authority or leadership center, to transmit the message of a certain type of social order. The copying or rebirth of architectural styles and stylistic elements occurs across great geographical distances and over long periods of time. These landmark styles are, in fact, a discourse of display and consolidation of the source leadership's superiority, a genuine show (spectacle), a demonstration of force, and an emergence—an unveiling of the panoply of technological evolution, aesthetic tastes, and culture of the social order that generated them. We are thus talking in this case about manipulation-as-spectacle through architecture. Architectural images congealed in cognitive maps reproduced trans-culturally or over time impact behavior by imposing adherence to a certain cultural identity, materialized through the acceptance of the authority of the culture that generated these images, which are mass-shared and up-graded in the smart city.

title: Playing for Quality: A Competitive Educational Game for Teaching Unit Testing in Computer Science Education
title_original: Playing for Quality: A Competitive Educational Game for Teaching Unit Testing in Computer Science Education
summary: Software testing is a foundational competence in computer-science curricula and a notoriously disengaging one for learners; a recurring concern for the games-based learning (GBL) community is whether gamified-testing interventions actually deepen learning or merely raise activity levels. This paper presents the design and a proof-of-concept evaluation of Test Royale, an educational game for teaching unit testing whose mechanics are deliberately bound to learning objectives at Bloom’s apply, analyse and evaluate levels: live mutation analysis (Stryker.NET) and coverage analysis (Coverlet) are surfaced as in-game feedback, and the score function is computed directly from validated quality indicators rather than from activity volume. The design is articulated through the Mechanics–Dynamics–Aesthetics (MDA) framework and grounded in the Octalysis core drives. We report a small mixed-methods pilot study with two complementary participant groups: sixteen undergraduate students in a Software Testing course (8 in a gamified condition, 8 in a non-gamified condition; Study 1) and eleven professional developers at an Egyptian fintech company (Study 2). In Study 1, the gamified condition outperformed the non-gamified condition on every measured quality indicator with large-effect-size differences (mutation score Δ = +8.2, d ≈ 0.81; branch coverage Δ = +10.7, d ≈ 0.96; line coverage Δ = +7.5, d ≈ 0.84; useful test LOC Δ = +12.1, d ≈ 1.23), with p < .05 for each and the pattern surviving Holm–Bonferroni correction across the five outcomes, while execution time did not differ significantly. In Study 2, the system achieved a System Usability Scale score of 80.0 (“excellent”; 95% CI [66.88, 93.12], n = 11), with self-reported motivation among already-motivated practitioners remaining high but not significantly increased. Given the small samples, the entanglement of game mechanics with feedback immediacy in our control condition, and the single-session design, we present these results as encouraging proof-of-concept evidence rather than confirmatory findings, and we describe a three-arm replication plan that disentangles game mechanics from feedback design.

title: Evidence of validity, reliability, and measurement invariance of the psychological characteristics related to sport performance questionnaire in Colombian athletes
title_original: Evidence of validity, reliability, and measurement invariance of the psychological characteristics related to sport performance questionnaire in Colombian athletes
summary: Background The assessment of psychological characteristics is crucial for the intervention and monitoring of sports performance. However, there is a lack of instruments for measuring psychological characteristics in Colombian athletes. Methods This research aimed to examine the validity and reliability of the scores obtained from the Psychological Characteristics related to Sport Performance Questionnaire (CPRD in Spanish). Two complementary studies were conducted: Study 1 included 1.305 athletes, comprising 412 women and 893 men, with an age range between 13 and 59 years, divided into age groups; Study 2 included 478 athletes, comprising 150 women and 328 men, with an age range between 13 and 37 years. Results The four-factor, 37-item CPRD demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for stress control (SC), influence of performance evaluation (IPE), and motivation (M), but inconsistent reliability for team cohesion (TC) (ω = 0.64; α = 0.65), although overall reliability was satisfactory. The four-factor CPRD showed adequate model fit indices. Although the questionnaire demonstrated adequate concurrent validity, convergent validity was not satisfactory. Inverse correlations were observed between the four-factor CPRD and burnout dimensions, and acceptable ratios supporting discriminant validity were identified, along with measurement invariance across sport modality, sex, and age groups (ΔCFI and/or ΔRMSEA ≤ 0.01). Conclusion The four-factor CPRD provides partial evidence of validity and reliability for assessing relevant psychological variables in the Colombian sports context; however, interpretations based on factor-level scores should be made with caution.

title: Gender assignment in L2 French by speakers of Polish: The effects of word endings, L1 transfer and masculine by default
title_original: Gender assignment in L2 French by speakers of Polish: The effects of word endings, L1 transfer and masculine by default
summary: This study examined the relative influence of three factors on gender assignment in L2 French by Polish learners in cases where the noun’s gender was unknown to them. Those three factors are as follows: the form of the noun, transfer effects from the first language (L1), and the assignment of masculine by default. Our participants were 1,115 adult native speakers of Polish who belonged to all levels of French proficiency. We selected 24 words for which both correct and incorrect gender assignment can be explained by only one of the three factors. Those words were presented sequentially online, in isolation, in the form of images accompanied by recordings of their pronunciation. Participants had to indicate which gender they thought the word possessed (masculine or feminine). Bayesian analyses showed all three factors to contribute to gender assignment, explaining up to 43% of the assignment process. Their combined explanatory power decreases as learners become better in French, and it is greater in the case of incorrect gender assignment. While relying mostly on masculine by default at beginning levels, as learners progress in French, they are influenced more by L1 transfer and word endings.

title: The Effect of Special Exercises Using a Mirror on Learning the Back Roundhouse Kick (Hajw - Jaki) among Taekwondo Learners Aged 12–14 Years
title_original: The Effect of Special Exercises Using a Mirror on Learning the Back Roundhouse Kick (Hajw - Jaki) among Taekwondo Learners Aged 12–14 Years
summary: This research objectives to determine the impact of utilizing a mirror as a teaching tool on learning the back roundhouse kick (Hajw - Jaki) in Taekwondo among learners aged 12-14. The researcher used an experimental design with two equivalent groups. The research sample consisted of 20 learners randomly separated into two same groups: an experimental group of 10 learners who learned using a mirror and a control group of 10 learners who learned using the traditional method without a mirror. The experiment lasted for six weeks with three training sessions per week, totaling 18 training sessions .The researcher used a form to evaluate the skill performance of the back roundhouse kick and employed pre- and post-tests to measure learning levels. The learning conditions for both groups were standardized in terms of coach, time, content, location and number of repetitions with the only difference being the use of a mirror. The data were statistically analyzed using the mean, standard deviation and t-tests for paired and independent samples.The results present a statistically significant development in the performance of both groups between the pre- and post-tests with the improvement being greater in the experimental group. The findings also indicated no significant differences between the two groups in the pre-test while significant differences emerged in the post-test in favor of the experimental group demonstrating the effectiveness of using a mirror in improving skill learning. The research concluded that the mirror is an effective teaching tool for learning complex motor skills in Taekwondo as it provides immediate visual feedback that contributes to correcting errors and improving balance, accuracy and motor coordination. The research recommended its adoption in teaching Taekwondo learners aged 12-14 and conducting similar studies on other skills and age groups.

The findings also indicated no significant differences between the two groups in the pre-test while significant differences emerged in the post-test in favor of the experimental group demonstrating the effectiveness of using a mirror in improving skill learning. The research concluded that the mirror is an effective teaching tool for learning complex motor skills in Taekwondo as it provides immediate visual feedback that contributes to correcting errors and improving balance, accuracy and motor coordination. The research recommended its adoption in teaching Taekwondo learners aged 12-14 and conducting similar studies on other skills and age groups.

title: The effect of macular carotenoids and omega-3 supplementation on performance in precision sports: the sport nutrition intervention in performance exercise (SNIPE) study
title_original: The effect of macular carotenoids and omega-3 supplementation on performance in precision sports: the sport nutrition intervention in performance exercise (SNIPE) study
summary: Background Macular carotenoids improve visual performance in healthy individuals, but these benefits have yet to be tested on athletes. The SNIPE study examined how the macular carotenoids [lutein (L), zeaxanthin (Z), meso-zeaxanthin (MZ)] with omega-3 fatty acids (ω3) impact visual functions and sports performance in precision sports. Methods In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 67 athletes and players randomly received either an active supplement containing L, Z, MZ + ω3 (the formulation), or a placebo containing sunflower oil over a 9 month period. Key measurements included blood serum L, Z and MZ concentrations, skin carotenoid score (SCS), visual acuity (VA) and contrast sensitivity (CS), subjective visual function, sleep health (SH), and sport specific performance tests during simulated competitions. Results Results showed that the active group, compared to placebo, exhibited statistically significant improvements in L (88%), Z (107%), MZ (0 to 0.226 μmol/L) blood concentrations, SCS (25%), CS at 6 cpd during dim condition ( p = 0.008, η 2 = 0.141), and SH in archery ( p = 0.023, η 2 = 0.242) and Egame ( p = 0.041, η 2 = 0.237). Sports performance also improved for the active group, including total shooting score of 60 shots ( p = 0.047, η 2 = 0.081) for shooters and archers, and simple motor time ( p = 0.018, η 2 = 0.302) and a suggestive trend toward faster choice reaction time ( p = 0.054, η 2 = 0.213) for Egame players, when compared to the placebo group. Conclusion The study provides novel evidence that supplementing with carotenoids and omega-3 fatty acids enhances visual function and sports performance in precision sport athletes and players. Further research should attempt to identify the exact mechanisms by which these nutrients are enhancing visual function. These findings highlight the opportunity to add these complementary bioactive nutrients of the eye and brain to athletes' diets to help achieve peak performance in sports. title: FRAMING ANALYSIS OF BONEK AND PERSEBAYA’S DEPARTURE TO AUSTRALIA IN ONLINE MEDIA DETIK.COM, KOMPAS.COM, AND TRIBUNNEWS.COM
title_original: FRAMING ANALYSIS OF BONEK AND PERSEBAYA’S DEPARTURE TO AUSTRALIA IN ONLINE MEDIA DETIK.COM, KOMPAS.COM, AND TRIBUNNEWS.COM
summary: This study analyzes media framing in the coverage of Persebaya Surabaya's supporters (Bonek) and the football club's departure to Perth, Australia, as reported by three leading Indonesian online media outlets: Detik.com, Kompas.com, and Tribunnews.com. These outlets were selected based on SimilarWeb data as of April 2026, which ranked them as the three largest online news media in Indonesia. The study employs Pan and Kosicki's framing analysis model, examining four dimensions of framing: syntactical, script, thematic, and rhetorical structures. This qualitative descriptive research uses textual observation as the primary data collection technique. Findings reveal that Detik.com framed the event as a technical training and pre-season preparation agenda, with Bonek's role relatively marginal. Kompas.com emphasized a diplomatic-governmental frame, highlighting the bilateral relationship between East Java Province and Western Australia. Tribunnews.com adopted an entertainment and supporter enthusiasm frame, centering on Bonek's tour program and activities in Perth. These divergent frames reflect each outlet's editorial tendencies and target audiences, contributing to broader understanding of media reality construction in Indonesian sports and sports diplomacy contexts.

title: Generalizable Lifelong Model Editing via Preference Optimization
title_original: Generalizable Lifelong Model Editing via Preference Optimization
summary: Knowledge editing enables rapid updates of specific factual knowledge in large language models (LLMs) without full retraining. However, more realistic scenarios call for a lifelong framework that handles continual updates rather than one-off modifications. In such settings, existing editing methods often overfit to target prompts, significantly degrading both the generalization of the edited knowledge and the model's general capabilities. To address this issue, we propose GLIME (Generalizable Lifelong Model Editing), which combines knowledge editing with preference optimization over generation behavior. GLIME further incorporates replay-based editing and a gradient constraint to preserve previously edited knowledge. Experimental results show that GLIME significantly improves knowledge generalization in lifelong editing settings while maintaining both editing performance and general capabilities.

title: The association between coach-athlete relationship and self-reported task, contextual, and overall athletic performance among university student-athletes
title_original: The association between coach-athlete relationship and self-reported task, contextual, and overall athletic performance among university student-athletes
summary: Introduction The coach-athlete relationship is a fundamental psychosocial factor associated with athlete performance. However, its associations with self-reported task performance, contextual performance, and overall athletic performance have not been sufficiently examined within a single model. Drawing on theoretical frameworks such as the 3C model and Self-Determination Theory, this study aimed to investigate the associations between the coach-athlete relationship and two performance sub-dimensions (task performance and contextual performance) and their composite overall score (athletic performance), with overall athletic performance operationalized as a composite score reflecting athletes' global self-perceived performance. Method This quantitative study employed a correlational survey design with 276 university student-athletes (154 male and 122 female) competing in individual and team sports. The Coach-Athlete Relationship Scale and the Athletic Performance Scale (comprising task performance and contextual performance sub-dimensions and an overall composite score) were used. Hierarchical regression analysis was conducted to examine the statistical association of the coach-athlete relationship with self-reported performance dimensions after controlling for demographic variables. Results The coach-athlete relationship was positively and significantly correlated with task performance (r = 0.412, p < 0.001) , contextual performance (r = 0.465, p < 0.001) , and overall athletic performance (r = 0.461, p < 0.001) . Hierarchical regression analysis showed that the coach-athlete relationship demonstrated a significant statistical association with task performance ( β = 0.514, p < 0.001) , contextual performance ( β = 0.563, p < 0.001) , and overall athletic performance (β = 0.560, p < 0.001) , after controlling for demographic variables. Conclusion A high-quality coach-athlete relationship is positively associated with athletes' self-reported task performance, contextual performance, and overall athletic performance. These findings suggest that the coach-athlete relationship may be important in relation to athletes' social, cooperative, and team-oriented behaviors. However, as all measures were self-reported, the results reflect perceived rather than objective performance.

title: Digitalization in sport psychology: A bibliometric analysis of emerging research trends
title_original: Digitalization in sport psychology: A bibliometric analysis of emerging research trends
summary: This study examines the conceptual structure, dominant research themes, and intellectual foundations of research on digitalization in sport psychology through a bibliometric analysis, aiming to map how the fragmented literature on digital service delivery, social media, virtual reality, wearable technologies, and athlete mental health is organized. Bibliographic records were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection using a Topic-field search that combined sport psychology, digitalization, and psychological outcome terms and was limited to English-language articles and reviews. The final dataset comprised 325 publications. Data were analyzed using the Bibliometric package in R through keyword frequency analysis, keyword co-occurrence network analysis, thematic mapping, and reference co-citation analysis. The keyword co-occurrence network separated into two main clusters: one organized around sport, performance, exercise, motivation, and social media, and the other around physical activity, mental health, children, anxiety, and depression. The thematic map located the physical activity/mental health and anxiety/depression clusters among the basic themes, while the sport/social media/gender cluster was positioned at the boundary between niche and motor themes. The reference co-citation network revealed four clusters anchored, respectively, by self-determination theory and sport-participation research, athlete social-media and measurement-model studies, elite-athlete mental health consensus and review literature, and mental-health stigma and help-seeking research. Because the analysis is cross-sectional, these results indicate conceptual proximity within the analyzed dataset rather than a demonstrated temporal shift toward integration. The study contributes a conceptual and intellectual map of this literature and identifies research priorities for sport psychologists, practitioners, and researchers, while its findings are limited by reliance on a single database and English-language publications.

title: Desigualdades de género en la elección de áreas del conocimiento: análisis longitudinal del Global Gender Gap Report (2017–2025)
title_original: Desigualdades de género en la elección de áreas del conocimiento: análisis longitudinal del Global Gender Gap Report (2017–2025)
summary: INTRODUCCIÓN. La paridad de género en la educación superior continúa siendo un desafío global, visible en la persistente segregación entre campos de estudio. Esta investigación examina la evolución de la participación de mujeres y hombres en 121 países a partir de ocho ediciones del Global Gender Gap Report correspondientes a 2017-2018 y 2020-2025. Su objetivo es identificar patrones disciplinares y describir su coexistencia con la evolución del Global Gender Gap Index. MÉTODO. Se realizó un estudio cuantitativo, documental y longitudinal. La base de datos integró información de 121 países correspondiente a ocho ediciones del Global Gender Gap Report (2017-2018 y 2020-2025), cuya unidad de análisis fue la combinación país-año-área del conocimiento. Se integraron las bases anuales, se clasificaron los países según las regiones del World Economic Forum y se excluyeron las observaciones sin información disciplinar. Se calcularon estadísticos descriptivos y se elaboraron representaciones gráficas para examinar tendencias globales y regionales. Para 2025 se comparó la participación femenina entre áreas mediante un ANOVA de Welch, pruebas post hoc de Games-Howell y una estimación del tamaño del efecto. RESULTADOS. El índice global pasó de .70 en 2017 a .72 en 2025, con diferencias persistentes entre regiones. Educación y Salud y Bienestar Social presentaron una mayor participación femenina, mientras que Ingeniería, Manufactura y Construcción, Tecnologías de la Información y la Comunicación y el conjunto STEM mostraron una participación masculina superior. title: Türk Karate Hakemlerinin psikolojik sağlamlık ve tükenmişlik düzeylerinin incelenmesi
title_original: Türk Karate Hakemlerinin psikolojik sağlamlık ve tükenmişlik düzeylerinin incelenmesi
summary: Spor ortamlarında artan performans baskısı ve mesleki yükler, hakemlerin psikolojik sağlamlık ve tükenmişlik düzeylerinin incelenmesini gerekli kılmaktadır. Bu araştırmanın amacı, karate hakemlerinin psikolojik sağlamlık ve tükenmişlik düzeylerini demografik ve mesleki değişkenler açısından incelemektir. Araştırma nicel yöntemle yürütülmüş olup çalışma grubunu aktif olarak görev yapan 297 karate hakemi oluşturmaktadır. Veri toplama aracı olarak Yetişkin Psikolojik Sağlamlık Ölçeği ve Maslach Tükenmişlik Ölçeği kullanılmış, veriler gönüllülük esasına dayalı olarak toplanmıştır. Elde edilen bulgulara göre cinsiyet değişkeninde ilişkisel, bireysel ve ailesel kaynaklar, toplam psikolojik sağlamlık, duygusal tükenme ve kişisel başarı; medeni durumda kültürel-bağlamsal ve ailesel kaynaklar ile duygusal tükenme; eğitim düzeyinde ilişkisel ve ailesel kaynaklar, toplam psikolojik sağlamlık ile tükenmişliğin tüm alt boyutları açısından anlamlı farklılıklar belirlenmiştir. Yaş değişkeninde bireysel, kültürel-bağlamsal ve ailesel kaynaklar, toplam psikolojik sağlamlık ile duygusal tükenme, duyarsızlaştırma ve kişisel başarı; karate yapma süresinde ise psikolojik sağlamlığın tüm alt boyutları ve toplam puanı ile tükenmişliğin tüm alt boyutlarında anlamlı farklılıklar saptanmıştır. Sonuç olarak, karate hakemlerinin psikolojik sağlamlık ve tükenmişlik düzeylerinin demografik ve branşa özgü deneyim değişkenlerine göre farklılaşabildiği belirlenmiştir.

title: Mental Health, Personality, Identity, and Adjusting to Life After Sports
title_original: Mental Health, Personality, Identity, and Adjusting to Life After Sports
summary: This study looked at how athletes adapt to life after competitive sports in relation to psychological issues. In publicly accessible podcast interviews, 95 former athletes, most competing at the collegiate or professional level, were examined using their own words. Claude and Gemini, two large multimodal models, independently coded each interview for four mental health outcomes: depression, anxiety, dependency, and identity confusion, as well as for a set of predictor variables, such as neuroticism, emotion regulation, athletic identity, identity foreclosure, intrinsic motivation, grit, social support, and retirement planning. A binary present or absence coding system was employed, and Gwet's AC1 was utilized to evaluate the two models' agreement. Four regression models were used to examine the predictors after the four outcomes were merged into a single mental health condition score. The best indicators of post retirement difficulties were neuroticism and identity foreclosure, with identity foreclosure predicting difficulty across two different models. While retirement planning, intrinsic motivation, and social support did not achieve significance, grittier athletes unexpectedly reported more difficulty, and stronger emotion regulation predicted less difficulty. The results imply that committing entirely to the athlete role, without exploring other parts of who you are, is a major risk factor for a harder transition, whereas maintaining ties to roles outside of sports facilitates a more seamless one.

title: General and sports nutrition knowledge and professionalism in athletes: A cross-sectional study
title_original: General and sports nutrition knowledge and professionalism in athletes: A cross-sectional study
summary: This study examined the relationship between general and sports nutrition knowledge and athlete professionalism and explored whether these constructs differed according to selected socio-demographic and sport-related characteristics. A cross-sectional correlational design was employed with 221 competitive athletes aged 18-34 years. Nutrition knowledge was assessed using the Turkish version of the General and Sport Nutrition Knowledge Questionnaire, while athlete professionalism was evaluated using the Professionalism Scale for Athletes. Group differences were examined using independent-samples t tests, and the association between nutrition knowledge and professionalism was evaluated using Pearson correlation and simple linear regression. Mean nutrition knowledge was 49.95±16.74, whereas mean professionalism was 4.06±0.58. Athletes who had received previous structured nutrition education demonstrated substantially higher nutrition knowledge than those without such education (59.0±14.7 vs. 44.2±15.5; p<0.001; Cohen’s d=0.97). Female athletes scored higher than male athletes (p=0.012; d=0.35), and individual-sport athletes scored higher than team-sport athletes (p=0.031; d=0.29), although these differences were small and exploratory. No meaningful association was observed between nutrition knowledge and athlete professionalism (r=0.04, p=0.553), and nutrition knowledge did not predict professionalism (R²=0.002, p=0.553). These findings indicate that factual nutrition knowledge and athlete professionalism represent largely distinct dimensions of athlete preparation. Structured nutrition education was the factor most strongly associated with greater nutrition knowledge, supporting the need for direct assessment and professionally delivered nutrition education rather than assuming nutritional competence from an athlete’s professional conduct.

title: The Heterogeneous Nature of the Relative Age Effect: The Role of Sport, Developmental Stage, and Selection Context
title_original: The Heterogeneous Nature of the Relative Age Effect: The Role of Sport, Developmental Stage, and Selection Context
summary: This systematic review aims to comprehensively examine the reflections of the Relative Age Effect (RAE) on athletic performance, athlete selection, and developmental advantage in child and adolescent athletes within the framework of sport type, developmental stage, and selection context. The study was designed in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and studies published between 2019 and 2025 were systematically reviewed. Following the title and abstract screening, 40 studies were evaluated, and after full-text assessment, 30 studies meeting the inclusion criteria were included in the analysis. The majority of the reviewed studies employed a cross-sectional design and involved athletes aged between 3 and 18 years.The findings indicate that the relative age effect is widely observed in sports contexts; however, the magnitude of the effect varies depending on sport type, age category, level of biological maturation, and the structure of selection systems. In particular, athletes born in the first quarter of the year exhibit higher representation and success rates in team sports requiring high levels of physical contact and strength, as well as in selective developmental stages. Conversely, the effect appears to be more limited in some sports characterised by open participation policies or a greater emphasis on technical skills. It is also observed that RAE is more pronounced in early childhood in terms of motor skills and physical fitness parameters; however, structured intervention programs may mitigate this inequality.In conclusion, the relative age effect is a multidimensional phenomenon that should be considered in athlete selection and development processes. The adoption of biological mat-uration-based approaches, flexible age categories, and multidimensional evaluation systems by sports federations and clubs is of critical importance in reducing potential talent loss.
