title: Assessing School Readiness for the Implementation of Modified Sports Competition in the Schools Division Office of Legazpi City
title_original: Assessing School Readiness for the Implementation of Modified Sports Competition in the Schools Division Office of Legazpi City
summary: The resumption of school-based sports following the COVID-19 pandemic required educational institutions to assess their preparedness in implementing modified sports competitions while ensuring learners' safety, policy compliance, and program effectiveness. This study assessed the readiness of schools in the Schools Division Office of Legazpi City in implementing Modified Sports Competition. Specifically, it examined the extent of school readiness in terms of school development plan, coaches and tournament managers, student-athletes, budget, trainings, learners' health and safety protocols, learners' rights and protection, and public relations; identified the major implementation constraints; documented the initiatives undertaken by schools; and developed an action plan to strengthen program implementation. Using a descriptive-quantitative research design, data were collected from 52 respondents composed of school heads, coaches, and tournament managers through a validated survey questionnaire. Weighted mean, frequency count, and ranking were employed in analyzing the data. Findings revealed that the overall readiness of schools was Extremely Ready (WM = 3.31). The highest-rated dimension was learners' rights and protection (WM = 3.71), followed by coaches and tournament managers (WM = 3.47) and public relations (WM = 3.43), while school development plan, budget, and trainings were rated Ready. Major implementation constraints included inadequate funding for sports facilities, shortage of qualified coaches, limited training venues, budget limitations, inadequate health facilities, concerns on learners' welfare, and limited promotional activities. Schools addressed these challenges through resource mobilization, capability-building activities, stakeholder collaboration, strengthened health and safety measures, and enhanced communication strategies. Based on these findings, a strategic action plan was developed to further strengthen the implementation of modified sports competitions in the Schools Division Office of Legazpi City.

title: Türkiye’de spor yönetiminde kadın olmak: Kadın yöneticilerin mesleki deneyimlerine yönelik nitel bir araştırma
title_original: Türkiye’de spor yönetiminde kadın olmak: Kadın yöneticilerin mesleki deneyimlerine yönelik nitel bir araştırma
summary: Bu araştırma, Türkiye’de spor yönetimi alanında görev yapan kadın yöneticilerin mesleki deneyimlerini nitel bir betimsel desen çerçevesinde derinlemesine incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Amaçlı örnekleme yöntemiyle seçilen, farklı kurumsal yapılarda (federasyon, il müdürlüğü, spor kulübü) en az iki yıl yöneticilik deneyimine sahip 12 kadın yöneticiyle yarı yapılandırılmış görüşmeler gerçekleştirilmiştir. Veriler Haziran 2025 ile Ocak 2026 tarihleri arasında toplanmış ve nitel içerik analizi yoluyla çözümlenmiştir. Bulgular; yönetici kimliğine inanılmaması, kariyer önündeki görünmez duvarlar, işyerinde eşitsiz muamele ve mücadele ve anlam bulma olmak üzere dört ana tema altında yapılandırılmıştır. Bulgular, Türkiye’deki spor örgütlerinde cinsiyete dayalı eşitsizliğin yalnızca bireysel önyargılarla değil, kurumsal kültür ve toplumsal normlarla ilişkili yapısal örüntülerle de bağlantılı olduğuna işaret etmektedir. Kadın yöneticilerin bu yapılarla edilgen biçimde yüzleşmediği; sahada görünür olma, sabır ve stratejiyle içeriden dönüşüm arayışı ve genç kadınlara rol model olma gibi aktif direniş pratikleri geliştirdiği dikkat çekici bir bulgu olarak öne çıkmaktadır.

title: The Mediating Role of Burnout Emotions in the Relationship between Emotional Intelligence and Psychological Well-Being Levels of Seafarers (The Case of Türkiye)
title_original: The Mediating Role of Burnout Emotions in the Relationship between Emotional Intelligence and Psychological Well-Being Levels of Seafarers (The Case of Türkiye)
summary: This study was conducted to examine the impact of seafarers' emotional intelligence levels on their psychological well-being and the mediating role of burnout in this effect. The research model and hypotheses were developed within the context of flow theory. The study population consisted of maritime employees in Türkiye. For this purpose, research data were obtained by responding to a survey conducted by 435 seafarers selected using a simple random sampling method from among seafarers working on ships in the port of Zonguldak. The study results indicated that seafarers' emotional intelligence levels significantly and positively impacted their psychological well-being, while significantly and negatively impacting their feelings of burnout. Conversely, seafarers' burnout significantly and negatively impacted their psychological well-being. In addition, it was determined that feelings of burnout had a mediating role in the relationship between seafarers' emotional intelligence levels and their psychological well-being. These findings indicate that emotional intelligence enhances seafarers’ psychological well-being partly by reducing burnout, highlighting burnout as an important mechanism underlying this relationship.

title: When the field does not contain what its name promises: An audit of completeness and recording conventions in a public database of 94,811 international judo contests
title_original: When the field does not contain what its name promises: An audit of completeness and recording conventions in a public database of 94,811 international judo contests
summary: Electronic records produced by sports federations during competition have replaced video observation as the empirical basis of performance analysis over the last decade.These records are usually queried event by event and come with no data dictionary, which prevents any assessment of the completeness of what is being used and favors mistaking absence of record for absence of the phenomenon.We audited the public interface of the international judo federation over a corpus of 94,811 contests from 239 competitions held between 2009 and 2026 and 166,292 actions with an identified performer.The procedure has two layers.The first applies seven measures to each field in isolation: fill rate, variability, temporal continuity, vocabulary stability, cross-table coherence, sentinel-value detection and competition-level non-recording detection.The second confronts each phenomenon with every source the corpus offers about it and with the rules in force in the period.All the findings of greatest consequence came from the second layer, and none of them would be detected by a conventional missing-data check.The recording convention for waza-ari-awasete-ippon changes during 2022, producing an apparent drop of 16.4 percentage points in the ippon rate without anything having changed in the sport; corrected, the rate is stable at about 77% from 2018 to 2024.A pattern compatible with a second change of convention, between 2011 and 2012, was also observed, but the present design cannot test it and it is recorded as a limitation.The golden-score indicator is not recorded in entire competitions, and the information only becomes usable through the union of three independent sources, with a time threshold specific to the rule in force in each year and category.Yuko has no field in the contests table, so that in 2026 no fewer than 23.6% of contests appear without a technical score although they have one.The duration field contains the value 240 in every record and conveys no duration, which is nevertheless recoverable from the clock of the actions table for 45% of contests from 2016 onward.As counter-evidence that the corpus reflects the sport when read correctly, three internal markers reproduce, without having been informed of them, three documented dates of rule change.Of the fifteen fields examined, four are reliable across the whole series, nine are usable under a documented restriction and two do not support analysis.We deliver the field-by-field classification, a verifiable correction for each contaminated series, a mapping between research question and feasibility, and the code that reproduces the technical validation of the audit on future retrievals of the source.

title: Sleep Quality by Sex and Habitual Ergogenic Aid Use in Athletes: A Cross-Sectional Study
title_original: Sleep Quality by Sex and Habitual Ergogenic Aid Use in Athletes: A Cross-Sectional Study
summary: This cross-sectional study examined the sex × habitual ergogenic aid use interaction in relation to sleep quality and described athletes’ primary product choices. The final analytical sample comprised 313 athletes (138 female and 175 male), including 112 habitual users (35.8%) and 201 non-users (64.2%). Habitual use was defined as use on at least two days per week for at least one year, and sleep quality was assessed with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). A two-way analysis of variance tested the main effects of sex and habitual use and their interaction. A small interaction was observed, F(1, 309) = 4.01, p = .0461, partial η² = .013. Female habitual users had higher PSQI scores than female non-users (8.00 ± 2.98 vs. 6.55 ± 2.76; d = 0.52, 95% CI [0.05, 0.99]), whereas the male groups were similar (5.75 ± 2.29 vs. 5.80 ± 2.84). Poor sleep (PSQI > 5) was observed in 81.0%, 58.1%, 49.5%, and 51.2% of these groups, respectively. Among habitual users, protein powder (25.3%) and creatine (25.1%) had the largest relative shares of primary product choices. In conclusion, the association between habitual ergogenic aid use and sleep quality may differ by sex, and this pattern should be confirmed in prospective studies that account for product type, dose, and timing of use.

title: Adolescent elite swimmers’ self-esteem and emotional states: Benefits of organized leisure-time activities
title_original: Adolescent elite swimmers’ self-esteem and emotional states: Benefits of organized leisure-time activities
summary: This study examined whether an Organized Leisure-Time Activities program (OLT3A) strengthens self-esteem and emotional states in elite adolescent swimmers. Twenty-five national-level swimmers (Mage = 14.44 ± 1.23 y) were randomized to a six-week OLT3A intervention or a waiting-list control. The protocol integrated creative non-sport activities, time-management workshops, and guided recovery within regular training periodization. Physical self-esteem dimensions, emotional states, and disturbed breaks were assessed across six time points using multilevel growth-curve analyses. Weekly semi-structured meetings provided qualitative context. OLT3A participants reported significantly higher Global Self-Esteem, Physical Self-Worth, Physical Condition, Happiness, and Excitement compared to controls. Group-by-time interactions indicated that OLT3A was associated with more favorable trajectories of Physical Self-Worth and Physical Condition, while reducing the progression of Anger. Qualitative material suggested that some participants perceived improvements in positive states, focus, schedule management, burden relief, and energy replenishment. These findings suggest that OLT3A may represent a promising practical strategy for supporting self-esteem and emotional states in adolescent athletes, while warranting cautious interpretation given the limitations of the present evidence.

title: Rising performance-efficiency demands in female junior tennis: A longitudinal analysis of ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors rankings, 2004–2025
title_original: Rising performance-efficiency demands in female junior tennis: A longitudinal analysis of ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors rankings, 2004–2025
summary: Long-term changes in ranking-point production efficiency among female players on the ITF World Tennis Tour Juniors were examined between 2004 and 2025. Year-end ranking data comprised 8,510 player-year observations from 5,919 players aged 12-18 years. Elite status was defined annually using a two-stage data-driven knee-point procedure: players were ordered according to Total Ranking Points (TRP), the knee percentile was identified from the smoothed Total Singles Points profile across this TRP-based ordering, and the threshold was applied to the same percentile scale. Performance efficiency was assessed using Singles PPE, Doubles PPE, and Total PPE, with Total PPE defined as TRP divided by total competitive event exposure. In pooled descriptives excluding 2020-2021, median Singles PPE was 64.62 in elite versus 26.56 in non-elite players; corresponding values were 48.57 versus 29.00 for Doubles PPE and 40.38 versus 17.71 for Total PPE. Positive Year × elite-status interactions were identified in linear player-year models adjusted for age, discipline-specific competitive event exposure, COVID-disrupted seasons, and repeated player observations, corresponding to additional average annual increases of 10.81%, 8.97%, and 9.25%, respectively. However, non-COVID natural-spline models showed that temporal differentiation was non-linear and did not support uniform monotonic widening across 2004-2025. In lagged sensitivity analyses, prior-year elite status was associated with higher subsequent PPE, but Year × prior-year elite-status interactions were not significant in the strict non-COVID specification. Forecasts based on 20 non-COVID annual elite medians projected higher PPE through 2030 under continuation of the observed linear trend, while event-exposure scenarios indicated fewer competitive event exposures associated with fixed TRP benchmarks at higher projected efficiency. These projections should be interpreted as conditional ranking-system scenarios rather than measures of physiological load or individual participation requirements. Overall, structurally defined elite players were characterised by persistently higher ranking-point production efficiency and significantly different, non-linear historical trajectories.

title: Analisis Efektivitas Serve-Receive dalam Pertandingan Final Bola Voli Indoor Putri pada POPNAS 2025
title_original: Analisis Efektivitas Serve-Receive dalam Pertandingan Final Bola Voli Indoor Putri pada POPNAS 2025
summary: Penerimaan servis memainkan peran penting dalam menentukan efektivitas pembangunan serangan dalam bola voli kompetitif; namun, studi empiris yang menganalisis efektivitas penerimaan servis pada tingkat final nasional pelajar masih terbatas, terutama dalam konteks Pekan Olahraga Pelajar Nasional XVII 2025. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis persentase penerimaan servis yang berhasil dan tidak berhasil pada setiap set pertandingan final bola voli dalam ruangan putri antara Jawa Barat dan Jawa Timur. Metode deskriptif kuantitatif digunakan dengan pendekatan observasi tidak langsung melalui analisis video pertandingan yang diunggah di YouTube. Subjek penelitian terdiri dari seluruh aksi penerimaan servis yang dilakukan selama tiga set pertandingan final. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan lembar analisis pertandingan yang mengklasifikasikan penerimaan servis ke dalam kategori berhasil dan tidak berhasil. Data dianalisis dengan menghitung frekuensi dan mengonversinya menjadi persentase untuk setiap set. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas penerimaan servis Jawa Barat meningkat dari 64,71% menjadi 73,33% dan 93,75%, sedangkan Jawa Timur mencatat 70%, 81,82%, dan 80%, masing-masing. Secara keseluruhan, efektivitas penerimaan servis antara Jawa Barat (77,26%) dan Jawa Timur (77,27%) relatif serupa, yang menunjukkan bahwa konsistensi kinerja sangat penting bagi stabilitas permainan. Efektivitas penerimaan servis juga menunjukkan tren peningkatan, dengan Jawa Barat menunjukkan stabilitas tertinggi pada set ketiga. Secara praktis, pelatih sebaiknya memprioritaskan latihan penerimaan servis yang terstruktur untuk meningkatkan konsistensi dan kinerja.

title: УСЛОВИЯ И ОСОБЕННОСТИ ПРИМЕНЕНИЯ ФИТНЕС-ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ В ОБРАЗОВАТЕЛЬНОМ ПРОЦЕССЕ ПОДГОТОВКИ УЧИТЕЛЕЙ НАЧАЛЬНЫХ КЛАССОВ
title_original: УСЛОВИЯ И ОСОБЕННОСТИ ПРИМЕНЕНИЯ ФИТНЕС-ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ В ОБРАЗОВАТЕЛЬНОМ ПРОЦЕССЕ ПОДГОТОВКИ УЧИТЕЛЕЙ НАЧАЛЬНЫХ КЛАССОВ
summary: The relevance of this study stems from the need to improve the general physical and professional-applied preparedness of future primary school teachers in the face of increasing psycho-emotional and static-dynamic stresses of teaching, as well as the need for the targeted implementation of health-preserving technologies in higher pedagogical education and teacher training. The purpose of this article is to theoretically substantiate and experimentally test the conditions and specifics of using fitness technologies in the educational process of preparing future primary school teachers. The methodological framework of the study includes an analysis of scientific and pedagogical works, a systematization of approaches to the classification of fitness technologies, pedagogical observation, questionnaires, a quasi-experimental "before-after" design with a control group, and testing the dynamics of students' physical fitness indicators and professional-applied preparedness over the course of the academic cycle. The study identified a set of conditions that ensure the effective application of fitness technologies (organizational and pedagogical, logistical, personnel, didactic, methodological, and motivational-value-based), and organized the main types of fitness technologies used in the training of future primary school teachers. Experimental data demonstrated a more significant increase in the physical fitness of students in the experimental group compared to the control group, as well as an increase in their level of professional and applied readiness for work in primary school. It is concluded that the scientifically and methodologically sound implementation of fitness technologies, while adhering to the identified set of conditions, promotes the development of physical performance, increased resistance to fatigue, and the development of a readiness in future primary school teachers to implement health-preserving practices in their professional activities and the school educational environment.

The methodological framework of the study includes an analysis of scientific and pedagogical works, a systematization of approaches to the classification of fitness technologies, pedagogical observation, questionnaires, a quasi-experimental "before-after" design with a control group, and testing the dynamics of students' physical fitness indicators and professional-applied preparedness over the course of the academic cycle. The study identified a set of conditions that ensure the effective application of fitness technologies (organizational and pedagogical, logistical, personnel, didactic, methodological, and motivational-value-based), and organized the main types of fitness technologies used in the training of future primary school teachers. Experimental data demonstrated a more significant increase in the physical fitness of students in the experimental group compared to the control group, as well as an increase in their level of professional and applied readiness for work in primary school. It is concluded that the scientifically and methodologically sound implementation of fitness technologies, while adhering to the identified set of conditions, promotes the development of physical performance, increased resistance to fatigue, and the development of a readiness in future primary school teachers to implement health-preserving practices in their professional activities and the school educational environment.

title: Analisis Tingkat Competitive Anxiety Atlet Panahan Jawa Barat Kategori Individu dan Beregu
title_original: Analisis Tingkat Competitive Anxiety Atlet Panahan Jawa Barat Kategori Individu dan Beregu
summary: Atlet sering kali mengalami competitive anxiety yang dapat memengaruhi performanya baik dalam kategori individu maupun beregu. Oleh karena itu, pada cabang olahraga panahan yang menuntut kestabilan emosi tinggi, pengukuran tingkat competitive anxiety sangat diperlukan.Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis tingkat competitive anxiety atlet panahan Jawa Barat kategori individu dan beregu. Dalam penelitian ini menggunakan metode deskriptif dengan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan sampel 15 atlet panahan Jawa barat. Instrumen yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini berupa kuesioner Competitive State Anxiety Inventory?2 Revition (CSAI-2R). Setelah data diperoleh, analisis data dilakukan dengan menggunakan uji korelasi SPSS Versi 29. Hasil penelitian menujukkan bahwa tingkat competitive anxiety atlit panahan kategori individu dan beregu memiliki perbedaan yang signifikan. Hal ini ditunjukkan dengan nilai rata-rata tingkat competitive anxiety atlet panahan kategori individu yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan kategori beregu. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa perbedaan kategori bermain memengaruhi tingkat competitive anxiety pada atlet panahan Jawa Barat. Oleh karena itu penulis menyarankan kepada pelatih untuk lebih memerhatikan program latihan, jangan hanya perlu berfokus pada aspek teknik, tetapi juga harus mencakup latihan mental seperti teknik relaksasi, visualisasi, pengendalian pernapasan, serta peningkatan kepercayaan diri.

title: The associations between wearable device feedback perception and athletes’ training load management behavior: the chain mediating role of physiological data literacy and recovery self-regulation
title_original: The associations between wearable device feedback perception and athletes’ training load management behavior: the chain mediating role of physiological data literacy and recovery self-regulation
summary: Introduction Despite the rapid proliferation of wearable devices in sport, athletes vary considerably in their ability to interpret device-generated physiological feedback, and the psychological pathways linking feedback perception to training load management remain insufficiently understood. This study introduces physiological data literacy (PDL) as a content-specific form of data literacy and examines whether PDL and recovery self-regulation (RSR) sequentially mediate the association between wearable device feedback perception (WFP) and training load management behavior (TLM). Methods Using a cross-sectional design, 357 active athletes (189 males and 168 females; mean age = 22.76 years, SD = 3.68) completed the wearable device feedback perception scale, physiological data literacy scale, recovery self-regulation scale, and training load management behavior scale. Path analysis with bias-corrected bootstrapping (5,000 resamples) was conducted. Results WFP showed a positive total association with TLM ( β = 0.511). Significant specific indirect associations were observed through PDL (standardized indirect effect = 0.083, 95% CI [0.032, 0.136]) and RSR (standardized indirect effect = 0.085, 95% CI [0.048, 0.128]). A significant sequential indirect association was also observed for the theoretically specified WFP → PDL → RSR → TLM ordering (indirect effect = 0.065, 95% CI [0.040, 0.098]). The direct WFP–TLM association remained significant after inclusion of both mediators. However, the reverse sequential model yielded identical AIC and BIC values. Discussion The findings are statistically compatible with a theoretically motivated sequential framework linking WFP, PDL, RSR, and TLM, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal precedence or causal direction. PDL represents a conceptually distinct competency that, together with RSR, warrants further examination in longitudinal and intervention research on wearable-supported training.

title: Adapted Volleyball, Social Belonging, and Inclusion: Experiences of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
title_original: Adapted Volleyball, Social Belonging, and Inclusion: Experiences of Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
summary: Self-Determination Theory posits that satisfying the three basic psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness is critical to individuals' learning and participation. In inclusive education, supporting these needs enables students not only to participate but also to develop a sense of belonging and meaningful attachment to the learning environment. This study examines how participation of students with intellectual disabilities in adapted sports activities in Türkiye's inclusive education context supports the construction of social connectedness, belonging, and interaction skills through autonomy, competence, and relatedness. An interpretative phenomenological analysis approach was used. Participants were ten individuals aged 18–40 with intellectual disabilities at varying levels of functioning and ten typically developing volunteers. Data were collected through audio recordings, semi-structured interviews, and reflective notes. Thematic analysis yielded four themes: (a) social bonds and experiences of reciprocal interaction, (b) construction of belonging and group adaptation, (c) strengthening social cohesion through communication, and (d) volunteers' emotional experiences and perceptions of inclusion. Adapted sports activities strengthen the social belonging and interaction of students with intellectual disabilities. This effect varies with individual support needs; genuine participation depends not on an adapted sports activity being offered, but on students feeling they belong and being supported in learning.

title: The Sources and Documentation of a Century of Deaf Sport in Poland (1922–2022)
title_original: The Sources and Documentation of a Century of Deaf Sport in Poland (1922–2022)
summary: Celem artykułu jest analiza źródeł i dokumentacji stuletniej historii sportu Głuchych w Polsce w latach 1922–2022. Opracowanie ukazuje ewolucję form utrwalania aktywności sportowej osób niesłyszących – od kronik klubowych i prasy środowiskowej po współczesne archiwa cyfrowe. Zastosowano metodę historyczno-porównawczą, krytykę źródeł oraz analizę treści, łącząc perspektywę historyczną z kulturową. Podstawę badań stanowią materiały archiwalne, wydawnictwa jubileuszowe, periodyki Polskiego Związku Głuchych i Polskiego Związku Sportu Niesłyszących, a także zbiory prywatne i internetowe repozytoria. Analiza pozwoliła wyodrębnić trzy zasadnicze etapy rozwoju dokumentacji sportu Głuchych w Polsce: okres przedwojenny (1922–1939), powojenny (1945–1991) oraz współczesny (1992–2022). W każdym z nich sport osób niesłyszących pełnił funkcję nie tylko rehabilitacyjną, lecz także kulturotwórczą i integracyjną. Współczesna cyfryzacja źródeł otwiera nowe możliwości badawcze, umożliwiając szerszy dostęp do danych i rekonstrukcję nieznanych dotąd aspektów historii sportu Głuchych. Artykuł stanowi wkład w rozwój metodologii badań nad historią kultury fizycznej środowisk mniejszościowych. Opracowania źródłowe o charakterze referencyjnym, publikowane w latach 2021–2024 i uporządkowane chronologicznie, wraz z zawartymi w nich źródłami podstawowymi oraz indeksami nazwisk, stanowią podstawę dla przyszłych interdyscyplinarnych badań nad aktywnością sportową mniejszości Głuchych.

Artykuł stanowi wkład w rozwój metodologii badań nad historią kultury fizycznej środowisk mniejszościowych. Opracowania źródłowe o charakterze referencyjnym, publikowane w latach 2021–2024 i uporządkowane chronologicznie, wraz z zawartymi w nich źródłami podstawowymi oraz indeksami nazwisk, stanowią podstawę dla przyszłych interdyscyplinarnych badań nad aktywnością sportową mniejszości Głuchych.

title: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
title_original: A Snow Sports Venue Low-Carbon Evaluation System Based on Life-Cycle Carbon Emissions
summary: Large-scale snow sports venues are characterized by unique terrain, seasonal operation modes, and long service lifespan. Consequently, a comprehensive assessment method is required to account for both life-cycle carbon emissions and multi-dimensional low-carbon performance. This study proposes a Sports Venue Low-carbon Evaluation System (SV-LCES) that integrates life-cycle carbon emission evaluation (LCCE) with multidimensional performance assessment. Using engineering inventories, EnergyPlus simulations, and emission factor methods, a life-cycle carbon emission model was developed and applied to the National Sliding Centre (NSC) and Yanqing Winter Olympic Village (YWOV), with the latter constructed as a supporting venue for the NSC. Carbon hotspots were identified, and an evaluation system was established through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and LCCE combined weighting and grey clustering. The results show that the operation and maintenance stage was the dominant contributor to the life-cycle carbon emissions, accounting for 56.39% of the total. The calculated carbon emission reduction rates of the NSC and YWOV were 40.17% and 46.37%, respectively, indicating a relatively small difference. However, after the low-carbon performance of the venues was comprehensively evaluated, SV-LCES distinguished their performance levels as Grade B for NSC and Grade A for YWOV. The proposed framework offers a holistic approach to low-carbon evaluation of large-scale sports venues and other energy-intensive public buildings.

title: Large Language Models Create Hallucinations in Response to Negated Text
title_original: Large Language Models Create Hallucinations in Response to Negated Text
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved significant advancements in natural language processing tasks, but they remain prone to generating hallucinations—outputs that are logically inconsistent or factually incorrect. While previous research has primarily focused on hallucinations in affirmative contexts, how negated contexts and knowledge lead LLMs into hallucination has received little attention. In this paper, we demonstrate that LLMs struggle to handle negation effectively, applying affirmative knowledge inappropriately, leading to hallucinations that contradict the negated input. Through a comprehensive analysis using probing protocols, we show that negated text induces previously underexplored types of hallucinations, compromising the logical consistency and factual accuracy of LLM outputs. We employ lens observations to trace, layer by layer, how Transformer-based models encode a negated input, revealing that the layer-wise prediction probabilities for pre- and post-negation inputs remain nearly indistinguishable. Additionally, our analysis extends to Korean, a morphologically distinct language, demonstrating that negation-induced hallucinations are not issues specific to English. Our findings suggest that current LLMs, across the evaluated tasks in both English and Korean, exhibit significant areas for improvement when processing negated text, raising concerns about their reliability in real-world applications. We discuss possible ways to mitigate these hallucinations, emphasizing the need for enhanced model architectures to better understand and process negation.

title: Return to sport assessment following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction - 82 consecutive cases
title_original: Return to sport assessment following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction - 82 consecutive cases
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study was to investigate different patient related factors associa/copted with objective return to sport (RTS) testing after an isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) following an optimised and standardized outpatient clinic setting. Methods From 2015 to 2019, patients with isolated ACL tears undergoing ACL reconstruction (ACLR) with hamstring autograft were included. All followed the same standardized rehabilitation protocol. RTS testing comprised isokinetic extensor (ISO Ext) and flexor (ISO Flex) strength, One-Leg Hop (OLH), Side Hop (SH), and Tapping Agility (TT). A Limb Symmetry Index (LSI) ≥ 90% defined the pass criterion for strength and hop tests; H/Q ≥ 50% was used for both limbs. Logistic regression assessed the influence of time after surgery, in-house vs. external rehabilitation and active/passive rehabilitation sessions on RTS pass rates ( α =0.05). Results Of 104 patients, 82 (45 male, 37 female; mean age 34 ± 11.2 years) completed RTS testing at 27.6 (±4.2) weeks after surgery. Patients completed 30 ± 16 strength and functional training sessions. Mean LSI was 92.8 (±11.1%) for OLH and 88.8 (±16.9%) for SH; mean H/Q was 53.9 (±10.8%) (affected) and 50.2 (±6.8%) (unaffected). Pass rates were 66.7% (OLH), 64.4% (SH), 32.4% (TT), 37.2% (ISO Ext), and 44.2% (ISO Flex). No consistent influencing factors were identified ( p > 0.05). Fewer active physiotherapy sessions were associated with higher pass rates for SH (OR 0.934; p = 0.041) and OLH (OR 0.906; p = 0.034). Conclusion Less than half of patients met the commonly used RTS criteria at 6.5 months after ACLR, even after isolated ACL injury treated by a single surgeon using a standardized surgical technique and standardized rehabilitation protocol. These findings argue against time-based RTS clearance and support continued criterion-based rehabilitation and RTS testing.

title: The 1980 Moscow Olympics Boycott
title_original: The 1980 Moscow Olympics Boycott
summary: When the United States government, following the Soviet Union’s invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979, initiated an international boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics, most of the national Olympic committees in Europe did not join Carter’s initiative. However, due to pressure from their respective governments, some of them did. Norway was an exception, as the country’s most important sports bodies chose to boycott the 1980 Olympics without any apparent pressure from the government. This chapter analyses, in a comparative manner, why Norway and Sweden (which chose to participate) reached different conclusions. Norway’s NATO-membership was only part of the explanation. Even more important was that there was a higher degree of institutional stability in Sweden than in Norway and, above all, that the Post-War heroic culture of remembrance from the Second World War influenced the decision to join the boycott in Norway.

title: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
title_original: Strategic Application of Post-exercise Cold-Water Immersion to Enhance Performance Recovery and Adaptation: An Umbrella Review of 15 Published Systematic Reviews with Meta-analysis
summary: BACKGROUND: Athletes commonly implement post-exercise cold-water immersion (CWI), with several meta-analyses having assessed its effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To thoroughly review, appraise, and summarise existing systematic reviews with meta-analyses (SRMA) examining the effects of post-exercise CWI on the recovery of exercise performance and adaptation. METHODS: An umbrella review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. PROSPERO registration: (CRD420251103267). Eight databases were searched, including Web of Science, Scopus, SPORTDiscus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Embase, MEDLINE, and PubMed. Systematic reviews with meta-analyses of peer-reviewed randomised controlled trials examining post-exercise CWI vs passive rest or other recovery modalities on performance, training adaptation, or physiological, biochemical, and perceptual outcomes in healthy humans were included, with restriction to the English language. RESULTS: Fifteen SRMAs published between 2011 and 2025, comprising 161 unique studies, were included. Overall methodological quality was low to critically low, and certainty of evidence was low to very low, mainly due to inconsistency and imprecision. Protocols of 10-15 min at 10-15 or 5-10 °C appear to be most effective for improving performance and recovery. Post-exercise CWI resulted in significant improvements in muscular power at 24 h post-high-intensity exercise and at 24-48 h post-eccentric exercise, and in jump performance at 24-48 h, despite impaired jump performance in the initial hours after post-exercise CWI. Endurance performance improved immediately after CWI, but CWI produced no later benefits or positive effects on adaptations. CWI did not improve muscular strength performance, and impaired strength and hypertrophic gains. CWI improved heart rate variability immediately after exercise, reduced muscle soreness up to 96 h, and lowered creatine kinase (CK) concentrations between 24 and 72 h, with no significant effects on C-reactive protein or interleukin-6 up to 72 h. No immediate impact on blood lactate or lactate dehydrogenase was found, although some reductions appear 24-72 h post-exercise. CONCLUSIONS: Post-exercise CWI confers outcome-specific recovery benefits but may impair resistance training adaptations with chronic use. These findings support a periodised, context-driven approach to CWI implementation rather than routine application after all exercise sessions.

title: Comprehensive analysis of the temperature stress of the ice sheet in a prefabricated curling ice rink
title_original: Comprehensive analysis of the temperature stress of the ice sheet in a prefabricated curling ice rink
summary: Prefabricated ice rinks represent a novel category of artificial ice rinks that exhibit significant potential due to low refrigeration energy consumption, multifunctional capabilities, and ease of assembly. Given the ice’s considerable thickness and significant temperature gradient, it is imperative to investigate the temperature-induced stresses. Three temperature models of the prefabricated rink, considering the actual thermal environment, were established based on the theory of heat transfer. Employing the sequential coupled analysis method, a refined model for analyzing temperature stress within the ice was established. A method for applying temperature to un-refined ice sheet was proposed, utilizing the mathematical functions derived from temperature distribution results. The distribution characteristics of temperature stress fields and the influence of various heat exchange processes were examined. Additionally, the effects of different thermal environment factors on temperature stress were analyzed, and parameters sensitivities were determined. The results show that honeycomb supports are not suitable for embedding constraints analogous to reinforced concrete. The critical temperature-induced tensile stress occurs beneath cooling tubes interfacing with ice, with its magnitude showing positive correlation with refrigerant-driven ice temperature reduction. In contrast, reducing ice temperature through thermal convection and radiation results in a decrease in tensile stress. Parameter analysis reveals that refrigerant constitutes the principal governing factor for temperature stress development. This study would contribute to the performance analysis of ice rinks under thermal-mechanical coupling effects.

title: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
title_original: Sporting Ambitions, Geopolitical Goals
summary: This chapter will cover Morocco’s engagement with international sport. The focus will be on how this country leverages sports events to advance its geopolitical, economic and cultural objectives. Morocco showcases its organisational capabilities and infrastructure by hosting prestigious events at the regional and global level, positioning itself as a relevant player in global sports governance. In particular, football serves as a cornerstone of Morocco’s sports diplomacy, highlighting its role as co-host (alongside Spain and Portugal) of the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup, its historic fourth place in 2022 and the men’s bronze medal in the Paris 2024 Olympics. These achievements, together with the development of scouting processes leading to the naturalisation of athletes from the diasporas, have amplified the national pride and elevated the country’s global visibility. A challenge for Moroccan sports diplomacy is the management of internal, regional and international political tensions, especially concerning Western Sahara, which has caused some sporting incidents with Algeria and Spain. Therefore, Morocco illuminates how African nations can globally use sports as a tool for soft power, geopolitical manoeuvring and the assertion of national identity.

title: Danish Sport Politics during the Cold War
title_original: Danish Sport Politics during the Cold War
summary: This chapter begins with an analysis of how the Danish Sports Federation responded to the Soviet Union’s crushing of the revolt in Hungary in 1956 and, just once, broke with the tradition not to mix sport and politics. After that, the article studies the beginning of sports cooperation between Denmark and the Soviet Union from 1963 until the ‘Prague Spring’ in 1968. The focus of the article is on how the Danish Sports Federation, the Danish Olympic Committee, the Danish press, the Danish Parliament and the Danish government responded to the boycott discussions connected to the Olympic Games in Moscow 1980. The article also comments on the Olympic Games in Los Angeles 1984 and the problems connected to some Danish participants who were members of the organization ‘Sports for Peace’.

title: The Effects of Muscle Soreness-Based Modified Training on Physical, Physiological, and Competition Performance in Cross-Country Skiers
title_original: The Effects of Muscle Soreness-Based Modified Training on Physical, Physiological, and Competition Performance in Cross-Country Skiers
summary: This study aimed to investigate the effects of muscle soreness-based modified training on the physical, physiological, and competition performance of cross-country skiers. A total of 30 cross-country skiers, aged 15–20 years, who had participated in competitions organized by the Turkish Ski Federation for at least five years, voluntarily participated in the study. The participants were divided into an experimental group (n = 15) and a control group (n = 15). Anthropometric measurements including height, body weight, body fat percentage (PBF), lean body mass (LBM), and body mass index (BMI) were recorded. Cardiopulmonary parameters were assessed using a maximal exercise test to determine VO₂max, VCO₂, respiratory quotient (RQ), maximum heart rate (HR), and VO₂max/HR ratio. One week later, the Wingate anaerobic test was conducted to evaluate peak, average, and minimum power, power drop, and total energy production. The experimental group followed a 12-week training program modified according to muscle soreness levels assessed using the Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale, while the control group continued their routine training program. Data were analyzed using paired-samples and independent t-tests (p < 0.05). Significant improvements were observed in the experimental group in peak, average, and minimum power, as well as total energy production in Wingate test results. Cardiopulmonary variables, including VO₂max, HR, and VO₂max/HR, also showed significant improvements. Between-group comparisons revealed significant differences in favor of the experimental group for anaerobic and selected cardiopulmonary parameters. Additionally, competition performance outcomes indicated significant improvements in race times, durations, and time differences in favor of the 2024 season. Muscle soreness-based modified training programs positively influence physical, physiological, and competition performance in cross-country skiers and can be considered an effective alternative training approach.

title: Rope nets – energy gain and sink
title_original: Rope nets – energy gain and sink
summary: Abstract The combination of cable nets with PV modules has been an approach for about 15 years that has only been implemented very rarely so far. The reasons for this are the flexibility, efficiency and load‐bearing capacity of PV modules. If the PV modules are positioned in between the meshes, they are exposed to wind and snow loads as well as temperature fluctuations. This means that the solar cells are involved in load transfer, which affects the durability of the solar cells and the contacts. The development of a lightweight, translucent cable net covered with PV modules up to a mockup of approx. 30 m 2 is presented. The potential to provide electricity directly on site in city centers and residential areas will be shown. The contribution to climate protection lies in avoiding the primary energy loss factor in PV systems outside built‐up areas as well as cooling the street space by shading surfaces and avoiding heating up sealed surfaces. The challenge in this approach lies in the development of the entire structure with a high level of acceptance for the planned locations. The tasks that have to be solved for this include design, building construction, energy and storage technology and the production of the construction as well as measurement technology and software development.

title: Pattern Recognition: Features of the Development of “Hiza Geri” and “Kin Geri” Motor Skills in 8-Year-Old Karateka
title_original: Pattern Recognition: Features of the Development of “Hiza Geri” and “Kin Geri” Motor Skills in 8-Year-Old Karateka
summary: Background and Study Aim. Determining the characteristics of teaching basic strikes will allow us to select the most rational modes for performing a number of tasks in the process of developing motor skills. Based on this information, a coach can predict the effectiveness of technique acquisition and optimize individual training. The purpose of the study was to determine the specific characteristics of teaching 8-year-old boys the forward knee strike “Hiza Geri Chudan” and the instep kick “Kin Geri” in Kyokushinkai karate. Materials and Methods: thirty-two 8-year-old boys participated in the study. To address the objectives, the following research methods were used: study and analysis of scientific and methodological literature, pedagogical observation, timing of learning tasks, a pedagogical experiment, methods of mathematical statistics, and methods of mathematical experimental design. The method of algorithmic prescriptions was used in the teaching process. Results. The centroid coordinate values for the two groups indicate significant differences in the learning of the “Hiza Geri Chudan” forward knee strike and the “Kin geri” instep kick techniques in 8-year-old children. Children mastered the motor tasks of Series 2-5 of the “Hiza Geri Chudan” kick training significantly better (p<0.05). As a result of experimental testing of the effectiveness of training programs and confirmation of the impact of different modes on the learning outcomes of individual exercises in six sets of tasks during the acquisition of the “Hiza Geri Chudan” and “Kin Geri” techniques, centroid coordinates were obtained for eight groups. Analysis of the group centroids classifying the learning outcomes of the strikes shows that the fourth exercise mode (groups 4 and 8) is the most universal for learning both the task sets and the “Hiza Geri Chudan” and “Kin Geri” techniques: four sets, 120-second rest interval. Conclusions. Discriminant models were created that classify young 8-year-old athletes into one of four specific groups with corresponding workloads (A1B1; A2B1; A1B2; A2B2) based on their learning performance. 8-year-old boys have higher rates of mastery of the “Hiza geri chudan” striking technique. The most significant difference in the quality of performance of training tasks is also observed between exercise execution modes. The analysis of group centroids indicates that in the process of mastering the technique of the “Hiza geri chudan” and “Kin geri” strikes by 8-year-old children, the fourth mode of performing physical exercises is universal and generalized: 4 approaches with rest intervals of 120 seconds.

title: Towards a mathematical theory of athletic training. Part 3. The theory of adaptation of energy metabolism to physical loads by Nikolai Ivanovich Volkov
title_original: Towards a mathematical theory of athletic training. Part 3. The theory of adaptation of energy metabolism to physical loads by Nikolai Ivanovich Volkov
summary: Relevance. In the 1960s–1970s the Soviet Union saw the beginning of the active application of mathematical methods in sport. However, the contribution of Nikolai Ivanovich Volkov, Doctor of Biological Sciences, Professor, founder of the research field of “sport bioenergetics” and creator of the corresponding department at the GTSOLIFK, to the construction of a mathematical theory of adaptation to strenuous muscular activity has not yet been systematized. Meanwhile, it was he who was the first to describe the kinetics of bioenergetic processes by a system of differential equations and to introduce the criteria of power, capacity and efficiency of the energy supply mechanisms. Objectives of the work — systematization, interpretation and comparative analysis of the ideas, models and results of N.I. Volkov relating to the theory of adaptation and its mathematical expression; identification of the structure of the model he proposed and of its place among other approaches; establishment of a typology of relations between his constructions and modern models. Methods. The scientific works and biographical materials of N.I. Volkov of 1965–2013 were analysed, including the papers of 1965, 1966 and 1968, his doctoral dissertation (1990) and the monograph “Sport Bioenergetics” (2011). A comparison was made with the approaches of N.N. Engwer, E. Banister and V.N. Seluyanov and with modern quantitative models of the bioenergetics of muscular activity, and the relations between the models were classified. Results. The mathematical model of adaptation of N.I. Volkov has been systematized: 1) a compartmental kinetic model of energy metabolism in which the dynamics of the oxidizable substrate is described by a second-order linear differential equation; 2) biexponential equations of the kinetics of O₂ uptake during work and in recovery and an equation of lactate dynamics in the form of a difference of two exponentials; 3) a system of criteria of power, capacity and efficiency for the alactate, glycolytic and aerobic mechanisms; 4) an apparatus for optimizing the training process — target functions, the zone of optimal loads and the design of an extreme experiment. The approach of N.I. Volkov has been compared with the approaches of N.N. Engwer, E. Banister and V.N. Seluyanov and characterized as mechanistic, proceeding from the kinetics of metabolic processes. The solution of the equations of the model has been compared with current views: the fast and slow exponential components of the kinetics of O₂ uptake correspond to phase II and to the slow component, while the calculated time of the maximum lactate content corresponds to that observed at a load above the maximal lactate steady state. It is established that R. Morton relied on the 1966 paper of N.I. Volkov, and his three-component model is regarded in the literature as a development of the models of N.I. Volkov. A typology of relations is proposed: direct citation, structural coincidence, conceptual correspondence, analogy and commonality of the object. It is shown that the notion of critical power and of the limited work reserve above it corresponds to the criteria of power and capacity of N.I. Volkov, the maximal lactate steady state to the notion of a critical load, and the models of reconstitution of this reserve are analogous to the equations of recovery kinetics. Conclusion. N.I. Volkov created the first integral mathematical theory of the adaptation of energy metabolism to physical loads in Russian sport science, which completes the series of four mathematical models of athletic training considered in the present cycle of papers and supplies in it the mechanistic link — a description at the level of the kinetics of metabolic processes. His equations and criteria retain their significance as a basis for modern models of training process management, while the forecast he formulated — the development of mathematical models of adaptation and automated systems for controlling the physical condition of athletes — defines the research agenda at the present time as well.

title: Influence of CrossFit-based training on the functional state of former elite athletes: evidence from sambo and judo
title_original: Influence of CrossFit-based training on the functional state of former elite athletes: evidence from sambo and judo
summary: Background and Study Aim. Former elite athletes often retain a high level of motor experience, technical coordination and psychological readiness for physical effort. However, after the end of a professional sport career, many of them experience reduced aerobic capacity, increased body mass, lower muscular endurance, slower recovery and decreased motivation for systematic training. These changes are especially relevant for former sambo and judo athletes because both sports require a complex combination of strength, power, anaerobic capacity, aerobic recovery, coordination, grip endurance and postural stability. CrossFit-based high-intensity functional training may be a suitable method for this population because it combines resistance exercises, metabolic conditioning and functional movements in a scalable format. The study aimed to determine the influence of an eight-week CrossFit-based training methodology on the functional state of former highly qualified sambo and judo athletes. Material and Methods. A pedagogical experiment was designed with former elite combat sport athletes aged 28–42 years. The pilot model included 24 men: 12 former sambo athletes and 12 former judo athletes. All participants had previous national or international competitive experience and had stopped regular professional training for at least two years. The proposed CrossFit-based programme lasted eight weeks and included three sessions per week. Each session consisted of mobility preparation, technical strength work, a scaled metabolic conditioning block and recovery exercises. Functional state was assessed before and after the intervention using resting heart rate, estimated VO2max, Harvard Step Test index, handgrip strength, 30-second push-up test, plank hold, body mass index, body fat percentage and heart rate recovery after standardized load. Paired t-tests were used for pre–post comparisons, and significance was accepted at p<0.05. Results. The model data showed positive changes in all main indicators after the eight-week programme. Resting heart rate decreased from 74.6±5.8 to 68.1±5.1 beats·min^-1 (p=0.001). Estimated VO2max increased from 41.8±4.7 to 46.9±4.9 ml·kg^-1·min^-1 (p=0.001). The Harvard Step Test index improved from 77.3±8.4 to 86.5±7.6 points (p=0.002). Heart rate recovery improved from 31.4±7.2 to 39.8±6.9 beats within the first minute (p=0.001). Muscular endurance also improved: push-ups increased from 32.1±7.8 to 40.6±8.3 repetitions (p=0.001), and plank hold increased from 93.5±28.4 to 128.7±31.2 seconds (p=0.001). Body fat percentage decreased from 22.4±3.8 to 20.1±3.5% (p=0.004). Conclusions. The developed CrossFit-based methodology may be considered an effective and practical approach for improving the functional state of former highly qualified sambo and judo athletes. Its scientific novelty lies in the adaptation of high-intensity functional training to the needs of former combat sport athletes through load scaling, joint protection, grip-strength maintenance, heart rate control and staged recovery. The programme may be recommended for further controlled studies with larger samples and long-term follow-up.

title: Rapid weight loss practices and methods among Mongolian judo athletes
title_original: Rapid weight loss practices and methods among Mongolian judo athletes
summary: [Purpose] Rapid weight loss is prevalent and potentially hazardous in combat sports; however, evidence among Mongolian athletes remains limited. This study characterized rapid weight loss practices among Mongolian judo athletes and compared behavioral practices and social influences between Limited-Method-Use and Combined-Method-Use profiles.[Methods] This cross-sectional study included 100 competitive Mongolian judo athletes. Of the 81 athletes who reported rapid weight loss, hierarchical cluster analysis classified 57 as Limited-Method-Use and 24 as Combined-Method-Use based on 12 weight-cutting modalities.[Results] Pre-competition rapid weight loss was reported by 81.0% of participants. Compared with the Limited-Method-Use group, the Combined-Method-Use group had greater body mass reduction (6.86% vs. 5.25%, p = 0.001) and post-competition body mass regain (6.62% vs. 5.04%, p = 0.001). The Combined-Method-Use group relied heavily on multifaceted dietary restrictions and thermal dehydration methods [sauna, fluid restriction, and plastic suit training (all p < 0.05)]. Regression analysis identified total body mass reduction percentage as the sole significant predictor of weight regain (β = 0.647, p < 0.001). Coaches and teammates were the primary social influences, whereas healthcare professionals had limited influence.[Conclusion] Rapid weight loss is deeply embedded as a normative practice within the Mongolian judo community, with many competitors adopting aggressive, dehydration-driven methodologies. The strong association between weight cuts and severe weight regain highlights the hazardous nature of these practices. These insights underscore the critical need for evidence-based sports nutrition education and preventative screenings targeting athletes and coaching staff.

The strong association between weight cuts and severe weight regain highlights the hazardous nature of these practices. These insights underscore the critical need for evidence-based sports nutrition education and preventative screenings targeting athletes and coaching staff.

title: Large language models show distinct multidimensional performance profiles and variable reproducibility in consensus‐based bone stress injury
title_original: Large language models show distinct multidimensional performance profiles and variable reproducibility in consensus‐based bone stress injury
summary: Abstract Purpose This study evaluated five publicly available large language model‐based systems using a multidimensional, expert‐based assessment of consensus‐based clinical questions on bone stress injuries. Methods Ten standardised questions derived from a 2025 international Delphi consensus on bone stress injuries were submitted to ChatGPT‐5, Perplexity AI, Claude 4, Google Gemini 2.5 and Microsoft Copilot. Responses were independently rated by clinical experts using a multidimensional evaluation framework covering accuracy, comprehensiveness, understanding, reasoning, clarity, potential harm and trust, each rated on a 5‐point Likert scale. Median scores were calculated for each question and model, and comparisons were performed using Kruskal–Wallis tests followed by Dunn's post hoc tests with Bonferroni correction. Interrater agreement was assessed using the weighted Gwet's agreement coefficient. Reproducibility was assessed by repeatedly submitting nine questions representing no, partial, and full expert consensus to each model, with response consistency scored from 1 to 3. Results Significant differences between models were observed for comprehensiveness, reasoning, clarity and trust (all p < 0.001), with no differences in accuracy or harm. ChatGPT‐5 and Claude 4 achieved significantly higher comprehensiveness scores, while ChatGPT‐5 and Google Gemini 2.5 had significantly higher reasoning scores than Microsoft Copilot. Claude 4 demonstrated significantly lower clarity than all other models. ChatGPT‐5 achieved significantly higher trust scores and showed the highest mean reproducibility score, followed by Perplexity AI and Gemini 2.5; Microsoft Copilot showed the lowest reproducibility. Interrater agreement ranged from fair to almost perfect, with substantial overall agreement. Conclusions Publicly available large language model‐based systems demonstrated moderate‐to‐high performance in addressing expert‐derived, consensus‐based questions on bone stress injuries, suggesting potential to support the communication of consensus‐based knowledge. However, performance varied across evaluation dimensions and reproducibility, indicating that large language models may support, but should not replace, primary consensus documents or expert clinical judgement. Level of Evidence N/A.

title: Ensuring Hygiene for All: Evaluating SDG 6.2 through the Sustainability of Public Sanitation
title_original: Ensuring Hygiene for All: Evaluating SDG 6.2 through the Sustainability of Public Sanitation
summary: Under Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6, specifically Target 6.2, the international community committed to ensuring access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all, with particular attention to the needs of women, girls, and individuals in vulnerable situations. Despite this commitment, public sanitation continues to be treated as a discretionary amenity rather than a core public service essential for dignity, mobility, and social participation. This paper examines the gap between the normative framework of SDG 6.2 and the lived realities of sanitation use through an integrated analytical approach that combines international comparative data with an exploratory empirical study conducted in Hungary. Moving beyond conventional metrics of access such as facility counts or service levels, the research highlights how formal equality in provision may translate into substantive inequalities in use. It demonstrates how capacity constraints, maintenance failures, and the lack of care-integrated and inclusive design generate disproportionate burdens for women, while drawing on selected international literature to reflect on broader exclusion and safety concerns in gender-segregated sanitation systems. The findings suggest that current monitoring frameworks, including indicator 6.2.1a, inadequately capture the qualitative dimensions of sanitation access, particularly those related to usability, safety, and dignity in public space. In response, the paper argues for a conceptual shift from infrastructure-based metrics toward a more comprehensive understanding of sanitation as a component of gendered and inclusive urban citizenship. The paper briefly reflects on implications for urban planning and governance, highlighting the relevance of institutional accountability and more inclusive, user-sensitive sanitation design within the broader human rights framework of the United Nations. Keywords: public sanitation, gendered citizenship, gender equality, right to sanitation

title: Survey Tingkat Keterampilan Servis Atas Pada Peserta Ekstrakurikuler Bola Voli di Sekolah Menengah Pertama
title_original: Survey Tingkat Keterampilan Servis Atas Pada Peserta Ekstrakurikuler Bola Voli di Sekolah Menengah Pertama
summary: Permasalahan dalam penelitian ini diketahui bahwa sebagian peserta ekstrakurikuler masih belum menunjukkan penguasaan yang optimal terhadap teknik – teknik dasar permainan bola voli. Salah satu teknik dasar yang masih menjadi kendala adalah servis atas. Kondisi tersebut diduga disebabkan oleh kemampuan peserta dalam menguasai teknik servis atas yang belum optimal, sehingga masih sering terjadi berbagai kesalahan dalam pelaksanaannya. Kesalahan tersebut antara lain servis pendek yang tidak mampu melewati net atau tidak mencapai daerah permainan lawan, serta servis panjnjag yang kurang akurat sehingga bola keluar dari area permainan sehingga mengakibatkan efektivitas servis sebagai serangan awal menjadi kurang maksimal dan berpotensi menurunkan kualitas permainan peserta secara keseluruhan.Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian deskriptif melalui metode survei. Populasi dalam penelitian ini populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah seluruh peserta ekstrakurikuler bola voli di SMP LPMD Suka Maju Rambah berjumlah 40 orang. Teknik penarikan sampel yang digunakan adalah Simple random sampling yaitu sampel sebanyak 20 orang yang dipilih secara acak sederhana. Instrumen yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini yaitu tes keterampilan servis atas bola voli. Teknik analisis data yaitu analisis deskriptif dengan menghitung nilai persentase P: F/N x 100 %. Hasil analisis data tes kemampuan servis atas dari analisis statistik deskriptif yang memperlihatkan nilai rata-rata (mean) sebesar 7,70, dengan skor terendah 6, skor tertinggi 10, standar deviasi sebesar 1,03, varians sebesar 1,06, dan rentang sebesar 4. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan servis peserta cukup baik dengan variasi kemampuan yang tidak terlalu signifikan antar peserta.

title: Oral contraceptive use and anterior cruciate ligament injury or reconstruction in women: A systematic review and meta‐analysis of very low‐certainty evidence
title_original: Oral contraceptive use and anterior cruciate ligament injury or reconstruction in women: A systematic review and meta‐analysis of very low‐certainty evidence
summary: Abstract Purpose To determine whether oral contraceptive use is associated with anterior cruciate ligament injury or reconstruction in women and to examine whether associations vary according to age, contraceptive formulation, duration of use and outcome definition. Methods PubMed, Scopus, Embase and Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS) were searched through 31 July 2026 (LILACS rerun with multilingual terms on 16 September 2026). Comparative observational studies were meta‐analysed. The primary analysis pooled adjusted or matched odds ratios (ORs) for reconstruction or operatively treated injury using random‐effects restricted maximum‐likelihood models with Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed with risk of bias in nonrandomised studies of exposures and certainty with grading of recommendations assessment, development and evaluation. Results Ten studies were included; seven were meta‐analysed. The primary analysis (four studies) showed no clear association (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.77–1.02; I 2 = 84%; τ 2 = 0.01; 95% prediction interval, 0.66–1.19). Two crude athlete studies and the active‐comparator cohort (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.89–1.01) also had CIs including 1. Adding one crude database estimate yielded OR 0.85 (95% CI, 0.74–0.98; I 2 = 90%; 95% prediction interval, 0.61–1.19). Leave‐one‐out results were unstable. The certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions The primary adjusted or matched analysis did not establish a clear association between oral contraceptive use and anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction or operatively treated injury; substantial heterogeneity, residual confounding and very low certainty of evidence preclude causal interpretation. Current evidence does not support initiating or selecting oral contraceptives for anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention. Well‐designed prospective studies with standardised exposure and outcome definitions are needed. Level of Evidence Level IV, systematic review of observational studies.

title: Perspectives in women's football (part 2) “time and money…money and time”: barriers faced by coaches of women & girls playing football in Australia, a mixed methods study
title_original: Perspectives in women's football (part 2) “time and money…money and time”: barriers faced by coaches of women & girls playing football in Australia, a mixed methods study
summary: Objective To explore characteristics and barriers faced by coaches of women's football in Australia. Design Cross-sectional survey study. Methods A convenience sample of coaches of women/girl's teams registered to play competitive football in Australia during the 2023/2024 season was recruited through targeted emails, social media, and physical fliers. Questionnaire data using open and closed questions were collected between May–September 2024. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and conventional content analysis. Results 44 coaches (17 women, 27 men) participated. Coaches generally reported having <10 years of coaching experience, with 34 (76%) being head coaches, and 16 coaches (36%) reported multiple coaching responsibilities with other teams or academies. Most coaches (84%) trained their teams 2 or more times per week, with an average of 116 training minutes per week. One coach reported that their team did not train. Twenty-nine coaches (66%) developed their own training plan, and most coaches (86%) had coached women or girls ≥50% of their career. Thirty-one coaches (70%) had access to coach education and training through their club or association. When asked "Has anything prevented them from achieving their full potential as a coach?", four categories were generated: competing priorities, financial burden, inadequate coaching support and individual factors. Conclusions Our study highlights the need to improve coaching pathways and monetary support to enable coaches to better support the next generation of women/girl football players in Australia.

title: Surveillance of Athletes’ Health in Resource-Constrained African Sports Contexts: Why Context Matters and Time To Catch Up
title_original: Surveillance of Athletes’ Health in Resource-Constrained African Sports Contexts: Why Context Matters and Time To Catch Up
summary: Athlete health surveillance is fundamental to understanding, preventing, and managing injuries, illnesses, and other health problems in sport. While standardized surveillance systems developed by organizations such as the International Olympic Committee (IOC) have substantially advanced sports medicine globally, their applicability across diverse African sporting environments remains insufficiently examined. Many existing surveillance approaches assume the availability of trained medical personnel, robust health infrastructure, standardized documentation systems, and stable sporting environments—conditions that are not readily accessible across Africa. The continent is not homogeneous; some countries and elite sporting programs have surveillance capacities comparable to international standards, while many others operate under significant resource constraints. This commentary aims to examine the limitations of conventional athlete health surveillance approaches in African settings and to advocate for context-sensitive, African-led surveillance systems capable of generating locally relevant evidence to inform injury prevention, health policy, and athlete welfare. Leveraging collaborations among African researchers, clinicians, universities, sports federations, healthcare organizations, and international partners offers an opportunity to develop sustainable surveillance systems while strengthening research and clinical capacity across the continent.

title: Gender eligibility regulations in international federations after 2022: Accommodation, transformation, and exclusion
title_original: Gender eligibility regulations in international federations after 2022: Accommodation, transformation, and exclusion
summary: In 2021, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) introduced the Framework on Fairness, Inclusion, and Non-Discrimination on the Basis of Gender Identity and Sex Variations, inviting international federations (IFs) to develop their own sport-specific competition policies for trans and Differences in Sex Development athletes. This article analyses the adoption of its 10 principles across 10 IFs, assessing whether the policies support transformative approaches to gender diversity in competitive sports. The findings show that IFs largely continue to reinforce restrictive norms, emphasizing testosterone thresholds while neglecting broader inclusivity. The analysed regulations rely on contested science, impose medical surveillance, and discriminate against affected athletes. The study highlights how the 2021 IOC Framework, despite its progressive rhetoric, failed to provide substantive guidance, thereby enabling IFs to actively produce exclusion by unknowing: ignoring readily available knowledge about gender diversity in elite sport.

title: CONSEQUÊNCIAS PSICOLÓGICAS DA APOSENTADORIA NÃO PLANEJADA E OS DESAFIOS EMOCIONAIS ENFRENTADOS POR ATLETAS SEM SUPORTE NO ENCERRAMENTO DA CARREIRA ESPORTIVA
title_original: CONSEQUÊNCIAS PSICOLÓGICAS DA APOSENTADORIA NÃO PLANEJADA E OS DESAFIOS EMOCIONAIS ENFRENTADOS POR ATLETAS SEM SUPORTE NO ENCERRAMENTO DA CARREIRA ESPORTIVA
summary: The transition from a sports career to post-competitive life constitutes a critical process, especially when it occurs abruptly or without planning. Athletes who experience this unexpected disconnection tend to show significant impacts in different dimensions, including physical, financial, psychological, and legal aspects. In the physical domain, the interruption of sports activities can result in loss of conditioning, functional limitations, and difficulties in adapting to a new lifestyle. From a financial perspective, the absence of proper planning can lead to economic instability, poor resource management, and debt. In the psychological field, difficulties related to the loss of athletic identity stand out, as well as the emergence of symptoms such as anxiety, depression, and a sense of emptiness. Additionally, legal and contractual issues may arise, especially in the face of a lack of legal guidance throughout the career. In this context, the present study aims to analyze the effects of unplanned sports retirement, with an emphasis on the risks to athletes' overall health. It is a literature review of national and international studies, which discusses the implications of detraining, economic instability, mental disorders, and contractual vulnerabilities in the lives of former athletes. The results indicate that the implementation of public policies and multidisciplinary follow-up programs is essential to promote a healthier transition and reduce the negative impacts of sports retirement.

title: Aging beyond older adults: Transdisciplinary perspectives on demographic change in Japan
title_original: Aging beyond older adults: Transdisciplinary perspectives on demographic change in Japan
summary: Population aging is increasingly recognized not merely as a demographic phenomenon, but as a broader societal transformation reshaping care systems, labor structures, infrastructure, communication, governance, and everyday social relations. Using Japan as an example of an advanced super-aged society, this paper examines how demographic aging and population shrinking interact with social, technological, institutional, and environmental systems across multiple domains of adaptation. Adopting a transdisciplinary narrative and integrative review approach, the study synthesizes literature spanning sustainability science, gerontology, migration studies, urban planning, linguistics, science and technology studies, and environmental governance. The analysis focuses on four interconnected domains: inclusive infrastructure and linguistic accessibility; technological adaptation and robotic care; caregiving, migration, and labor transformation; and nature-based well-being. The review demonstrates that adaptation in aging societies depends on hybrid systems that combine public welfare institutions, technological interventions, migration pathways, community-based support, and family caregiving. While Japan has advanced barrier-free infrastructure, Universal Design legislation, Yasashii Nihongo initiatives, long-term care systems, and assistive technologies, major tensions persist, including labor shortages, unequal caregiving burdens, technological dependence, and barriers to migrant integration. The findings also show that interventions initially designed for older adults frequently generate co-benefits for migrants, disabled persons, children, caregivers, and local communities. The paper argues that demographic aging cannot be effectively addressed by isolated sectoral or disciplinary responses. Instead, aging societies require integrated and adaptive approaches connecting infrastructure, labor systems, migration, communication, technology, environmental design, and caregiving across multiple stakeholder groups. Japan's experience offers insights for societies undergoing similar demographic transitions.

title: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
title_original: French Sports Diplomacy and Soft Power Acquisition
summary: This chapter examines the trajectory and future of French sports diplomacy in the wake of the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games. While the Games were widely acclaimed as a success, they also signalled the end of a political and diplomatic cycle in which mega-events served as the cornerstone of France&s;s international influence. This raises a central question: does France possess a coherent and durable sport diplomacy, or has it relied primarily on the opportunistic use of major events to project its image abroad? The chapter traces the institutionalisation of sports diplomacy in France since the early 2010s, through initiatives such as the appointment of a Sport Ambassador and the creation of interministerial structures. It highlights notable achievements—including the Paris 2024 bid, greater French representation in international federations, and the global recognition of organisational expertise—while underscoring enduring structural, political, and conjunctural limitations. The analysis ultimately argues that the future of French sports diplomacy will depend on its ability to move beyond an event-driven approach and to articulate a sustainable, strategically integrated vision of sport as an instrument of foreign policy.

title: Systematic process for design and manufacturing of ergonomic handles for para-table tennis: a case study
title_original: Systematic process for design and manufacturing of ergonomic handles for para-table tennis: a case study
summary: Abstract Wheelchair table tennis serves as an affordable and accessible means of enhancing the physical and psychological well-being of individuals with tetraplegia; however, limited hand mobility and grip strength continue to constrain performance. To address these issues, this study presents a systematic, end-to-end workflow for designing and manufacturing customized, competition-legal table tennis handles tailored to tetraplegic athletes, evaluated through a single-athlete feasibility case study rather than a clinical or sports-performance validation. The process integrates hand geometry capture, computer-aided design (CAD) refinement through iterative additive prototyping, and final fabrication using optimized materials and surface finishing. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a case study was conducted comparing an athlete’s performance using the old and new handles in terms of accuracy, control, and overall playing performance. In this single-athlete case study, successful shots showed roughly $$2.4\times$$ the odds of success with the new handle across drills. As a proof-of-concept evaluation, these findings are preliminary and indicate an association observed in one athlete, not a demonstrated causal effect, and are not intended to generalise to tetraplegic players more broadly. The customized handle was also reported by the athlete to be more comfortable and easier to use.
