title: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
title_original: Olympic-patterned pentaboron emitter featuring highly distorted geometry enables efficient solution-processed ultrapure green OLEDs
summary: Efficient, ultrapure green organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) fabricated via wet processing are crucial for ultrahigh definition displays but remain highly challenging due to the paucity of suitable emitters. Herein, we developed Oly-BN, a novel multipleresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitter featuring a distinct Olympic-patterned boron-distribution. The zigzag doped heteroatom polycyclic aromatic framework enables near-degenerate singlet/triplet excited states. Integrating para-N-π-B motifs helps regulate the triplet manifold and emission color point, enabling energetically accessible higher lying triplet excited states with enhanced spinorbit coupling, while also suppressing low-frequency structural relaxation and modulating the optical bandgap. Oly-BN in toluene exhibits vivid green emission at 522 nm with a narrow full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 17 nm, a photoluminescence quantum yield of 95%, and a fast reverse intersystem crossing rate constant of 6.9×106 s−1. Additionally, its highly twisted conformation weakens intermolecular interactions and favors bright, solid-state emission. The nonsensitized solution-processed OLEDs deliver ultrapure green electroluminescence with a CIEy value up to 0.73, and achieves an optimized maximum external quantum efficiency of 39.4%, which remains high at 29.9% at 1000 cd m-2. This work not only provides a promising highly saturated green emitter for solution-processed OLEDs but also demonstrates the importance of precisely integrating heteroatoms in modulating photophysical properties of MR-TADF emitters.

title: From norms to practice: benchmarking International Sports Federations against the UN anti-corruption framework
title_original: From norms to practice: benchmarking International Sports Federations against the UN anti-corruption framework
summary: Abstract International Sports Federations (ISFs) occupy a structurally unique position in the global governance landscape: private associations incorporated under Swiss civil law that simultaneously exercise binding transnational regulatory authority over their respective sports domains. While Swiss association law is the dominant legal form across the Olympic Movement, this sample is intentionally jurisdictionally diverse, spanning Swiss, German, British, and Malaysian entities. Since each of these jurisdictions is party to UNCAC, the UNODC benchmark applies consistently across the sample irrespective of where each federation is headquarted. Although the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (United Nations 2004) and a comprehensive suite of UNODC guidance instruments have established precise standards for private organisations, no systematic empirical study has evaluated the extent to which ISF anti-corruption frameworks reflect these standards. This study addresses that gap through a researcher-led normative document benchmarking study of six summer Olympic ISFs, selected across three governance tiers identified by the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations (ASOIF) governance assessment. Employing a 41-question, four-point scoring instrument derived directly from five UNODC source documents, the study evaluates each ISF’s publicly available governance instruments against eight dimensions: leadership commitment, risk assessment, prohibited conduct scope, financial integrity, conflict of interest management, reporting mechanisms, training and education, and enforcement architecture. The findings reveal a structural pattern of partial alignment: ISFs demonstrate reasonable policy coverage at the level of normative commitments but systematic deficiency at the operational and oversight levels. Most critically, all six federations exhibit a significant deficit of internal financial crime controls. This absence encompasses gaps in corruption risk assessment, post-employment restrictions, and the structural independence of investigatory functions. The study concludes with a typology of governance archetypes observable across the cohort and targeted policy recommendations grounded in the UNODC normative architecture.

title: Powerless and overlooked: a longitudinal examination of marginalised communities in major sport events
title_original: Powerless and overlooked: a longitudinal examination of marginalised communities in major sport events
summary: The agenda of hosting major sport events (MSEs) has long been a political priority, promising transformation for host communities, yet the experiences of vulnerable and marginalised populations within this agenda remain understudied. This study examines how marginalisation is manifested in the context of MSEs, the extent to which legacy promises align with marginalised residents’ needs and interests, and how power dynamics shape their experiences and engagement with such events. Drawing on Lukes’ theory of power, the study adopts a longitudinal qualitative design, collecting data through seven focus groups with disadvantaged communities before and after the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games. Data were analysed following the principles of qualitative longitudinal research, integrating analysis of themes, cases, and time, attending to temporal depth and process. Findings showed that existing socioeconomic challenges shaped participants’ perceptions of the Games and reinforced their exclusion, with event priorities and recognition of needs structured by uneven power relations instead of a straightforward balance of benefits and costs. A persistent divide between material needs and aspirational interests left event participation secondary for marginalised residents, while promotional rhetoric intensified feelings of exclusion where structural barriers and unmet needs remained unaddressed. Longitudinal comparison revealed more continuity than change, as distrust in government and daily struggles sustained a self-perpetuating cycle of disengagement. Extending theories of power through an intersectional lens, the study highlights the importance of MSE planning and legacy delivery that recognises marginalised populations and addresses underlying inequalities, so that the benefits of hosting such events can be more equitably shared.

title: Effects of Acute Caffeine Supplementation on Performance and Physiological Responses in CrossFit: A Systematic Review and Three-Level Meta-Analysis
title_original: Effects of Acute Caffeine Supplementation on Performance and Physiological Responses in CrossFit: A Systematic Review and Three-Level Meta-Analysis
summary: Objectives: We quantified the influence of acute caffeine (CAF) supplementation on CrossFit performance and physiological outcomes and examined potential effect modifiers. Methods: Randomized crossover studies involving CAF supplementation in CrossFit were identified through systematic searches of multiple electronic databases. Performance effect sizes were expressed as Hedges’ g and pooled within a three-level random-effects framework, while physiological outcomes were synthesized using conventional two-level models. Effect modification was examined across training status (recreationally active vs. trained) and CAF delivery form (capsule vs. beverage). Meta-regression was additionally used to assess whether relative CAF dose was associated with changes in CrossFit performance. Results: The final synthesis comprised seven studies with 103 participants, including 13 women. A small favorable effect of CAF was found for overall CrossFit performance (g = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.05–0.22), accompanied by a higher blood lactate concentration (g = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.23–0.82). Stratified estimates favored CAF in recreationally active participants (g = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.06–0.34) and when administered in capsule form (g = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.06–0.29); nevertheless, evidence for between-subgroup differences was absent (all p subgroup > 0.05). The relative CAF dose did not explain variation in performance effects in either the linear (β1 = 0.04, p = 0.570) or nonlinear model (β2 = −0.004, p = 0.578). Conclusions: The available evidence suggests a small ergogenic benefit of acute CAF supplementation for selected CrossFit performance outcomes, accompanied by elevated blood lactate concentrations. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant moderating effect of training status and supplementation protocols. However, the limited number of studies and predominance of male participants warrant cautious interpretation. Future research should prioritize larger randomized controlled trials, greater representation of female athletes, and more standardized CrossFit performance protocols.

title: Acute caffeine strategies for improving performance in combat sports: a structured narrative review
title_original: Acute caffeine strategies for improving performance in combat sports: a structured narrative review
summary: Objective: This structured narrative review updates and contextualizes evidence on acute caffeine strategies in combat sports, with emphasis on performance effects, delivery form, combined interventions, and factors that may explain inconsistent findings. Methods: A structured literature search was conducted in Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, PubMed, and SPORTDiscus. Eligible reports involved trained amateur, competitive, or professional combat sport athletes, evaluated an acute caffeine intervention administered before or during exercise or sport specific performance testing, and included at least one physical, cognitive, or technical tactical performance outcome. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity in sport discipline, caffeine protocol, comparator, and outcome measures. Results: Forty three reports met the eligibility criteria. Fourteen evaluated combined caffeine protocols, whereas 29 evaluated caffeine supplementation alone. Combined protocols included caffeine with sodium bicarbonate, carbohydrate, L theanine, Rhodiola rosea, warm up music, conditioning activity, post activation performance enhancement, or mouth rinsing. These strategies showed potential context specific benefits, particularly when caffeine was combined with warm up music or conditioning activity, but they did not establish a general advantage over isolated caffeine supplementation. For caffeine supplementation alone, favorable findings were reported for selected simulated combat outcomes, Special Judo Fitness Test performance, strength, power, muscular endurance, reaction related outcomes, and repeated high intensity activity. However, null findings were also common, even within commonly used doses of 3 to 6 mg/kg. Perceived exertion and heart rate were generally unchanged, whereas blood lactate more frequently increased following caffeine ingestion. Conclusions: Acute caffeine supplementation may improve selected performance outcomes in combat sport athletes, but responses vary across disciplines, tasks, athlete characteristics, dosing strategies, delivery forms, and competition formats. Doses of 3 to 6 mg/kg remain the most frequently studied protocols, but individual responses should be assessed during training before competition. Evidence for high or repeated doses, rapid delivery forms, and combined strategies remains preliminary.

title: Homo Olympicus: Olimpismo como instrumento de formação humana
title_original: Homo Olympicus: Olimpismo como instrumento de formação humana
summary: In Brazil, Physical Education training has historically favored biological and technicist approaches to the detriment of philosophical, sociological and humanistic foundations aimed at the integral understanding of the human being. In this context, Olympism, conceived by Pierre de Coubertin as a philosophy of life based on the balance between body, mind and spirit, presents itself as an important pedagogical possibility for contemporary physical education. This theoretical essay aimed to analyze the concept of Homo Olympicus in contemporary society and discuss how Olympic Education can contribute to human formation in the context of contemporary educational and school sport. It is a theoretical essay, with a qualitative approach and analytical-descriptive character, based on bibliographic review and documentary analysis. The theoretical path was structured from the category’s philosophy of education, sports pedagogy, corporeality, fair play, educational sport and the anthropological concepts of Homo Ludens, Homo Gymnasticus, Homo Sportivus and Homo Olympicus. The results indicate that Olympic Education expands the pedagogical possibilities of sport by overcoming the restricted logic of performance and hypercompetitiveness, valuing principles such as respect, friendship, cooperation, excellence and citizenship. It was also evidenced that informal fair play and the valorization of corporeality contribute to overcoming reductionist perspectives present in school Physical Education. It is concluded that Olympism can be understood as a philosophy of education and a formative instrument for the construction of critical, autonomous and socially committed subjects.
abstract: In Brazil, Physical Education training has historically favored biological and technicist approaches to the detriment of philosophical, sociological and humanistic foundations aimed at the integral understanding of the human being. In this context, Olympism, conceived by Pierre de Coubertin as a philosophy of life based on the balance between body, mind and spirit, presents itself as an important pedagogical possibility for contemporary physical education. This theoretical essay aimed to analyze the concept of Homo Olympicus in contemporary society and discuss how Olympic Education can contribute to human formation in the context of contemporary educational and school sport. It is a theoretical essay, with a qualitative approach and analytical-descriptive character, based on bibliographic review and documentary analysis. The theoretical path was structured from the category’s philosophy of education, sports pedagogy, corporeality, fair play, educational sport and the anthropological concepts of Homo Ludens, Homo Gymnasticus, Homo Sportivus and Homo Olympicus. The results indicate that Olympic Education expands the pedagogical possibilities of sport by overcoming the restricted logic of performance and hypercompetitiveness, valuing principles such as respect, friendship, cooperation, excellence and citizenship. It was also evidenced that informal fair play and the valorization of corporeality contribute to overcoming reductionist perspectives present in school Physical Education. It is concluded that Olympism can be understood as a philosophy of education and a formative instrument for the construction of critical, autonomous and socially committed subjects.

title: Purity, dirt and danger: symbolic dimensions of anti-doping in elite sports
title_original: Purity, dirt and danger: symbolic dimensions of anti-doping in elite sports
summary: This article critically explores elite athletes’ accounts on anti-doping policy and practice and how ideas of purity, dirt and danger shape their experiences and actions within it. Theoretically, we draw from Mary Douglas’ influential ideas on purity and danger. These ideas encompass the idea that separating dirtiness from cleanness provides a way to systematically create and maintain symbolic, societal and cultural order. A secondary analysis of data from 13 qualitative interviews with elite athletes in three different sports dispersed over five geographical continents shows a strict conviction of the importance of distinguishing the pure from the impure. The analysis played out as practices and experiences of assurance, regulation and shaming. Athletes respond to the perceived danger of crossing purity boundaries by enacting precise measures to avoid ‘pollution’, positioning their own bodies as sites for constructing and defending these boundaries. This article contributes important insights for policymakers by demonstrating how anti-doping practices may reinforce moral hierarchies that stigmatise certain athletes. We argue that understanding the symbolic dimensions of purity in anti-doping efforts is essential for developing fairer, more inclusive sport governance.

title: Tirzepatide in Sport after Inclusion in the WADA Monitoring Program: An Updated Narrative Review of Body Composition, Muscle Preservation and Potential Performance Implications
title_original: Tirzepatide in Sport after Inclusion in the WADA Monitoring Program: An Updated Narrative Review of Body Composition, Muscle Preservation and Potential Performance Implications
summary: Background: Tirzepatide, as a dual agonist of the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors, has become one of the most effective pharmacological therapies used to treat obesity and metabolic disorders. Growing interest in its potential use among physically active individuals and the inclusion of tirzepatide markers in the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) monitoring program for 2026 highlight the need to reassess the significance of this substance in sports. Aim: The aim of this study was to update the available data on tirzepatide in the context of sports. Material and methods: A narrative review of the current literature on tirzepatide, incretin receptor agonists and their use in the context of sports was conducted. The analysis included clinical trials, systematic reviews, publications on body composition, metabolism, and exercise adaptation, as well as WADA regulatory documents. Results: Tirzepatide effectively reduces body weight and improves metabolic parameters. However, available evidence mainly concerns individuals with obesity or type 2 diabetes, rather than athletes. Changes in lean body mass during therapy may be relevant for physically active individuals, especially in sports requiring high strength and power. Although weight reduction could be beneficial in weight-class sports. Further studies are needed to assess the long-term impact of tirzepatide on athletic performance and to address the ethical issues associated with its use. Conclusions: Tirzepatide currently has no proven effect on enhancing athletic performance. However, its impact on body weight and body composition may be important for athletes. The inclusion of tirzepatide in WADA’s monitoring program highlights the need for further research into its potential misuse, its effects on muscle, and the long-term consequences of its utilization in the athletic population.

title: Correction of psychosomatic status in veterans during the early rehabilitation stage after combat injury: A cross-sectional study
title_original: Correction of psychosomatic status in veterans during the early rehabilitation stage after combat injury: A cross-sectional study
summary: Introduction. The prevalence of long-term psychosomatic consequences of combat stress and combat injury (up to 48.3% three years later) justifies the relevance of identifying targets for psychosomatic status correction already during the early rehabilitation stage. Numerous reports of hyperactivation of the sympathoadrenal and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal systems as a central pathophysiological link in excessive allostatic load and the breakdown of adaptation emphasize the need to consider autonomic disorders as an independent target for psychological and psychophysiological intervention. Objective. To substantiate autonomic dysregulation as a target for correcting psychosomatic status within a psychological intervention framework during early rehabilitation in veterans who sustained combat injuries. Materials and methods. The study included 54 male combat veterans aged 18–55 years (mean age: 29 ± 9.3 years) with documented frontline exposure of at least six months. Assessments were performed on postoperative days 3–5 following surgery for combined blast-induced injuries. Based on the severity of post-traumatic symptoms, participants were stratified into three groups: Group 1 ( n = 20, 38%): no symptoms; Group 2 ( n = 22, 40%): subclinical symptomatology; Group 3 ( n = 12, 22%): pronounced symptomatology. The study used psychodiagnostic testing and assessment of the functional state of the autonomic nervous system based on heart rate variability parameters, performed by variational cardiointervalometry (UPFT-1/30 Psychophysiologist). Mathematical and statistical processing of the results was performed using the Statgraphics Plus statistical software package. Results. The intensification of post-traumatic stress reactions occurs against the background of exacerbation of neurotic and somatic complaints. The predominance of the central regulatory circuit is a key pathogenetic mechanism in the development of psychosomatic disorders. Direct correlations were found between the intensity of somatic complaints and the degree of psychological maladaptation ( r = 0.978, p ≤ 0.01). It was established that 100% of military personnel with a high level of psychological adaptation (≤ 70 points) had types I and II of autonomic regulation (predominance of the central circuit). Comprehensive assessment of their autonomic status suggests the transformation of mental symptomatology into autonomic nervous system dysregulation, which at this stage is detectable only by instrumental methods. The increased tension of regulatory systems and enhanced activity of stress-implementing systems of autonomic regulation in this group of patients directly correlate with inverted anxiety ( r = 0.671, p ≤ 0.01) and conversion ( r = 0.493, p ≤ 0.01) scales, indicating compensatory hyperactivation of the central regulatory circuit as a physiological basis for maintaining a state of psychological well-being. Conclusions. Psychological maladaptation and somatic complaints are pathodynamically associated with vegetative dysregulation. The system of early psychological intervention during the inpatient rehabilitation stage should be aimed at preventing the development of delayed psychosomatic disorders and should be structured taking into account the severity of post-traumatic symptomatology and the functional state of the autonomic nervous system. In addition to routine psychodiagnostic methods, functional assessment of the autonomic nervous system is recommended. Mandatory cognitive behavioral psychotherapy, as prescribed by current clinical guidelines, should be complemented by psychophysiological rehabilitation interventions aimed at restoring vagosympathetic balance.

title: A transatlantic cleavage in sport regulation: French policy responses to the Enhanced Games
title_original: A transatlantic cleavage in sport regulation: French policy responses to the Enhanced Games
summary: This article examines how the Enhanced Games (EG), a sporting competition explicitly permitting the use of performance-enhancing pharmacological substances, destabilize national sport regulation in France. Drawing on the participation of French sprinter Mouhamadou Fall, the only French athlete officially engaged in the inaugural edition of the EG, we analyze the rhetorical and institutional confrontations triggered by his public announcement of October 23, 2025. The public stance taken by an elite athlete already sanctioned for doping and unlicensed since 2023 compelled sporting authorities to make their moral and regulatory boundaries explicit. The study combines three empirical sources: Fall's public statements between October 2025 and May 2026 (press interviews, a long-form YouTube interview, an EG promotional video, and Instagram posts, n = 54); a review of the French press from June 2023 onward ( n = 97); and institutional communications from French and international sporting and anti-doping bodies ( n = 4). Results show that Mouhamadou Fall deploys three registers of legitimation: bodily autonomy, medical supervision, and fair remuneration for sporting labor. French institutions respond with a coordinated normative reaffirmation, without engaging substantively with the health or economic questions raised. This case reveals a displacement of the doping controversy toward a dispute over status, value, and the governance of sporting labor, and crystallizes a transatlantic cleavage between the European tradition of public regulation and a market-driven logic of performance contracting.

title: Old argumentative plays on a new field? Contributions from sport ethics to the ethical analysis of artificial intelligence
title_original: Old argumentative plays on a new field? Contributions from sport ethics to the ethical analysis of artificial intelligence
summary: Abstract In the ethics of artificial intelligence, a recurring anxiety concerns the deskilling argument: the worry that delegating distinctively human tasks to AI erodes valuable capacities and there by diminishes meaning. This article argues that philosophy of sport offers underutilized but illuminating resources for analyzing this concern. Drawing ondebates over biomedical enhancement in sport ethics, I identify four argumentative strategies—centered on the values of agency, effort, natural talent, and narrativity—that sport philosophers have developed to evaluate themoral costs of skill-displacing technology. These “old plays,” I contend, can be productively transplanted onto the “new field” of AI ethics, where analogous debates about skill erosion, meritocracy, difficulty, and human identityremain contested. Sports, understood as games of physical skill, constitute a privileged analytical setting: their emphasis on process over outcome makes the exercise of skill especially visible and prominent. By recovering insights from thinkers such as Bernard Suits, Scott Kretchmar, John Gleaves, Michael Sandel, and Alasdair MacIntyre,this article advances two aims: to vindicate the philosophical contribution of sport ethics as a discipline, and to enrich normative reflection on AI’s deskilling potential with arguments already tested in analogous debates.

title: Impact of Allergic Rhinitis-Induced Sleep Disruption on Cognition and Physical Performance in Athletes: A Narrative Review
title_original: Impact of Allergic Rhinitis-Induced Sleep Disruption on Cognition and Physical Performance in Athletes: A Narrative Review
summary: Background: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a pervasive condition among competitive athletes, especially in endurance and aquatic disciplines. IgE-mediated Th2-type inflammation causes mucosal edema and increased upper airway resistance, forcing nocturnal mouth-breathing mechanics. This instability triggers frequent micro-arousals and disrupts sleep architecture, leading to documented reductions in restorative slow-wave and rapid eye movement sleep. Aim: To synthesize evidence on how AR-mediated sleep fragmentation degrades neurocognitive function, motor control, and physical output in athletes, while evaluating the safety and efficacy of contemporary pharmacotherapy. Material and methods: Narrative review integrating clinical, immunological, somnological, and sports science research from primary databases, including PubMed and Scopus. Results: Systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines and nocturnal airway obstruction disrupt sleep-wake regulation centers. Resulting fragmentation impairs executive function, spatial working memory, and reaction times. Physiological decrements manifest as reduced aerobic efficiency, decreased explosive power, and diminished agility, often accompanied by an elevated rate of perceived exertion. While sedating first-generation antihistamines further impair performance and sleep architecture, intranasal corticosteroids and second-generation antihistamines provide effective symptom relief without cognitive impairment or World Anti-Doping Agency compliance issues. Conclusions: AR-induced sleep disruption is a significant, underdiagnosed performance-limiting factor. Proactive allergy screening, longitudinal sleep tracking, and the optimization of non-sedating therapeutic regimens are essential for safeguarding athlete health and maintaining the competitive edge.

title: Ultra-processed Foods and Athletes: Current Insights on Classification, Use, Awareness, and Impact—A Narrative Review
title_original: Ultra-processed Foods and Athletes: Current Insights on Classification, Use, Awareness, and Impact—A Narrative Review
summary: There is growing concern about the impact of food processing on human health and planetary health, with greater dietary exposure to ultra-processed foods being associated with a higher risk of adverse health outcomes. While athletes are encouraged to follow a food first approach, there are situations, where meeting performance goals is not achievable with everyday foods and drinks. In such cases, sports foods, protein-fortified foods, or discretionary foods, which due to their formulation are typically ultra-processed, may be recommended to help achieve specific goals. This review aimed to summarise the existing research on patterns of sports food and ultra-processed food use by athletes. A narrative review methodology was employed. Relevant literature was identified via searches in Google Scholar, Scopus, Web of Science and peak sporting body websites. There is little research on athletes and planetary health. Consumer awareness and knowledge of ultra-processed foods is an emerging area of research; no published studies in athletes were identified. The frequency of processed foods consumption by athletes has been explored in four small studies, with results suggesting frequent use of ultra-processed foods, though classification inconsistencies limit application. No studies specifically asked athletes about their reasons for consuming ultra-processed foods. Convenience and performance were common considerations for athletes when choosing general and sports foods. Benefits of ultra-processed food consumption include microbiological safety, convenience and ease of use. Current literature offers limited insight into how planetary health considerations influence athletes' food choices, and athletes' knowledge, awareness and consumption of ultra-processed foods. Further research is needed to understand the prevalence and patterns of use of sports foods and ultra-processed foods, and how dietitians/nutritionists can help athletes optimise their nutritional strategies which support performance and promote planetary health.

title: Eating for performance: an evaluation of food consumption patterns and adherence to dietary guidelines in elite wheelchair basketball players
title_original: Eating for performance: an evaluation of food consumption patterns and adherence to dietary guidelines in elite wheelchair basketball players
summary: This study evaluated dietary habits, hydration practices and adherence to nutritional recommendations in elite Spanish wheelchair basketball players, examining differences by sex and functional classification. Sixty-six athletes from first-division teams completed the validated Food4Me Food Frequency Questionnaire, and adherence was assessed using national dietary guidelines. Overall compliance with recommendations was low, the most athletes consumed fruits, vegetables, legumes, cereals and fish below recommended frequencies, while dairy, red meat and eggs generally met guidelines. Fruit intake was below recommendations in all women and in 91.2% of men, and a significant sex difference emerged only for dairy, with lower consumption in women. By functional classification, dairy intake was also lower among athletes with greater functional limitation. Most players (80.3%) did not follow any specific diet. Hydration practices were suboptimal, with 66.7% of women consuming ≤0.5 L of water during training compared with 15.8% of men, and athletes with grade 1 functionality drinking less water during matches than those with grade 4. These findings indicate limited adherence to dietary guidelines and insufficient hydration practices in this population, underscoring the need for tailored, disability-informed nutritional education strategies to support dietary adequacy and performance.

title: Percentile-Based Normative Standards for Strength Assessment Beyond Linear Bodyweight Multipliers in Competitive Powerlifters
title_original: Percentile-Based Normative Standards for Strength Assessment Beyond Linear Bodyweight Multipliers in Competitive Powerlifters
summary: BACKGROUND: Bodyweight multipliers (BM = L/M, where L denotes the absolute load lifted in kilograms and M the athlete's recorded body mass) represent the dominant benchmarking heuristic in strength and conditioning. However, because relative strength declines non-linearly with body mass, a single fixed threshold is not equally attainable across the body-mass spectrum, and these static standards provide no lift-specific, percentile-based reference for practitioner use. METHODS: A large-scale dataset of drug-tested, classic competitive powerlifters was analyzed to establish empirical percentile-based normative standards. A "Best-Ever" filter was applied to isolate each athlete's peak performance, yielding a final sample of N = 101,898 athletes (aged 21-49). Quantile regression was employed to independently estimate normative percentiles (50th, 75th, 90th, and 99th) and evaluate mass-dependent changes in relative strength across all three lifts. A Loess smoothing procedure was applied to percentile values summarized across weight classes to visualize mass-dependent performance trends. All athletes were retrospectively mapped into current International Powerlifting Federation (IPF) weight categories to produce absolute-load normative atlases stratified by lift, sex, and weight class. The internal lift ratio, the percentage contribution of each lift to the competitive total, was additionally quantified across the mass spectrum. RESULTS: A systematic, non-linear decrease in relative BMs was observed across all performance percentiles (p < 0.001). The smoothed male 99th percentile deadlift multiplier declined from 4.37 in the 59 kg class to 2.65 in the 120+ kg category. A progressive mass-dependent decline was identified, with the rate of relative strength decay becoming significantly steeper at elite tiers (99th percentile) compared to intermediate levels (50th percentile). Female athletes exhibited a steeper mass-dependent decline in bench press and squat performance compared to males. The internal lift ratio shifted systematically from deadlift-dominance in lightweight categories (~ 42%-45%) to a substantially narrower gap between deadlift and squat contribution in heavyweight classes (~ 39% vs ~37%). CONCLUSION: Traditional linear BM benchmarks are not equally attainable across body-mass classes and lack the resolution to support lift-specific athlete assessment. The empirical percentile-based normative framework established in this study provides coaches and researchers with a transparent, data-driven tool that accurately reflects the distribution of competitive performance across body mass categories. A practical normative atlas expressed in absolute kilograms is provided as a directly applicable field tool.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bodyweight multipliers (BM = L/M, where L denotes the absolute load lifted in kilograms and M the athlete's recorded body mass) represent the dominant benchmarking heuristic in strength and conditioning. However, because relative strength declines non-linearly with body mass, a single fixed threshold is not equally attainable across the body-mass spectrum, and these static standards provide no lift-specific, percentile-based reference for practitioner use. METHODS: A large-scale dataset of drug-tested, classic competitive powerlifters was analyzed to establish empirical percentile-based normative standards. A "Best-Ever" filter was applied to isolate each athlete's peak performance, yielding a final sample of N = 101,898 athletes (aged 21-49). Quantile regression was employed to independently estimate normative percentiles (50th, 75th, 90th, and 99th) and evaluate mass-dependent changes in relative strength across all three lifts. A Loess smoothing procedure was applied to percentile values summarized across weight classes to visualize mass-dependent performance trends. All athletes were retrospectively mapped into current International Powerlifting Federation (IPF) weight categories to produce absolute-load normative atlases stratified by lift, sex, and weight class. The internal lift ratio, the percentage contribution of each lift to the competitive total, was additionally quantified across the mass spectrum. RESULTS: A systematic, non-linear decrease in relative BMs was observed across all performance percentiles (p < 0.001). The smoothed male 99th percentile deadlift multiplier declined from 4.37 in the 59 kg class to 2.65 in the 120+ kg category. A progressive mass-dependent decline was identified, with the rate of relative strength decay becoming significantly steeper at elite tiers (99th percentile) compared to intermediate levels (50th percentile). Female athletes exhibited a steeper mass-dependent decline in bench press and squat performance compared to males. The internal lift ratio shifted systematically from deadlift-dominance in lightweight categories (~ 42%-45%) to a substantially narrower gap between deadlift and squat contribution in heavyweight classes (~ 39% vs ~37%). CONCLUSION: Traditional linear BM benchmarks are not equally attainable across body-mass classes and lack the resolution to support lift-specific athlete assessment. The empirical percentile-based normative framework established in this study provides coaches and researchers with a transparent, data-driven tool that accurately reflects the distribution of competitive performance across body mass categories. A practical normative atlas expressed in absolute kilograms is provided as a directly applicable field tool.

title: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR SPORTS MANAGEMENT IN SUPPORTING PEOPLE WITH EPILEPSY IN SPORT
title_original: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR SPORTS MANAGEMENT IN SUPPORTING PEOPLE WITH EPILEPSY IN SPORT
summary: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that affects millions of people worldwide, including professional athletes. Despite the historical stigma surrounding the condition, numerous prominent athletes have achieved elite-level careers, challenging stereotypes about its limitations. This paper explores the relationship between epilepsy and sport, focusing on successful athletes diagnosed with epilepsy and the impact of the condition on their careers. It also analyzes the role of sports management in creating an inclusive environment by identifying barriers, opportunities, and strategies for improving managerial practice. Through an interdisciplinary approach, the study offers concrete guidelines for sports institutions, educational systems, and public policy, with particular emphasis on comparative recommendations for Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. From a management perspective, the research examines how sports programs can be designed, organized, and monitored to ensure that they are inclusive, safe, and sustainable. A managerial approach enables structured risk and resource management, thereby creating a sustainable, long-term support system for people with epilepsy in sport.

title: THE ROLE OF MENTAL HEALTH IN COMPETITIVE SPORT: PREVALENCE, RISK FACTORS, AND MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES OF PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS AMONG ATHLETES
title_original: THE ROLE OF MENTAL HEALTH IN COMPETITIVE SPORT: PREVALENCE, RISK FACTORS, AND MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES OF PSYCHIATRIC CONDITIONS AMONG ATHLETES
summary: Background. Historically, the sports culture has prioritized "mental toughness," often viewing psychological vulnerability as a contradiction to elite performance. However, growing evidence suggests that competitive athletes face a unique constellation of various stressors, which if not identified early and treated adequately, may result in mental health disorders. Aim. To draw attention to the importance of psychological well-being of an athlete detailing prevalence, risk factors and specifics of various mental health conditions in competitive sports and to outline the role of integrated management strategies. Material and methods. A narrative review of existing literature was conducted, incorporating cross-sectional surveys, prospective cohort studies and systematic reviews focused on elite and ultra-endurance athletes. Results. Prevalence rates for mental health symptoms in athletes are comparable or even higher than among the general population, with depression and anxiety affecting up to 34% of elite cohorts. Specific risk factors include musculoskeletal injuries, career transitions, and the individual nature of certain sport disciplines. Conclusions. Integrated management requires a core multidisciplinary team (CMT) to provide holistic care that balances clinical stability with athletic performance maintenance.

title: СОЦІАЛЬНИЙ ЗАХИСТ СПОРТСМЕНІВ У СИСТЕМІ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ СПОРТУ: РОЛЬ СПОРТИВНИХ ФЕДЕРАЦІЙ У ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННІ ОРГАНІЗАЦІЙНО-ПРАВОВИХ МЕХАНІЗМІВ
title_original: СОЦІАЛЬНИЙ ЗАХИСТ СПОРТСМЕНІВ У СИСТЕМІ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ СПОРТУ: РОЛЬ СПОРТИВНИХ ФЕДЕРАЦІЙ У ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННІ ОРГАНІЗАЦІЙНО-ПРАВОВИХ МЕХАНІЗМІВ
summary: The professionalisation and commercialisation of modern sport intensify the risks of injury, psychological exhaustion, contractual instability, and athletes’ legal vulnerability, necessitating the development of a comprehensive system of social protection. Existing regulation remains fragmented due to the coexistence of public law norms and the internal rules of sports organisations, as well as the uneven institutional capacity of sports federations to ensure standards, monitor their implementation, and provide access to effective legal protection. Materials and methods. The aim of this study is to examine the role of sports federations as institutional integrators of athletes’ social protection within the framework of sustainable sport development and to develop organisational and legal mechanisms for its implementation. The methodology combines a systems approach, doctrinal legal analysis, comparative legal analysis, and legal modelling to construct a multi-level governance architecture. Results. Athletes’ social protection is defined as a comprehensive set of legal, organisational, financial, and medical-psychological guarantees, covering labour and quasi-labour relations, insurance and compensation, medical support, mental health, safeguarding, protection of minors, maternity and paternity support, dual careers, integrity mechanisms, independent dispute resolution, and personal data protection. An organisational-legal model of “state – sports federation – club/organiser” is proposed, featuring a clear allocation of competences, coordination and control mechanisms, compliance tools, and independent complaint-review procedures. A system of process-based monitoring indicators is developed, with the potential to evolve into performance indicators. Conclusions. The findings indicate that sports federations perform a key integrative function in aligning social policies and transforming public law requirements into replicable practices. The proposed model has practical significance for improving governance efficiency, decision predictability, accountability, and trust in sport institutions. It may also serve as a methodological basis for developing internal federation regulations, standard contracts, insurance programmes, safe-environment policies, and monitoring procedures. Further research should focus on testing the proposed model and validating the indicators across different sport contexts.

title: Depression in Competitive Athletes and Antidepressant Treatment: A Narrative Review of the Efficacy of Drugs From Different Classes and Their Impact on Sports Performance.
title_original: Depression in Competitive Athletes and Antidepressant Treatment: A Narrative Review of the Efficacy of Drugs From Different Classes and Their Impact on Sports Performance.
summary: The aim of this narrative review was to collect and critically appraise the existing findings on the pharmacological treatment of depression in competitive athletes, with particular emphasis on antidepressant drugs from different classes and their impact on physical performance and anti-doping status. Material and methods. The PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science databases were searched for papers published between 1990 and 2025, combining terms related to depression, competitive sport and individual drug classes. Clinical studies, reviews and expert statements were included. Results. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors remain the first-line treatment owing to their favorable safety profile, although their adverse effects may affect training. Serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors and bupropion require consideration of cardiovascular and thermoregulatory effects. Tricyclic antidepressants are now used less often because of cardiotoxicity. The anti-doping status of most drugs is permitted, yet some substances are subject to monitoring. Conclusions. Therapeutic decisions in athletes should be individualized, taking into account the discipline, the adverse-effect profile and anti-doping regulations. Randomized trials in this population are lacking.

title: Intersectional futures: gender equity, transgender inclusion, and the politics of sport governance in Alberta
title_original: Intersectional futures: gender equity, transgender inclusion, and the politics of sport governance in Alberta
summary: This paper examines the intersection of gender equity, transgender inclusion, and sport governance in Alberta within a broader context of colonialism, misogyny, and digital gender-based violence. Drawing on intersectional feminist theory, critical sport scholarship, and contemporary policy analysis, we argue that Alberta’s Fairness and Safety in Sport Act (Bill 29) institutionalizes gender surveillance under the guise of protection, disproportionately affecting transgender, non-binary, racialized, and otherwise equity-denied girls and women. Situating this legislation within historical patterns of settler colonialism and masculine dominance in sport, we demonstrate how eligibility verification frameworks reproduce racialized and gendered hierarchies while intensifying body policing and psychosocial harm among youth. The analysis further connects sport governance to escalating online misogyny, AI-facilitated sexual exploitation, and ideologically motivated violent extremism, illustrating how policies that normalize bodily suspicion intersect with broader ecosystems of gender-based violence. Rather than enhancing fairness or safety, such regulatory approaches risk reinforcing exclusion, stigma, and institutional distrust. The paper concludes by outlining policy and safeguarding interventions that prioritize privacy, self-identification, and structural accountability, positioning sport governance as a critical site where broader struggles over bodily autonomy, legitimacy, and belonging are negotiated.

title: A Theoretical Solution to the Doping Problem: Talk About It!
title_original: A Theoretical Solution to the Doping Problem: Talk About It!
summary: What effect would talking about doping have? All players in a classical doping game have the option of telling their opponent that they will announce their doping decision before the sports competition is executed. What effects, if any would such a move have? This question is analysed in the paper at hand. As opposed to most people’s intuition, the effect on classical doping games is limited. Still, some peculiar situations prove otherwise.

title: Efficacy of Multi-Nutrient Supplementation on Improving Physical Endurance and Sports Performance of Physical Education Students, University of Mysore, India
title_original: Efficacy of Multi-Nutrient Supplementation on Improving Physical Endurance and Sports Performance of Physical Education Students, University of Mysore, India
summary: The present study was designed to comprise development of the nutritional supplement (Nutrisport) and its’ sensory and acceptability analysis. Then a convenient sample of 12 male students aged between 21-25 years were randomly selected for physical endurance assessment. Both cardio-respiratory and muscular endurance tests were performed on the subjects. Cardio-respiratory endurance test refers to the ability to continue or persist in strenuous tasks involving large muscle groups for extended periods of time. This type of endurance was assessed by having the subjects run on a treadmill set at a speed of 15KM/hr. Then on exhaustion, time taken to exhaustion, distance covered and the amount of calories burnt by each subject were noted and recorded. Muscular Endurance test was assessed by having the subjects perform press-ups, and counting the number of presses completed to exhaustion. Then the subjects were rated according to the Canadian society for exercise physiology reference by age group and sex. Keywords: Multi-Nutrient Supplementation, Physical Endurance, Sports Performance, Physical Education Students, University of Mysore

title: Physical And Physiological Responses of Amateur Sprinters to Kola Nut Consumption as a Trado-Ergogenic Aids
title_original: Physical And Physiological Responses of Amateur Sprinters to Kola Nut Consumption as a Trado-Ergogenic Aids
summary: The purpose of the study was to find out how certain body physical and physiological response variables will be affected due to Kola nut consumption of amateur sprinters. A Quasi experimental research of the randomized control group pre-test post-test research design was adopted, in which there were two groups, one control and the other experimental. The experimental group was further sub divided into three groups with each administered with different quantities of Kola nut, in the order of (i) 100mg.kg-1 of body weight, (ii) 150mg.kg-1 of body weight, (iii) 200mg.kg-1 of body weight. All the four sub-groups were subjected to pre-test and post-test performance of 50m race during the pre-test and post-test exercises. The sample for the study was made up of 16 male students who were athletes and had trained at least three times in a week. They were selected using simple random sampling technique from the population of non-habitual kola nut eater. They were of the age range of 19 – 30 years. Thirty pieces of red colour kola nuts (Kola nitida) were bought from the market at Okene in Kogi State, Nigeria. The descriptive statistic of mean, standard deviation and range, and the dependent t-test inferential statistics at 0.05 alpha level were used to analyze the results. The findings show that there were differences in speed test and body responses to kola nut ingestion; it was therefore recommended that athletes and their handlers should be careful in consuming kola nut when in sport competition, and the general public should know that kola nut affect some physiological processes of the body.

title: Identidad de género y deporte: debate en X sobre la participación de Imane Khelif en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024
title_original: Identidad de género y deporte: debate en X sobre la participación de Imane Khelif en los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024
summary: Purpose: This study analyses the polarisation of public discourse on the social network X (formerly Twitter) surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation in the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. The aim is to examine how different positions on gender identity, fairness and legitimacy in elite sport are constructed, disseminated and contested. Methodology: A total of 35,676 posts from 25,984 unique users were collected and analysed using the professional tool Tweet Binder during the period 27 July to 10 August 2024. Automated sentiment analysis based on natural language processing (NLP) was applied, classifying posts into four categories (positive, negative, neutral and undefined), supplemented by temporal, linguistic and key-actor analysis. Results: Significant polarisation was identified. Although positive posts outnumbered negative ones (18% versus 17%), critical publications generated twice as many impressions (194.8 million versus 93.3 million). Public figures such as Elon Musk and J.K. Rowling amplified the controversy with posts exceeding 670 million combined views. Activity peaks coincided with key events such as Angela Carini's withdrawal. Conclusions: Social media platforms function as spaces of symbolic confrontation where emotionally negative content achieves greater reach. Misinformation about the athlete's medical condition fuelled reductionist narratives. Digital discourse may influence future sports regulations on inclusion and fairness.

title: Entrepreneurial interest, career development, and economic independence among athletes: a systematic literature review (2020–2026)
title_original: Entrepreneurial interest, career development, and economic independence among athletes: a systematic literature review (2020–2026)
summary: Athletes face relatively short and uncertain career trajectories, making career transition and economic independence important concerns. This systematic literature review examined how entrepreneurial interest, entrepreneurship education, financial literacy, and related competencies support athletes’ career development, employability, and economic independence. Following the PRISMA 2020 framework, a structured search of the Scopus database identified 134 records, of which 50 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative and thematic synthesis. The findings revealed four major themes: the role of sport-specific competencies and entrepreneurship education in developing entrepreneurial intention and self-efficacy; the contribution of dual-career and structured transition programs to post-career entrepreneurship; the broader economic benefits of sport-related social entrepreneurship; and the moderating effects of gender, sport discipline, and institutional support. Overall, entrepreneurial competencies and educational support can strengthen athletes’ career adaptability, employability, and economic independence during and after their sporting careers. Future research should emphasize longitudinal designs, cross-national comparisons, and validated measures of athlete-specific entrepreneurial self-efficacy.

title: The Association Between Sleep Quality, Training Load and Injury Risk in Athletes
title_original: The Association Between Sleep Quality, Training Load and Injury Risk in Athletes
summary: Sleep is an essential component of athletic recovery, yet inadequate sleep is common among athletes and may influence both performance and injury risk. Training load also plays an important role, particularly when high workloads are combined with insufficient recovery. This article examines the relationship between sleep quality, training load, and injury risk in athletes. Current evidence suggests that poor sleep is associated with impaired recovery, reduced physical and cognitive performance, and a higher likelihood of musculoskeletal injury. Excessive or rapidly increasing training loads may further increase this risk when recovery is inadequate. However, the relationship is complex and influenced by individual, psychological, and environmental factors. Monitoring sleep and training load may therefore help coaches, athletes, and medical staff identify periods of increased risk and improve recovery strategies. Further prospective research is needed to establish clearer causal relationships.

title: “Continue or quit?” Configurations of career resources and their association with career termination: a person-oriented study with Swiss elite athletes
title_original: “Continue or quit?” Configurations of career resources and their association with career termination: a person-oriented study with Swiss elite athletes
summary: Successful athletic careers require sustained dedication and the effective management of multiple career resources. While athletic identity, health, and social support are known to influence athletes’ career sustainability, their combined impact on career continuation or retirement remains unclear. This study applied a person-oriented approach to identify distinct configurations of career resources among Swiss elite athletes and to examine their linkage to career continuation or termination two years later. A total of 559 national team athletes (46.9% female, 53.1% male; Mage = 25.05 years, SD = 5.46) completed assessments of athletic identity, physical and psychological health, and social support in 2022. Career status (n = 96, 17.2%, retired; n = 463, 82.8%, continued) was reassessed in 2024. Cluster analyses identified five distinct clusters reflecting different configurations of resources. Two clusters differed in their odds of retirement within two years: athletes with above-average athletic identity had reduced odds (OR = 0.50), while those with below-average athletic identity had increased odds (OR = 2.71), compared with the remaining three clusters. These findings indicate that distinct configurations of career resources may contribute to retirement decisions among elite athletes. Practically, individualized career counseling and proactive support may enhance athletes’ ability to sustain healthy, successful, and satisfying careers or to make informed retirement decisions. Future research should examine dynamic resource interactions and the quality of transitions using multi-wave longitudinal designs.

title: TREINAMENTO INTESTINAL EM ATLETAS DE ALTO RENDIMENTO
title_original: TREINAMENTO INTESTINAL EM ATLETAS DE ALTO RENDIMENTO
summary: O treinamento intestinal consiste na aplicação planejada e progressiva de estratégias nutricionais destinadas a melhorar a tolerância gastrointestinal do atleta durante sessões prolongadas e competições de alta intensidade. Em atletas de alto rendimento, sintomas como náuseas, refluxo, cólicas, distensão abdominal, urgência fecal e diarreia podem comprometer o desempenho, especialmente quando há elevada ingestão de carboidratos, desidratação, estresse térmico ou redução do fluxo sanguíneo esplâncnico. Este capítulo tem como objetivo discutir os fundamentos fisiológicos do treinamento intestinal, seus principais métodos e sua aplicabilidade na preparação esportiva. Foi realizada uma revisão narrativa da literatura científica sobre função gastrointestinal durante o exercício, estratégias de ingestão de carboidratos, hidratação, fibras, probióticos e periodização nutricional. A literatura indica que a exposição repetida a estratégias de alimentação e hidratação durante o exercício pode favorecer a adaptação perceptiva e funcional do trato gastrointestinal, aumentando a capacidade de ingestão e absorção de nutrientes. A intervenção deve ser individualizada, considerando modalidade, duração, intensidade, ambiente, preferências alimentares e histórico de sintomas. Conclui-se que o treinamento intestinal é uma ferramenta complementar da nutrição esportiva e deve ser realizado de maneira gradual, monitorada e integrada ao planejamento técnico, físico e médico do atleta.

A literatura indica que a exposição repetida a estratégias de alimentação e hidratação durante o exercício pode favorecer a adaptação perceptiva e funcional do trato gastrointestinal, aumentando a capacidade de ingestão e absorção de nutrientes. A intervenção deve ser individualizada, considerando modalidade, duração, intensidade, ambiente, preferências alimentares e histórico de sintomas. Conclui-se que o treinamento intestinal é uma ferramenta complementar da nutrição esportiva e deve ser realizado de maneira gradual, monitorada e integrada ao planejamento técnico, físico e médico do atleta.

title: Doping-related attitudes and intentions among Croatian athletes: Examining theory of planned behavior constructs and broader psychosocial correlates
title_original: Doping-related attitudes and intentions among Croatian athletes: Examining theory of planned behavior constructs and broader psychosocial correlates
summary: Bacckground: Doping continues to pose persistent challenges in competitive sport. Although prior studies have investigated Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) constructs together with a range of psychosocial correlates of doping, evidence from large and heterogeneous athlete samples remains limited.Objective: This study provides a large-sample contextual replication and extension of previous TPB-based doping research by examining associations among TPB constructs, performance-enhancement attitudes, self-esteem, achievement goal orientation, sport motivation, descriptive norms, and self-reported use of prohibited substances for performance enhancement in 988 Croatian athletes from team and individual sports.Methods: Analyses included psychometric evaluation, descriptive statistics, bivariate correlations, group comparisons, and hierarchical multiple regression.Results: Overall, 7.6% of participants reported prohibited substance use at least once during their sporting careers. Male athletes reported more favorable doping-related and performance-enhancement attitudes and stronger behavioral intentions. Individual-sport athletes and athletes in the lower competition-level group more frequently reported lifetime prohibited-substance use. Higher self-esteem, stronger task orientation, and greater intrinsic motivation were associated with less favorable doping-related and performance-enhancement attitudes and weaker behavioral intentions, whereas lower self-esteem, ego orientation, extrinsic motivation, and amotivation were associated with more permissive attitudes and stronger behavioral intentions. Attitudes toward doping showed the strongest unique association with behavioral intention, followed by performance-enhancement attitudes and subjective norms. The findings replicate previously established associations between TPB constructs and doping intention while extending the evidence base by demonstrating systematic associations with a broader set of psychosocial characteristics in a large sample of Croatian athletes.Conclusion: These findings provide context-specific evidence that may inform future longitudinal research and the development of psychosocially informed anti-doping interventions.

title: In-orbit monitoring for dynamic detector-oriented containment of TID-induced degradation in CMOS-TDI sensor systems
title_original: In-orbit monitoring for dynamic detector-oriented containment of TID-induced degradation in CMOS-TDI sensor systems
summary: Abstract Space-borne CMOS-based sensor systems with time delay and integration (TDI) functionality are susceptible to the radiation environment in orbit. Total ionizing dose (TID) impacts CMOS detector structures and considerably deteriorates performance and image quality. We investigated dynamic detector-oriented methods to counteract TID-induced degradation effects. We equipped the CMOS-TDI detector system with in-orbit monitoring capabilities applying charge injection and subsampling to reveal inherent detector operation feedback and enable system adaptation during operation. Thus, the impact of radiation was significantly contained. The charge transfer efficiency (CTE) accordingly reached the pre-radiation level. The relative charge loss was reduced by a factor of 8.1, yielding a substantial improvement in CTE, and hence, in the geometric resolution. We further applied device compact modeling, aiming for a comprehensive system model to facilitate adequate prediction of performance degradation caused by TID, which could be generally applied to upcoming designs of the CMOS-TDI detector family after external validation.

title: General Anaesthesia in Athletes: Physiological Adaptations, Pharmacological Nuances, and Clinical Management
title_original: General Anaesthesia in Athletes: Physiological Adaptations, Pharmacological Nuances, and Clinical Management
summary: Background. Years of high-intensity training induce profound cardiovascular, autonomic and body-composition adaptations that may influence the response to general anaesthesia. The trained athlete therefore represents a distinct perioperative population. Aim. To appraise and synthesise evidence on the perioperative care of athletes undergoing general anaesthesia, focusing on cardiovascular and autonomic adaptation, body composition and drug disposition, preoperative and airway assessment, induction and maintenance, anaesthetic technique, performance-enhancing drugs, and anti-doping regulations. Material and methods. A narrative review of the scientific literature was conducted, drawing on anaesthesiology, cardiology and sports medicine sources. Results. Endurance training produces eccentric cardiac hypertrophy with balanced four-chamber dilation and increased resting vagal tone, whereas resistance training promotes a concentric pattern. Pronounced vagal predominance may contribute to clinically significant perioperative bradyarrhythmias in highly trained endurance athletes, as described in case reports. Lean body weight may be considered when dosing hypnotic induction agents in highly muscular patients, although supporting evidence derives mainly from obese populations and remains unvalidated in athletes. Greater muscular strength has been associated with higher Modified Mallampati scores. Undisclosed performance-enhancing drug use may increase perioperative risk through coronary disease, myocardial fibrosis and hypercoagulability. The World Anti-Doping Agency Code also creates specific considerations for prescribing anaesthesiologists. Conclusions. General anaesthesia in athletes requires an individualised, evidence-informed approach. Recognition of physiological adaptations, thorough cardiovascular and airway assessment, cautious drug dosing and preparedness for unexpected bradyarrhythmia are essential.

title: The Landscape of Doping in Indian Sports: Contemporary Challenges and Deliberations
title_original: The Landscape of Doping in Indian Sports: Contemporary Challenges and Deliberations
summary: The menace of doping in the Indian sporting ecosystem is well acknowledged, but the social ramifications of the process have not been explored in depth. The paper aims to reflect upon the intricate social dynamics of doping structured by various socio-economic factors, cultural narratives, and the widespread availability of doping substances. Through ethnographic fieldwork in western Uttar Pradesh (India), the study uncovers the practice of doping among junior athletes, a significant lack of awareness of anti-doping frameworks among junior/adolescent athletes and Athlete Support Personnel (ASP) regarding anti-doping policies. It highlights the crucial role of suppliers in fostering a dopogenic environment. The findings illustrate a concerning landscape where regulatory efforts and initiatives by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in India encounter obstacles due to a deficiency in the reach of educational frameworks and a cultural perception of doping as a pathway to success. The paper advocates for an intersectional approach to anti-doping frameworks, stressing the importance of collaboration among stakeholders to cultivate a culture of fair play, particularly in India&s;s aspirations to host the 2036 Olympic Games.

title: Effects of endurance training on spirometric parameters in male long-distance runners
title_original: Effects of endurance training on spirometric parameters in male long-distance runners
summary: Objectives The aim of this study was to compare spirometric parameters between recreational male marathon runners (MR) and a control group (CG) representative of the male population of the Pomerania region to assess the association between endurance training and pulmonary function. Methods A total of 31 amateur MR and 82 men in the CG aged 35–66 years participated in this study. The CG represented the male population of the Pomerania region (Poland). The analysis included basic spirometric parameters: forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), Tiffeneau index (FEV1/FVC), and the potential confounding factors: body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), smoking status, and history of obstructive lung diseases. Results Recreational MR demonstrated significantly higher FVC and FEV1 values than the CG, both in absolute values and as percentages of predicted values ( p < 0.001). Mean FVC was 5.24 ± 0.68 L in MR and 4.58 ± 0.95 L in controls, whilst mean FEV1 was 4.14 ± 0.55 L and 3.55 ± 0.88 L, respectively. No significant differences were observed in the Tiffeneau index (FEV1/FVC), smoking status, or prevalence of obstructive lung diseases between the groups. Although anthropometric parameters differed between groups, they were not significantly associated with spirometric outcomes. Conclusions Recreational male MR demonstrated significantly higher FVC and FEV1 values than controls from the general male population. No significant differences were observed in the prevalence of obstructive airway disorders. Because of the relatively small sample size and cross-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted with caution. Further longitudinal studies are needed to better clarify the relationship between endurance training and pulmonary function.

title: Pool Chlorination By-Products and Airway Hyperresponsiveness in Swimmers: Pathomechanism, Pulmonary Diagnostics and Preventive Management — A Narrative Synthesis of Evidence Published Since 2020
title_original: Pool Chlorination By-Products and Airway Hyperresponsiveness in Swimmers: Pathomechanism, Pulmonary Diagnostics and Preventive Management — A Narrative Synthesis of Evidence Published Since 2020
summary: Background: Competitive swimmers train in indoor facilities where chlorine-based disinfection generates volatile by-products like trichloramine. Aquatic disciplines report the highest prevalence of lower airway dysfunction of any sporting group. The clinical picture, often labelled ‘swimmer’s asthma’, sits between classical exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and chemically mediated airway disorder. Aim: To synthesise evidence (2020 onwards) on mechanisms by which chlorination by-products and sustained hyperpnoea injure airway epithelium in swimmers, appraise diagnostic strategies, and set out preventive and pharmacological options within anti-doping constraints. Material and methods: This narrative synthesis retrieved PubMed/MEDLINE records (Jan 2020–Jul 2026), combining exposure, respiratory, and anti-doping terms. Priority was given to consensus statements, meta-analyses, and clinical trials. Results: Meta-analyses place lower airway dysfunction prevalence at 21.8% across athletes and 39.9% in aquatic disciplines. The dominant mechanism combines osmotic/mechanical stress from hyperpnoea with chemical irritation, disrupting the epithelial barrier. Club cell protein 16 marks this disruption, though interpretation is complicated by acute vs. chronic changes. Symptom-based diagnosis performs poorly; objective bronchoprovocation is required (eucapnic voluntary hyperpnoea shows 46% sensitivity, 74% specificity). Inhaled beta-2 agonists are permitted below daily thresholds, but the therapeutic-to-reportable margin is narrow. Conclusions: Swimmers' airway hyperresponsiveness is an occupational disorder of mixed osmotic and chemical origin, not classical asthma. Objective testing must precede prescription, treatment must align with anti-doping limits, and environmental control of by-products requires greater clinical emphasis.

title: Creazione della salute
title_original: Creazione della salute
summary: Il libro è pensato per milioni di persone, potenzialmente per ogni individuo, che desidera essere sano e sentirsi al meglio ogni giorno. Non tratta della cura delle malattie, ma della creazione consapevole e costante della salute attraverso uno stile di vita sano e armonioso: prevenire invece di riparare.

title: Difficulties Encountered by Coaches in Teaching Student Athletes
title_original: Difficulties Encountered by Coaches in Teaching Student Athletes
summary: This research determined the level of difficulties encountered by teacher-coaches in teaching student-athletes in a mega-sized public secondary school in a medium-sized division of the Negros Island Region during School Year 2020–2021, as a basis for a strategic intervention plan. A descriptive research design was employed, using a total enumeration of 50 public secondary school teacher-coaches across five sports categories (individual, dual, team, para-games, and combative). Data were gathered using a researcher-made survey questionnaire validated by experts (CVI = 4.50) and tested for internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.813). Data were analyzed using frequencies, percentages, weighted means, and the Mann–Whitney U test. Results revealed that the majority of coaches were older (52.0%), married (58.0%), and non-MAPEH majors (68.0%). Coaches experienced a moderate level of difficulty in Sports Skills Development (M = 2.88) and high levels of difficulty in Sports Support Services (M = 3.63) and Sports Management (M = 4.07). The most prominent challenges were accessing professional development programs (M = 4.84), providing suitable training venues and spaces (M = 4.34), and conducting regular consultations and planning sessions among coaches (M = 4.48). Inferential analysis via the Mann–Whitney U test indicated no significant differences in coaching difficulties when respondents were grouped by age and civil status (p > 0.05). However, significant differences were found in Sports Skills Development (U = 67.50, p = 0.000) and Sports Management (U = 147.00, p = 0.007) according to specialization, with non-MAPEH majors experiencing significantly greater difficulty than MAPEH majors. The study concluded that operational challenges in sports programs stem primarily from resource constraints and a lack of formal sports specialization among teacher-coaches, highlighting the urgent need for structured coaching capacity-building, facility adaptation, and institutionalized communication frameworks.

title: Islamic Teachings as an Internal Discipline System in Athlete Development: A Narrative Review and the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model
title_original: Islamic Teachings as an Internal Discipline System in Athlete Development: A Narrative Review and the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model
summary: Discipline underpins high-performance behaviour, and sport psychology has examined it through self-regulation, motivation, resilience, and moral behaviour. Religion has also been studied in athletes, but mainly as a coping resource, an identity marker, or a participation constraint rather than as a self-regulatory system. This narrative review examines how Islamic ethical teachings intersect with established discipline constructs in sport, and proposes the Prophetic Athlete Discipline Model (PADM), which links spiritual, behavioural, moral, and physical dimensions of athlete discipline. Scopus and PubMed were searched purposively in September 2026 using three strings covering religion and sport psychology, Muslim athletes, and Islamic ethical constructs in sport, supplemented by citation tracking from two anchor reviews. Of the (N = 2,286) records screened on title, abstract, and keywords, (n = 70) were retained. Islamic primary sources were handled separately and restricted to Quranic verses, authenticated Prophetic traditions, and established works of Islamic ethics. The retained literature is dominated by cross-sectional and qualitative designs, contains one longitudinal study (n = 1) and three intervention studies (n = 3), and is concentrated in Western settings. Across four domains, Islamic constructs correspond functionally with intention-based motivation, ritual and self-control, moral identity, and recovery behaviour. Qualifying evidence is also present: negative religious coping is associated with adverse pre-competition emotion, the protective component of religiosity appears existential rather than devotional, and Ramadan observance reduces sleep and high-intensity performance. Islamic teachings can be read as a candidate self-regulatory architecture rather than a peripheral cultural variable, but PADM is untested. Its value depends on whether its domains explain variance beyond general religiosity and existing psychological constructs. Instruments now exist to test that.

title: Iron Deficiency in Athletes — Current State of Knowledge
title_original: Iron Deficiency in Athletes — Current State of Knowledge
summary: Introduction and Purpose. Iron deficiency is common among athletes and may occur before anemia develops. Its significance is less clear when iron stores are depleted despite normal hemoglobin. This review summarizes current evidence on iron deficiency in athletes, with particular emphasis on iron deficiency without anemia (IDNA), athletic performance, diagnosis, and management. Materials and Methods. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search was supplemented by Google Scholar and reference screening. Publications from January 2015 to August 2026 were considered, with earlier studies included when relevant to fundamental aspects of iron metabolism, diagnosis, or treatment. Results. Iron deficiency in athletes results from interacting factors, including increased requirements, inadequate intake, reduced iron availability, and iron losses. Ferritin remains the principal marker of iron stores, although inflammation and inconsistent diagnostic thresholds complicate its interpretation. The functional effects of IDNA are variable. More pronounced depletion appears more likely to impair endurance performance, while increases in ferritin after supplementation do not consistently translate into improved performance. Conclusions. Iron status should be interpreted alongside laboratory findings, symptoms, risk factors, and training demands. Management should focus on correcting documented deficiency and identifying its underlying cause rather than supplementation aimed solely at increasing iron stores or enhancing performance.
