title: Contesting gender politics in the 2023 Women’s World Cup: Chinese fans’ online reactions to athlete activism and kissgate
title_original: Contesting gender politics in the 2023 Women’s World Cup: Chinese fans’ online reactions to athlete activism and kissgate
summary: This qualitative social media study investigates how Chinese football fans discussed gender‑related athlete activism and the sexual harassment scandal (‘kissgate’) involving Spanish player Jenni Hermoso during and after the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Using thematic and discourse analysis to analyse relevant comments on the Dongqiudi mobile app, the findings reveal strong hostility towards gender activism, exemplified by the criticism of Megan Rapinoe and the mockery of Chinese female players even when they challenged gender norms without demanding equal pay or identifying as feminists. Unlike American fans, who often claim that sports and politics should not mix when attacking athlete activism, football fans in China, where modern sport has long been bound up with the nationalistic attempts to revive the Chinese nation, dismissed feminism without relying on such an apolitical understanding of sport. By contrast, reactions to the ‘kissgate’ scandal were overwhelmingly critical of the aggressor and supportive of the victim, suggesting that the #MeToo movement may have shaped attitudes towards sexual harassment, even in male-dominated spaces – although without improving feminism’s image. The findings highlight a nuanced dynamic: anti-feminist sentiment coexists with selective support for anti-harassment efforts. This study contributes to scholarship on contemporary athlete activism by demonstrating how sports fans’ responses are shaped by nation-specific forms of nationalism and the global rise of right‑wing populism.

title: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
title_original: Virginia Woolf: dance, rhythm, movement
summary: Despite the rich cultural exchange between the arts in the late-nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, particularly between dance and literature, the study of rhythm, movement, and dance has been relatively neglected in Woolf studies. Moving beyond the current critical focus on ballet, this thesis draws on Virginia Woolf’s biographies, diaries, essays, juvenilia, letters, and novels, alongside the socio-cultural history of dance and feminist theories of the body and gendered movement, to explore how Woolf’s use of physical expression, dance, and rhythmic variation might upend orthodox masculinity, patriarchal oppression, and social class hierarchies. Chapter one looks at how Woolf employs circle- or couple-dances in The Voyage Out (1915) to explore embodiment, gender fluidity, and social control. Formally staid ballroom dance, regarded as a manifestation of patriarchy, is replaced with vibrant Bacchanalian movements that mirror modern dance’s focus on spontaneous, voluntary motion. Chapter two argues that Orlando’s ballet-inflected steps test the limits of conservative masculinity, embracing alternative forms. It goes on to consider the figure of the female Olympic ice-dancer as a possible source of inspiration for Princess Sasha Romanovich, whose fluid movement across the ice resists conformity. Chapter three delves into human/nonhuman dance-related movement in Flush: A Biography (1933), To the Lighthouse (1927) and The Waves (1931), examining how ingenious female artists breach gender boundaries by operating outside male-dominated models. Consequently, Woolf’s engagement with the nonhuman is less concerned with destabilising humanist values than with deepening her critique of gender inequality. The final chapter investigates how the foxtrot and embodied movement in The Years and Between the Acts (1941) critique social hierarchies, reflecting the novelist’s democratic response to elitism. As such, this thesis intervenes in, and contributes to, various debates in Woolf studies, offering fresh insights into Virginia Woolf’s engagement with embodiment, gender, and social politics.

title: Post-race lactate, clearance velocity, and recovery protocols in youth competitive swimming
title_original: Post-race lactate, clearance velocity, and recovery protocols in youth competitive swimming
summary: Post-race cool-downs play a crucial role in enhancing lactate clearance and recovery in competitive swimming. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a 1200 m cool-down protocol in facilitating blood lactate removal across different race distances. It also explored the relationship between perceptual and physiological markers of eff ort and recovery, specifically: (a) the correlation between Total Quality of Recovery (TQR) and pre-race lactate concentrations, and (b) the association between Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) and post-race lactate concentrations. A total of 26 male and female swimmers (17.83 ± 2.25 years) were included. Capillary blood samples were collected at three time points—Pre-Race Lactate (PreRLa), Post-Race Lactate (PoRLa), and Post-Cool Down Lactate (PoCDLa)—during a state-level meet. TQR and RPE were recorded at the start and end of each race, respectively. Lactate Clearance % and Lactate Clearance Velocity were calculated for analysis. We used SPSS 23 for statistical tests, with significance set at p < .05. Results showed significant differences in PoRLa concentrations across race distances (p = .001), with higher post-race lactate accumulation in 100 m swimmers. Although Lactate Clearance was similar across distances, Lactate Clearance Velocity was highest in the 100 m group. No significant differences were observed in TQR and RPE scores. Correlation analysis revealed a strong positive relationship between PoRLa and Lactate Clearance Velocity (r = .916) and a moderate positive association between PoR-La and PoCDLa (r = .523). These findings demonstrate differences in post-race lactate responses and clearance velocity across swimming events. The study provides practical insights to refi ne cool-down protocols and optimize recovery strategies tailored to the unique metabolic demands of competitive swimmers.

It also explored the relationship between perceptual and physiological markers of eff ort and recovery, specifically: (a) the correlation between Total Quality of Recovery (TQR) and pre-race lactate concentrations, and (b) the association between Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) and post-race lactate concentrations. A total of 26 male and female swimmers (17.83 ± 2.25 years) were included. Capillary blood samples were collected at three time points—Pre-Race Lactate (PreRLa), Post-Race Lactate (PoRLa), and Post-Cool Down Lactate (PoCDLa)—during a state-level meet. TQR and RPE were recorded at the start and end of each race, respectively. Lactate Clearance % and Lactate Clearance Velocity were calculated for analysis. We used SPSS 23 for statistical tests, with significance set at p < .05. Results showed significant differences in PoRLa concentrations across race distances (p = .001), with higher post-race lactate accumulation in 100 m swimmers. Although Lactate Clearance was similar across distances, Lactate Clearance Velocity was highest in the 100 m group. No significant differences were observed in TQR and RPE scores. Correlation analysis revealed a strong positive relationship between PoRLa and Lactate Clearance Velocity (r = .916) and a moderate positive association between PoR-La and PoCDLa (r = .523). These findings demonstrate differences in post-race lactate responses and clearance velocity across swimming events. The study provides practical insights to refi ne cool-down protocols and optimize recovery strategies tailored to the unique metabolic demands of competitive swimmers.

title: Beyond Procedural Justice: Responding to intergroup-level authority decisions
title_original: Beyond Procedural Justice: Responding to intergroup-level authority decisions
summary: The present thesis builds on the relational models of procedural justice (RMPJ) put forward by Tyler and colleagues, which theorise about the importance of authorities being fair in the way they make their decisions. In this view, fair procedures symbolically inform people of their social standing in the society and through this, authorities can gain legitimacy. The present work expands on these models in two ways. First, it proposes that the analysis of authority-subordinate interactions should move beyond the individual-level research, to consider group and intergroup-level interactions. Secondly, it argues that identification with a social group in the first place can be a determinant of perceptions of fairness and the subsequent judgements of the decisions made by authorities. Eight experimental studies investigating group members’ responses to the intergroup-level authority decisions were conducted. The main findings suggest that (a) feelings of loyalty to one’s group increase preference for ingroup favouring decisions regardless of whether these decisions are fair or not, (b) culture and its underpinning values can shape perceptions of fairness in relation to authority decisions, and (c) people generally expect authorities to be fair to others regardless if they are of low or high social standing, but ideologies about the structure of the social hierarchy can inform these expectations of fairness. The findings are discussed in the light of the RMPJ and the implications for governing divided societies.

title: Brazilian diplomacy and technological autonomy: from the 2005 GGE to the 2025 OEWG and AI governance
title_original: Brazilian diplomacy and technological autonomy: from the 2005 GGE to the 2025 OEWG and AI governance
summary: This study examines the extent to which Brazilian foreign policy has strengthened technological autonomy amid the expansion of global digital governance. It argues that Brazil pursues a pragmatic autonomy strategy: gaining normative prominence in multilateral cybersecurity and artificial intelligence forums while simultaneously reducing its dependence on external infrastructure and suppliers at the same pace. To test this claim, this study proposes a second-generation exploratory Digital Sovereignty Index, building on the GEPSI framework with a focus on longitudinal autonomy dynamics, built from open-source data, structured into five sub-indexes, and calculated for three time points (2005, 2015, and 2026). The analysis combines longitudinal measurements, document analysis, and historical narrative analysis. The results confirm a persistent asymmetry: normative autonomy advances substantially faster than technical-corporate autonomy, supporting a broader argument about the limits of diplomatic agency for semiperipheral states.

title: Funny Bones
title_original: Funny Bones
summary: Judging from the sway of dystopian and (post)-apocalyptic scenarios in contemporary Anthropocene fiction, our concern for climate change and ecological upheaval has been particularly receptive to narrative forms derived from the catastrophic imaginary, with comic modes often getting evicted from the province of environmentalist thought. Chris Flynn’s novel Mammoth (2020) is a notable exception, deploying humor to culturally process loss, (ecological) grief, and memory. Flynn’s use of the conventions of the it-narrative, with a mastodon fossil as the novel’s narrator, brings the scales of megafauna extinctions, imperial expansion, resource extractivism, and de-extinction eschatology into a shared fold of planetary temporality, where the comic register is offered as a medium for rethinking multi-species encounters and (pre)historical acts of aggression. In attending to the political animation of fossils in the narrative, whose stories shuttle across spatial and temporal scales, this paper examines how the novel’s use of humor illuminates the legacies of species extinctions and colonialism, while its engagement with the ethics of de-extinction abates the novel’s satirical sting. In this, Mammoth’s loyalties are shown to oscillate between critique and conformity, highlighting the ethical impasse of comedy as a genre of the Anthropocene.

title: Fungal hyphae through the lens of microfluidic devices: From biological properties to novel therapeutic opportunities
title_original: Fungal hyphae through the lens of microfluidic devices: From biological properties to novel therapeutic opportunities
summary: Fungal diseases are increasingly being recognized as a major health problem worldwide. Advancing therapeutic approaches against fungal pathogens require comprehensive knowledge of their biological properties, which enable fungi to explore host environments, interact with host cells and coinhabiting microorganisms, adopt colonization and infective strategies. Thus, fungus intrinsic as well as extrinsic mechanisms functionally cooperate for successful host infection and disease development. In this regard, fungal hyphae, i.e. long, filamentous structures with polarized tip growth, represent a unique feature of multicellular fungi and play critical roles during the infectious process, calling for in-depth characterization of their functional and structural properties. In this context, reproducing hyphal growth in physiological conditions represents a fundamental prerequisite for disease modeling and therapeutic development. For their potential to accommodate and interconnect cells and miniature tissues, microfluidic devices stand as unique opportunities in this direction by overcoming acknowledged limits of animal models and traditional cell cultures. Based on these premises, we herein provide an overview of the use of microfluidic devices in the study of fungal hyphae, from the investigation of their biological properties to the analysis of inter-organismal networking, including the interaction between fungal hyphae and host cells. By dissecting hyphal strategies of environmental navigation as well as modalities of cell-cell interactions, resorting to microfluidics devices may provide novel opportunities for therapeutic targeting of fungal pathogens, in line with the objectives of the World Health Organization.

title: The Korean ‘Minbak’ as an environmental bubble: motivations, experiences, and the paradox of cultural immersion among Korean travellers
title_original: The Korean ‘Minbak’ as an environmental bubble: motivations, experiences, and the paradox of cultural immersion among Korean travellers
summary: This study examines Korean travellers’ use of Minbaks (Korean guesthouses) in Europe, introducing the ‘pulsating bubble’ framework that challenges static conceptualisations of environmental enclaves. Through netnography of 192 Korean travel blogs (2023–2025), we demonstrate that Minbaks function as re-pressurisation chambers enabling sustained cultural immersion. Korean travellers engage in cyclical rhythms, whereby daytime exploration depletes physiological and psychological resources while nighttime Minbak stays restore capacity through Korean food, linguistic comfort, and social networks. Integrating Cohen's bubble theory with Maslow's hierarchy reveals how satisfying lower-order needs creates capacity for higher-order cultural engagement. The Korean concept of jeong (정), affective bonds transcending transactional exchange, illuminates how cultural specificity shapes belonging needs that Maslow's universalist hierarchy cannot capture. These findings reframe ethnic enclaves as enabling infrastructure for sustained independent travel by non-Western visitors.

title: Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
title_original: Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
summary:
Through the perspective of the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption and opportunity it engendered, this chapter follows a transformative effect of EdTech and Digital education in India particularly in Nagaland through analysis. Drawing upon national policy frameworks, conceptual literature on educational technology, and contextual evidence based on the case of Nagaland, the chapter considers the rapid migration to digital learning as an emergency strategy (in response to the ongoing institution closures) based on the stark shifts in pedagogical practice, access to education services, and preparedness. The findings show that, including the ability of national programmes such as NEP 2020, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and others, to promote access to digital tools was low within periphery or hill areas (e.g., Nagaland), due to lack of infrastructural resources, digital divide, unprepared teachers and economic/social divides, and more. The pandemic exposed the deep social and infrastructure divides in connectivity, device availability, assessment and learner engagement, with implications that were especially grave in rural and tribal settings. Although it accelerated the pace of innovation and the application of blended and low-tech learning practices teachers have been experimenting with digital platforms and the post-COVID recovery process, including remedial programmes and hybrid instruction. The chapter also discusses that blended learning is the most fitting, viable and sustainable approach for reaching the technological level in the field of educational technology at Nagaland. It implies that technology-mediated education can improve equity, quality, and resilience, but only under the conditions of inclusive policy design, strong digital infrastructure, vigorous teacher capability building, and culturally appropriate digital content.
Keywords: Educational technology, digital learning, COVID-19, Nagaland, online education, Challenges, blended learning

title: The Rise of Augmented Reality in Teacher Education: a Bibliometric Analysis of Research
title_original: The Rise of Augmented Reality in Teacher Education: a Bibliometric Analysis of Research
summary:
In the digital era, immersive learning media is increasingly popular in the educational sphere. The use of this media has fuelled research on digital learning, including the use of Augmented reality, which facilitates learning to be more real and immersive.  This study aims to present data on the significance of bibliometric trends in Augmented Reality as immersive media in teacher education. The research method uses bibliometric analysis. Data analysis was carried out with the help of Biblioshiny and VOSviewer applications, with a total of 344 literatures processed from the Scopus database from 2007 to 2025.Three important insights into Augmented Reality (AR) research in teacher education are revealed by the bibliometric study. First, since 2007, the field has grown exponentially, with the United States, China, and Spain emerging as the top contributors. At the same time, nations like Saudi Arabia and Turkey are showing increasing engagement, demonstrating the worldwide relevance of AR. Second, there is a significant lack of research on teacher training and professional development, despite the fact that student-centered applications are extensively emphasized in the literature (as shown by high-frequency phrases like "students" and "teaching"). This suggests that this is an area that requires more investigation.
Third, interdisciplinary tendencies are apparent, with strong ties between AR and game-based learning, STEM education, and language acquisition. However, co-occurrence analysis shows that there are still few direct connections to teacher education practices. Ultimately, even though AR has the potential to revolutionize education, more disciplinary applications and teacher-focused frameworks should be given priority in future studies to properly realize its effects in learning environments.

title: Entry Points to US Education: Accessing the Next Wave of Growth
title_original: Entry Points to US Education: Accessing the Next Wave of Growth
summary: Entry Points to US Education: Accessing the Next Wave of Growth focuses on the imperative need to modernize international education as a result of the changes in international student mobility.  Centered around the ten entry points, the book looks into the distinct preferences and approaches of Generation Z (Gen Z) students, offering data-driven strategies to navigate the ten entry points to U.S. undergraduate degrees. This book also provides actionable strategies and model practices and encourages a national dialogue around student engagement to enhance (in the context of) global mobility.  Editors  Jing Luan is Provost Emeritus of San Mateo Colleges of Silicon Valley (San Mateo County Community College District) and former President of the Association of International Enrollment Management.  Leilt Habte is the Associate Director of the Transfer Center at the University of California Berkeley Center for Educational Partnership.  David L. Di Maria is a Senior International Officer and Associate Vice Provost for international education at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County.  Krishna Bista is a Professor of Higher Education in the Department of Advanced Studies, Leadership and Policy at Morgan State University, Baltimore, Maryland.

title: Career Choice: Cross-Sectional Study of Dental Students
title_original: Career Choice: Cross-Sectional Study of Dental Students
summary: Background: The choice of professional career is a crucial decision that affects students’ lives. The objective of our study was to identify the factors involved in the career choice of the students at the faculty´ Mohamed 6 of dentistry in Casablanca.Materials and Methods: An anonymous voluntary self-administered questionnaire was distributed to 1st year students. This questionnaire includes 10 closed questions divided into two sections: the first section provides information on socio-demographic data, and the second is dedicated to the factors that influenced the students’ choice. Descriptive and analytical statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25, with a significance threshold of p < 0.05.Results: We collected 130 questionnaires, with a response rate of > 99.2%. 62.3 Of the respondents, 62.3% were female. The choice of dentistry was made for 82.7% of the students before obtaining the baccalaureate; 61.5% of the students chose dentistry first; altruism and the status of the profession were the most important factors in the choice of dental studies; the significant difference between the choice factors related to gender was altruism.Conclusion: Students were mainly influenced by altruism and professional status when choosing dental studies. Understanding these factors is essential for supporting students.

title: Dollars and Degrees: The Asymmetric Impact of State Appropriations on STEM and Non-STEM Fields
title_original: Dollars and Degrees: The Asymmetric Impact of State Appropriations on STEM and Non-STEM Fields
summary:
Abstract
                  This study examines the differential impact of state appropriations on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and non-STEM degree completion at U.S. public four-year institutions. Using a panel dataset from 2003 to 2019 and a Bartik-style instrumental variables approach, I find that state funding disproportionately affects STEM degree completion, with little to no impact on non-STEM degrees. A 10% increase in state appropriations leads to a 3.4% increase in STEM degrees conferred, primarily four years after the funding change. This effect is concentrated among male students, science STEM majors, and non-selective institutions. Increased state support leads to higher institutional spending and more STEM programs-factors that affect STEM degree completion more than non-STEM fields.

Using a panel dataset from 2003 to 2019 and a Bartik-style instrumental variables approach, I find that state funding disproportionately affects STEM degree completion, with little to no impact on non-STEM degrees. A 10% increase in state appropriations leads to a 3.4% increase in STEM degrees conferred, primarily four years after the funding change. This effect is concentrated among male students, science STEM majors, and non-selective institutions. Increased state support leads to higher institutional spending and more STEM programs-factors that affect STEM degree completion more than non-STEM fields.

title: Polycystic Kidney Disease: Public Education
title_original: Polycystic Kidney Disease: Public Education
summary: Polycystic Kidney Disease: Public Education is a comprehensive guide designed to provide essential information and support to patients, families, and caregivers dealing with this genetic disorder. It is based on our earlier publication, the medical book Polycystic Kidney Disease. The book thoroughly explains PKD, a condition that leads to the formation of numerous cysts in the kidneys, eventually causing various health issues and potentially leading to kidney failure. The book begins by detailing what PKD is, including its genetic causes and the impact it has on kidney function. It describes common symptoms such as high blood pressure, pain in the back and sides, blood in the urine, and recurrent urinary tract infections, helping readers recognize and understand these warning signs. Diagnostic methods are clearly outlined, covering the use of imaging tests like ultrasounds, CT scans, and MRIs, along with blood and urine tests that assess kidney function. The importance of genetic testing is also discussed, providing insight into how it confirms the presence and type of PKD. Treatment options are a major focus of the book. It explains how to manage symptoms and slow disease progression through controlling high blood pressure with medications such as ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers. For those with advanced PKD, the book discusses critical treatment options such as dialysis and kidney transplantation. It explains the procedures, benefits, and considerations of hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, and provides a clear overview of the kidney transplant process. Polycystic Kidney Disease: Public Education is a vital resource for anyone affected by this condition, providing knowledge, practical advice, and hope for managing PKD effectively and improving quality of life. The information is presented in simple terms to ensure it is understandable for all readers, making it an essential tool for anyone looking to increase their knowledge about PKD and its management.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
title_original: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
summary: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Exploring Geographic Differences in High School Math Curricula, College Enrollment, and Postsecondary Math Remediation
title_original: Exploring Geographic Differences in High School Math Curricula, College Enrollment, and Postsecondary Math Remediation
summary: Few studies have examined the relationship between remedial and developmental education and rural students (Koricich & Boylan, 2019). In our analysis, we explore patterns in high school math course-taking and subsequent enrollment in remedial college math courses for rural/town students compared to a baseline nationally representative cohort of suburban students. Using restricted high school transcript data from the High School Longitudinal Study (HSLS:09), our logistic regression results reveal that rural/town students were more likely to take lower-level math courses when entering high school and were less likely to take advanced math courses before graduating. We contextualize these findings by considering possible differences in math Opportunities to Learn (OTLs) in rural/town high schools, finding that rural/town schools were less likely to offer advanced math courses and math support programs compared to suburban schools. We then examine enrollment in postsecondary education and find that rural/town students in our sample were more likely to enroll at two-year colleges compared to four-year colleges. We observed no differences in remedial course-taking between rural/town students and suburban students attending two-year colleges, but rural/town students attending four-year colleges were more likely to take remedial math courses than their suburban peers, even after controlling for a variety of demographic and academic factors. We discuss the implications of beginning high school in lower-level math courses and the importance of early interventions to support students’ readiness for college math.

title: The Role of Attachment Styles and Spiritual Intelligence in Predicting Women’s Emotional Divorce
title_original: The Role of Attachment Styles and Spiritual Intelligence in Predicting Women’s Emotional Divorce
summary: Background: Emotional divorce refers to a situation in which the emotional relationship, support, passion, warmth, attention, love, and intimacy between couples (husband & wife) decline or diminish. Such conditions lead to an unaffectionate marital life to the point that the couples are only together under one roof. Accordingly, the present study aimed to explore the role of attachment styles and spiritual intelligence in predicting emotional divorce in women. Methods: This study employed a descriptive-correlational design. The research population included all women filing for divorce who were referred to marriage counseling and couple therapy centers in districts 5 and 6 in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. In total, 400 women who met the inclusion criteria were selected as the study participants using voluntary response and convenience sampling techniques. The required data were collected by the Emotional Divorce Scale, the Adult Attachment Scale, and the Self-Report Measure of Spiritual Intelligence. The collected data were analyzed using the multiple regression analysis method in SPSS V. 22. Results: The obtained results suggested a significant positive relationship between the anxious-avoidant attachment style and emotional divorce (P<0.01). Furthermore, there was a significant negative relationship between spiritual intelligence and emotional divorce; the higher the spiritual intelligence, the lower the emotional divorce (P=0.02). Accordingly, spiritual intelligence and anxious-avoidant attachment style can predict emotional divorce (Multiple Regressions= -0.58). Conclusion: The present study data suggested that premarital education and counseling before spouse selection help in examining the personality traits of the parties. Moreover, paying attention to the role of health professionals, such as family counselors, psychologists, and psychiatric nurses in providing premarital counseling and education to couples and emphasizing the role of spiritual intelligence and attachment styles may prevent emotional separation and divorce among couples.

title: The Effects of Relaxing Music on Life Distress and Maternal-fetal Attachment in Pregnant Women
title_original: The Effects of Relaxing Music on Life Distress and Maternal-fetal Attachment in Pregnant Women
summary: Background: Although pregnancy and motherhood are enjoyable experiences, they are associated with numerous biopsychological changes requiring adaptation. The present study aimed to assess the effects of relaxing music on life distress and Maternal-Fetal Attachment (MFA) in pregnant women. Methods: This was a quasi-experimental study with a pre-test, post-test and a control group design. The research population included all Iranian pregnant women referring to Laleh Hospital in Tehran City, Iran, in 2020. In total, 30 women were selected using the convenience sampling method and randomly assigned into the intervention and control groups (n=15/group). The required data were collected using the Life Distress Inventory (LDI) and the Maternal-Fetal Attachment Scale (MFAS). The intervention group listened to relaxing music for twelve 45-50-minute sessions in the morning and during routine midwifery visits; however, the controls received no intervention. The collected data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Covariance (MANCOVA) in SPSS V. 22. Results: The obtained results indicated that the intervention group reported a lower level of life distress in the post-test, compared to the controls (P=0.0001, F=15.860). The intervention group also achieved a higher mean score on MFA, than the control group (P=0.0001, F=35.872).  Conclusion: According to the present research findings, reproductive health, nursing professionals, and psychologists could recommend music as a complementary therapy to reduce stress and distress experienced by expecting mothers and to improve MFA.

title: PENGAJARAN MAYA GURU INOVATIF PENDIDIKAN ISLAM DALAM ERA PANDEMIK COVID-19 VIRTUAL TEACHING OF INNOVATIVE ISLAMIC EDUCATION TEACHERS IN THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ERA
title_original: PENGAJARAN MAYA GURU INOVATIF PENDIDIKAN ISLAM DALAM ERA PANDEMIK COVID-19 VIRTUAL TEACHING OF INNOVATIVE ISLAMIC EDUCATION TEACHERS IN THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ERA
summary: This study explored the virtual teaching methods practised by the innovative Islamic Education teachers in the Covid-19 pandemic season and its issues. This case study is conducted qualitatively as it is based on a phenomenon. Four participants were selected based on the purposive sampling technique. Four criteria were set, namely; 1) recognized as an innovative teacher, 2) produced teaching innovations, 3) teaching Islamic Education, and 4) approachable and collaborative. Innovative teachers were selected as the participants of the study because they face the crisis calmly and able to find the best solutions. Data were collected using in-depth online interview. The findings showed that five themes were discussed by the participants, namely; 1) preparation, 2) preparation of teaching materials, 3) class schedule, 4) types of teaching, and 5) virtual teaching challenges. title: Narratives of young coaches’ participation rights in sports clubs: negotiating the liminal spaces of childhood and adulthood
title_original: Narratives of young coaches’ participation rights in sports clubs: negotiating the liminal spaces of childhood and adulthood
summary: Youth’s participation in, and drop-out from, grassroots sport has attracted considerable attention from scholars. Yet, there has been little focus on youth as rights bearers, in particular, research on young people’s participation rights. This article examines how young coaches and other significant actors in sports clubs (e.g. managers, adult coaches, parents, children) discursively construct youths’ right to be heard in all matters that affect them, acknowledging that free expression is a precondition for realizing all other rights (UNCRC 1989). Young coaches represent an interesting case to study because they are classified as children with specific rights, yet in their role as coaches they are authority figures for children. The study’s premise is that children have a right to play and participate in meaningful leisure, as well as a right to be heard and numerous other rights, but the processes involved in realizing these rights are saturated by power imbalances and micropolitics. Thus, from a critical narrative perspective, it asks, ‘how is young coaches’ ‘right to be heard’ narrated, what discourses are drawn upon and what subject positions are made available?’ The critical discourse analysis reveals that narratives about youths’ ‘right to be heard’ are seemingly scarce. Taken-for-granted ‘Truths’ about traditional forms of competitive sport and persistent narratives that valorize adult knowledge, often casting youth as ‘incompetents’/’immature’ and lacking a capacity to express a valid opinion, are more common. In addition, current neoliberal pressures for clubs to commodify children’s sport, can be seen to displace ideas that promote forms of governance in which power can be shared across generations.

title: Effects of plyometric and combined resistance-plyometric training on agility and vertical jump performance in youth basketball players
title_original: Effects of plyometric and combined resistance-plyometric training on agility and vertical jump performance in youth basketball players
summary: This study compared the effects of plyometric training and combined strength training on vertical jump performance, agility, and reactive strength in competitive youth basketball players. A parallel-group randomized controlled trial involved 30 male athletes (15–17 years) assigned to either a plyometric group (PLYO, n = 15) or a combined strength group (COMB, n = 15). Performance was assessed using countermovement jump (CMJ), T-test agility, and reactive strength index (RSI) before and after the intervention. Significant improvements over time were observed across all variables (p < 0.001), with no baseline differences between groups (p > 0.05). However, significant group × time interactions were found for CMJ (F = 8.92, p = 0.006), agility (F = 10.37, p = 0.003), and RSI (F = 12.45, p = 0.002), indicating greater gains in the COMB group. Specifically, CMJ improved by 7.21 cm vs. 4.45 cm, agility by −0.86 s vs. −0.47 s, and RSI by 0.49 vs. 0.26 in COMB and PLYO, respectively. These findings suggest that combined strength training elicits superior neuromuscular adaptations, likely due to enhanced force production and stretch–shortening cycle efficiency.

title: [Traducción al español] El efecto de la fortaleza mental en la relación entre las creencias irracionales sobre el rendimiento y los niveles de ansiedad de rasgo de los deportistas turcos: un análisis de mediación
title_original: [Traducción al español] El efecto de la fortaleza mental en la relación entre las creencias irracionales sobre el rendimiento y los niveles de ansiedad de rasgo de los deportistas turcos: un análisis de mediación
summary: PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to examine the mediating effect of mental toughness in the relationship between irrational performance beliefs and trait anxiety in individual and team athletes. METHODOLOGY: A total of 452 licensed athletes, including 150 females (mean age= 20.07 ± 2.20), 302 males (mean age = 20.35 ±3.64), 18 years old and above, who do individual and team sports in the province of Istanbul, participated in the study. "Irrational Performance Beliefs Inventory-2 (iPBI-2)", "Sports Anxiety Scale 2 (SAS-2)", "Scale of Mental Toughness in Sports (SCI)" and "Personal Information Form" were applied to the participants. In the analysis of the data, correlation and regression analyses and mediation analysis were performed. RESULTS: The findings showed that mental toughness mediated significantly in the relationship between irrational performance beliefs and trait anxiety. In addition, a significant relationship was observed between irrational performance beliefs, disintegration and commitment sub-dimensions of mental toughness, and trait anxiety. As a result, all subdimensions of irrational beliefs that are intertwined with the emotions, minds and thoughts of the athletes are among the subdimensions of mental toughness, which is expressed as the ability to recover against the negative thoughts and pressures encountered during the performance process, to try to reach the determined goals and to stick to their goals despite the disintegration and difficult conditions. CONCLUSION: It is observed that the subdimensions of commitment and the athletes' trait anxiety play a role in determining the distraction subdimension and the general level.

title: Scientific attitude, academic self-concept, and learning outcomes among sports specialised junior high students
title_original: Scientific attitude, academic self-concept, and learning outcomes among sports specialised junior high students
summary: This study aimed to examine whether scientific attitude and academic self-concept were associated with learning outcomes among eighth-grade students at a sports-specialised junior high school in Surakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative ex post facto design was employed. The study involved 64 students selected through total sampling. Data were collected using the Scientific Attitude Questionnaire, the Academic Self-Concept Scale, and first-semester report-card knowledge scores in Mathematics, Indonesian Language, Science, English, and Physical Education. Descriptive statistics, Pearson zero-order correlations, variable-level normality screening, multicollinearity diagnostics, and multiple linear regression analysis were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics version 26. The regression model was statistically significant (F(2ⓜ,61)=346.668, p<.001) and explained 91.9% of the variance in learning outcomes (R^2=.919; adjusted R^2=.916). Scientific attitude was significantly associated with learning outcomes and made a significant unique contribution to the regression model (B=1.413, SE=.093, β=.897, t=15.237, p<.001). In contrast, academic self-concept was not significantly associated with learning outcomes after scientific attitude was controlled for (B=.205, SE=.156, β=.077, t=1.315, p=.193). Among the predictors examined, scientific attitude comprising curiosity, critical thinking, inventiveness, and persistence showed the stronger unique statistical association with learning outcomes. These findings indicate that sports-specialised schools may support students’ academic engagement by incorporating inquiry-oriented learning, structured problem-solving, and reflective activities alongside athletic development.

title: Evaluating the usability and practicality of a proposed carbon footprint methodology and tool for National Olympic Committees
title_original: Evaluating the usability and practicality of a proposed carbon footprint methodology and tool for National Olympic Committees
summary: Robust carbon footprint methodologies and tools are increasingly required across the sport sector, yet National Olympic Committees lack a standardised, sector-specific approach. A bespoke carbon footprint methodology and accompanying calculation tool were developed for this purpose; however, technical rigour alone does not ensure that intended users can apply them. This study evaluates the usability and practicality of the proposed methodology and tool through direct engagement with end-users. Fourteen staff members from different National Olympic Committees applied the methodology and tool within their organisations over a four-to-six-week period, then completed the System Usability Scale and a semi-structured interview. The tool achieved a mean System Usability Scale score of 68.4, corresponding to a grade C and a marginal-high acceptability rating. Usability was rated positively, whereas learnability scored below the neutral midpoint, and scores correlated strongly with participants' years of experience (r = .99). Interviews indicated that effectiveness was the strongest dimension and learnability the weakest, with data collection identified as the main source of effort. Participants judged the methodology rigorous and credible but recommended improved onboarding, validation, and guidance to support less experienced users and wider adoption.

title: Mathematical Thinking Styles in Mathematical Modeling Activities in High School
title_original: Mathematical Thinking Styles in Mathematical Modeling Activities in High School
summary: This paper aims to investigate evidence of high school students’ mathematical thinking styles in the development of mathematical modeling activities. The paper presents an analysis of data collected through written records from two high school students engaged in mathematical modeling activities. The analysis employed idea association trees to support the identification of thinking style evidence manifested in the students’ productions. The results indicate that the mathematical thinking styles manifested by the two analyzed students were predominantly analytical in nature, evidenced using algorithmic procedures, sequential calculations, and the decomposition of the problem situation into parts. These findings suggest that, even in mathematical modeling activities, students preferentially resort to formal and symbolic strategies, possibly due to the school culture historically associated with teaching.

title: Psychological Profiles of Basketball Players Across Different Playing Positions: A Comparative Study
title_original: Psychological Profiles of Basketball Players Across Different Playing Positions: A Comparative Study
summary: Basketball is a high-intensity sport in which physical fitness, technical proficiency, cognitive abilities, and psychological characteristics interact to influence athletic performance. The psychological demands of the game may vary considerably according to the specific responsibilities associated with different playing positions. Point guards are required to demonstrate decision-making, confidence, and composure, whereas shooting guards may require motivation, aggression, and the ability to recover quickly from performance errors. Small forwards must exhibit adaptability and mental toughness, while power forwards and centers require resilience, concentration, emotional control, and composure under physical and competitive pressure. The present study focuses on the comparative psychological profiles of basketball players across the five conventional playing positions: point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, and center. The study examines psychological characteristics including concentration, mental toughness, aggression, stress tolerance, and broader personality attributes. A comparative approach is proposed to identify positional variations in psychological characteristics and to examine the extent to which role-specific demands are reflected in players' psychological profiles. The study is significant for coaches, sports psychologists, talent-identification professionals, and athletes because it may contribute to position-specific psychological training, player development, and performance enhancement. The investigation also addresses a research gap arising from the relatively limited and inconsistent evidence concerning psychological differences among basketball players across specific playing positions.

title: How Cyber Deterrence Theory and Cyber Persistence Theory can adopt an actor-centric approach: a rapid review
title_original: How Cyber Deterrence Theory and Cyber Persistence Theory can adopt an actor-centric approach: a rapid review
summary: Cyber deterrence and cyber persistence theories are commonly used to develop strategies to respond to unwanted behaviour in cyberspace. Whilst there is abundant academic research on the applicability of deterrence theory to cyberspace, and a growing compendium of works on cyber persistence theory, much research views cyber actors as a homogenous entity or broken into a binary of state vs non-state actors. This paper instead proposes taking an actor-centred approach. Performing a rapid review of cyber deterrence and cyber persistence theory, it finds there are five factors that impact actors: attribution, communication, cost, credibility (unique to deterrence) and interconnection (unique to persistence). Using abductive reasoning, the paper then identifies seven actor traits that may shape these factors: location, motives, technical skills, perception of the state, culture, personal connections and social status. By providing an initial framework linking the factors of these theories to characteristics of cyber actors, the paper highlights how variation between actors may influence the operation of deterrence and persistence based approaches. It is hoped that future research can examine the applicability and efficacy of these theories across states, cybercriminals, hacktivists, proxy actors, and other hybrid forms of cyber actor that blur traditional state/non-state distinctions.

title: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
title_original: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
summary: Abstract Crude oil transport is a vital component of global energy supply chains; however, it is riddled with systemic risks, including human error, infrastructure fragility, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory deficiencies. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of crude oil transport, with particular emphasis on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG), a semi-autonomous territory that has emerged as a significant oil producer despite enduring geopolitical instability. By triangulating peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, regulatory documents, and primary survey data from 150 public respondents and 50 tanker drivers and owners within the KRG, this study articulates the multifaceted risks associated with road-based crude oil transport. Economic regression analysis, employing logistic regression, difference-in-differences, and ordered probit models, reveals that regular safety training reduces the odds of an accident by 58.4% (p=0.005); the 2023-2025 KRG-Turkey pipeline suspension caused approximately $12.5 billion in economic losses; and pipeline resumption increased realised prices by 38.50 per barrel (p<0.001). Key findings indicate that public awareness of transport risks is moderate, with only 11% expressing high confidence in regulatory oversight; 73% of respondents identified tanker accidents as their primary environmental concern; 46% of drivers reported experiencing accidents, while 74% witnessed spills or leaks; infrastructure deficits, including poor road conditions reported by 68% of drivers and inadequate equipment, constitute primary operational hazards; and geopolitical disruptions aggravate safety vulnerabilities by increasing reliance on higher-risk road transport. Cost-benefit analysis indicates that driver training programmes and GPS tracking mandates yield benefit-cost ratios of 25.4:1 and 25.7:1, respectively. The paper proposes a novel analytical framework that integrates human factors, security threats, and regulatory responses, offering evidence-based recommendations for policy reform in conflict-affected oil-producing regions.

title: Gratitude to nature, environmental stewardship, and well-being in 10 countries
title_original: Gratitude to nature, environmental stewardship, and well-being in 10 countries
summary: Abstract People may feel grateful to nature for its provisions, as both anecdotal accounts and emerging research evidence suggest. The present study further explores this experience—referred to as gratitude to nature—by examining its relationships with other nature-related constructs, environmental stewardship, psychological well-being, and physical health across 10 countries from both the Global North and Global South. We assessed the Gratitude to Nature Scale’s measurement invariance and construct validity across these diverse social contexts and observed consistently positive associations between gratitude to nature and experience with nature, nature connectedness, and anthropomorphism of nature. Our findings also reveal that individuals who possessed stronger gratitude to nature were more likely to engage in various forms of pro-environmental behaviors and that stronger gratitude was significantly linked to both hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, and to self-reported physical health to a lesser degree. Overall, these results encourage future research to investigate the potential of interventions based on gratitude to nature for fostering ecological stewardship and promoting well-being. This research contributes to the emerging relational discourse on human-nature relationships by emphasizing the affective connection between people and the natural world. It also echoes recent calls for cross-cultural studies in the study of human–environment relationships.

title: Effects of Native Language on Students’ Academic Performance in English in North – Eastern Nigerian Polytechnics
title_original: Effects of Native Language on Students’ Academic Performance in English in North – Eastern Nigerian Polytechnics
summary: This study dwells on the effect of native language on students’ academic performance in English language with a focus on North-Eastern Nigerian Federal Polytechnics. Namely, these include Federal Polytechnic, Bali, Kaltungo, Mubi, Damaturu and Bauchi precisely. The target participants of this study are students of National Diploma (ND) who have been taken English as general studies from some departments in the study area. Six departments are sampled using simple random sampling technique accordingly. The study intends to use a cross-sectional survey design and questionnaires as an instrument for data collection from the participants. A mixed method which involves both quantitative and qualitative are utilized for summary of data using descriptive statistics from the tables. On the other hand, qualitative data are put under the tables and follow with explanations. A judgement rule is drawn to decide significant findings and insignificant findings in the study. The Interlanguage Theory, proposed by Larry Selinker in 1972, is highly relevant to this study as it provides a framework for understanding how learners' native languages influence their second language acquisition, particularly in educational settings. The results find out that the use of native language have some negative effects on academic performance of the students in English language in Federal Polytechnics, under study. Therefore, the findings showcase that native language affects the participants' academic performance such as writing and speaking in English as a language of instruction. In response to that, some useful recommendations such as the teaching methodology should be interactive in English for a classroom rapport. That will motivate the students to participate more and improve their performance in the target language. In essence, this corresponds to a claim makes by Krashen who posits that once the adequate input is made available in a L2 class, the grammar will come up automatically. So, the results are useful for English language teachers, students, curriculum developers, young scholars and interested person or organization.

Therefore, the findings showcase that native language affects the participants' academic performance such as writing and speaking in English as a language of instruction. In response to that, some useful recommendations such as the teaching methodology should be interactive in English for a classroom rapport. That will motivate the students to participate more and improve their performance in the target language. In essence, this corresponds to a claim makes by Krashen who posits that once the adequate input is made available in a L2 class, the grammar will come up automatically. title: Atmospheric fingerprints of urbanization: Satellite-based detection of nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide dynamics in a tropical highland city
title_original: Atmospheric fingerprints of urbanization: Satellite-based detection of nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide dynamics in a tropical highland city
summary: Rapidly growing medium-sized cities in the tropics may exhibit complex spatial patterns of combustion-related air pollutants while remaining poorly represented by conventional ground-based monitoring networks.This study characterizes nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), and carbon monoxide (CO) over Malang City, East Java, Indonesia, using Sentinel-5P TROPOMI observations for selected periods in 2021 and 2025.Tropospheric column densities were processed in Google Earth Engine and converted to estimated ambient concentrations using a mixing-height formulation.The estimates were classified according to the Indonesian air pollution standard index and compared with available ministry in situ observations and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) reanalysis using regression, root mean square error, and mean absolute error.City-mean concentrations were lower in the analysed 2025 periods than in 2021 for NO 2 (5.36 to 4.60 μg/m 3 ) and CO (1.571 to 1.465 μg/m 3 ).Because the two years were not sampled in the same months, each difference was recomputed across every possible month subset.Only the CO difference proved robust (-6.7%, envelope -7.3% to -6.1%); the NO 2 difference was robust in direction but not in magnitude (-24.9% to -3.5%); and the apparent SO2 decrease reversed to an increase when restricted to the months common to both years (-60% to +34%) and is therefore not reported as a difference.Spatial patterns differed among pollutants: NO 2 maxima occurred along northern and western built-up corridors, SO 2 was higher near the eastern and southern industrial periphery, whereas CO was relatively homogeneous, with a coefficient of variation below 2%.Agreement with in situ observations was weak for NO 2 and absent for SO 2 , with no satellite-reference correlation reaching statistical significance (p ≥ 0.09) and every confidence interval on r spanning zero, indicating that satellitederived concentrations are more appropriately interpreted as spatial screening estimates.The principal contribution is a multi-pollutant characterization of Malang as a tropical highland city with limited ground-based monitoring, revealing contrasting spatial signatures of NO 2 , SO 2 , and CO.These findings demonstrate the potential of satellite observations to complement sparse ground-based monitoring in data-limited tropical urban environments.

title: Disclosing pollution: causal impacts of key emission unit listings on Shanghai's housing market
title_original: Disclosing pollution: causal impacts of key emission unit listings on Shanghai's housing market
summary: Abstract We provide causal estimates of the effect of Shanghai's key emission unit listings on nearby housing prices. Implemented in 2016, the disclosure policy requires annual public disclosure of designated polluting firms and their pollution information. Using repeated cross-sectional data on Shanghai housing transactions from 2015 to 2022, we apply a heterogeneity-robust staggered difference-in-differences estimator to identify dynamic capitalization effects while addressing treatment heterogeneity, treatment reversibility and time-invariant omitted variables. We find that each additional disclosed key emission unit within 1,000 m reduces nearby housing prices by 1.31 per cent, with larger declines for suburban properties than for properties in the urban core. By examining ongoing industrial pollution under a unified disclosure framework, our findings extend prior U.S. and Chinese studies that focus on legacy contamination or specific pollutants. The results highlight the policy relevance of pollution transparency and inform China's nationwide implementation.

title: Beauty–bloodbath, vulnerability–vengeance: Representations of Draupadi in popular culture
title_original: Beauty–bloodbath, vulnerability–vengeance: Representations of Draupadi in popular culture
summary: This article examines postcolonial feminist re-imaginings of Draupadi, a central figure in the Mahabharata, across contemporary genres, specifically Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni’s novel The Palace of Illusions (2008), Mahasweta Devi’s short story “Draupadi” (1981), and Saraswati Nagpal’s graphic novel Draupadi: The Fireborn Princess (2012). Through a conceptual framework of four metaphoric binaries: “Beauty–Bloodbath and Vulnerability–Vengeance”, it interrogates the construction of female agency, mythic symbolism, and embodied resistance in a postcolonial feminist context. Draupadi emerges as a transmedial icon whose cultural representations speak to contemporary gendered violence, caste oppression, and the politics of memory. These texts challenge patriarchal and nationalist appropriations of the epic heroine, repositioning Draupadi as a site of contestation, rage, and political critique. Drawing on concepts from feminist, intersectional, and visual culture theory, the article explores how myth functions not only as cultural memory but also as a mutable narrative space for articulating resistance and reimagining justice.

title: Nationalism as Imperialism in Disguise: Re‐Examining Global Citizenship and Chinese Identity in Hong Kong
title_original: Nationalism as Imperialism in Disguise: Re‐Examining Global Citizenship and Chinese Identity in Hong Kong
summary: ABSTRACT This Research Note responds to Yang's (2026) study of global citizenship and Chinese identity in Hong Kong by advancing three interrelated critiques. First, we argue that globalism and nationalism in Hong Kong are historically co‐constituted. Yang's interpretation places global citizenship, Chinese identity and Hong Kong identity within a global, national and subnational hierarchy without sufficiently examining the historical relationship among them. Second, we propose that the state‐led project labelled ‘Chinese nationalism’ in Hong Kong may be understood as imperial governance pursued through the language of national belonging. Secondary analysis of longitudinal survey data (HKPORI, 2007–2022) supports this reframing, revealing that the expansion of ‘glocal’ identification resulted mainly from declining Chinese identification rather than a comparable rise in global identification. Third, we contend that coding Hong Kong nationalism as local or subnational identity creates a blind spot that obscures a documented form of stateless nationhood. Together, these interventions call for a more historically grounded and conceptually critical engagement with nationalism in contested Chinese contexts.

title: Different Cues Leading to Meaningful Differences in Contact Mat Countermovement Jump Assessment in Collegiate Team Sport Athletes: A Preliminary Study
title_original: Different Cues Leading to Meaningful Differences in Contact Mat Countermovement Jump Assessment in Collegiate Team Sport Athletes: A Preliminary Study
summary: Contact mats estimate countermovement jump (CMJ) height via flight time, assuming consistent body positioning at take-off and landing. However, foot landing technique, specifically soft versus stiff landings, may alter ankle and joint angles, potentially biasing jump height measurements. This study investigated the effect of externally cued ankle-focused landing styles- specifically ball-of-foot (“soft”) versus heel-first (“stiff”) landings on CMJ height measured by a contact mat in collegiate male team sport athletes. One hundred male team sport athletes (age 21.4 years; height 182.3 cm; weight 78.6 kg) performed CMJs under randomized, counterbalanced soft (ball-of-foot, greater plantar flexion) and stiff (heel-first, minimal plantar flexion) landing conditions. Jump height was measured with the Just Jump contact mat using the Bosco protocol. Participants completed three trials per condition; average jump heights obtained under the soft and stiff landing conditions were compared using paired t-tests, while Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis assessed the relationship and agreement between two landing styles. CMJ height was significantly greater during stiff landings (48.50 ± 5.51 cm) compared to soft landings (45.62 ± 5.80 cm), with a mean difference of 2.88 cm (p = 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.28). A strong positive correlation (r = 0.92) indicated consistent ranking across conditions, but Bland-Altman analysis revealed systematic bias and moderate variability between landing styles. Landing technique substantially influences CMJ height measurements using a contact mat, with stiff landings producing inflated jump heights. However, this preliminary study did not include biomechanical verification of landing mechanics, which should be considered in future research.These findings highlight the need for standardized, explicit ankle landing instructions during CMJ testing to ensure accuracy and comparability of results in sport performance assessment and monitoring.

Jump height was measured with the Just Jump contact mat using the Bosco protocol. Participants completed three trials per condition; average jump heights obtained under the soft and stiff landing conditions were compared using paired t-tests, while Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis assessed the relationship and agreement between two landing styles. CMJ height was significantly greater during stiff landings (48.50 ± 5.51 cm) compared to soft landings (45.62 ± 5.80 cm), with a mean difference of 2.88 cm (p = 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.28). A strong positive correlation (r = 0.92) indicated consistent ranking across conditions, but Bland-Altman analysis revealed systematic bias and moderate variability between landing styles. Landing technique substantially influences CMJ height measurements using a contact mat, with stiff landings producing inflated jump heights. However, this preliminary study did not include biomechanical verification of landing mechanics, which should be considered in future research.These findings highlight the need for standardized, explicit ankle landing instructions during CMJ testing to ensure accuracy and comparability of results in sport performance assessment and monitoring.

title: Beyond Time Loss: Position-Specific Injury-to-Performance Pathways After Hand Fractures in Elite European Football
title_original: Beyond Time Loss: Position-Specific Injury-to-Performance Pathways After Hand Fractures in Elite European Football
summary: Background: Hand fractures are common sports injuries, but the same diagnosis may carry different performance consequences according to how essential the hand is to a player's role.We investigated whether fracture burden and the broader injury-to-performance pathway differed by playing position, from injury phenotype and acute absence to competitive reintegration and sustained participation.Materials and methods: This retrospective matched cohort study linked manually validated public injury reports with league appearances from the five major leagues, Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, and Ligue 1 from 2007/08 through 2024/25.Of 35,952 injury records, 329 candidate records with possible hand or wrist injuries (0.9%) were reviewed, from which 148 fracture events (45.0% of candidates) in 142 players were retained.Primary analyses compared incidence, time loss, competitive return, and one-year participation after the publicly reported injury end.Exploratory analyses tested position-specific fracture phenotype and the time period from the public injury-end milestone to first subsequent appearance in one of the five major leagues.Results: Fracture phenotype differed by position (chi-square = 21.48,P < .001;Cramér's V = 0.38): finger/phalangeal fractures accounted for 31 of 63 goalkeeper events (49.2%) versus 15 of 85 outfield events (17.6%) (odds ratio (OR), 4.52; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.15-9.52),whereas metacarpal fractures accounted for 10 of 63 goalkeeper events (15.9%) versus 34 of 85 outfield events (40.0%) (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.13-0.63).Goalkeepers faced greater time loss than outfielders, even within the same fracture subtype (position-by-subtype interaction, P = .407).Median time loss was 43 days among 63 goalkeeper events versus 18 days among 85 outfield events (adjusted ratio, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.58-2.79).By 90 days, 17 of 45 goalkeepers (37.8%) versus 55 of 68 outfield players (80.9%) had reappeared competitively.Of 103 fracture episodes with an observed appearance after the reported injury end, 14 of 35 goalkeeper episodes (40.0%) versus seven of 68 outfield episodes (10.3%) required more than 90 additional days to reappear (aOR, 6.94; 95% CI, 2.06-23.41;false discovery rate-adjusted q = .005).In the matched cohort, a 30% or greater participation decline occurred in 10 of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases (55.6%) versus 21 of 72 goalkeeper controls (29.2%)(aOR, 3.30; 95% CI, 1.08-10.08),with a fracture-by-goalkeeper interaction OR of 5.74 (95% CI, 1.46-22.66);this interaction estimate was based on a small subgroup of 18 goalkeeper fracture cases.Conclusions: The important positional signal extends beyond the already expected higher fracture incidence in goalkeepers.Playing position was associated with differences in fracture phenotype, acute burden, the transition from the publicly reported injury-end milestone to subsequent competitive selection, and subsequent participation.Return-to-play counseling should therefore distinguish the publicly reported injury-end milestone from subsequent competitive reintegration and incorporate role-specific hand function rather than calendar time alone.

title: دراسة تحليلية لواقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية
title_original: دراسة تحليلية لواقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية
summary: هدف البحث الى بناء وتطبيق مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية، والتعرف على واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية. وانتهج الباحث المنهج الوصفي بالأسلوب المسحي لملاءمته طبيعة المشكلة، وتم اختيار مجتمع البحث من مدرسي التربية الرياضية في مديرية تربية الرصافة الثالثة وعددهم (420) مدرس ومدرسة، اما عينة البحث فتكونت من (200) مدرس ومدرسة التربية الرياضية، اي بنسبة (47.61%) من مجتمع البحث. وتم تقسيم العينة الى ثلاث عينات: عينة التجربة الاستطلاعية، عينة البناء، عينة التطبيق. بعدها قام الباحث ببناء مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية على وفق ما يلي :تم صياغة عدد من العبارات الخاصة بمقياس المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية للحصول على النتائج وبما يتلائم وطبيعة عمل مجتمع البحث وعددها (25) عبارة. وبعد الإجراءات التي تم ذكرها، قام الباحث بأجراء التجربة الاستطلاعية على عينة من (15) فرد، في (14/01/2025)، لغرض تهيئة الظروف المناسبة عند تطبيق الاختبار الرئيسي. بعدها تم تطبيق المقياس على عينة البناء البالغ عددها (95) فرداً وذلك للمدة من (21/1/2025) لغاية (2/2/2025) وإن الغرض من إجراء هذه التجربة هو بناء مقياس واقع المهارات والقدرات الإبداعية لمشرفي النشاط الرياضي والكشفي من وجهة نظر مدرسي التربية الرياضية. واستقر المقياس بصيغته النهائية على (25) عبارة. وبعد ان تم بناء المقياس قام الباحث بتطبيق صورة المقياس النهائية على عينة البحث والبالغ عددها (90) فرداً، وذلك للمدة من (5/3/2025) ولغاية (2/4/2025). بعدها تم مناقشة النتائج ورفدها بالمصادر العلمية.

title: The association between data-driven training monitoring and athlete burnout: a chain-mediated indirect path between performance anxiety and psychological exhaustion
title_original: The association between data-driven training monitoring and athlete burnout: a chain-mediated indirect path between performance anxiety and psychological exhaustion
summary: Introduction Data-driven training monitoring has enhanced the precision of training-load assessment, fatigue detection, and training regulation in competitive sport. However, continuous data collection, performance metric comparisons, and evaluative feedback may also constitute emerging sources of psychological stress for athletes. Drawing on the Technology Stress Generators Model, the Challenge–Hindrance Stressor Framework, and the Job Demands–Resources Model, this study examined the relationships among data-driven training monitoring stress (DTMS), evaluative anxiety, psychological exhaustion, and athlete burnout, as well as potential differences across gender and sport type. Methods Cross-sectional questionnaire data were collected from 588 active athletes. Confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, bootstrap tests of indirect effects, and multigroup analysis were conducted to examine the hypothesized relationships and between-group differences. Results DTMS was significantly and positively associated with evaluative anxiety, psychological exhaustion, and athlete burnout. Evaluative anxiety and psychological exhaustion each constituted a significant indirect pathway between DTMS and athlete burnout, and the sequential indirect pathway through evaluative anxiety and psychological exhaustion was also statistically significant. Multigroup analysis further showed significant between-group differences in the association between DTMS and evaluative anxiety. This association was stronger among female athletes than among male athletes and stronger among athletes in physical endurance sports than among those in skill-based sports. Discussion The findings suggest that data-driven training monitoring should extend beyond the technical objectives of data acquisition and assessment accuracy to incorporate psychologically informed practices. Particular attention should be given to the interpretation of monitoring data, the communication of anomalous indicators, and the delivery of evaluative feedback to reduce the psychological burden potentially associated with data-intensive monitoring.

title: Povezanost izbranih gibalnih sposobnosti s tekmovalno uspešnostjo v alpskem smučanju v kategoriji U12
title_original: Povezanost izbranih gibalnih sposobnosti s tekmovalno uspešnostjo v alpskem smučanju v kategoriji U12
summary: Spodaj podpisana Kaja Hladnik izjavljam, da:-je predloženo zaključno delo izključno rezultat mojega lastnega raziskovalnega dela; -predloženo zaključno delo ni nastalo na podlagi nepooblaščene rabe sistema (generativne) umetne inteligence, kot je opredeljeno v Stališčih Univerze na Primorskem do rabe umetne inteligence, -sem poskrbel/-a, da so dela in mnenja drugih avtorjev oz.avtoric, ki jih uporabljam v predloženem zaključnem delu, navedena oz.citirana v skladu z navodili fakultete, -sem poskrbel/-a, da so vsa dela in mnenja drugih avtorjev oz.avtoric navedena v seznamu virov, ki je sestavni element predloženega zaključnega dela in je zapisan v skladu z navodili fakultete, -sem pridobil/-a vsa dovoljenja za uporabo avtorskih del, ki so v celoti prenesena v predloženo zaključno delo in sem to tudi jasno zapisal/-a v predloženem zaključnem delu, -se zavedam, da je plagiatorstvo -predstavljanje tujih del, bodisi v obliki citata bodisi v obliki skoraj dobesednega parafraziranja bodisi v grafični obliki, s katerim so tuje misli oz.ideje predstavljene kot moje lastne -kaznivo po zakonu (Zakon o avtorskih in sorodnih pravicah (Uradni list RS, št.16/07 -uradno prečiščeno besedilo, 68/08, 110/13 in 56/15), prekršek pa podleže tudi disciplinskim ukrepom Univerze na Primorskem v skladu z njenimi pravili, -se zavedam posledic, ki jih dokazano plagiatorstvo lahko predstavlja za predloženo zaključno delo in za moj status na fakulteti, -je zaključno delo lektorirano in urejeno skladno z navodili fakultete.Soglašam z objavo magistrske naloge v Repozitoriju UP.

title: Sporda Çocukluk Dönemi Kötü Muamele Ölçeği (ÇDSKMÖ): Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
title_original: Sporda Çocukluk Dönemi Kötü Muamele Ölçeği (ÇDSKMÖ): Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
summary: Bu çalışmanın amacı, bireylerin çocukluk dönemindeki spor yaşantılarında deneyimledikleri kötü muamele davranışlarını retrospektif olarak değerlendirmeye yönelik geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı geliştirmek ve geliştirilen Çocukluk Dönemi Sporda Kötü Muamele Ölçeği’nin (ÇDSKMÖ) psikometrik özelliklerini incelemektir. Araştırma metodolojik ölçek geliştirme deseninde yürütülmüştür. Olasılıklı olmayan uygun örnekleme yoluyla, 18 yaşından önce spora katılmış ve spor bilimleri alanında öğrenim gören 400 genç yetişkine ulaşılmıştır. Veri seti açımlayıcı faktör analizi (AFA) ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi (DFA) için 200’er kişilik iki bağımsız gruba rastgele ayrılmıştır. Alan yazın taramasıyla oluşturulan 56 maddelik havuz, uzman değerlendirmeleri ve ön deneme sonrasında 52 maddeye indirilmiştir. AFA sonucunda duygusal istismar, cinsel istismar, fiziksel istismar, ihmal ve akran zorbalığı alt ölçeklerinin her birinin tek boyutlu yapı gösterdiği ve nihai formun 45 maddeden oluştuğu belirlenmiştir. Faktör yükleri 0,658–0,905, açıklanan varyans oranları %52,371–%72,183 ve Cronbach alfa katsayıları 0,884–0,938 arasında değişmiştir. Bağımsız örneklemde yürütülen DFA, beş alt ölçekli yapıyı ve alt ölçeklerin ortak bir üst yapı altında değerlendirilmesini desteklemiştir (χ²/sd=0,65; RMSEA=0,005; NFI=0,96; CFI=0,99; GFI=0,98). Sonuçlar, ÇDSKMÖ’nün bireylerin çocukluk dönemindeki spor yaşantılarında deneyimledikleri kötü muamele davranışlarını davranış temelli ve çok boyutlu biçimde retrospektif olarak değerlendirmede kullanılabilecek geçerli ve güvenilir bir öz-bildirim aracı olduğunu göstermektedir.

title: International sport policy meets national cultures: reinterpreting qualitative interview data to understand Safe Sport implementation
title_original: International sport policy meets national cultures: reinterpreting qualitative interview data to understand Safe Sport implementation
summary: With challenges related to interpersonal violence in sport as a backdrop, this paper examines how cultural institutions operate across societal contexts and what this means for Safe Sport implementation in six European Mediterranean countries: Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Malta, Portugal and Spain. In an earlier study, interviews with individuals educating and recruiting coaches (n = 60, 10 from each country) and thematic analysis identified three institutions that constrain Safe Sport implementation: patriarchy, a winning (at-all-costs) attitude and an orientation towards blindness and silence. In this paper, we conduct a theory-driven secondary analysis of the same data, understanding institutions as three pillars(regulative, normative and cultural-cognitive) to examine how these institutions are carried and reproduced across three carriers of interrelated contexts: the state, the family and sport. The analysis demonstrates that the states’ weak regulative role allows these institutions to function, families socialise their members into accepting them and in sport they operate largely unchallenged. For Safe Sport implementation to progress, several carriers of institutions must change relatively simultaneously. States must provide not only laws but protection systems for those who report harm; families must socialise children to recognise and speak about unacceptable behaviour; and sport organisations need structures that support rather than penalise disclosure.
