title: Bifurcation point or inertial process? (Reflections on cosmic evolution and the current state of civilization)
title_original: Bifurcation point or inertial process? (Reflections on cosmic evolution and the current state of civilization)
summary: The article examines the problem of the contemporary state of earthly civilization through the lens of cosmic evolution, while the author consciously distances himself from both eschatological predictions and speculative projects of "returning to space." In contrast to popular concepts of cosmotechnology (Yuk Hui) and Russian cosmism (S. Semyonov), which interpret space more as a metaphor for cultural or spiritual transformation, a rigorous epistemic and cultural optics is proposed: space is viewed not as an abstract whole, but as a successive change of local earthly wholes &#8210; physical, biological, and anthropo-social. The methodological framework of the article consists of three approaches: discrete understanding of evolution (the change of wholes and laws), dialectical combination of the regular and the singular, as well as a cultural analysis of the change of historical types of culture. The author relies on Aristotle's distinction between natural and active processes, complementing it with modern catastrophe theory (R. Thom) and the synergetic paradigm (bifurcation points, strange attractors). The central thesis of the article is that the transition from one cosmic integrity to another does not occur smoothly, but through dramatic "bifurcation points," where random factors and "big ideas," framed into new semiotic systems and technology, play a decisive role. As a historical case, the invention of the Egyptian pyramids is examined, where the religious problem of the pharaoh's death is resolved through the creation of complex schemes and technical innovations, which are both a product of regular development and a singular event. The main conclusion relates to modern culture, which formed after the Westphalian world. The realization of "big ideas" (mastery of nature, construction of the state, religious and national sovereignty) has led to impressive successes, but also to systemic deviations, conflicts, and crises. The author notes that contemporary civilization has found itself at a bifurcation point, the risks of which (nuclear weapons, ecological collapse, social chaos) far exceed historical analogues. The question of whether this situation will become a point of no return or a process of reassembly remains open and depends on humanity's ability for reflection, rejection of outdated big ideas, and readiness for compromises.

title: Alexey Yavlinsky: Seriality as an Artistic Method
title_original: Alexey Yavlinsky: Seriality as an Artistic Method
summary: The subject of the research is the serial method in the work of Alexei Yavlensky based on the materials of the cycles: "Variations," "Mystical Heads," "Faces of the Savior," "Abstract Heads," and "Meditations." This work traces the sequential transformation of the same motif from a landscape impression to a human face and then to a highly generalized image. Special attention is given to the repeated reference to the discovered form, where each new work becomes another stage in its further development. It analyzes how the degree of synthesis, the nature of composition, the relationship of color masses, and the role of pictorial texture change from cycle to cycle. "Meditations" are regarded as a late stage in this process, in which the human face acquires a generalized and sacred character. The connection between the serial practice and the understanding of color as the main means of expressing inner content is revealed. The study employs formal-stylistic, comparative-typological, and iconological methods. With their help, works from different cycles are compared, stable and changing elements of the plastic structure are identified, and the development of the serial principle is recorded. The conducted analysis shows that seriality for Yavlensky is not just a technique allowing for the unification of several works around a single motif, but rather a method of creative thinking. The scientific novelty lies in substantiating the role of seriality in the formation of Yavlensky's method. Unlike the approach that considers cycles in isolation, here, their internal continuity and the general working principle of the artist with the image are traced. This allows for establishing how the solutions found in the landscape "Variations" continue in portrait painting, and how the nature of this process changes in subsequent series. title: FOLLOWING ROUSSEAU: THE PROBLEM OF EDUCATION IN FRENCH AND RUSSIAN GENRE PAINTING OF THE 18TH CENTURY
title_original: FOLLOWING ROUSSEAU: THE PROBLEM OF EDUCATION IN FRENCH AND RUSSIAN GENRE PAINTING OF THE 18TH CENTURY
summary: The subject of this study is the impact of Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s educational thought on the development of the moralizing family genre in eighteenth-century French painting and its reception in Russian art during the second half of the century. The article aims to identify visual representations of childhood, domestic education, parental responsibility, and family life in works by Jean-Baptiste-Sim&#233;on Chardin, Jean-Baptiste Greuze, Jean-Honor&#233; Fragonard, Ivan Yakimov, and Jean-Baptiste Leprince. Particular attention is given to Rousseauist concepts of education in accordance with nature, the child’s age-specific needs, the primacy of parental care, and criticism of the practice of entrusting infants to wet nurses. The research employs comparative-historical, formal-stylistic, iconographic, and iconological approaches. Its source base includes Rousseau’s Emile, or On Education, Denis Diderot’s writings, Russian memoirs of the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, literary texts, paintings, and reproductive engravings. Comparison of French and Russian material makes it possible to trace both visual correspondences and the cultural mechanisms through which Enlightenment pedagogical ideals were adapted within Russia. The study establishes that Chardin’s paintings foreground domestic instruction, play, work, and childhood as a distinct stage of life; Greuze formulates images of family virtue, filial duty, and moral guidance; and Fragonard addresses the consequences of separating children from their parents. It shows that engravings, private collections, and the Imperial Academy of Arts facilitated the dissemination of the French moralizing genre in Russia. In Yakimov’s family scenes, Ivan Khemnitser’s fable, and Leprince’s Russian subjects, the French sentimental-didactic model was reinterpreted either as an idealization of patriarchal domesticity or as a socially critical depiction of poverty and family hardship. The findings contribute to the study of Russo-French artistic exchange, genre painting, and the visual history of childhood.

title: From Text to Being: The Transductive Symbolism of Andrei Bely as an "Ontosemiotic Operator"
title_original: From Text to Being: The Transductive Symbolism of Andrei Bely as an "Ontosemiotic Operator"
summary: The focus of the study is the operational layer of the prose of Andrei Bely, where the text functions as a mechanism that initiates an ontological rupture. The analysis draws on the philosophy of Gilbert Simondon and the semiotics of Yuri Lotman. This overarching worldview allows us to examine how the symbol loses its representative function and gains the status of an ontosemiotic operator. This transductive operator interacts with pre-individual tension, each time leaving this process unfinished. Rhythmic disruptions, color entropy, syntactical collapse, as well as figures of the double, the automaton, and the mask form a unified mechanism. This mechanism marks a failure in the process of individuation. Bely's text does not depict a crisis of subjectivity but rather presents it as an ongoing process of becoming. The proposed approach allows us to see Bely's prose not only as a literary monument but also as an active model of the crisis of becoming, which is now reproduced in algorithmic environments and on digital platforms. The methodology is based on a combination of processual ontology and semiotic-cultural approaches. It employs methods of interpreting philosophical and literary texts, conceptual analysis, and comparative modeling. Processual ontology and the semiotics of culture create a dual optics and allow for the description of the operational layer of Bely's prose. Despite the fact that for Simondon the sign or signification appears only in the later stages of the process of individuation, while for Lotman, conversely, the semiosphere precedes any act of signification and serves as a condition for the possibility of meaning, there is a fundamental difference between these positions. However, for the analysis of Bely, this difference is not an obstacle but a resource. We are not attempting to reduce one theory to another or declare them mutually consistent. Our approach is pragmatic. We will use the concept of "ontosemiotic operator" as a working metaphor that captures the dual nature of Bely's symbol. The symbol in Bely simultaneously resolves metastability and generates meaning at the boundary of the semiosphere. Where incompatibility arises between ontological and semiotic perspectives, we will view this as an indication of real tension within Bely's text itself, rather than as a deficiency in our methodology. In other words, the contradiction between Simondon's and Lotman's approaches becomes for us not a problem but a heuristic tool.

title: Ethno-oriented vocal style in Chinese musicals
title_original: Ethno-oriented vocal style in Chinese musicals
summary: This article examines a vocal style characterized by the extensive use of techniques borrowed by musical theatre performers from folk singing. The author describes the vocal-technical characteristics of these techniques and analyzes their expressive potential through the study of specific works. Particular attention is paid to mintong singing, which most often serves as the vehicle for ethnic identity in Chinese musicals and is the product of a synthesis between folk and popular vocal styles. The author further clarifies that the term "folk singing" ("ethnic singing") in China has various interpretations: it can be used both to denote the authentic manner of folklore practitioners and to describe a synthetic style that incorporates elements of European bel canto, folk singing, and the vocal techniques of traditional operas. The author compares ethnic, pop, and mintong singing across a number of vocal and technical parameters. For clarity, the comparison results are presented in a table.  The study uses stylistic and performance analysis methods, as well as a comparative analysis method to identify the specific features of mintong vocal style. The author concludes that the inclusion of ethnic singing techniques in musical vocal parts offers great expressive potential. This applies both to the use of the synthetic mintong style and to more direct recourse to folk singing techniques and traditional (particularly Peking) opera. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the detailed analysis of a number of vocal parts in Chinese musicals, examining their technical characteristics, stylistic distinctiveness, and expressive capabilities. The analysis suggests that stylistic blends incorporating various ethnic components make it possible to convey  a wide range of musical images and to portray diverse character traits and theatrical situations. The author also believes that the use of ethnic singing techniques is a crucial factor in shaping the national identity of the musical genre in China and can contribute to its popularization beyond the country's borders.

title: Gnostic formation of modern culture: code, activation indicators, diagnostic rule
title_original: Gnostic formation of modern culture: code, activation indicators, diagnostic rule
summary: The article substantiates the concept of gnostic formation as an operational category for the analysis of contemporary culture. Its subject is a methodological apparatus designed to distinguish the lexical presence of gnosis in contemporary culture from its structural fulfillment. The vocabulary of gnosis is increasingly employed in accounts of technoculture, digital environments, and mass narratives, while the scholarly credentials of the very category of "Gnosticism" have come under radical criticism in the study of religion. The existing approaches – genealogical, typological, critical, descriptive, motif-oriented, and studies of actors' self-descriptions in conspiracist milieus – register the presence of the gnostic vocabulary but lack a procedure that admits of a negative outcome: the diagnosis is recognized wherever the optics are directed.  The methodological core of the article is a threefold distinction: the gnostic code as a generative grammar; activation indicators as the observer's instrument; and the gnostic formation as a configuration of discourses and practices in which the code is dominant. The three members deliberately differ in epistemological status: the formation belongs to observable cultural reality, the code is an analytical reconstruction of its structural grammar, and the indicators belong to the observer's operational apparatus. The diagnostic rule admits of a negative outcome. The model is tested on a diachronic series of condition configurations, on historical material providing negative controls, on the postmodern and the metamodern-digital phases of contemporary culture, and on a corpus of ten studies. The novelty of the research resides in the threefold distinction itself, which separates three questions that previous approaches have been forced to answer at once – what is reproduced, how it is to be recognized, and when its dominance may be asserted; in a system of indicators governed by a diagnostic rule that allows the diagnosis to fail; and in the criterion of convergent genesis, which states the conditions under which the reproduction of the code without a channel of transmission would be assertible. The principal conclusions are as follows. The activation of the code's core is registered in the metamodern-digital configuration of contemporary culture, while the formation itself retains the status of a candidate pending an independent test of dominance. Negative outcomes are obtained at all four scales of the apparatus's application: the individual artifact, the corpus, the historical configuration, and the cultural phase. The thesis of a second Hellenism is operationalized as the reassembly of a configuration of conditions rather than a claim about the similarity of epochs, and convergent genesis retains the status of a hypothesis concerning the mechanism. The proposed procedure of transferring the grammar without the portrait is offered as a reproducible alternative both to typological portraiture and to the accusatory use of the category.

Its subject is a methodological apparatus designed to distinguish the lexical presence of gnosis in contemporary culture from its structural fulfillment. The vocabulary of gnosis is increasingly employed in accounts of technoculture, digital environments, and mass narratives, while the scholarly credentials of the very category of "Gnosticism" have come under radical criticism in the study of religion. title: Art of the New Objectivity in the context of the socio-political situation of the Weimar Republic
title_original: Art of the New Objectivity in the context of the socio-political situation of the Weimar Republic
summary: This article is devoted to studying the question of how the social and political situation in Germany during the Weimar Republic influenced the formatiom of the original artistic iconography of the subjects in the New Objectivity artistic movement. As the object of research, some artworks by German artists belonging to this movement (G. Gross, O. Dix, M. Beckman) have been selected. Carried out on a socially relevant topics, they can be considered as a kind of visual chronicle of the social life in interwar Europe. The main subject of study are trends in the social and political life of the Weimar Republic, which influenced the formation of the artistic iconography of the New Objectivity. Its classification is considered as the main research task of the article, where parallels are made between different events of social and political life in Germany during the Weimar era and some groups of plots. The research methods used are formal-stylistic and iconographic analysis, the comparatist method and the principle of historicism. The scientific novelty of the article consists in the fact that for the first time in the historiography of the New Objectivity, a relationship is established between the subject matter of its artworks and the events of the time, whose pictorial reinterpretation took the form of so-called conceptual images. The article shows that the German art of the 1920s and 1930s was characterized by an existence of a large number of artistic images-concepts, which together form an artistic picture of the world in the art of the New Objectivity. By forming a vast iconography of social and political subjects, they represented not only an important form of creative expression, but also an effective means of public communication, allowing the main items of the current political agenda to be effectively transmitted in the visual form.

title: Creative proto&#8209;industries: a retrospective analysis of commercial practices in European visual arts before the era of industrialization
title_original: Creative proto&#8209;industries: a retrospective analysis of commercial practices in European visual arts before the era of industrialization
summary: The subject of the research is pre-industrial forms of production, promotion, and mass consumption of artistic products in Europe, considered as a historical prototype of modern creative industries. The author analyzes commercial practices of the European art market over five centuries – from the printed graphics of Master E. S. and the "Pand" market of the mid-15th century to the campaigns of T. J. Barrett and the series of A. Mucha at the turn of the 19th and 20th centuries. The research examines price segmentation of supply, the workshop organization of P. P. Rubens, art dealing in the Netherlands, exhibition enterprises of J. Tayers and E. Gambar, the phenomenon of the "sensational painting," the salon system, and secondary monetization through reproductions and souvenir products. These practices are compared with contemporary formats: the studios of J. Koons and D. Hirst, blockbuster exhibitions, and museum merchandising. The chronological and geographical scope of the study covers Germany, Flanders, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and France. The work is built on an interdisciplinary approach that combines art studies, cultural studies, and economic history. The main tool is a comparative and historical-typological analysis of various cases, supplemented by the terminology of T. Adorno, M. Horkheimer, W. Benjamin, and G. Debord. The scientific novelty lies in the overarching comparison of disparate precedents and the derivation of six stable typological invariants: the replication of a once-successful formula, segmentation of supply according to audience purchasing power, division of labor with the shift of authorship to the status of a brand, the formation of an intermediary institution, monetization of events and experiences, and secondary monetization through reproduction rights and souvenir products. A significant result is the author's constructed logic of the gradual complexity of these mechanisms: from the commodification of sacred images in the 15th century to the institutional infrastructure and manufactural production of the 17th century, then to paid experiences and the salon system of the 18th and 19th centuries, and finally to the merging of high art with commercial branding at the turn of the 19th and 20th centuries. The final conclusion that the terminological fixation of creative industries in the late 1990s marks not the birth of the industry, but the moment it acquires means of total scaling, whereas the concept of autonomous art is presented as a historically localized construct of the Romantic era, is articulated correctly and follows from the presented material.

title: Museification of Chinese Academic Painting in the Second Half of the 20th Century: The Example of the National Art Museum of China
title_original: Museification of Chinese Academic Painting in the Second Half of the 20th Century: The Example of the National Art Museum of China
summary: This article focuses on the National Art Museum of China as the object of research. Based on the comparison of publications, analysis of collection catalogs and exhibition materials, as well as final documents and open archives prepared by the museum staff regarding the dissemination of works from the collection, the process of museification of Chinese academic painting in the second half of the 20th century after its inclusion in the national museum's funds is traced; institutional mechanisms and value rethinking in areas such as collecting, exhibiting, scientific research, and art historical narrative are analyzed. The "academic painting" discussed in this article has a special meaning in the context of 20th-century China. It refers to the painting tradition that developed within the educational system of modern art universities—primarily the Central Academy of Fine Arts and the Zhejiang Academy of Fine Arts (renamed the China Academy of Art in 1993) – based on realistic plastic training and consistently manifested in nationwide art exhibitions, state-themed visual arts, and the creation of works on significant historical subjects of national importance, rather than being an expansive designation for all artistic creativity of art academy instructors in China in the second half of the 20th century. The study employs methods of art studies and museum studies analysis, examination of exhibition history, and analysis of documentary sources; it looks at institutional practices and value construction of academic painting after its inclusion in the national museum's collection. The article notes that academic painting, which flourished in socialist China in the second half of the 20th century, significantly enriched the collections of state museums of visual arts due to its resonance with the state narrative rooted in popular understanding of history, as well as its own artistic significance, the most notable example being the National Art Museum of China. The museification of academic painting was carried out through institutional mechanisms of the museum and the personal will of artists, resulting in the transformation of painting from creative achievements of the academic education system into national heritage. In this process, the National Art Museum of China played a dual role of "selection" and "narrative construction." This process not only enriched the museum's collection but also contributed to elevating the artistic status of academic painting.

title: The Aesthetic Dimension of Urban Design: On the Conditions for the Emergence of Aesthetic Experience
title_original: The Aesthetic Dimension of Urban Design: On the Conditions for the Emergence of Aesthetic Experience
summary: This article identifies the aesthetic qualities produced by design in a fragment of the urban environment and establishes their role in organizing the conditions of possibility of aesthetic experience. The relevance of the study stems from the need to clarify the aesthetic status of reconstructed spaces, which reorganization has become, over the past two decades, a leading practices in the transformation of major Russian cities and to expand the conceptual framework describing such qualities. The object of the study is a fragment of the urban environment of the reconstructed type, its subject, its aesthetic qualities and the conditions of their actualization in the aesthetic experience. The methodological basis is aesthetic analysis, drawing on studies of the urban environment (E. Ass, L. Salmin), on conceptions of aesthetic experience (J. Dewey, A. Berleant), and on research into environmental design in Russian aesthetic theory (E. Kondratiev, N. Barsukova). The typology of design situations (V. Shimko) grounds the identification of the reconstructed type, while the framework of postmodernist aesthetics (V. V. Bychkov, N. Mankovskaya) and architecture (C. Jencks, I. Dobritsyna) serves as reference point for describing the design attitude towards the site’s previous state. The analysis correlates two levels of description: modes of realising the design intention and aesthetic qualities as characteristics of the fragment organized. We identify techniques for preservation and discernible restoration of losses (which ensure the restoration process and the accessibility of the site’s authentic layer), as well as techniques for citation, stylization, and juxtaposition (which ensure the qualities of citation, stylization, eclecticism). The systematization is tested on the Zotov Centre, where these qualities possess conditions of actualization. The integrity of aesthetic experience is ensured by correlating differing qualities within a single environmental situation. It is precisely the design organization shapes the conditions for the emergence of an aesthetic experience.

Shimko) grounds the identification of the reconstructed type, while the framework of postmodernist aesthetics (V. V. Bychkov, N. Mankovskaya) and architecture (C. Jencks, I. Dobritsyna) serves as reference point for describing the design attitude towards the site’s previous state. The analysis correlates two levels of description: modes of realising the design intention and aesthetic qualities as characteristics of the fragment organized. We identify techniques for preservation and discernible restoration of losses (which ensure the restoration process and the accessibility of the site’s authentic layer), as well as techniques for citation, stylization, and juxtaposition (which ensure the qualities of citation, stylization, eclecticism). The systematization is tested on the Zotov Centre, where these qualities possess conditions of actualization. The integrity of aesthetic experience is ensured by correlating differing qualities within a single environmental situation. It is precisely the design organization shapes the conditions for the emergence of an aesthetic experience.

title: Smart culture: cognitive, ethical, and existential limits of technological evolution
title_original: Smart culture: cognitive, ethical, and existential limits of technological evolution
summary: This study examines transformations in personal value orientations and cognitive mechanisms against the backdrop of ubiquitous smartization. The phenomenon of "smart culture," conceptualized as a complex multilevel system, serves as the object of analysis. This system integrates techno-social practices, algorithmic patterns of behavior, and identity shifts under the influence of smart technologies that have evolved from simple intermediaries into active creators of perception mechanisms. The following key aspects of the problem are delineated: the covert substitution of critical reflection with routine data processing; the reduction of moral choice to simplified binary algorithms; and the ontological lability of the self within the context of continuous network connectivity. Fundamental attention is paid to the immanent contradiction between the declared anthropocentricity of the smart environment and the empirically recorded practice of exploiting users' cognitive potential, whose activity is transformed into transparent raw material for collecting predictive behavioral indicators. The theoretical-methodological foundation – an interdisciplinary synthesis of philosophical anthropology, cognitive neuroscience, and the sociology of technology, augmented by theories of distributed cognition, surveillance economics, and post-structuralist dismantling of identity – is supplemented by empirical data derived from a mass questionnaire survey of 6,057 respondents (schoolchilds and educators of the Ryazan Oblast), conducted by the author in 2025-2026. The scientific novelty of the research lies in formulating the concept of the "immanent exhaustion" of smart culture. This phenomenon is regarded not as a byproduct of external technological or sociocultural threats, but as a dialectical mechanism of self-destruction immanent to the very essence of total quantification and unrestricted algorithmic optimization. The author introduces elements of their proprietary theory into scholarly discourse: "cognitive parasitism" — the suppression of neurocognitive resource formation by algorithms; "ontological dispersion" – the rift between the user's perception of smart technologies and their objective algorithmic nature; alongside a detailed conceptualization of "algorithmic heteronomy" – human moral dependence on machine-mediated decisions masquerading as one's own choice. In conclusion, it is argued that the antagonisms inherent in the contemporary smart environment precondition society's transition to the Seventh Information Revolution and Industry 5.0. According to the author's concept, through the synergistic effect of smartization processes, bioengineering augmentation, and cyborgization, this stage forms the epistemological and ontological foundations for the onset of the Second Quantum Revolution and the emergence of quantum culture, which opens the era of Industry 6.0 for humanity.

title: The rondo form in the compositions for a cappella choir by M. Ravel and V.A. Gavrilin
title_original: The rondo form in the compositions for a cappella choir by M. Ravel and V.A. Gavrilin
summary: The subject of this study is the problem of form formation as one of the most relevant issues in contemporary musical culture. The object of the research is the examination of modern methods of refracting the rondo form in a cappella choral music of the 20th century. The aim of this article is to study the rondo form in the compositions for a cappella choir "Ronde" from the cycle "Three Songs for A Cappella Choir" by M. Ravel and "Don Kapitan" by V.A. Gavrilin. The author examines in detail such aspects of the topic as the peculiarities of the structure of the literary-textual source and the revelation of the stylistics of the choral writing of the composers. A number of key positions are identified: thematicism, form formation, choral texture, writing technique. Special attention is paid to the issues related to neo-folk and neoclassical stylistic orientations in the works of foreign and domestic composers. The methodology consists of a synthesis of historical and theoretical methods. Based on this, the historical prerequisites for the realization of the rondo form in vocal-choral genres of the 20th century have been identified. Particular attention is given to the achievements of I.F. Stravinsky, S.S. Prokofiev, A. P&#228;rt, A.G. Schnittke, and E.V. Denisov. The main conclusion of the conducted research is the paradigm of the deep connection between the traditional and the innovative in contemporary a cappella choral music. In particular, this position became a defining factor for the creativity of the French composer Maurice Ravel, from the first half of the 20th century, and the St. Petersburg master Valery Alexandrovich Gavrilin, from the second half of the past century. A significant contribution of the author to the disclosure of the topic is the study of the previously unexamined a cappella choruses "Ronde" by M. Ravel and "Don Kapitan" by V.A. Gavrilin. The novelty of the study lies in the fact that it presents materials for the first time on the reframing of neo-folk tendencies in the choral heritage of M. Ravel and neoclassical tendencies in the works of V.A. Gavrilin. Emphasis is placed on the need to study the historical and theoretical aspects of the formation and development of neo-folk and neoclassical stylistic trends in a cappella choral music of the 21st century. In this regard, the achievements of 20th-century composers, particularly M. Ravel and V.A. Gavrilin, stand out from the general line and are historically significant phenomena.

title: Ethical frameworks in the context of Agile transformation in IT (the case of Rostelecom)
title_original: Ethical frameworks in the context of Agile transformation in IT (the case of Rostelecom)
summary: The article provides a socio-philosophical reflection on the phenomenon of ethical frameworks that emerge in the process of Agile-transformation of Russian IT companies. The author postulates that these frameworks function not as normative systems, but as discursive practices that produce new forms of sociality and power in the context of "managed self-organization." Synthesizing the methodological apparatus of postmodern philosophy (M. Foucault, J.-F. Lyotard, J. Deleuze and F. Guattari) with sociocultural analysis reveals the process of hybridization as a key mechanism for adapting global management narratives to local conditions. Empirical evidence, based on the case of Rostelecom, demonstrates how these rhizomatic ethical systems legitimize performative effectiveness. The analysis shows how disciplinary control is translated into mechanisms of digital transparency and self-optimization, ultimately forging a new type of corporate subjectivity aligned with the demands of a flexible, post-industrial economy. This study specifically examines the implementation of the "KARMA Framework" at Rostelecom, revealing a hybrid model where the rhetoric of autonomy and self-organization is strategically deployed. The findings illustrate that this adaptation often reinforces existing power structures by digitizing traditional oversight, thereby creating a potent, legitimizing discourse for a modernized form of hierarchical control. The paper introduces and develops the concept of "managed self-organization" as a critical lens to understand this paradoxical power dynamic. It argues that this model represents a form of digital governmentality, where control is exercised not through direct coercion, but through the very architectures of participation and visibility. The research concludes that the resulting ethical framework serves primarily as a technology for shaping a compliant, self-managing subject, highlighting the risks of such hybridization devolving into a full-blown simulacrum of agility, devoid of its emancipatory potential.

title: The material culture of Islamic calligraphy in China: from pen to paper
title_original: The material culture of Islamic calligraphy in China: from pen to paper
summary: The subject of the study includes an analysis of the material culture of Chinese Islamic calligraphy; and the objects of the study are the writing instruments, ink, paper and bodily techniques, and educational practices shaping specifics of the Chinese Hui Muslims calligraphy. The special attention is paid to the Sini style as a local variant of Islamic calligraphy which emerged from the adaptation of Arabic scripts to Chinese brush techniques and the aesthetics of ink painting. The transition from kalam to paintbrush is analyzed, along with the influence of a Chinese ink and xuan paper on the character of line, as well as the connection between the material parameters of writing with the rhythm of movement, bodily discipline, and the spiritual focus of the master. Question of how material objects and writing techniques forming mechanism for preserving Islamic identity in Chinese cultural context is given special importance. It is concluded that a Chinese Islamic calligraphy represents stable form of intercultural synthesis in which Islamic canon maintains religious legitimacy while simultaneously acquiring plastic and material qualities of Chinese aesthetic tradition. The methodological basis of the research comprises cultural analysis, comparative-historical method, visual-anthropological approach, and the theory of material culture. The study’s scientific novelty is explained by the necessity of the systemic analysis of the Chinese Islamic calligraphy which includes a material-corporeal practice, so as the writing instrument, the material of the writing operas and the writing technique. They are viewed as the constitutive elements of an artistic and religious experience. The study of the material culture of the sini Islamic calligraphy has led to the following conclusions. The study of the material practice culture of the sini Islamic calligraphy allows to make the following conclusions. Firstly, the Sini calligraphy in China is an art practice which means using of the material means such as the tools, an ink, a paper and the specifics of the manual writing technique. Secondly, the transition from the kalam technique to the brushpainting technique and the use of the Chinese ink and huan paper and also an evolution of the compositional style demonstrate how the Islamic graphic tradition was adapted to the Chinese material culture. Thirdly, it has been demonstrated that the material and the spiritual synthesis interact within Islamic calligraphy. The were formulated the prescriptions regarding physical discipline. Fourthly, the intercultural synthesis involving the Islamic calligraphy arises from more than just the borrowing of an imagery or the styles. The hybrid nature of the new ideas of the Islamic calligraphy is proved by the specifics of the material artistic culture. These are specifically, the tools, the materials for the writing operas, an ink, a handling of the brushpainting, and the established pedagogical methods of teaching the sini technique.

title: Features of the conceptualization of the term "mass culture" in western and chinese academic traditions
title_original: Features of the conceptualization of the term "mass culture" in western and chinese academic traditions
summary: The subject of the research is the content and semantic specificity of the concept of "mass culture" in Western (Western European and American) and Chinese academic traditions. The author examines in detail aspects such as interpretations of key terms like "mass," "mass culture," "popular culture," and their synonymous series in English and Chinese. Special attention is given to the historical and cultural context of the formation of these concepts: in the Western tradition, critical approaches by Ortega y Gasset, Macdonald, Horkheimer, and Adorno link mass culture with the culture industry and endow it with negative connotations, and analytical approaches by Birmingham’s turn; in China, the influence of the May Fourth Movement and the activities of the League of Leftist Writers, which shaped the enlightening and ideologically oriented perception of "&#22823;&#20247;&#25991;&#21270;" (mass culture). Within the subject, classifications of types of culture, characteristics of synonymy and antonymy of terms, and the specifics of mass culture functions in each of the examined contexts are analyzed. A comparative analysis is applied to the definition of key concepts in the two cultural traditions. Methods of semantic and terminological analysis, comparison of synonymous and antonymous series in English and Chinese, and a historical-contextual approach are used to identify factors that influenced the formation of interpretations. The methodology relies on critical texts of Western theorists and materials from the Chinese humanities tradition. The novelty of the research lies in the systematic comparison of the semantics and value connotations of the concept of "mass culture" in Western and Chinese academic traditions, based on linguistic and historical-cultural analysis. A significant contribution to the study of the topic is the identification of fundamental differences in the perception of the category "mass" and the functions of mass culture: in Western thought, it is interpreted as a product of the culture industry, associated with manipulation, standardization, and opposition to high culture, then it is considered as a complex field of meaning generation; while in the Chinese context, it is understood as a tool for enlightening the broad masses and an element of ideological integration. The main conclusions are: the existence of two fundamentally different paradigms for understanding mass culture, determined by the specifics of historical and sociocultural development; the significance of its enlightening function in the Chinese tradition as a key meaning-forming factor; and the necessity to consider the cultural-historical context when making intercultural comparisons of terms, as differences in semantics and evaluative connotations reflect fundamental divergences in understanding the role of the "mass" in society.

title: Youth Cultural Diplomacy in the 21st Century: Institutional Mechanisms of Cooperation between China, Russia, and Belarus
title_original: Youth Cultural Diplomacy in the 21st Century: Institutional Mechanisms of Cooperation between China, Russia, and Belarus
summary: The article is dedicated to the institutional mechanisms of youth cultural diplomacy in China, Russia, and Belarus in the context of expanding humanitarian, educational, and cultural exchanges in the 21st century. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that the growth in the number of joint initiatives does not yet allow for a clear assessment of the formation of a sustainable trilateral system of interaction. The aim of the research is to identify the institutional architecture of youth cultural diplomacy in the three countries, the composition of its key actors, coordination mechanisms, forms of youth participation, as well as to determine the degree of development of the trilateral cooperation framework. Special attention is given to the role of the state, universities, international organizations, and youth associations, the development of network connections, and the transition from event-based formats to recurring programs of joint activities and sustainable practices of intercultural interaction among the youth of the three countries. The study is based on a relational approach to public diplomacy and a comparative qualitative-quantitative analysis of 50 official documents from China, Russia, and Belarus from 1995 to 2026. The corpus includes national regulations, bilateral agreements, and documents from the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). Each document served as the primary unit of analysis. Comparative, content, institutional, and network analyses were employed. It was established that national models differ in normative emphases while retaining the leading role of the state. Universities and educational institutions are represented in 32 out of 50 documents and act as the main operators of practical interaction. However, the developed bilateral ties do not form an autonomous trilateral system, as after Belarus joins the SCO in 2024, the overall framework is primarily shaped within the multilateral infrastructure of the organization. A discrepancy was identified between the institutional inclusion of youth and their direct involvement in agenda-setting. The digital component is only embedded in four documents. The scientific novelty lies in the operationalization of the concept of "institutional ecosystem of youth cultural diplomacy," highlighting its levels and developing an original model for the transition from event-based interaction to sustainable cooperation. It was concluded that the political framework is a necessary but insufficient condition for institutional sustainability. The ecosystem arises from the combination of state coordination, permanent organizational networks, digital infrastructure, and youth subjectivity.

title: ФИЛОСОФИЯ ХОЛИЗМА Я.Х. СМЭТСА В СОВЕТСКОМ НАУЧНОМ И ОБЩЕСТВЕННОМ ДИСКУРСЕ
title_original: ФИЛОСОФИЯ ХОЛИЗМА Я.Х. СМЭТСА В СОВЕТСКОМ НАУЧНОМ И ОБЩЕСТВЕННОМ ДИСКУРСЕ
summary:
В статье прослеживаются формирование и эволюция восприятия холизма в СССР с 1930-х по 1980-е гг. В советской науке наблюдался устойчивый интерес к философии холизма южноафриканского государственного деятеля Я.Х. Смэтса (1870–1950), не-смотря на ее явное противоречие с официальной идеологией диалектического материализма. Учение Смэтса, рассматривавшееся в контексте не африканской, а западной «буржуазной» мысли, подвергалось резкой идеологизированной критике. Это учение обвиняли не только в идеализме, мистицизме и телеологии, но и в том, что оно служит философским обоснованием империализма и расовой сегрегации, которую Смэтс последовательно проводил в Южной Африке. Подробный критический разбор в советских публикациях, при отсутствии русских переводов первоисточников, парадоксальным образом способствовал ознакомлению научной аудитории с основными положениями этой философии. Центральные идеи холизма о несводимости целого к сумме его частей перекликались с учением В.И. Вернадского о биосфере и разработками других отечественных оппонентов механистического редукционизма. С 1960-х гг. произошло смягчение критики и постепенное, хотя и опосредованное, усвоение холистических принципов, чему способствовало развитие кибернетики и теории систем. Эти принципы были переосмыслены и ассимилированы в рамках диалектического материализма, что позволило советским ученым развить собственный системный подход к анализу сложных явлений. Таким образом, философия Смэтса, бу-дучи объектом критики, оказала косвенное, но существенное влияние на советскую научную мысль, стимулировав отход от редукционизма. В постсоветской России холизм рассматривается как универсальный междисциплинарный методологический подход, применяемый в медицине, экологии, психологии и языкознании.
                  This study investigates the phenomenon of sustained interest in Jan Smuts’s philosophy of holism within Soviet science, despite its stark contradiction with the official ideology of dialectical materialism. This paper analyzes the evolution of holism’s reception in the USSR from the 1930s to the 1980s. Initially, Smuts’s doctrine, perceived as part of Western “bourgeois” thought, faced harsh ideological criticism for its idealism, teleology, and connection to the political activities of its author, an ideologue of British imperialism. The paper argues that, in the absence of translated primary sources, detailed critiques in Soviet publications paradoxically served as the main channel for introducing the scientific community to the core tenets of this philosophy. It reveals how holism’s central ideas about integrity and the irreducibility of the whole to the sum of its parts resonated with the work of Soviet academics, particularly with Vladimir Vernadsky’s theory of the biosphere. The study demonstrates that over time, especially in the late Soviet period, the criticism softened, leading to a gradual, implicit absorption of holistic principles. These principles were reinterpreted and assimilated within the framework of the systemic approach, which became widely accepted in Soviet science. Thus, Smuts’s philosophy, while a target of criticism, exerted an indirect yet significant influence on Soviet scientific thought, stimulating a departure from mechanistic reductionism and fostering the development of a holistic worldview. In post-Soviet Russia, holism has transformed into a universal interdisciplinary methodological approach.

title: Философия и искусство:  трансформация отношений и проблема практического использования
title_original: Философия и искусство:  трансформация отношений и проблема практического использования
summary: В статье обсуждаются две основные проблемы: отношение искусства и философии, имея в виду высказывание М. Хайдеггера о ведущей роли искусства, и вопрос о связи этих дисциплин и практик с политикой, который обсуждали многие исследователи. Анализируются ключевые высказывания Платона, Аристотеля, И. Канта и М. Хайдеггера, связанные с этими проблемами. Автор утверждает, что не существует произведений философии и искусства не ориентированных прагматически, что реконструкция всегда выявляет подобный интерес. Он считает необходимым различать гуманистические и негуманистические прагматические интересы. В первом случае философ или художник (писатель, композитор, дизайнер) работает на человека, культуру и благо, а не на эгоистические интересы отдельных лиц и субъектов.   Характеризуются особенности философии и искусства. Общее в том, что философ и художник создают искусственные семиотические реальности, которые, однако, воспринимаются и переживаются пользователями (читателями, зрителями, слушателями) как естественные события и процессы. При этом философ решает экзистенциальные проблемы, поставленные временем (любовь, смерть, возможность непротиворечиво мыслить определенное явление, справедливость и др.). Их решение предполагает познание явлений и действительности, достигаемые путем построения схем и идеальных объектов. Философ специализируется также на создании картин, объясняющих реальность, в которой существуют эти схемы и идеальные объекты, на полемике с другими философами, на критике и рефлексии. Художник, создавая произведения, порождает реальность, позволяющую разрешать значимые для него  проблемы (и проблемы пользователя), а также проживать и переживать события привлекательного мира (реальности). Сегодня люди вошли в полосу цивилизационных и социальных трансформаций, которые многие осознают как глубокий кризис. Одновременно эта ситуация предоставляет богатые возможности для работы философов и художников (для критики уходящих форм и структур, анализа современности, рационального и художественного прогнозирования будущего).

title: ФИЛОСОФИЯ ЗДОРОВЬЯ В НАСЛЕДИИ МЫСЛИТЕЛЕЙ ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОЙ АЗИИ И МУСУЛЬМАНСКОГО ВОСТОКА: ИСТОРИКО-ФИЛОСОФСКИЙ И БИОЭТИЧЕСКИЙ АНАЛИЗ
title_original: ФИЛОСОФИЯ ЗДОРОВЬЯ В НАСЛЕДИИ МЫСЛИТЕЛЕЙ ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОЙ АЗИИ И МУСУЛЬМАНСКОГО ВОСТОКА: ИСТОРИКО-ФИЛОСОФСКИЙ И БИОЭТИЧЕСКИЙ АНАЛИЗ
summary: В статье проведён историко-философский анализ представлений о здоровье в наследиимыслителей Центральной Азии и мусульманского Востока. Рассмотрены философские, этические имедицинские взгляды Абулькасима аз-Захрави, Махдума Азама, Ахмада Дониша, Абдурауфа Фитрата иАбдуллы Авлони, раскрывающие взаимосвязь физического, духовного и нравственного здоровьячеловека. Особое внимание уделено эволюции философии здоровья, вопросам профилактикизаболеваний, формированию здорового образа жизни, социальной ответственности и становлениюбиоэтических представлений. Показано, что идеи выдающихся мыслителей сохраняют научную ипрактическую значимость в современных условиях и могут служить концептуальной основой дляразвития философии здоровья и биоэтики.

title: ДЖОРДАНО БРУНО И ЕГО ФИЛОСОФИЯ ПРИРОДЫ В «АКРОТИЗМЕ»: ПРЕДИСЛОВИЕ К ПЕРЕВОДУ
title_original: ДЖОРДАНО БРУНО И ЕГО ФИЛОСОФИЯ ПРИРОДЫ В «АКРОТИЗМЕ»: ПРЕДИСЛОВИЕ К ПЕРЕВОДУ
summary: The article serves as a preface to the first Russian translation of a fragment (Theses II–XV) from Giordano Bruno’s principal anti-Aristotelian work, «Camoeracensis acrotismus». This text belongs to the largely unexplored corpus of Bruno’s Latin writings and remains mostly inaccessible in the major European languages. The article examines the genesis of the text, its polemical context, and its thesis format. Special attention is given to Bruno’s method, which combines a recognition of Aristotle’s achievements with a radical revision of his teachings. The author demonstrates that in the «Camoeracensis acrotismus» Bruno redefines the boundaries between physics and metaphysics, introduces the concept of the universe as limitless being, and reinterprets the notions of substance, motion, and nature. Consequently, «Camoeracensis acrotismus» emerges not as a scholastic commentary but as a programmatic work that lays the foundations for a metaphysics of nature, which Bruno identifies with infinite being, the One, and God.

title: Solidarism as a Political Philosophy of Moderation in the Works of G.K. Gins
title_original: Solidarism as a Political Philosophy of Moderation in the Works of G.K. Gins
summary: The article aims to reconstruct the political-philosophical content of G.K. Gins’s concept of solidarism and to determine its heuristic potential for analyzing contemporary political conflicts and social polarization. The working hypothesis is that Gins’s solidarism is not an intermediate compromise among liberalism, conservatism, and socialism, but an autonomous normative-political model for reconciling the interests of the individual, society, and the state. The methodological framework combines content analysis of Gins’s texts, discourse analysis of key concepts in his political language (including solidarism and solidarity), and elements of a comparative approach that juxtapose solidarism with competing ideological traditions. The study concludes that its theoretical contribution lies in advancing a scholarly interpretation of Gins’s solidarism as an evolutionary model of political moderation in which the state functions not only as an institution of coercion – without excluding coercion when justified – but also as a mechanism of normative coordination that channels social energy toward consensus and the reproduction of solidarity. The approach’s key novelty is shown to lie in overcoming the crisis of «guiding ideas» through an ethically oriented political framework in which material progress is conceptually aligned with moral unity, and individual freedom with the common good. Scientifically, this comparison expands the analytical toolkit for polarization research by treating moderation and solidarism as an alternative to dualistic models of political conflict that tend to foster radicalization. Practically, the findings can inform strategies for de-escalating ideological confrontation and strengthening consensual mechanisms in society.

title: ЭКСПОЗИЦИЯ КАК СОБЫТИЕ: ФИЛОСОФИЯ МУЗЕЙНОЙ СРЕДЫ
title_original: ЭКСПОЗИЦИЯ КАК СОБЫТИЕ: ФИЛОСОФИЯ МУЗЕЙНОЙ СРЕДЫ
summary: Аннотация. В статье рассматриваются вопросы создания и функционирования музейных экспозиций как одного из ключевых факторов их публичной самопрезентации, а также эффективности его культурно-образовательной и коммуникационной деятельности. Музейная экспозиция представлена как целостная художественно-научная система, в которой экспонат, как часть музейной коллекции становится не только объектом хранения, но и носителем исторических и культурных смыслов. Рассмотрены и проанализированы особенности построения экспозиций в зависимости от профиля музея – художественного, исторического, археологического, краеведческого, естественно-научного и мемориального. Особое внимание уделено следующим универсальным принципам современной экспозиционно-выставочной деятельности: научная обоснованность, логика тематико-хронологической структуры, экспозиционная выразительность, доступность, аутентичность и сохранность музейных предметов. Обращено внимание на пространственную организацию экспозиции как инструмента визуальной коммуникации, интерпретации и эмоционального взаимодействия со зрителем.

title: Конфликт как норма
title_original: Конфликт как норма
summary: This article examines the agonistic turn in democratic theory, focusing primarily on the work of Chantal Mouffe. The starting point is the diagnosis of a systemic crisis of liberal democracy, which, contrary to the optimistic predictions of the late twentieth century, has not disappeared but has assumed new and more acute forms. The author demonstrates that classical deliberative models (Rawls, Habermas), oriented toward rational consensus, prove theoretically untenable and politically dangerous, as they bracket out the ineradicable antagonism inherent in any pluralistic political community. The core of the analysis centers on Mouffe's key concepts: hegemony as a temporary and contestable representation of totality; agonism as a “tamed” form of antagonism; and her critical reconceptualization of citizenship and the public sphere. Particular attention is paid to Mouffe's intellectual sources, especially her polemical engagement with Carl Schmitt, from whom she borrows the understanding of the political as a field of conflict while radically reworking his conclusions in a democratic direction. However, the article goes beyond exposition to consider productive correctives proposed by Nancy Fraser (on material inequality and subaltern counterpublics) and Adela Cortina (on the ethical foundation of agonism and the cultivation of moral subjects), which help overcome the weaknesses of the agonistic approach — its institutional underdevelopment and neglect of socio-economic conditions for participatory equality. Ultimately, the agonistic model emerges not as a completed political program but as a critical optic that demands ongoing reflection and incompleteness — an invitation to a struggle waged not for annihilation, but for recognition of the opponent's legitimacy.

The starting point is the diagnosis of a systemic crisis of liberal democracy, which, contrary to the optimistic predictions of the late twentieth century, has not disappeared but has assumed new and more acute forms. The author demonstrates that classical deliberative models (Rawls, Habermas), oriented toward rational consensus, prove theoretically untenable and politically dangerous, as they bracket out the ineradicable antagonism inherent in any pluralistic political community. The core of the analysis centers on Mouffe's key concepts: hegemony as a temporary and contestable representation of totality; agonism as a “tamed” form of antagonism; and her critical reconceptualization of citizenship and the public sphere. Particular attention is paid to Mouffe's intellectual sources, especially her polemical engagement with Carl Schmitt, from whom she borrows the understanding of the political as a field of conflict while radically reworking his conclusions in a democratic direction. However, the article goes beyond exposition to consider productive correctives proposed by Nancy Fraser (on material inequality and subaltern counterpublics) and Adela Cortina (on the ethical foundation of agonism and the cultivation of moral subjects), which help overcome the weaknesses of the agonistic approach — its institutional underdevelopment and neglect of socio-economic conditions for participatory equality. Ultimately, the agonistic model emerges not as a completed political program but as a critical optic that demands ongoing reflection and incompleteness — an invitation to a struggle waged not for annihilation, but for recognition of the opponent's legitimacy.

title: Формирование авторитетного высказывания на рубеже Античности и Средневековья
title_original: Формирование авторитетного высказывания на рубеже Античности и Средневековья
summary: This article examines Canon 13 of the Second Council of Seville (619), a short anti-Monophysite treatise composed of biblical and patristic quotations. Taking this text as a case study, it addresses the mechanisms by which authoritative theological utterances were constructed at the transition from Antiquity to the Middle Ages. The article first provides a general overview of the canon's structure, which, it is argued, cannot be reduced to a simple “Scripture versus Tradition” model. Biblical quotations appear as testimonia, that is, witnesses endowed with absolute authority by virtue of their divine origin and accepted unconditionally as a matter of faith. By contrast, the judgments (sententiae) of the Church Fathers are associated with argumenta: the products of human rational reflection, grounded in biblical testimony and delimiting the range of permissible interpretations of the biblical text. These sententiae acquire a special authority and the status of second-order testimonia when gathered into a chronologically organized florilegium that embodies Tradition and the line of transmission of the apostolic rule of faith from its divine source. The article further demonstrates the use of methods characteristic of Isidore of Seville and related to grammatical categories, above all differentia and etymologia. The “etymological,” or, more precisely, “genealogical,” narrative situates Canon 13 within the framework of Tradition. Finally, brevity (brevitas) serves as a key means of condensing earlier textual authority and making the text as persuasive as possible. Moreover, in both its brevity and its functions, the theological utterance may be likened to the Creed. The combination of intellectual procedures described here, employed in the formation of an authoritative utterance, appears to be in many respects characteristic of Visigothic Spain in general and of Isidore of Seville in particular.

title: Церковь и территориально-административное деление в городах Центральной Испании к концу XIII – середине XIV в. как сюжет интеллектуальной истории
title_original: Церковь и территориально-административное деление в городах Центральной Испании к концу XIII – середине XIV в. как сюжет интеллектуальной истории
summary: The article is devoted to the role of the religious factor in the system of territorial-administrative organization of the free cities of Central Spain from the late 13th to the mid-14th century, in which by this time stable traditions of local self-government had developed in the form of territorial communities — concejo. The latter united within their boundaries both the city itself and the adjacent rural area. The decisive role of the Church in the system of organizing the concejo was determined by the fact that the key element of this organization was the urban or rural church parish (Lat. collatio, Old Caste collaçion), which was, in essence, the only territorial-administrative unit within the boundaries of the concejo community. It is no coincidence that all categories of officials directly connected with the community were elected by church parishes. In a broader sense, ethno-confessional affiliation determined the principle of compact settlement within the city limits of representatives of ethno-confessional communities — Christians, Muslims and Jews. And the non-Christians lived only in special quarters — morerias (Muslims) and juderias (Jews). This situation can only be explained by the limited subjectivity of the concejo as an authority. From the very beginning the community did not have the ability to “reformat” its space in a territorial-administrative sense, and therefore was forced to adapt to existing organizational forms.

title: Алгоритмическая власть: кибернетическая рациональность и политические следствия
title_original: Алгоритмическая власть: кибернетическая рациональность и политические следствия
summary: This article examines algorithmic power, understood as a form of power based on the collection and analysis of data for the purpose of modelling and pre-emptively shaping possible behavior, through the lens of Michel Foucault's analytics of power. Drawing on a critical engagement with the concepts of algorithmic governmentality developed by Antoinette Rouvroy and Thomas Berns and instrumentarian power by Shoshana Zuboff, the article identifies the distinctive features of algorithmic power. It argues that predictive and preventive forms of governance, as well as governance through interventions in the milieu, are inherited from the biopolitical security apparatuses described by Foucault. At the same time, algorithmic power is characterized by its a-signifying nature and operates outside the production of meaning and subjectivity, abandoning orientation toward statistical norms and shifting from causal explanation to the optimization of correlations. Particular attention is paid to the capacity of algorithmic power to exercise continuous control through real-time feedback loops. The notion of algorithmic governmentality is critically reassessed: it is argued that algorithmic techniques of power, in conjunction with computer science, do not constitute a self-standing governmentality but rather operate within a broader form of rationality shaped by cybernetics. Cybernetic rationality not only provides the operational principles of algorithmic governance but also makes algorithmic mechanisms a rational and legitimate means of intervening in behavior. Finally, the article explores the political consequences of the spread of algorithmic power, including the erosion of the public sphere, the disappearance of the boundary between private and public life, and the threat posed to the fundamental conditions of the political: plurality, difference, unpredictability, and natality — which are increasingly displaced by the logic of predictive optimization.

title: Постмодернизм с Сэмом Лейком
title_original: Постмодернизм с Сэмом Лейком
summary: This article examines the video game Alan Wake 2 (2023, Remedy Entertainment) as a prominent example of a postmodern text. The author proceeds from the assumption that, despite sustained scholarly interest in postmodernism in literature and cinema, the specific forms of its manifestation in video games remain insufficiently studied. Jeffrey Weinstock's work is used as a point of departure; however, the postmodern features he identifies are treated not as a strict taxonomy, but as a heuristic model for analyzing an artistic text. The theoretical basis of the study is Brian McHale's concept of postmodernist poetics, according to which postmodernism is defined primarily by an ontological dominant. The article identifies six postmodern features most consistently manifested in Alan Wake 2: foregrounded textuality, camp, intertextuality, ontological questions, the deconstruction of unified identity, and suspicion toward metanarratives. Methodologically, the study is situated within the field of ludonarratology and considers the game not only as a narrative text, but also as an interactive system in which the production of meaning is shaped by the player's actions, rules, interface, and the structure of progression. The article argues that the central feature of the game is its pronounced metanarrative structure: its narrative tells the story of a writer who creates a text that directly affects the reality of other characters while simultaneously depending on the player's actions. The author concludes that the interactivity of the video game medium allows for a deeper exploration of postmodern ontological questions concerning the relation between fiction and reality, as well as the deconstruction of the subject. Special attention is paid to the two storylines associated with Alan Wake and Saga Anderson, in which metanarrative structures and ontological questions receive their clearest expression. The article concludes that Alan Wake 2 not only demonstrates key features of postmodernist poetics, but also makes visible those properties of the video game medium that are themselves connected with ontological instability: the splitting of the subject between player and avatar, the multiplicity of possible world-states, and the coexistence of rules with fictional reality. Thus, the game constitutes an important object for the study of postmodern techniques in digital culture.

title: Фигуративные стратегии медиафилософии
title_original: Фигуративные стратегии медиафилософии
summary: The article is a theoretical review of figurative models in continental media philosophy and their conceptual potential for understanding contemporary media communication. The transition to the digital phase of social development calls for a return to the fundamental philosophical question of what media is. Through the method of comparative conceptual analysis, the article reconstructs the logic by which media philosophy moves from organicist technological determinism to media ontology and temporal eventfulness, and on this basis advances a working definition of media communication as a cultural interface. B. Stiegler's figure of the prosthesis describes media as a technology of memory that exteriorizes mnemonic function: media do not extend the sense organs but rather externalize the very form of their internal organization, making possible epiphylogenesis — the accumulation of human experience outside the biological body. M. Serres, through the figure of the parasite, reframes noise and communicative breakdown as productive tension that renews the system, giving the organicist model of media a cybernetic and eco-Darwinist dimension. S. Krämer develops the figure of the transparent messenger as a model of the non-generative medium — one that preserves distance between communicants without producing meaning, disappearing at the moment its mission is fulfilled. In T. Barker's account, the figure of the hybrid event describes media communication not as linear transmission but as processual-relational becoming, in which the human, machinic, affective, and temporal are interwoven into a single event-network. The comparison identifies four dimensions of mediality integrated within the author's model of media communication as a cultural interface. The interface organizes bodily access to the medium, the preservation of experience, the positions of participants, and feedback. Literal and optical grammatizations are distinguished by temporal organization, the mode of sign fixation, and the regime of user action. In hybrid formats, both logics may operate simultaneously at different levels of the interface.

title: Эволюция образа мистического тела Церкви в религиозно-философском дискурсе Англии и Франции XIV–XV вв.
title_original: Эволюция образа мистического тела Церкви в религиозно-философском дискурсе Англии и Франции XIV–XV вв.
summary: The metaphor of the mystical body of the Church historically emphasized the unity of Christians and their loyalty to God. In the late Middle Ages, due to the struggle between secular rulers and popes, this metaphor began to acquire a different meaning: the body of the Church has begun to separate from the figure of the Pope. As a result of the changes within the Catholic Church — the Western Schism of 1378–1415, the growth of lay religious movements — the metaphor of the mystical body became quite a popular argument in the debates over Church issues of 14th and 15th centuries, for instance, among the Conciliarists, who advocated for the convocation of a church council. Jean Gerson referred to the image of the mystical body several times in his sermons and treatises, arguing for the need to heal the “sickness” of the mystical body (the schism) by unifying and convening a council to elect a new pontiff. The metaphor of the body became an argument against the dual leadership of the Church: just as a body cannot have two heads, the coexistence of the Avignon and Roman pontiffs was likewise impossible. At the same time, this image was also utilized by poets, such as Eustache Deschamps in France and John Gower in England. The article demonstrates how the image of the mystical body was co-opted by critics of Church vices and used for polemical purposes, to promote the independence of secular power from church hierarchies, and to argue for the necessity of convening a council of all believers to elect a single pope.

title: Представления о традиции в нарративах Женской секции Испанской фаланги
title_original: Представления о традиции в нарративах Женской секции Испанской фаланги
summary: This article examines conceptions of tradition in the narratives of the Female Section of the Spanish Falange (1934–1977), the women's organization of Francoist Spain led by Pilar Primo de Rivera (1907–1991). Despite the extensive scholarship on Francoism and Falangism, the ways in which the Female Section engaged with tradition and the mechanisms through which it symbolically constructed it remain largely unexplored. The aim of this study is to reconstruct these conceptions and to demonstrate how tradition functioned as an instrument for legitimizing political power and shaping national identity. Methodologically, the article adopts a constructivist approach, treating tradition not as an immutable cultural heritage but as a dynamic ideological construct whose symbolic content is shaped by political context and continuously redefined in accordance with ideological objectives. The source base consists of Pilar Primo de Rivera's memoirs and speeches, as well as the programmatic documents of the Female Section and the Spanish Falange. The article identifies two principal vectors through which tradition was constructed in the ideology of the Female Section: the medieval-catholic vector and the folk vector. The former is centered on medieval and catholic representations of Spain, while the latter is explored through the activities of Coros y Danzas, revealing the appropriation of regional folklore, its reinterpretation, and its incorporation into a unified national cultural canon.

title: Замечания о релевантной коннексивной логике без сокращения
title_original: Замечания о релевантной коннексивной логике без сокращения
summary: This paper presents a metatheoretical study of CRW, a consistent connexive relevant logic without the contraction axiom. In CRW, Aristotle's and Boethius' theses are provable, and the antecedents and consequents of all its implicative laws share at least one propositional variable. What distinguishes CRW from other connexive relevant logics with a similar class of laws is the preservation of consistency: there is no formula in CRW such that both it and its negation are theorems. Moreover, owing to the absence of contraction, the standard derivation of Curry's paradox is blocked in CRW. The semantics of CRW is based on the notion of a commutative monoid — an algebra with a commutative associative operation and a neutral element. These properties allow the elements of the algebra's domain to be substantively interpreted as finite collections of empirical dossiers — concrete observations, experiments, and measurements. The paper proves the soundness of the axiomatization of CRW and its semantic completeness with respect to the calculus. It is shown that CRW is a conservative extension of the implicative fragment of the relevant logic RW. The completeness proof employs the canonical model method, building on the technique of A. Urquhart as adapted by Y. Weiss. Together, these results establish the adequacy of the axiomatics and semantics, i.e., the coincidence of the classes of provable and valid formulas of CRW.

title: Советское и советский человек. Пролегомены к пониманию
title_original: Советское и советский человек. Пролегомены к пониманию
summary: The phenomena of the “Soviet” and the “new Soviet man” are not a historical accident or an exceptional product of Marxist doctrine. Their unique existence in the USSR requires going beyond the narrow chronological framework of 1917–1991. The article argues that the Soviet system could have arisen and did arise on the specific soil of Russia, became a natural embodiment of the deep, centuries-old constants of Russian historical development (imperialism, autocracy, fusion of power and property, servility of the institution of the church and the fundamental obedience of the people), transformed under the slogans of the modernization breakthrough. Throughout its history, the Soviet system has consistently and purposefully cultivated submission as an active ideological willingness or a consensual, forced practical reaction of a Russian or Soviet person, seeking to make it his fundamental positive property — the willingness to be guided in everything by an imperious will. The assessment of Soviet society and the “new Soviet man” from the point of view of critics of Stalinism in no way can be explained as “historical necessity” or “universally valid justice”.

title: О переводе фрагмента трактата Кардена Ле Бре «О суверенитете короля»
title_original: О переводе фрагмента трактата Кардена Ле Бре «О суверенитете короля»
summary: The publication is dedicated to the translation from French into Russian of a fragment of the political treatise “On Sovereignty” by the French lawyer and state councilor Cardin Le Bret (1558–1655). The first two chapters of the first book are presented. The first chapter is devoted to the issue of royal power, the second chapter — to the definition of sovereignty. The translation is provided with comments. The introductory article provides a short biographical note on the life of Sieur Le Bret. In the article, there are shown his political ties with representatives of the highest political circles of the French Kingdom in the mid-17th century, such as Cardinal de Richelieu and Chancellor Seguier. Le Bret's political ideas were associated with the previous political tradition of justifying strong royal power through the concept of sovereignty. The introductory article provides a short analysis of the terminology of the treatise using the translated fragment as an example. The idea of royal power is closely related to the idea of a role of the sovereign in the administration of Commonwealth. At the same time, it is shown that the definition given by Le Bret is based not only on the theological concept of power, but also on the law on insult to Majesty (“lèze-Majesté”). Le Bret's treatise is important for understanding both the transformations of the idea of royal power and the logic of the further evolution of absolutism. Until now there were no translations of the treatise On Sovereignty into Russian, even in fragments.

Le Bret's treatise is important for understanding both the transformations of the idea of royal power and the logic of the further evolution of absolutism. Until now there were no translations of the treatise On Sovereignty into Russian, even in fragments.
